description: United Airlines Chief Executive Oscar Munoz promised on Wednesday to accommodate any passengers concerned about flying Boeing Co's 737 MAX jets once regulators deem the aircraft safe to fly again.

title: Next round of U.S. tariffs on China at least a month away: Mnuchin
description: The United States is at least a month from enacting its proposed tariffs on $300 billion in Chinese imports as it studies the impact on American consumers, U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin said on Wednesday.

title: Renewed U.S.-China trade tensions push down Wall Street
description: Wall Street's major indexes dipped on Wednesday as inflamed trade tensions between the United States and China weighed on investor sentiment.

title: Musk's SpaceX sues U.S. Air Force over rocket-building contracts: filings
description: Billionaire Elon Musk's SpaceX accused the U.S. Air Force of breaking contracting rules when it awarded money to three rocket makers but passed on Musk's rival bid, and said the tender should be reopened, according to a court filing unsealed on Wednesday.

title: Ikea plans to open first Mexico store in 2020
description: IKEA, the world's largest furniture seller, will open its first store in Mexico next year and plans to launch other stores around the country, the company said on Wednesday, as it expands in Latin America to counter growing competition in its core U.S. and European markets.

title: Lloyd's of London plans to merge governance bodies -source
description: Lloyd's of London is proposing merging two of its governance bodies, the council and the board which together oversee the insurance market, to reduce overlap, a source familiar with the matter said.

title: GE needs to end infighting, fix quality, tighten management: CEO
description: General Electric Co, once seen as the epitome of corporate greatness, is trying to end infighting between its divisions, tighten up management and fix quality problems in its products, Chief Executive Officer Larry Culp said on Wednesday.

description: Qualcomm Inc illegally suppressed competition in the market for smartphone chips by threatening to cut off supplies and extracting excessive licensing fees, a U.S. judge ruled, a decision that could force the company to overhaul its business practices.

title: Daimler CEO announces sweeping cost review as he bows out
description: Daimler's Chief Executive Dieter Zetsche announced a sweeping cost review on Wednesday, his last day in office, as he bid farewell to shareholders following more than a decade at the helm of luxury carmaker Mercedes-Benz.

title: U.S. Justice Department staff recommends blocking T-Mobile-Sprint deal, sources say
description: The U.S. Justice Department's antitrust division staff has recommended the agency block T-Mobile US Inc's $26 billion acquisition of smaller rival Sprint Corp, according to two sources familiar with the matter.

description: U.S. bond markets are "flirting" with a yield curve inversion that could signal slower economic growth ahead, Dallas Federal Reserve Bank President Robert Kaplan said on Wednesday.

description: Honda Motor Co said on Wednesday it is recalling 137,000 new sport utility vehicles (SUVs) following reports of three injuries tied to sudden air bag deployments in the United States.

title: T-Mobile-Sprint deal would boost prices, hurt poorest U.S. consumers, experts say
description: Concessions by T-Mobile US Inc to win U.S. government approval to buy Sprint Corp will likely lead to higher prices for the poorest Americans, many of whom use prepaid wireless plans, analysts and activists said.

description: More than 100 public health and anti-tobacco organizations are calling on Facebook Inc, Instagram, Twitter and Snap Inc to take "swift action" to curb advertising of tobacco products on their platforms.

description: The U.S. economy should grow at a solid 2.25-2.50% rate this year, with inflation moving up to the Federal Reserve's target, putting rates in the right place, a top Fed official said on Wednesday.

description: Radio frequency chipmaker Qorvo on Tuesday joined mobile parts maker Lumentum Holdings Inc in halting shipments to Huawei Technologies, following export restrictions by the United States government.

description: Washington's blacklisting of technology giant Huawei has taken a toll on U.S. semiconductor shares, but China-listed firms have rallied as investors bet they can gain from Beijing's stepped-up efforts to build a homegrown supply chain.

description: An international trade fair in North Korea this week may be the largest such event on record, analysts said on Tuesday, with hundreds of Chinese and other foreign vendors taking part despite sanctions pressure.

description: Airbus is sticking to its 2019 delivery goals as it makes progress in resolving industrial problems at its Hamburg single-aisle jet plant, the planemaker's recently appointed operations chief said on Tuesday.

description: J.C.Penney Inc on Tuesday warned of a "meaningful impact" on its private and national brands from U.S. President Donald Trump's potential fourth round of tariffs on Chinese imports.

title: Turkish Airlines chairman expects Boeing 737 compensation, to meet Friday
description: Turkish Airlines expects compensation from Boeing Co for losses over the grounding of 12 737 Max aircraft, the chairman of Turkey's flagship carrier was quoted as saying, adding that he would meet Boeing's chief executive on Friday.

title: Some major Deutsche Bank investors want chairman to go early: sources

description: U.S. drugmaker Merck & Co Inc on Tuesday agreed to buy Peloton Therapeutics Inc for $1.05 billion in cash, gaining access to the privately held company's lead kidney cancer drug candidate.

description: From submitting their fingerprints to giving up their tax records, Wells Fargo & Co's next chief executive will go through a vetting process that could rival that of top U.S. government officials.

title: France to push ahead with 5G launch in 2020 despite Huawei woes
description: France will launch the deployment of its 5G network as planned in 2020 despite current difficulties faced by China's Huawei which could push some telecoms operators to modify their source of supply, the telecoms regulator said Tuesday.

title: Huawei believes Europe will keep faith in company: executive

description: U.S. fliers still consider ticket prices the most important factor when choosing a flight, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll, suggesting two fatal crashes of Boeing Co 737 MAX jets have had little impact on consumer sentiment.

title: U.S. factory output drops for third time in four months
description: Declining output of cars and machinery led U.S. factory production to fall unexpectedly in April, a sign the economy is losing a step as a trade war with China intensifies.

title: WhatsApp security breach may have targeted human rights groups
description: WhatsApp said on Tuesday that a security breach on its messaging app had signs of coming from a government using surveillance technology developed by a private company, and it may have targeted human rights groups.

title: JPMorgan Chase will invest $125 million in programs to encourage people to save money
description: JPMorgan Chase & Co will provide $125 million over the next five years to nonprofit groups in the United States and abroad that help people save, pay down debt and improve their credit scores, the bank said on Wednesday.

title: Nissan set for weakest profit in 11 years as Ghosn woes, bleak sales weigh
description: Nissan Motor Co forecast a 28% plunge in its annual operating profit, putting it on course for the weakest earnings in 11 years and underscoring its struggle to turn the page after former Chairman Carlos Ghosn was ousted.

title: Exclusive: Trump expected to sign order paving way for U.S. telecoms ban on Huawei
description: President Donald Trump is expected to sign an executive order this week barring U.S. companies from using telecommunications equipment made by firms posing a national security risk, paving the way for a ban on doing business with China's Huawei, three U.S. officials familiar with the plan told Reuters.

title: China's retail sales growth slumps to 16-year low as trade war risks rise
description: China reported surprisingly weaker growth in retail sales and industrial output for April on Wednesday, adding pressure on Beijing to roll out more stimulus as the trade war with the United States escalates.

title: China says it will support firms in boosting R&D spending
description: China will support firms in boosting their spending on research and development, state television cited the cabinet as saying on Wednesday.

title: Walmart mulls stock market listing for UK arm Asda
description: Walmart, the world's biggest retailer, said it is considering a stock market listing for its British supermarket arm Asda, whose attempt to combine with rival Sainsbury's was blocked by the UK regulator last month.

title: IKEA says in final stages of talks to invest in Northvolt
description: IKEA is in the final stages of talks with Northvolt about participating in the battery startup's fundraising for a factory, the world's biggest furniture retailer said on Wednesday.

title: SoftBank leads $200 million investment in India's Grofers
description: Japan's SoftBank Group Corp has led an investment round of more than $200 million in online grocery startup Grofers India through its Vision Fund, the New Delhi-based company said on Wednesday, upping competition in a hotly chased market in the country.

title: Rising U.S. oil output helps fill gap left by Iran, Venezuela: IEA
description: The world will require very little extra oil from OPEC this year as booming U.S. output will offset falling exports from Iran and Venezuela, the International Energy Agency said on Wednesday.

title: China says it is only taking actions in self defense in U.S. trade dispute
description: China's Foreign Ministry said on Wednesday the United States was defining the two countries' dispute over trade as a trade war, and China was only taking action in self-defense.

title: Trump calls trade war with China 'little squabble,' says talks ongoing
description: U.S. President Donald Trump on Tuesday called the trade war with China "a little squabble" and insisted talks between the world's two largest economies had not collapsed, as investors remained on guard for a further escalation of tit-for-tat tariffs.

title: Startups target banks' small business customers in FX payments drive
description: Revolut and TransferWise are signing up thousands of small businesses a month for foreign exchange payments, touting slicker service and lower fees as they try to take on banks in a sector with flows of $7 trillion a year.

title: French fashion group Kering pledges to hire only over-18 models
description: Kering, the French fashion group whose brands include Gucci and Saint Laurent, said it would only work with models aged over 18, as the fashion industry aims to tighten up its ethical guidelines.

title: U.S. tariffs against Airbus would harm Delta: airline official
description: U.S. imposition of tariffs against the European Union over aircraft subsidies would cause "serious harm" to Delta Air Lines since the U.S. carrier is already under contract to buy several billion dollars worth of Airbus aircraft, a senior airline official said on Wednesday.

title: WhatsApp informs Irish regulator of 'serious security vulnerability'
description: Facebook's WhatsApp has informed its lead regulator in the European Union, Ireland's Data Protection Commissioner (DPC), of a serious security vulnerability on its platform, the DPC said on Tuesday.

title: Beyond Meat surges after coffee chain Tim Hortons adds vegan sausages to menu
description: Shares of Beyond Meat rose as much as 16% on Wednesday after Canada's Restaurant Brands International Inc's coffee chain Tim Hortons said it will introduce three new sandwiches using the vegan burger marker's plant-based sausages

title: Buffett's Berkshire unveils $861 million Amazon stake
description: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway Inc said it owned $860.6 million of Amazon.com Inc shares at the end of March, after the billionaire admitted to underestimating the online retailer and its Chief Executive Jeff Bezos.

title: Ford recalling 273,000 vehicles in North America that could roll away
description: Ford Motor Co is recalling nearly 273,000 Ford Fusion and Ranger pickup trucks in North America that could roll away if the gear is not in "park" mode, the second largest U.S. automaker said on Wednesday.

title: Alibaba beats revenue expectations on cloud boost
description: Chinese e-commerce giant Alibaba Group Holding Ltd beat fourth-quarter revenue forecasts on Wednesday, thanks to growth in its core business and its diversification into cloud computing and other services.

title: U.S. judge dumps 'Pooey Puitton' lawsuit against Louis Vuitton
description: Louis Vuitton has won the dismissal of a lawsuit by a California toy company that accused the French luxury goods maker of trying to interfere with its sales of a poop-shaped toy purse for children, Pooey Puitton.

title: Trade group to hold meeting of airlines affected by Boeing's grounded 737 MAX
description: A trade group is inviting airlines that use Boeing Co 737 MAX jets to meet next week to discuss challenges they face as a result of the grounding of the airline model involved in two fatal crashes, as they prepare to reintroduce the planes into operation.

title: Mexico says it is close to U.S. metals tariff deal, waiting for Canada
description: Mexico is close to resolving its dispute with the United States over steel and aluminum tariffs without quotas but hopes Canada can reach a similar agreement before completing it, a senior Mexican official said on Wednesday.

title: Cisco beats earnings target, says has cushioned supply chain from tariffs
description: Cisco Systems Inc reported better-than-expected quarterly earnings on Wednesday and gave an upbeat sales forecast for the current period, saying that minimal sales exposure to China and changes to its supply chains have helped cushion the blow of U.S.-China trade dispute.

title: Not right time for Mexico to target new U.S. products in steel dispute: official
description: Progress being made between Washington and Mexico City toward repealing U.S. tariffs on steel means it is not the right time for Mexico to target new U.S. products in retaliation for the duties, a senior Mexican official said on Wednesday.

title: Big U.S. hedge funds regain ardor for FAANGs in first quarter: filings
description: Some of the biggest, highest-profile U.S. hedge fund investors and money managers fell back in love with FAANGs in the first quarter, according to regulatory filings released on Wednesday.

title: Macy's CEO says tariff escalation could hurt business
description: Macy's Inc said on Wednesday the latest tariffs on Chinese imports by Washington are hitting its furniture business and warned investors that additional levies would leave its clothing and accessory categories vulnerable as well.

title: Wall St. ends higher as trade worries ease
description: U.S. stocks closed higher on Wednesday as reports that U.S. President Donald Trump would hold off on imposing tariffs on imported cars and parts eased growth concerns even as economic data disappointed investors.

title: FAA expects Boeing to submit 737 MAX fix soon for approval
description: Federal Aviation Administration acting chief Dan Elwell told lawmakers on Wednesday he expects Boeing Co to submit a software fix for the grounded 737 MAX involved in two fatal crashes for approval soon, and said he was concerned by the planemaker's lengthy delay in disclosing a software anomaly.

title: Boeing made mistakes on 737 MAX says Southwest CEO, hopeful planes return in U.S. summer
description: Boeing Co made mistakes with its 737 MAX planes that need to be addressed, Southwest Airlines Co Chief Executive Officer Gary Kelly told shareholders on Wednesday, but he said he is still hopeful that the jets grounded after two crashes will return to service in the U.S. summer.

title: Advisory firms say AIG shareholders should vote 'no' on executive pay
description: American International Group Inc shareholders should vote against compensation packages for top executives at the insurer's annual meeting next week, according to two advisory firms that hold sway over investor votes.

title: Harvey Weinstein's former film studio plans to liquidate in bankruptcy
description: The film studio once run by Harvey Weinstein said it plans to liquidate in bankruptcy, as it tries to resolve civil lawsuits against former directors and officers arising from sexual misconduct claims against the onetime Hollywood mogul.

title: WeWork starts $2.9 billion property platform with Canada's CDPQ
description: The We Company, parent of workspace provider WeWork, said on Wednesday it has created a $2.9 billion real estate investment platform with funding from one of Canada's largest pension funds, building on ties with private equity firm the Rhone Group.

title: Supersonic jets must be no noisier than existing planes: airports group
description: A new generation of U.S.-produced commercial supersonic jets must be no louder than existing planes or risk exacerbating existing complaints over noise from air traffic, Angela Gittens, director of Airports Council International (ACI) said.

title: GE says it needs time for power-plant unit to recover
description: General Electric Co tamped down enthusiasm about a quick recovery in its power-plant unit on Wednesday, and an analyst said the company was not "telling the whole story" about purported market-share gains at its ailing power unit.

title: Nestle in talks with EQT Partners to sell skin health unit: source
description: Nestle SA is in exclusive talks with a consortium led by private equity firm EQT Partners for a sale of its skin health unit, according to a source familiar with the matter.

title: Commerzbank to hold supervisory board meeting to discuss strategy: sources
description: Commerzbank plans to hold an extraordinary meeting of its supervisory board on May 21 to discuss strategy, people  familiar with the matter said on Wednesday.

title: U.S. bank regulator will vet next Wells Fargo CEO
description: A top U.S. bank regulator said on Wednesday it will vet Wells Fargo & Co's pick for its next chief executive, a development that could complicate the scandal-hit lender's efforts to find a permanent replacement for CEO Tim Sloan.

title: Pelosi had 'productive meeting' with U.S. trade representative on deal: aide
description: U.S. House of Representatives Speaker Nancy Pelosi had a "productive meeting" with U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer almost entirely focused on a new United States-Mexico-Canada (USMCA) trade deal, one of her aides said on Wednesday.

title: Exclusive: Kone looks at options for potential Thyssenkrupp elevator deal - sources
description: Finland's Kone is assessing the viability of a bid for Thyssenkrupp's 14 billion euro ($15.7 billion) elevators division even as the German conglomerate pursues plans to list it, four people familiar with the matter said.

title: Canada's Freeland: U.S. tariffs would make USMCA ratification problematic
description: Canadian Foreign Minister Chrystia Freeland said on Wednesday that ratification of the U.S.-Mexico-Canada trade agreement would be very problematic as long as U.S. tariffs on steel and aluminum remain in place.

title: Global stocks gain after Trump auto-tariff delay, weak data pressures yields
description: U.S. and European stock indexes gained on Wednesday after news that U.S. President Donald Trump planned to delay tariffs on auto imports, offsetting earlier pressure on equities from weak U.S. and Chinese economic data that helped depress bond yields.

title: MBDA boss faces battle of wits as Airbus strategy chief
description: The chief executive of European missile maker MBDA is returning to Airbus as head of strategy as the planemaker seeks to modernize its factories and explore future options in defense.

title: Boeing, aerospace group urge limits to U.S. tariffs over EU subsidies
description: Senior officials from Boeing Co and a U.S. aerospace trade group on Wednesday urged the U.S. government to narrowly tailor any tariffs imposed on the European Union over illegal aircraft subsidies to avoid harming American manufacturers.

title: Weak U.S. retail sales, industrial output highlight slowing economy
description: U.S. retail sales unexpectedly fell in April as households cut back on purchases of motor vehicles and a range of other goods, pointing to a slowdown in economic growth after a temporary boost from exports and inventories in the first quarter.

title: Trump defends China trade battle, vows deal will happen
description: U.S. President Donald Trump on Tuesday defended his trade war with China as tensions escalated and markets extended their losses, promising a deal with Chinese President Xi Jinping soon, even as fears escalated about a protracted battle.

title: China says it hopes U.S. does not underestimate its determination
description: China's foreign ministry said on Tuesday that it hopes the United States does not underestimate its determination to protect its interests, even as Washington threatened to extend tariffs to virtually all Chinese imports.

title: Factbox: Tariff wars - duties imposed by Trump and U.S. trading partners
description: China on Monday raised tariffs on $60 billion of U.S. goods in retaliation for President Donald Trump's decision to increase tariffs on $200 billion worth of Chinese imports last week, escalating the trade war between the world's two largest economies.

title: PG&E proposes court order for CEO, board to tour town destroyed by wildfire
description: PG&E Corp on Monday submitted a proposed order to a U.S. District Court judge that would require the power provider's chief executive and board to visit the California town of Paradise by July 15, to see the destruction caused by a wildfire in November that may be linked to the company's equipment.

title: India delays levying retaliatory tariff on U.S. goods to June 16
description: India delayed on Tuesday the implementation of higher tariffs on some goods imported from the United States to June 16, according to a government statement.

title: Oil prices jump on drone attack on Saudi Aramco facilities
description: Oil prices rose on Tuesday after top exporter Saudi Arabia said explosive-laden drones launched by a Yemeni armed movement aligned to Iran had attacked facilities belonging to state oil company Aramco.

title: JPMorgan says UK PM May unlikely to survive beyond the end of June
description: U.S. investment bank JPMorgan said on Tuesday it was difficult to see British Prime Minister Theresa May surviving beyond the end of June.

title: U.S. leaves rare earths, critical minerals off China tariff list
description: The United States has again decided not to impose tariffs on rare earths and other critical minerals from China, underscoring its reliance on the Asian nation for a group of materials used in everything from consumer electronics to military equipment.

title: India's Jet Airways sees management exodus as rescue hopes dim
description: The chief executive and two other senior figures at Jet Airways have quit, the Indian company said on Tuesday, further eroding any hopes of a rescue of the debt-laden carrier that grounded operations last month.

title: Mexico's rising oil nationalism faces debt-rating crisis
description: Mexican President Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador took office in December vowing to revive state-owned energy company Pemex and put the brakes on foreign investment to give the public a bigger cut of the country's oil wealth.

title: Saudi Aramco bets on oil supply to Europe, trading expansion
description: Saudi Aramco aims to boost its oil supply to Europe by 300,000 barrels per day (bpd) within the next two years as it expands its trading operations there with an office opening this summer in London, a senior company executive said.

title: Cash-rich Canadian oil firms favor buybacks as other options narrow
description: Canadian oil producers are raking in the highest revenues in five years thanks to strong global oil prices and Alberta's production cuts, but government intervention has hamstrung their spending abilities, encouraging many to buy back shares and pay down debt.

title: U.S. LNG companies Cheniere and Tellurian see U.S.-China trade spat as short term
description: Executives from U.S. liquefied natural gas (LNG) companies Cheniere Energy and Tellurian on Tuesday said they view the trade dispute between China and the United States as temporary, with no major impact on their ability to sell LNG.

title: EU regulators to investigate Insurance Ireland data pooling system
description: EU antitrust regulators opened an investigation on Tuesday into Insurance Ireland's data pooling system, concerned that conditions set by the association to access the system may block rivals in violation of EU competition rules.

title: Iran insists on ramping up oil sales to stay in nuclear pact: sources
description: Iran insists on exporting at least 1.5 million barrels per day (bpd) of oil, triple May's expected levels under U.S. sanctions, as a condition for staying in an international nuclear deal, sources with knowledge of Iran-EU talks said.

title: Record level of funds hedge against stocks fall: BAML survey
description: Global investors' equity allocations fell 6 percentage points in May and over a third of fund managers have taken out protection against sharp stock market falls in coming months, Bank of America Merrill Lynch's latest monthly survey found on Tuesday.

title: Fed's Williams says policymakers need to better prepare for lower interest rate world
description: Torturously slow recoveries from recessions and low inflation are here to stay unless policymakers can get a better grip on how to stabilize the global economy in an era of lower interest rates, a top Federal Reserve policymaker said on Tuesday.

title: Fed's Williams says tariffs boost U.S. inflation, weigh on growth
description: Tariffs imposed by President Donald Trump on Chinese goods in the escalating trade war between the two countries will boost U.S. inflation and could dampen economic growth, a top Federal Reserve policymaker said on Tuesday.

title: Goldman Sachs bought Commerzbank's claim in Saudi's biggest debt saga: sources
description: Goldman Sachs has bought a claim against The International Bank Corporation (TIBC), a Bahraini bank whose default 10 years ago triggered the biggest financial crisis in Saudi Arabia, three sources familiar with the matter said.

title: Huawei is not controlled by China, executive says
description: Huawei is a private company that is not controlled by the Chinese government and would refuse to hand over information to Beijing although no such request has been made, the firm's Vice President of Western Europe said on Tuesday.

title: Volkswagen will use Traton proceeds to internationalize truck business: CEO
description: Volkswagen will use proceeds of an initial public offering of its Traton trucks unit to invest in the "internationalization" of the division, Chief Executive Officer Herbert Diess said on Tuesday.

title: Starbucks, Mercon announce separate sustainability loans
description: Starbucks and Mercon Coffee Group separately announced sustainability-focused loan facilities on Monday, signaling the coffee sector's growing emphasis on sustainability as climate change and low global prices threaten the future of the crop.

title: Members only: U.S. retailers revamp loyalty schemes for Amazon era
description: With private fitting rooms, members-only stores and clever apps, U.S. department stores are reinventing their old and tested loyalty programs to fend off the challenge from e-commerce giant Amazon.com Inc and other online rivals.

title: Trump and Xi to meet after defiant China hits U.S. with new tariffs
description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Monday he would meet Chinese President Xi Jinping next month as the trade war between the world's two largest economies intensified, sending shivers through global markets.

title: Trump says U.S. farmers to get $15 billion in aid amid China trade war
description: President Donald Trump said on Monday that his administration was planning to provide about $15 billion in aid to help U.S. farmers whose products may be targeted with tariffs by China in a deepening trade war.

title: Ralph Lauren's North America woes cloud profit beat, shares down nearly 8%
description: Luxury apparel maker Ralph Lauren Corp beat Wall Street estimates for quarterly profit on Tuesday, benefiting from higher demand in international markets, but weak sales in its biggest market, North America, disappointed investors.

title: No sign that Beijing will offer a no-spy deal: Germany
description: There is no sign that China is offering a "no-spy" agreement of the kind that would help telecommunications equipment maker Huawei in its bid for contracts to build Germany's next-generation mobile networks, a German Interior Ministry spokesman said on Tuesday.

title: Trump says U.S.-China trade talks have not collapsed
description: U.S. President Donald Trump on Tuesday said trade talks with China had not collapsed, characterizing the trade war between the world's two largest economies as "a little squabble."

title: Boeing deliveries hammered by 737 MAX groundings
description: Boeing Co handed over 24 percent fewer jet airplanes in the first four months of 2019 compared with the same period a year earlier as the grounding of its top-selling 737 MAX aircraft halted deliveries for a second month.

title: Oil prices rise over 1% on drone attack on Saudi Aramco facilities
description: Oil prices rose over 1% on Tuesday after top exporter Saudi Arabia said explosive-laden drones launched by a Yemeni-armed movement aligned to Iran had attacked facilities belonging to state oil company Aramco.

title: Uber drivers are contractors, not employees, U.S. labor agency says
description: Drivers for ride-hailing company Uber Technologies Inc are independent contractors and not employees, the general counsel of a U.S. labor agency has concluded, in an advisory memo that is likely to carry significant weight in a pending case against the company and could prevent drivers from joining a union.

title: Nissan faces long, rocky road to cut U.S. discounts, rental sales
description: Nissan Motor Co Ltd said on Tuesday it had hit "rock bottom" with a 45% drop in annual operating profit. The automaker's troubles in the United States, including a failure to deliver on a slew of promises to dealers, are a major reason why.

title: U.S. growth would have contracted without trillions in government, consumer debt: Gundlach
description: U.S. growth appears to be based "exclusively" on government, corporate and mortgage debt and the economy would have contracted if the United States had not added trillions in debt, Jeffrey Gundlach, chief executive of DoubleLine Capital, said in an investor webcast on Tuesday.

title: U.S. to take 'fresh look' at opening automakers' key spectrum band
description: The U.S. Federal Communications Commission plans to vote in June on launching a new review of a key spectrum band reserved for automakers that could boost Wi-Fi use, a person briefed on the matter said on Tuesday.

title: Google to push new ads on its apps to snare shoppers
description: Whether you are Googling on the couch, fiddling with Maps in the car or swiping through the Discover feed on the toilet, expect Alphabet Inc's Google to put ads in several new spots this year.

title: Stocks bounce back as trade rhetoric cools
description: U.S. stocks on Tuesday reclaimed some of the ground lost in the prior day's steep sell-off, with tariff-sensitive technology stocks leading the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq higher as investors were heartened by a tonal shift in U.S.-China trade rhetoric.

title: Global stocks bounce back as Trump downplays U.S.-China trade fight
description: U.S. and European stocks regained ground on Tuesday after President Donald Trump downplayed the U.S.-China trade war as "a little squabble" a day after a spike in tensions between the world's two largest economies rattled financial markets.

title: U.S. Treasury chief to plan for trade meeting in China soon: spokesman
description: U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin will plan for another trade meeting in China at some point soon, a Treasury spokesman said on Tuesday, adding to President Donald Trump's earlier statements that U.S. dialogue with Beijing was continuing.

title: U.S. Senate moves forward on plan to develop electric vehicle supply chain
description: U.S. lawmakers on Tuesday moved closer to developing a national electric vehicle supply chain policy, with senators voicing bipartisan support for legislation designed to parry China's dominance in metals production and battery manufacturing.

title: Bayer nears seven-year low after $2 billion award in Roundup trial
description: Bayer shares fell by as much as 5 percent on Tuesday after a California couple were awarded more than $2 billion in the largest U.S. jury penalty over allegations its Roundup weed killer causes cancer.

title: Factbox: More Roundup trials, appeals in store for Bayer after $2 billion verdict
description: Bayer shares continued to fall on Tuesday after a California jury on Monday awarded more than $2 billion in damages to a couple who alleged that the company's glyphosate-based weed killer Roundup caused their cancers.

title: Nissan earnings slide fuels Renault deal pressure
description: Renault is quietly pushing for a change of Nissan leadership as a prelude to merger talks, sources at both companies said, after the Japanese carmaker warned of a further earnings slide in the wake of the Carlos Ghosn scandal.

title: Disney takes control of Hulu to challenge Netflix, Amazon
description: Walt Disney Co said it will take full control of the Hulu service in a deal with Comcast Corp, as it vies for a bigger piece of the global video streaming market dominated by companies such as Netflix Inc.

title: Senate Majority Leader McConnell says 'nobody wins a trade war'
description: Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell said on Tuesday that "nobody wins a trade war" but he hoped President Donald Trump's tactics in negotiations China would put the United States in a better position to move trade talks forward with Beijing.

title: Huawei willing to sign 'no-spy' pacts with governments: chairman
description: Huawei  is willing to sign no-spy agreements with governments, including Britain, the Chinese telco company's chairman said on Tuesday, amid U.S. pressure on European countries to shun the firm over espionage concerns.

title: Exclusive: UniCredit advances toward bid for Germany's Commerzbank – sources
description: UniCredit has stepped up preparations for a potential bid for Germany's Commerzbank by drafting in investment bankers including a former top German official, three people familiar with the matter said.

title: Volkswagen wins worker backing for restructuring with $1.1 billion battery plan
description: Volkswagen workers backed a restructuring of the world's largest carmaker on Tuesday after Chief Executive Herbert Diess pledged to spend 1 billion euros ($1.1 billion) on a new battery cell production plant near its headquarters in Lower Saxony.

title: VOI makes European push in crowded electric scooter-sharing market
description: Sweden's VOI Technology plans to put a new fleet of thousands of electric scooters on European streets this summer to fend off competition in an increasingly crowded market.

title: ConocoPhillips will not chase expensive Permian deals, CEO says
description: ConocoPhillips Chief Executive Officer Ryan Lance on Tuesday repeated a pledge to restrain spending, saying the U.S. oil producer would not be drawn into pricey mergers and acquisitions.

title: Britain downplays Huawei threat to U.S. intelligence sharing
description: Britain would never take a decision on Huawei and 5G that would threaten its intelligence sharing alliance with the United States but it also does not want a new Cold War with China, Foreign Secretary Jeremy Hunt said on Tuesday.

title: ChargePoint sounds alarm on electric vehicle charging standards
description: A leading operator of charging stations has sounded the alarm on a proposed technical standard that it says could hamper mass adoption of electric vehicles by making it harder to charge them at home or at work.

title: GE books more power plant orders, beats Mitsubishi, Siemens: sources
description: General Electric Co won the most orders in the sharply contracting market for new gas-fired power plants in the first quarter, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: OPEC sees more 2019 demand for its oil as it keeps cutting output
description: OPEC said on Tuesday that world demand for its oil would be higher than expected this year as supply growth from rivals including U.S. shale producers slows, pointing to a tighter market if the exporter group refrains from raising output.

title: Carrefour and TerraCycle launch 'Loop' test in Paris to tackle waste
description: French retailer Carrefour and U.S. waste recycling company TerraCycle launched on Tuesday the test for their 'Loop' initiative which they hope will tackle the problems of plastic waste threatening to destroy the environment.

title: Walmart fights back against Amazon with one-day shipping in some U.S. markets
description: Walmart Inc is stepping up its battle with Amazon.com Inc by offering one-day delivery without a shipping fee, weeks after Amazon announced a similar offer - a move that will intensify the race to deliver orders to shoppers faster.

title: Rapid bitcoin rally cheers crypto market investors, others wary
description: Bitcoin hit its highest level in 10 months on Tuesday, raising hopes among cryptocurrency enthusiasts of greater mainstream acceptance as an escalating U.S.-China trade war roiled global markets, but others urged investor caution.

title: Renault diesel allegations upheld by court study: report
description: A French probe into alleged emissions cheating by Renault is a step closer to possible court action, Le Monde reported on Monday, after a technical report confirmed that some of its diesel engines were configured to emit more pollutants outside official test conditions.

title: China hikes tariffs on U.S. goods after Trump warning
description: China said on Monday it would impose higher tariffs on most U.S. imports on a revised $60 billion target list, hitting back at a tariff hike by Washington on $200 billion of Chinese goods in a further escalation of a bitter trade war.

title: Taiwan's Foxconn readies chip boss to succeed Gou as chairman: sources
description: Foxconn is poised to nominate chip unit boss Liu Young to succeed Terry Gou as chairman in a surprise choice by the iPhone assembler, two people with direct knowledge of the matter said.

title: Norway clears way for Euronext to secure Oslo Bors in Nasdaq battle
description: Euronext won approval from Norway's Ministry of Finance to buy up to 100% of Oslo Bors on Monday, effectively ending a five-month battle with Nasdaq for one of the last independent stock market operators in Europe.

title: Bed Bath & Beyond long-time CEO steps down following investor pressure
description: Bed Bath & Beyond Inc's  long-time Chief Executive Officer Steven Temares stepped down on Monday, following pressure from a group of activist investors that had been pushing for his ouster and a shakeup of the furnishing retailer's board.

title: Oil supply crunch to test OPEC's spare capacity
description: Oil production capacity could fall to under one percent of global oil demand by the end of the year if OPEC compensates falling production from Iran and Venezuela, leaving oil prices exposed to sharp swings in the event of unplanned outages, analysts say.

title: U.S.-Chinese tariffs seen cutting global growth by 0.15%: Societe Generale
description: The latest U.S. and Chinese round of planned tariffs on each other's imports may reduce global economic growth by 0.15% and lower China's gross domestic product by 0.5% and U.S. GDP by 0.25%, Societe Generale's U.S. chief economist said on Monday.

title: Deutsche Bank talks with UBS on asset management deal stall: sources
description: Talks have stalled between Deutsche Bank and UBS on a tie up of their asset management businesses due to differences over who would control the combined entity, people familiar with the matter said.

title: Daimler's CEO designate will push alliances to cut costs
description: Daimler will cut development costs of new Mercedes-Benz cars by a significant amount by 2025 and will intensify alliances with rivals as a way to improve margins, Ola Kaellenius, the future chief executive, said on Monday.

title: Italian bank fund won't plug entire Carige capital hole: sources
description: Italian banks will not step in to plug a capital shortfall at regional lender Banca Carige after U.S. fund manager BlackRock pulled out of a planned rescue bid, sources said, making a state bailout for the bank more likely.

title: BlackRock pullout makes state role in Carige rescue more plausible: Moody's
description: The decision of U.S. asset manager BlackRock to pull out of the rescue of Italian troubled bank Carige makes state intervention more plausible, Moody's Investors Service said on Monday.

title: Six Chinese entities banned from exporting sensitive U.S. goods
description: The U.S. Commerce Department said on Monday it banned six Chinese technology entities, one Pakistani firm and five based in the United Arab Emirates from exporting sensitive U.S. technologies and other goods.

title: Trump warns China not to retaliate against tariff hike
description: U.S. President Donald Trump on Monday warned China not to retaliate against a hike in tariffs he imposed last week and said that the nation "will be hurt very badly if you don't make a deal."

title: Bar rises for shale takeovers as Chevron bows out of Anadarko fight
description: Chevron Chief Executive Michael Wirth's decision to opt out of a bidding war for Anadarko Petroleum Corp has raised the bar for deals, and dampened expectations that oil majors will drive a new wave of consolidation in U.S. shale.

title: Exclusive: Impossible Foods raises $300 million with investors eager for bite of meatless burgers
description: Impossible Foods, which makes a meatless plant-based burger and is backed by celebrities like Serena Williams and Katy Perry, said on Monday it has raised $300 million in the latest round of funding ahead of a possible initial public offering.

title: Exclusive: Turkey presses banks to agree high-stakes bailout of bad energy loans
description: Turkey's plan to clean up some $13 billion in bad energy loans, one of the worst hangovers from last year's currency crisis, is taking shape even as some banks hold out for the government to agree to safeguards and higher electricity prices.

title: Chinese group to delay bailout funding for Apple supplier Japan Display
description: A Chinese-Taiwanese group is delaying an up to 80 billion yen ($729.33 million) investment planned as part of a rescue deal for Apple Inc supplier Japan Display as it wants to reassess the target's prospects, the Japanese firm said.

title: TV networks emerge as obstacles on YouTube's hunt for ads
description: Three years ago, the beginning of the end of the U.S. television business looked certain when one of the largest ad buying agencies vowed to move a big chunk of its purchases to YouTube from TV budgets.

title: Novartis vows to fight U.S. price-fixing claims against Sandoz unit
description: Novartis on Monday said claims of price fixing against its Sandoz generics unit amid a U.S. probe of 20 drugmakers are without merit, with the Swiss company vowing to fight allegations in a lawsuit filed last week.

title: EU trade chief sees possible extension to May 18 deadline for U.S. car tariffs: newspaper
description: European Trade Commissioner Cecilia Malmstroem expects U.S. President Donald Trump to delay a May 18 deadline for U.S. tariffs on cars imported from the European union, according to an interview published in the Sueddeutsche newspaper on Monday.

title: Germany liaising with EU on U.S. car tariffs, won't speculate on U.S. timing: ministry
description: Germany is liaising closely with the European Union on a U.S. threat to impose higher car tariffs, the Economy Ministry said on Monday, adding that the German government would not speculate about the timing of the U.S. decision.

title: China defiant toward U.S. on trade, Kudlow urges strong enforcement steps
description: The United States and China appeared at a deadlock over trade negotiations on Sunday as Washington demanded promises of  concrete changes to Chinese law and Beijing said it would not swallow any "bitter fruit" that harmed its interests.

title: Exclusive: Bosch goes for platinum-light fuel cells
description: Global automotive supplier Bosch expects platinum to play only a minor role in its new fuel cells, giving precious metal markets scant benefit even as the technology gains momentum for pollution-free transport.

title: French fashion group Kering sets guidelines on animal welfare
description: French fashion group Kering, whose brands include Gucci and Saint Laurent, said it had set out internal guidelines for dealing with the welfare of animals, as fashion companies look to tighten their ethical standards.

title: U.S. agriculture secretary urges Japan to reach trade deal
description: U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Sonny Perdue urged Japan on Monday  to move swiftly to clinch a trade deal with Washington on farm products and other goods, in a way that would treat his country fairly as "premier customer."

title: Trump says the U.S. is 'right where we want to be with China'
description: President Donald Trump said on Sunday that the United States is "right where we want to be with China," adding that Beijing "broke the deal with us" and then sought to renegotiate.

title: China says it will never surrender to foreign pressure amid trade dispute
description: China's foreign ministry said on Monday the country will never surrender to foreign pressure after Washington renewed its threat to impose tariffs on all Chinese imports in an escalating trade dispute.

title: Australia's export billions go missing, statisticians suspected
description: Australia's export earnings are booming as resource prices surge but a statistical quirk means tens of billions of dollars go missing from main measures of growth, making the economy seem weaker than it actually is.

title: Norway paves way for Euronext takeover of Oslo Bors
description: Norway will allow Euronext to take a majority stake in Oslo Bors VPS, the country's finance ministry said on Monday, confirming an earlier statement by Euronext.

title: Bayer says Monsanto likely kept files on influential people across Europe
description: Bayer said on Monday its Monsanto unit, which is being investigated by French prosecutors for compiling files of influential people such as journalists in France, likely did the same across Europe, suggesting a potentially wider problem.

title: Ray-ban owner EssilorLuxottica draws line under Franco-Italian feud
description: EssilorLuxottica declared an end to a feud between its French and Italian partners on Monday, saying it would drop all legal proceedings and focus on integrating the eyewear group formed by last year's 54 billion euro ($61 billion) merger.

title: In setback for Apple, U.S. Supreme Court lets App Store antitrust suit proceed
description: A divided U.S. Supreme Court on Monday gave the go-ahead to an antitrust lawsuit accusing Apple Inc of forcing consumers to overpay for iPhone software applications, a decision that could lead to billions of dollars in damages and put at risk the company's lucrative way of selling apps.

title: Wells Fargo CEO search hobbled by pay limitations: sources
description: (This May 10th story corrects paragraph 7 to say Wells Fargo may need to match stock-based compensation a candidate has at a current employer, not that company may need to match vested shares.)

title: British telco giant Vodafone offloads NZ business to Brookfield, Infratil
description: Vodafone Group Plc on Monday agreed to sell its New Zealand business for NZ$3.4 billion ($2.23 billion) to a consortium comprising of New Zealand-based Infratil Ltd and Canada's Brookfield Asset Management, in a deal the telecom giant says would help reduce its debt.

title: Tokyo prosecutors detail Ghosn's alleged cash transfer in revised indictment: Kyodo
description: Tokyo prosecutors have filed a request to revise the content of their indictment of Carlos Ghosn for aggravated breach of trust, providing further details on alleged cash transfers involving the former Nissan boss and a Saudi friend, Kyodo news reported.

title: Japan Finmin Aso: Sino-U.S. trade war won't trigger economic crisis
description: Japanese Finance Minister Taro Aso said on Tuesday the Sino-U.S. trade war would not immediately trigger an economic shock on the scale of the "Lehman shock", though the friction between the world's two largest economies is unlikely to be resolved easily.

title: Trump says he feels U.S.-China trade talks 'going to be very successful'
description: President Donald Trump said on Monday he was optimistic about resolving the U.S. trade dispute with China.

title: What's at stake for Europe Inc in a trade spat with Washington
description: Europe's listed companies are expected to generate 1.2 trillion euros (£1.04 trillion) in revenue from the United States this year, highlighting what's at stake as global trade tensions grow and earnings and economic growth stall.

title: Cellphones and laptops on latest USTR China tariff list, drugs excluded
description: A list of products subject to possible U.S. tariffs on about $300 billion of Chinese imports will include cellphones and laptop computers but not pharmaceuticals and rare earth materials, the U.S. Trade Representative's Office said on Monday.

title: Long fight over error in JPMorgan loan to GM settles for $231 million
description: Lenders and hundreds of investors agreed on Monday to pay $231 million to end their decade-long legal fight over a clerical error in a $1.5 billion loan to General Motors that was administered by JPMorgan Chase & Co , according to court documents.

title: Amazon extends lead as top retail brand in Kantar/WPP survey
description: Amazon has almost doubled its brand value to $316 billion as it expands in areas like entertainment and smart speakers, while China's Alibaba is now the world's second most valuable retail brand, a survey showed on Tuesday.

title: Investors brace portfolios for longer U.S.-China trade war
description: Investors are losing faith that a U.S.-China trade deal could happen soon and are bracing their portfolios for a more prolonged battle that could hamper global growth.

title: Bitcoin tops $8,000 as it hits highest since July 2018
description: Bitcoin surged to more than $8,000 late on Monday, its highest level since July last year, as the cryptocurrency's rally gained further momentum.

title: Exclusive: Truckmaker Scania signs Northvolt battery deal, in talks on equity
description: Volkswagen truck brand Scania has signed a battery supply deal with Sweden's Northvolt and is in talks about making an equity investment as part of the startup's efforts to raise 1.5 billion euros ($1.68 billion), Scania's head said on Monday.

title: Wall Street hit hard by escalation of tariff war
description: Wall Street's main indexes tumbled on Monday after Beijing announced plans to retaliate with higher tariffs on U.S. goods, raising fears that another round of tit-for-tat measures could push the U.S. economy toward recession.

title: U.S. liquefied natural gas shipments to China face mounting tariffs
description: China said on Monday it would raise tariffs on liquefied natural gas (LNG) imports from the United States amid a series of additional levies, a move that could further reduce U.S. LNG shipments to the world's fastest growing importer of the fuel.

title: U.S. exempts water filters, camera parts from China tariffs
description: The Trump administration on Monday announced that it will  exempt a broad range of additional Chinese-made products from 25 percent U.S. tariffs, including industrial equipment, water filtering equipment, small electric motors, remote control devices and stereoscopic microscopes.

title: Uber CEO expects further pressure as shares add to losses, down 12%
description: Uber Technologies Inc's shares fell 12% on Monday, more than doubling their losses since the ride-hailing giant's poorly received market debut, and its chief executive officer said he expected the stock to remain under pressure in the coming months.

title: Wall Street shudders as U.S.-China trade war intensifies
description: Wall Street sank on Monday after China defied Washington by announcing retaliatory tariffs, the latest salvo in the two countries' increasingly belligerent trade war, sending investors fleeing equities for less risky assets.

title: Fed's Kaplan says interest rates are about where they should be
description: Dallas Federal Reserve Bank President Robert Kaplan on Monday said that the Fed should neither be cutting nor raising interest rates but should "move off to the side and be patient."

title: Apple revamps its TV app ahead of streaming service launch
description: Apple Inc on Monday rolled out a new television-watching app for its devices and some Internet-connected TVs, an effort to gain more revenue from reselling other companies' programming and, later this year, its own original shows.

title: Billionaire Schwartz makes $2.6 billion bet on Canada's WestJet Airlines
description: Billionaire Gerry Schwartz pounced on Canada's WestJet Airlines on Monday as his private equity firm Onex Corp offered to buy the struggling airline for C$3.5 billion ($2.6 billion), betting it can turn around its recent decline by taking the company private.

title: China says U.S. policies are causing existential damage to the WTO
description: China said on Monday U.S. policies are threatening the existence of the World Trade Organization, setting out a string of grievances in a WTO "reform proposal" published by the WTO on its website.

title: Facebook raises minimum wage for U.S. contract workers to $20/hour
description: Facebook Inc said on Monday it was raising its minimum wage for all U.S. contract workers, reacting to rising costs of living as it faces intense scrutiny over the treatment of ordinary employees and their pay.

title: Fed's Kaplan says he's vigilant but patient on U.S.-China tensions
description: Dallas Federal Reserve Bank President Robert Kaplan on Monday said he is "extremely vigilant" on the escalating trade tensions between the United States and China, though it could take months before there is more clarity on how the talks are shaping up.

title: U.S. drops plan to require vehicle brake-throttle override system
description: The Trump administration said Monday it will drop rules first proposed in 2012 that would have required automakers to install brake-throttle override systems to prevent runaway vehicles.

title: Trump says no decision yet on levying tariffs on more Chinese goods
description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Monday he was has not made a decision to go ahead with tariffs on another $325 billion in goods from China and said he plans to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the G20 summit next month.

title: Volkswagen to make batteries in Germany, slim down
description: Volkswagen will invest almost 1 billion euros ($1.1 billion) in battery cell production at a facility in western Germany and is seeking to simplify the group by spinning off or selling units, the automaker said on Monday.

title: Exclusive: Amazon rolls out machines that pack orders and replace jobs
description: Amazon.com Inc is rolling out machines to automate a job held by thousands of its workers: boxing up customer orders.

title: Fed can lower rates if U.S.-China trade spat causes slowdown: Rosengren
description: The Federal Reserve has the tools it needs, including lowering interest rates, to respond to any slowdown resulting from the U.S.-China trade spat, a top Fed policymaker told Reuters on Monday, adding that he is not necessarily expecting such a need now.

title: Fed officials see risks in weaker inflation expectations, trade row
description: A drop in the consumer outlook for inflation and intensifying trade tensions drew caution from Federal Reserve officials on Monday as policymakers faced fresh market volatility and a renewed set of risks.

title: Stocks dive, yuan weakens as U.S.-China trade fight intensifies
description: Global stock markets tumbled on Monday and the Chinese yuan weakened to its lowest level since December as the trade war between the United States and China escalated.

title: South Korea's latest big export: Jobless college graduates
description: Cho Min-kyong boasts an engineering degree from one of South Korea's top universities, a school design award and a near-perfect score in her English proficiency test.

title: China's door to talks with U.S. on trade always open: state media
description: China's door to talks with the United States about their trade dispute is always open, but China will not yield on important issues of principle, state media said on Sunday.

title: Germany's Thyssenkrupp to seek new steel partners, CEO tells paper
description: Thyssenkrupp will still seek partners for its steel operations after abandoning a European merger with India's Tata Steel, Chief Executive Guido Kerkhoff said in comments published on Sunday.

title: Bayer hires law firm to investigate Monsanto stakeholder file issue
description: Bayer said on Sunday it was hiring an external law firm to investigate French media complaints that Monsanto, the U.S. seed maker it took over last year, had compiled a file of influential personalities.

title: SoftBank set to invest in British financing group Greensill
description: A prospective deal between SoftBank Group Corp's Vision Fund and UK-based financing group Greensill Capital could be announced as early as Monday, a city source told Reuters.

title: Teva Pharm CFO says company did not conspire to fix prices
description: Teva Pharmaceutical Industries' chief financial officer on Sunday reiterated that the company has done nothing wrong in the wake of a price-fixing lawsuit filed by 44 U.S. states.

description: Emirates Chief Commercial Officer Thierry Antinori has resigned, a spokeswoman said on Sunday, days after the Gulf airline announced its weakest profit in a decade.

title: Insys says it may be forced to file for bankruptcy due to litigation cash crunch

description: Huawei Technologies Co Ltd lawyer James Cole's prior work at the U.S. Department of Justice created conflicts of interest that should disqualify him from defending the Chinese company in a case of alleged bank fraud and sanctions violations, U.S. prosecutors said in a filing on Friday.

description: China's BAIC Group is seeking to buy a stake of up to 5 percent in Daimler as a way to secure its investment in Chinese Mercedes-Benz manufacturing company Beijing Benz Automotive, three sources familiar with the matter told Reuters.

description: Bayer said on Saturday it did not accept "unethical behavior" following a French investigation into a suspected file assembled by the German company's seed making unit Monsanto to influence various personalities in France.

description: Management and labor leaders at Germany's Thyssenkrupp have agreed on a way forward after the industrial conglomerate announced a fresh restructuring drive that could lead to the loss of 6,000 jobs.

title: U.S. states accuse Teva, other drugmakers, of price-fixing: lawsuit
description: U.S. states filed a lawsuit accusing Teva Pharmaceuticals USA Inc of orchestrating a sweeping scheme with 19 other drug companies to inflate drug prices - sometimes by more than 1,000% - and stifle competition for generic drugs, state prosecutors said on Saturday.

title: China still 'cautiously optimistic' on U.S. trade talks despite new tariffs
description: China and the United States have agreed to hold more trade talks in Beijing, Vice Premier Liu He said as U.S. President Donald Trump ordered his trade chief to begin the process of imposing tariffs on all remaining imports from China.

title: U.S. bargaining power won't improve if China trade war intensifies: Global Times editorial
description: China's nationalist Global Times tabloid said in an editorial on Sunday that the United States would not have more bargaining chips at the negotiation table with China once the trade war intensifies.

description: Etihad Airways is interested in re-investing in embattled Indian carrier Jet Airways for a minority stake, subject to certain conditions, a spokesman for the Middle Eastern carrier said on Friday.

description: Alfried Krupp von Bohlen und Halbach Stiftung - Thyssenkrupp's biggest shareholder - said it had supported the company's management in its joint venture plans with India's Tata Steel and the planned split up.

description: Activist investor Cevian Capital on Friday said Thyssenkrupp urgently needed a fundamentally new direction after the company announced abandoning plans to hive off its steel business and split up the rest of the conglomerate.

title: Chinese group sells Hamleys toy stores to India's Reliance Industries
description: Hamleys, the world's oldest toy retailer, is set to pass from Chinese to Indian control after Reliance Industries Ltd said it had agreed to buy the British high street icon in a deal worth $88.5 million.

description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Friday he was in "absolutely no rush" to finalize a trade agreement with China as negotiators from both countries prepared to continue talks in Washington, in a sign that discussions could go past this week.

description: PepsiCo Inc has formally withdrawn lawsuits against Indian farmers that the snack food and drinks maker had accused of infringing its patent by cultivating a potato variety, the company and the growers said on Friday.

title: State Bank of India gets sealed bid for Jet Airways from Etihad
description: A unit of State Bank of India, which is overseeing the bidding process for Jet Airways Ltd, said on Friday it had received a sealed bid from Etihad Airways, and it would submit the bid to lenders of the ailing carrier for examination.

title: Elevator spin-off sends Thyssenkrupp short sellers running for cover
description: Thyssenkrupp shares leapt 20 percent on Friday as investors rushed to cover bearish bets after the conglomerate announced plans to list its best business, a move long hoped-for by investors.

title: Value of Canadian building permits gains 2.1% in March
description: The value of Canadian building permits rose 2.1% in March, driven higher by construction plans in the four Western provinces, after falling a revised 5.1% in February, Statistics Canada data showed on Friday.

title: Amazon holds talks with workers in Poland as strike threatened
description: Amazon said on Friday it was in talks with employees in Poland after unions threatened strike action, seeking higher pay in distribution centres.

title: Foxconn's Gou to keep board seat as he bids for Taiwan's presidency
description: Terry Gou, chairman of Apple supplier Foxconn, will retain a seat on the company's proposed board, a company filing showed on Friday, as he plans to run in Taiwan's 2020 presidential election.

title: Occidental's victory over Chevron for Anadarko
description: Before Occidental Petroleum Corp clinched a deal on Thursday to buy Anadarko Petroleum Corp for $38 billion, it pursued its U.S. oil and gas exploration and production rival for nearly two years, culminating in the sector's most high-profile public contest since the 1980s.

description: A united front among members of the billionaire Sackler family behind painkiller OxyContin is showing signs of strain from litigation over who bears responsibility for the deadly U.S. opioid epidemic.

description: Germany's Thyssenkrupp will embark on a fresh restructuring and list elevators, its most successful business, after regulatory opposition sunk plans to hive off its steel division, unravelling its previous break-up proposal.

title: Etihad submits bid for India's Jet, eyes minority stake
description: Middle Eastern carrier Etihad Airways has submitted a bid for a stake in India's Jet Airways, the unit of State Bank of India (SBI) overseeing the sale of the stricken airline said on Friday.

description: British finance minister Philip Hammond said on Friday he was hopeful the United States and China would step back from a potential trade war that risked causing very serious damage to Britain and the world economy.

description: India's antitrust watchdog has ordered an investigation into Alphabet Inc's unit Google for allegedly abusing the dominant position of its popular Android mobile operating system to block rivals, two sources aware of the matter told Reuters.

title: Tata Steel to explore all options for European unit after ThyssenKrupp JV falls apart
description: India's Tata Steel Ltd said on Friday it will explore all options for its European steel business after its proposed joint venture with German steel giant ThyssenKrupp AG failed to secure regulatory approval.

title: Billionaire Bezos unveils moon lander mockup, embraces Trump's lunar timetable
description: Billionaire entrepreneur Jeff Bezos unveiled on Thursday a mockup of a lunar lander being built by his Blue Origin rocket company and touted his moon goals in a strategy aimed at capitalizing on the Trump administration's renewed push to establish a lunar outpost in just five years.

title: China expresses regret over U.S. tariff hike, vows countermeasures
description: China on Friday said it "deeply regrets" the United States' decision to increase tariffs on $200 billion worth of Chinese goods to 25% from 10%, adding without elaborating that it would take necessary countermeasures.

title: From Paris to Omaha: How Occidental CEO out-maneuvered Chevron in Anadarko bid
description: Occidental Petroleum chief executive Vicki Hollub was caught off guard when U.S. oil giant Chevron swooped in last month with a $33 billion offer to buy Anadarko Petroleum, the oil and gas exploration and production firm she had been wooing for nearly two years.

title: AB InBev files for Hong Kong IPO of Asia business to raise $5 billion
description: The world's biggest brewer, Anheuser-Busch InBev, filed  plans on Friday to spin off its Asian business via a Hong Kong initial public offering, in a deal which two sources with knowledge of the matter said could be worth at least $5 billion.

title: SoftBank Group shares tumble as Uber prices IPO at lower end

description: The London Metal Exchange (LME) has appointed Standard Chartered and ConocoPhillips board member Gay Huey Evans as its new chairwoman, the first in its 142-year history.

title: China urges U.S. to respect market economy after China Mobile denied entry
description: China urged Washington on Friday to stop putting "unreasonable pressure" on Chinese companies after U.S. regulators voted to deny market access to China Mobile Ltd and suggested they could revoke approvals given to two other Chinese carriers.

title: Thyssenkrupp to IPO elevator unit, scraps corporate split
description: Thyssenkrupp on Friday scrapped plans to break into two parts in favor of a listing of its prized elevator unit, responding to a massive decline in its share price since the breakup plans were unveiled in September.

title: Britain concerned by U.S.-China trade tensions: UK PM's spokeswoman
description: Britain is concerned by the escalating tariff tensions between the United States and China and believes no one benefits from a trade war, a spokeswoman for Prime Minister Theresa May said on Friday.

title: First day of U.S.-China trade talks ends; Trump's tariff hike set to take effect
description: Top U.S. and Chinese trade negotiators concluded the first of two days of talks on Thursday to rescue a trade deal that is close to collapsing as Washington prepares to go ahead with plans to hike tariffs on hundreds of billions of dollars of goods imported from China.

title: Tata Steel says EU not likely to ok Thyssenkrupp JV
description: Tata Steel on Friday said that the European Commission does not intend to clear its proposed joint venture with Germany's Thyssenkrupp.

title: Virgin Atlantic in, IAG out of race for Thomas Cook airline business
description: The chief executive of British Airways owner IAG ruled out bidding for Thomas Cook's airline unit on Friday, a day after rival Virgin Atlantic was reported to be interested in part of the business.

title: Cashing out in Uber's IPO: China, Russia and the Middle East
description: In 2015, Uber Technologies Inc went on a fundraising spree in China, tapping venture capitalists and state-backed corporations for cash and connections to try and navigate the Chinese regulatory environment.

title: Uber valued at $82 billion in IPO as market jitters, Lyft woes weigh
description: Uber Technologies Inc priced its initial public offering on Thursday at the low end of its targeted range for a valuation of $82.4 billion, hoping its conservative approach will spare it the trading plunge suffered by rival Lyft Inc.

title: Thyssenkrupp open to partnerships in car parts, plant divisions
description: Thyssenkrupp could seek partnerships for its car parts and plant engineering units if that is the best option to develop them, its chief executive said, adopting a similar approach taken by industrial conglomerate Siemens.

title: Top Chinese trade negotiator leaves U.S. trade representative's office
description: China's top trade negotiator Liu He left the U.S. Trade Representative's office on Friday morning, after talks aimed at resolving a trade dispute between the United States and China.

title: Occidental Petroleum CEO defends premium for Berkshire Hathaway investment
description: Occidental Petroleum Corp Chief Executive Officer Vicki Hollub on Friday defended the company's deal with Berkshire Hathaway Inc's Warren Buffett that paved the way to winning its $38 billion acquisition of Anadarko Petroleum Corp.

title: Uber shares likely to fall in stock market debut
description: Uber Technologies Inc shares are likely to open below their initial public offering price of $45 in their long-awaited market debut on Friday, early price indications showed.

title: Wall St. snaps losing streak after Trump's upbeat trade comments
description: U.S. stocks rebounded from early losses on Friday to snap a four-day losing streak after U.S. President Donald Trump and Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin said trade talks between the United States and China were "constructive."

title: Factbox: Here are nine categories of consumer products impacted by Trump's new tariffs

title: U.S. plans more aid for farmers amid China trade spat
description: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Sonny Perdue said on Friday that President Donald Trump had asked him to create a plan to help American farmers cope with the heavy impact of the U.S.-China trade war on agriculture.

description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc is nearing a deal to buy boutique wealth management firm United Capital Financial Partners Inc for several hundred million dollars, a source told Reuters.

description: Uber Technologies Inc's conservative initial public offering could not keep its shares from sinking in their trading debut on Friday, fueling debate on Wall Street over whether the outcome of the most anticipated listing since Facebook Inc would weigh on other Silicon Valley unicorns.

title: French prosecutor opens investigation over suspected Monsanto file
description: The French prosecutor on Friday said it had opened a preliminary investigation into a suspected file assembled by Bayer's seed maker Monsanto to influence various personalities in France.

description: The United States and China made no progress in trade talks this week in Washington as U.S. negotiators rejected Chinese Vice Premier Liu He's arguments in favor of China's proposed legal changes to a draft agreement, two sources familiar with the talks told Reuters.

title: Trade-sensitive stocks on ropes as uncertainty weighs
description: A week of worsening fears on Wall Street leading up to Washington's increase on tariffs on Chinese goods has taken a toll on stocks that rely heavily on global trade.

title: 'We are the rightful owners' of Anadarko, Occidental CEO tells shareholders
description: Occidental Petroleum Chief Executive Vicki Hollub on Friday touted her $38 billion deal for Anadarko Petroleum Corp and defended the pricey terms she negotiated in a 90-minute session with billionaire investor Warren Buffett to secure the deal without seeking shareholder approval.

title: Instant view: U.S.-China trade talks end with deal uncertain
description: U.S. President Donald Trump on Friday said he was in no hurry to sign a trade deal with China as Washington imposed a new set of tariffs on Chinese goods and negotiators ended two days of talks to try to salvage an agreement.

title: China, U.S. agree to hold more trade talks: Vice Premier Liu He
