title: Holiday sales boost Target forecasts, shares jump
description: Target Corp forecast 2019 profit above Wall Street estimates on Tuesday as investments to draw more shoppers online and in stores drove a jump in holiday sales, sending its shares up 5 percent.

title: Harley-Davidson scoots into kids electric bikes with StaCyc deal
description: Harley-Davidson Inc moved into kids electric bikes on Tuesday with the purchase of California-based StaCyc Inc, tapping a new business outside its declining core market in classic motorcycles.

title: Exclusive: Romania's opposition seeks Huawei ban in telecom infrastructure
description: Romania's biggest opposition party will trigger a public inquiry into Huawei's contribution to critical infrastructure and seek to bar it from 5G network development due to mounting security concerns, its IT expert said on Tuesday.

title: Mexican farmers urge 'mirror' tariffs on Trump's rural base
description: Leaders of Mexico's agricultural sector are urging "mirror measures" on U.S. farm imports in politically sensitive products such as yellow corn and poultry, in an effort they argue would counter decades of subsidized imports from the United States.

title: China to slash taxes, boost lending to prop up slowing economy
description: China sought to shore up its slowing economy through billions of dollars in planned tax cuts and infrastructure spending, with economic growth at its weakest in almost 30 years due to softer domestic demand and a trade war with the United States.

title: China to take steps to boost domestic consumption this year: state planner
description: China's state planner said on Wednesday that the government will implement measures to further boost domestic consumption this year.

title: Suits and ties now optional, Goldman Sachs hedges dress code
description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc said on Tuesday that it is relaxing the dress code for all its employees, a move once considered unimaginable for the Wall Street firm's leagues of monk-shoed partners and bankers in bespoke suits.

title: GE's CEO warns of negative industrial cash flow in 2019, shares drop
description: General Electric Co's chief executive surprised investors on Tuesday by forecasting a net cash outflow from its industrial businesses this year mainly due to its ailing power-plant unit, a gloomy outlook that sent shares and bonds tumbling.

title: Southwest says mechanics' disruption costing millions weekly
description: A dispute with its mechanics union is costing Southwest Airlines Co millions of dollars in lost revenues a week as well as millions of dollars in costs related to flight cancellations and delays, chief executive Gary Kelly said on Tuesday.

title: Oil prices flat; focus on OPEC-led output cuts, Libya oilfield
description: Oil prices hovered near flat on Tuesday as the market balanced OPEC-led efforts to tighten crude supply with the restart of Libya's biggest oilfield and the prospect of weaker demand.

title: Papa John's founder Schnatter to exit board in settlement
description: Papa John's founder John Schnatter is leaving its board of directors as part of a settlement resolving a bitter dispute for control of the world's third-largest pizza chain.

title: JetBlue still weighing transatlantic business case: executive
description: JetBlue Airways Corp is still considering a business case for a potential launch of transatlantic flights from New York and Boston, Chief Commercial Officer Marty St. George said on Tuesday, a decision that is expected this year and possibly as soon as next month.

title: Top Tesla shareholder says Musk 'doesn't need to be CEO': Barron's
description: Tesla Inc's largest shareholder expressed its support for Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk, but acknowledged that it was open to a different role for the electric carmaker's founder and CEO, Barron's reported on Tuesday.

title: Stocks slip, dollar gains as China cuts growth target
description: A gauge of world stock markets recovered from early declines but was slightly lower on Tuesday as China cut its growth targets to a 30-year low but added more stimulus, while strong U.S. economic data sent the dollar to a two-week high.

title: Airbus books order for 21 helicopters from Air Medical Group
description: European aircraft maker Airbus Tuesday said it booked an order for 21 helicopters from U.S.-based Air Medical Group Holdings.

title: Kohl's profit view beats forecast as tie-ups, new items lure shoppers
description: Kohl's Corp forecast full-year profit above Wall Street estimates on Tuesday, as partnerships with Amazon  and a range of new brands attract more shoppers.

title: Wall Street slips as GE swoons, key market level looms
description: Wall Street's main indexes dipped in a choppy session on Tuesday as a drop in General Electric shares countered positive retailer earnings and investors eyed a key resistance level for the benchmark S&P 500 after the market's strong run.

title: Delta dangles future order for 200 jets, considering Alitalia investment
description: Delta Air Lines fueled the appetite of planemakers on Tuesday after Chief Executive Ed Bastian said the airline planned to replace some 200 Boeing 757 and 767 aircraft over the next decade.

title: Tesla blames misprinted label for China customs hiccup
description: Tesla Inc said on Tuesday that China's customs authorities have accepted the electric carmaker's plan to resolve problems with the clearance of its Model 3 sedans that centered around misprinting of labels.

title: BMW wants clear guidance from Mexico government for investment plans
description: German carmaker BMW, which is building its first plant in Mexico, is looking for clear signs from the new government of President Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador that would guarantee stability to invest in the country, a top executive said.

title: U.S. new home sales at seven-month high; services sector picks up
description: Sales of new U.S. single-family homes rose to a seven-month high in December, but November's outsized jump was revised lower, pointing to continued weakness in the housing market.

title: Retail stocks set to bypass tariff woes but face aftershock risk
description: Shares of U.S. retail and consumer goods companies appear set to emerge largely unscathed from the trade dispute between the United States and China.

title: Chevron, Exxon take turns wooing investors with shale boasts
description: The two biggest U.S. oil companies tried to outdo each other on Tuesday, boasting about their prowess in shale to lure investors to their side.

title: Investor pushes L Brands to spin off Victoria's Secret
description: Activist investor Barington Capital on Tuesday urged L Brands to separate its Victoria's Secret and Bath & Body Works businesses, in an effort to turn around the struggling consumer brands owner.

title: Trump moves to scrap trade privilege for India, Delhi plays down impact
description: U.S. President Donald Trump looked set to open a new front in his trade wars with a plan to end preferential trade treatment for India that allows duty-free entry for up to $5.6 billion worth of its exports to the United States.

title: Jeans maker Diesel USA files for bankruptcy
description: Diesel USA Inc, the denim and accessory brand known for its jeans, filed for bankruptcy on Tuesday, blaming mounting losses, a sales plunge, expensive leases and cyber fraud.

title: Huawei calls for common cybersecurity standards amidst concerns
description: Huawei, in the spotlight over the security risks of its telecom equipment gear, urged governments, the telecoms industry and regulators on Tuesday to work together to create a common set of cybersecurity standards.

title: JPMorgan backs away from private prison finance
description: JPMorgan Chase & Co has decided to stop financing private operators of prisons and detention centers, which have become targets of protests over Trump administration immigration policies.

title: T-Mobile spent $195,000 at Trump Hotel in D.C. since merger announcement
description: T-Mobile Us Inc's chief executive, John Legere, and other company leaders have spent $195,000 on hotel stays and other expenses at the Trump International Hotel in Washington since the company sought approval for a $26 billion merger with Sprint last April, documents released on Tuesday show.

title: AT&T restructures WarnerMedia to gird for Netflix fight: memo
description: AT&T Inc is restructuring its WarnerMedia business, according to a memo sent to employees on Monday and seen by Reuters, as it girds for a streaming video battle with Netflix Inc and Walt Disney Co.

title: Huawei CFO suing Canada over December arrest
description: The lawyers for Huawei Chief Financial Officer Meng Wanzhou are suing the Canadian government, its border agency and federal police, alleging their client was detained, searched and interrogated for three hours in violation of her constitutional rights.

title: Southwest to begin Hawaii service from California on March 17
description: Southwest Airlines said on Monday it will begin flying to the Hawaiian capital of Honolulu from Oakland, California on March 17 with special launch fares as low as $49 through mid-June.

title: Vale shares fall after CEO is 'temporarily' ousted after dam disaster
description: Shares in Brazil's Vale SA, the world's largest iron-ore miner, fell on Monday after its CEO Fabio Schvartsman and three other executives resigned over the weekend following a dam collapse in January that left over 300 dead.

title: Rolls-Royce scales back on joining fighter jet project with Turkey's Kale Group
description: British engine maker Rolls-Royce Holdings Plc confirmed it had scaled back efforts to join a Turkish program to build a new fighter jet with Turkey's Kale Group.

title: Huawei said to be preparing to sue U.S. government: source
description: Chinese telecoms equipment company Huawei plans to announce a lawsuit against the United States government on Thursday on grounds related to a defense bill, a source with knowledge of the matter told Reuters.

title: Explainer: What is the fuss about European Central Bank TLTRO loans?
description: The European Central Bank is expected to give banks fresh long-term loans known as TLTROs to keep credit flowing to companies in the euro zone, in the hope that an already marked economic downturn will not be exacerbated by a sudden crunch in lending.

title: Google rejects Australian regulator's call for scrutiny, denies market power
description: Alphabet Inc's Google has rejected calls by Australia's competition regulator for tougher scrutiny of its operations, denying that it enjoys market power in online searches and advertising, documents published on Monday showed.

title: Honeywell sees slowing demand for civilian helicopters over next five years
description: Honeywell International Inc expects to deliver 4,000 helicopters for civilian use through 2023, down from 4,200 it forecast last year, on the back of a slowing global economy, the U.S. industrial conglomerate said on Monday.

title: Qualcomm launches patent challenge to Apple ahead of antitrust case
description: Qualcomm Inc on Monday kicks off a patent challenge to Apple Inc, capping off a two-year legal strategy to put pressure on the iPhone maker before a major antitrust lawsuit between the two goes to trial in April.

title: Easier for China to face tariffs than bend to U.S. pressure
description: China will acknowledge concessions made in any trade deal with the United States for the sake of stabilizing shaky relations, but is unlikely to yield to demands it alter its economic model even if faced with continued tariffs, many trade experts believe.

title: Volvo to limit car speeds in bid for zero deaths
description: Volvo Cars said on Monday it will introduce a 180 km per hour (112 mph) speed limiter on all new vehicles as the Swedish automaker seeks to burnish its safety credentials and meet a pledge to eliminate passenger fatalities by 2020.

title: Ghosn lawyer says he's optimistic former Nissan head could soon win bail
description: The lawyer for former Nissan Motor Co Ltd Chairman Carlos Ghosn on Monday said he was optimistic the ousted executive could win bail in the near future, after being held in custody at a detention center in Japan for over three months.

title: U.S. and China said to appear close to deal to roll back tariffs
description: The United States and China appear close to a deal that would roll back U.S. tariffs on at least $200 billion worth of Chinese goods, as Beijing makes pledges on structural economic changes and eliminates retaliatory tariffs on U.S. goods, a source briefed on negotiations said on Sunday.

title: Barclays bosses fretted over Qatar deal in 2008 fundraising
description: Top Barclays executives worried that investors in the bank's 2008 emergency fundraising would go "nuts" if Qatar was given a better deal unfairly, a London court heard on Monday.

title: Office Depot and Alibaba team up to tap small and medium businesses
description: Office Depot on Monday teamed up with Alibaba Group Holdings Ltd to launch a co-branded e-commerce website, seeking to tap into the opportunities of selling to small and medium businesses in the United States.

title: EU set for trade talks with U.S. on March 6 amid concern over tariffs
description: The European Union's top trade officials will update their U.S. counterparts this week on progress in obtaining a negotiating mandate for a EU-U.S. trade deal on industrial goods and raise concern over existing and potential future U.S. tariffs.

title: Ghosn's family taps U.N. rights working group to show violations in detention
description: Carlos Ghosn's lawyers have submitted a dossier to a United Nations' working group which showed that the former head of Renault's rights had been violated during detention in Japan, one if his lawyers said on Monday.

title: Musk says $35,000 Model 3 to reach volume production mid-year
description: Tesla Inc Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk said on Monday production of the $35,000 version of the electric carmaker's Model 3 will start this month, but would not reach "volume production" until mid-year.

title: Ghosn lawyer optimistic on bail prospects, pledges new defense strategy
description: The lawyer of ousted Nissan Chairman Carlos Ghosn on Monday said he was optimistic the detained executive could win bail with a promise to submit to surveillance, and that he would pursue a fresh strategy to defend against financial misconduct charges.

title: Google plans to ban political ads before Canada election
description: Alphabet Inc's Google will ban political advertising on its platform before the Canadian federal election, after the country introduced stringent transparency rules.

title: Volkswagen signs e-vehicle startup as first partner for production platform
description: Volkswagen has signed German start-up e.GO Mobile as the first external partner for its modular platform for electric vehicles (EV), as it seeks to simplify production across a variety of models.

title: Exclusive: OxyContin maker Purdue Pharma exploring bankruptcy - sources
description: OxyContin maker Purdue Pharma LP is exploring filing for bankruptcy to address potentially significant liabilities from roughly 2,000 lawsuits alleging the drugmaker contributed to the deadly opioid crisis sweeping the United States, people familiar with the matter said on Monday.

title: Lockheed gets $1 billion down payment for Saudi THAAD missile system
description: Lockheed Martin Corp will receive the first payment toward the installation a $15 billion missile defense system in Saudi Arabia as part of a $110 billion arms package the Trump administration said it negotiated with the Kingdom in 2017, the Pentagon said on Monday.

title: Wall Street drops after weak data, healthcare slump
description: Wall Street's major indexes fell on Monday, weighed down by a weak U.S. construction spending report and declines in healthcare shares, as an initial rally on optimism over a U.S.-China trade deal faded.

title: Barrick says open to Nevada joint venture talks with Newmont
description: Barrick Gold Corp Chief Executive Mark Bristow said on Monday he wants to speak immediately with Newmont Mining Corp about a proposed Nevada joint venture, even as his company moves to take a $18 billion takeover offer directly to Newmont shareholders.

title: Will $14.5 billion plug GE's long-term care insurance hole? Some experts say 'No'
description: General Electric Co is setting aside one of the largest amounts ever to cover potential losses on policies that provide long-term care in nursing facilities and patients' homes. But insurance experts are concerned that may not be enough.

title: U.S. shares falter, investors await U.S.-China trade deal
description: U.S. stock indexes closed lower while the dollar edged higher on Monday, as investors appeared to need some convincing the United States and China would reach a trade agreement and weaker-than-expected construction data did not help their mood.

title: Dollar nudges up on hopes for U.S.-China trade deal
description: The dollar rose against a basket of major currencies on Monday on traders' bets that China and the United States are moving closer to a trade deal that would end sparring between the world's two biggest economies.

title: Tesla to unveil Model Y on March 14, says Musk
description: Tesla Inc will unveil its Model Y on March 14 at an event in LA Design Studio, Chief Executive Elon Musk said on Sunday.

title: GM set to end production at Ohio plant Wednesday
description: General Motors Co said on Monday it expects to end production of the Chevrolet Cruze at its Lordstown, Ohio assembly plant on Wednesday, the first of five plants it is idling this year in North America.

title: U.S. seeks to cut dialysis costs with more home care versus clinics
description: The Trump administration is working on a new payment approach for treating kidney disease that favors lower cost care at home and transplants, a change that would upend a dialysis industry that provides care in thousands of clinics nationwide.

title: U.S. construction spending falls, fourth quarter GDP seen revised lower
description: U.S. construction spending unexpectedly fell in December as investment in both private and public projects dropped, leading economists to expect that the government will trim its economic growth estimate for the fourth quarter.

title: Wall Street weekahead: U.S. stock reign may not last over other regions
description: U.S. stock prices are outpacing those in most other regions to start 2019, but the gap is narrow and some investors are eyeing potential catalysts to tip the scales to the rest of the world.

title: Israeli stocks rise despite attorney-general plan to indict Netanyahu
description: Israeli shares opened higher on Sunday morning, shrugging off news that the country's attorney-general intends to indict Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on corruption charges.

title: White House to host CEOs for workforce advisory meeting
description: The White House on Wednesday is hosting major chief executives who joined a Trump administration advisory board on workforce issues.

title: Vale's CEO, other executives, to step down after Brazil dam burst
description: Brazilian iron ore miner Vale SA Chief Executive Fabio Schvartsman and several other senior executives resigned on Saturday in what the company described as a temporary move, after one of its mining dams burst in January, killing hundreds.

title: German carmakers to invest 60 billion euros in electric cars and automation: VDA
description: Germany's car industry is to invest nearly 60 billion euros ($68 billion) over the next three years on electric cars and automated driving, the head of the VDA car industry association said ahead of the Geneva motor show.

title: French tax on internet giants could yield 500 million euros per year: Le Maire
description: A three percent tax on the French revenue of large internet companies could yield 500 million euros (568.5 million pounds) per year, French Finance Minister Bruno Le Maire said on Sunday.

title: Brexit casts shadow over stands at Geneva car show
description: The usual mix of sports cars, offroaders and family saloons will be on display at the Geneva motor show this week, but with one big difference from previous years - they may be about to become harder and costlier to make, and more expensive to buy.

title: China says U.S. trade talks progress 'well received'
description: The "substantive progress" China and the United States have made in their trade talks has been "well-received" in both countries and around the world, a senior Chinese official said on Monday, maintaining Beijing's previous upbeat assessment of discussions.

title: U.S. agency probing two fatal Tesla crashes in Florida since last Sunday
description: U.S. authorities are investigating a fatal Tesla Inc Model S crash in Florida last Sunday that killed the driver and caused a massive fire, the second fatal Tesla crash in the state this week being probed, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) said on Saturday.

title: Porsche says it is dealing with tax investigation issues
description: Volkswagen's Porsche unit on Sunday said it was cooperating with state prosecutors to clear up investigations into alleged tax debts related to early retirees and taxable benefits enjoyed by former top executives.

title: AT&T plans to revamp CNN’s digital arm: WSJ
description: John Stankey, the AT&T executive at the helm of WarnerMedia, is planning to revamp cable news network CNN's digital operation, believing it isn’t reaching its potential and requires more investment, the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday.

title: Head of French carmaker PSA says Europe's CO2 cuts will threaten jobs: Le Figaro
description: The EU's plans to slash carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions from vehicles and push carmakers to go electric will threaten 13 million jobs in Europe's auto industry and benefit Asia, the head of French carmaker PSA told Le Figaro.

title: Investors spooked by Brazilian Vale's surprise CEO shake-up
description: Investors were skeptical on Sunday about the surprise decision by Brazil's Vale SA to remove its high-profile chief executive in the wake of a deadly January accident at one of the world's largest iron ore miner's facilities.

title: KKR poaches Goldman Asia investment banking chair Richdale
description: KKR & Co Inc has poached Kate Richdale, Goldman Sachs Group Inc chair of Asia investment banking ex-Japan.

title: Exclusive: Huawei plans billions in dividends for staff despite row with U.S. - sources
description: China's Huawei is set to reward employee shareholders with a 3 percent rise in cash dividends that are worth billions of dollars, according to company sources and Reuters calculations - a move expected to boost morale as it battles a U.S.-led drive against its telecom gear.

title: China says it welcomes delay on U.S. tariff increase
description: China said on Saturday that it welcomed the release of language from the United State Trade Representative's office (USTR) delaying a scheduled hike in U.S. tariffs on $200 billion worth of Chinese goods.

title: U.S. says rejects WTO's 'straitjacket' of trade obligations
description: The Trump administration filed another salvo at the World Trade Organization on Friday, saying U.S. trade policy was not going to be dictated by the international body and defending its use of tariffs to pressure China and other trade partners.

title: Tesla's store-shuttering strategy may pull the rug out of solar
description: Tesla Inc's sudden decision to shutter the bulk of its stores around the world raises a red flag over the future of its solar branch, a declining business it paid $2.6 billion for in a controversial 2016 deal.

title: Trump asks China to lift tariffs on U.S. farm products
description: U.S. President Donald Trump said he had asked China to immediately remove all tariffs on U.S. agricultural products because trade talks were progressing well.

title: Apple holders vote down proposal to disclose ideology of director nominees
description: Apple Inc shareholders on Friday defeated a shareholder proposal from a conservative group that would have required the company to disclose the "ideological perspective" of nominees for its board of directors.

title: Volkswagen's flagship VW brand missed margin goal in 2018: Spiegel
description: Volkswagen's flagship VW brand missed its margin target in 2018 as operating profits declined despite growth in top-line revenues at the German carmaker, news weekly Spiegel reported on Friday, citing unpublished figures.

title: Exclusive: Apollo bets on Clearway Energy, defying PG&E bankruptcy fallout
description: Private equity firm Apollo Global Management LLC has amassed a 6 percent stake in Clearway Energy Inc, a renewable energy producer whose shares were hit after one of its customers filed for bankruptcy, people familiar with the matter said on Friday.

title: Norway's Aker BP switching gears from M&A to exploration
description: Norwegian oil and gas company Aker BP is switching emphasis from M&A toward exploration, taking a potentially riskier path to increase its resources after years when it has relied on acquisitions to add the bulk of its new barrels.

title: Canada PM speaks to Trump about tariffs, sources see little progress
description: Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau spoke to U.S. President Donald Trump on Thursday about American tariffs on steel and aluminum, Trudeau's office said on Friday, but well-placed sources said there was little sign of progress.

title: Another Kroger unit to stop accepting Visa credit cards due to high fees
description: U.S. supermarket chain Kroger Co on Friday said its Smith's Food and Drug Stores division will stop accepting Visa Inc's credit cards, starting April 3, because of excessive transaction fees.

title: A day of reckoning for the ECB?
description: The European Central Bank has downplayed a global slowdown for months, but it will finally take a tentative step next week to prop up the euro zone economy, signaling fresh stimulus to keep banks lending.

title: Tesla debuts $35,000 Model 3, sees loss in first quarter
description: Tesla Inc said on Thursday it would not be profitable in the first quarter, as it offered for the first time a $35,000 version of its Model 3 sedan and said its global sales would now be online-only, steps designed to increase demand and cut overhead costs for the electric vehicle maker.

title: EBay announces review of StubHub, Classifieds in deal with activists
description: EBay Inc on Friday announced a review of its StubHub and eBay Classifieds businesses and said it would appoint two new directors to its board, as part of an agreement with activist investors to avert a proxy contest.

title: EU states block putting Saudi Arabia, U.S. territories on dirty-money list
description: European Union member states unanimously rejected on Friday a proposal to blacklist Saudi Arabia and four U.S. territories for lax controls on terrorism financing and money laundering, sources told Reuters.

title: Customer deposits need protection in no-deal Brexit: EU watchdog
description: The EU bank watchdog has urged member states to protect customer deposits in branches of British banks in the European Union if Britain leaves the bloc this month with no deal.

title: Glencore highlights trade as 'foremost risk', others growing
description: Glencore said trade barriers are its "foremost risk", but climate, political, legal and other potential dangers have become more pressing for the mining and trading group.

title: India's growth may decelerate further despite election spending
description: Billions of dollars of pre-election spending by the Indian government and political parties in the next two months is  unlikely to stop the nation's economy from slowing further,  economists said.

title: Caesars bows to Icahn demands on board, sale still eyed
description: U.S. casino operator Caesars Entertainment Corp has struck a deal with investor Carl Icahn that appoints three new directors to its board, although the billionaire hedge fund manager continues to press for a sale of the company.

title: Euro zone's triple-A bond drought persists after ECB steps away
description: High-grade euro zone debt remains scarce even though the European Central Bank has stopped its huge purchases of new bonds, intensifying concerns that banks will face future collateral shortages and highlighting the need for safe assets.

title: Southwest takes mechanics union to court over flight disruption
description: Southwest Airlines filed a lawsuit against its mechanics union on Thursday, accusing the workers of an illegal campaign to disrupt operations in order to improve their position in prolonged labor talks.

title: Japan's Subaru plans biggest-ever global recall over brake lights
description: Subaru Corp plans to recall around 2.3 million vehicles globally over a brake light problem, in what would be the automaker's biggest-ever recall as it grapples with a series of quality-related issues following rapid expansion.

title: Saipem and former managers face trial in profit warning case
description: An Italian judge has ordered oil contractor Saipem and former executives to stand trial on charges of market manipulation and false accounting, the company said on Friday, confirming an earlier report.

title: German juggernaut may face economic jam as tariffs and Brexit loom
description: Germany faces the risk of steep U.S. tariffs on cars and a no-deal Brexit, a double whammy which could bring a golden decade of growth in Europe's powerhouse economy to an end.

title: Big U.S. pension funds ask electric utilities for decarbonization plans
description: Top U.S. pension funds are asking electric utilities to accelerate efforts to cut carbon emissions but will not force the issue with proxy resolutions this spring, hoping market shifts and falling prices for renewable energy have already made executives and directors receptive to the goal.

title: JPMorgan keeps Venezuela in emerging bond indexes: fund managers
description: JPMorgan has retained dollar-denominated debt issued by Venezuela and its state-run oil company PDVSA in a key emerging market bond index as part of its monthly rebalancing, according to two fund managers.

title: Pompeo says world should have eyes wide open about Chinese tech risks
description: U.S Secretary of State Mike Pompeo said on Friday that the world should be "eyes wide open" about the risks of using Chinese technology, and that there could be problems for American firms operating in certain places where Huawei equipment was deployed.

title: China's fledgling junk bond market spawns new breed of vulture funds
description: When the Shanghai-traded bonds of conglomerate China Minsheng Investment Group plunged 40 percent over two days in January after news it had missed a repayment, Beijing-based hedge fund manager Jash Zhang smelled blood.

title: William Hill 2019 outlook in line as U.S. expansion ramps up
description: British bookmaker William Hill Plc said on Friday that 2019 results would be in line with market expectations while reporting a slight dip in full-year adjusted operating profit, as it booked more costs to expand in the U.S.

title: Gap to separate Old Navy brand, close stores; shares soar 25 percent
description: Gap Inc will separate its better-performing Old Navy brand and shutter about 230 stores of its struggling namesake apparel business, in one of its biggest restructuring efforts to energize sales, sending shares surging 25 percent on Thursday.

title: Private equity investors fret about managers overpaying for deals
description: Some of the world's biggest private equity investors raised concerns this week that the $3.4 trillion leveraged buyout industry is overheating, as more fund managers pay top dollar for acquisitions that could prove costly down the line.

title: Gap shares surge 24 percent as Wall Street praises split
description: Gap Inc shares surged as much as 24 percent on Friday as a number of Wall Street analysts lauded the company's decision to separate its better-performing Old Navy brand.

title: U.S. auto sales fall in February on weak SUV demand
description: Automakers on Friday reported a decline in U.S. light vehicle sales for February as demand for SUVs slows after years of rapid growth, pointing to a drop in overall sales in 2019.

title: BNP Paribas to cut up to 2,500 jobs at its Belgian bank
description: BNP Paribas reached an agreement with unions over a plan to cut as many as 2,500 jobs at its Belgian retail banking unit by 2021 as part of an effort to bring down costs.

title: Southwest Airlines readies Hawaii flights in West Coast push
description: Southwest Airlines Co will soon begin flying to Hawaii from California, as part of the budget-friendly carrier's push to boost leisure travel from the West Coast, an executive said on Friday.

title: Jaguar Land Rover to announce major UK investment: BBC
description: Luxury carmaker Jaguar Land Rover, part of Tata Motors Ltd, is preparing to announce hundreds of millions of pounds worth of investment in Britain, the BBC reported on Friday.

title: U.S. companies adapt to 'endless' China tariffs
description: U.S. manufacturers are accelerating their shift out of China, coming to terms with a new reality: the Trump administration's tariffs will not go away any time soon.

title: U.S. Trade Representative issues notice on delay of China tariff increase
description: The United States Trade Representative's office (USTR) has released language to delay a scheduled hike in tariffs on $200 billion worth of Chinese goods, due to be published in the Federal Register next week.

title: U.S. safety agencies to investigate fatal Tesla crash in Florida
description: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) said they are sending teams to investigate a fatal crash in Florida on Friday involving a Tesla Inc car and a semi-trailer.

title: Huawei to be arraigned in U.S. fraud case in New York on March 14
description: Huawei Technologies Co Ltd and two affiliates will be arraigned on March 14 in U.S. District Court in Brooklyn, New York, on accusations the company committed bank and wire fraud and violated sanctions against Iran, according to a court filing on Friday.

title: Canada to allow extradition case against Huawei executive
description: The Canadian government, as expected, said on Friday it would allow an extradition hearing to proceed against Meng Wanzhou, the chief financial officer of Huawei Technologies Co Ltd who was detained in Canada late last year.

title: Tesla enters uncharted territory after move to dismantle store network
description: Tesla Inc's move to dismantle its network of high-end showrooms as part of a plan to launch the long-awaited cheaper version of its Model 3 sedan has pushed the electric carmaker into uncharted territory for an industry that has long relied on physical stores to move the metal.

title: Tesla settles in cash $920 million convertible bond obligation
description: Tesla Inc has paid off a $920 million convertible bond obligation in cash, a company spokesperson said on Friday.

title: Mexico eyes fresh U.S. targets for tariffs to pressure Trump over steel
description: Mexico's government on Friday threatened to slap duties on new U.S. products in retaliation for the Trump administration's steel and aluminum tariffs as it seeks to turn up pressure on Washington to exempt it from the measures.

title: Wall St. Week Ahead: U.S. stock reign may not last over other regions
description: U.S. stock prices are outpacing those in most other regions to start 2019, but the gap is narrow and some investors are eyeing potential catalysts to tip the scales to the rest of the world.

title: Canada approves Huawei extradition proceedings, China seethes
description: The Canadian government, as expected, on Friday approved extradition proceedings against the chief financial officer of Huawei Technologies Co Ltd, prompting a furious reaction from China.

title: Take Five: U-turn if you want to! World markets themes for the week ahead
description: Following are five big themes likely to dominate thinking of investors and traders in the coming week, and the Reuters stories related to them.

title: Blackstone CEO Schwarzman pockets at least $568 million in 2018: filing
description: Blackstone Group LP Chief Executive Stephen Schwarzman pocketed at least $567.8 million in 2018 dividends and compensation, making him yet again the private equity industry's highest earner, a regulatory filing showed on Friday.

title: Intellia CEO not involved in Starboard's Bristol-Myers board challenge
description: Intellia Therapeutics Inc Chief Executive John Leonard, who U.S. drug maker Bristol-Myers Squibb Co said last week was nominated by hedge fund Starboard Value LP to sit on its board, is not affiliated with the effort, an Intellia spokeswoman said on Thursday.

title: Cultural clash overshadowing Barrick's Newmont bid
description: Conflicting cultures and management styles are overshadowing Barrick Gold Corp's $18 billion bid for rival Newmont Mining Corp, becoming factors just as important to the deal's success as whether or not the pair's lucrative assets in Nevada and elsewhere fit well together.

title: U.S. consumer spending, factory data point to weak first quarter GDP growth
description: U.S. personal income fell for the first time in more than three years in January and consumer spending dropped by the most since 2009 in December, putting the economy on a weak growth path early in the first quarter.

title: U.S. trade chief courts auto union to back North American trade pact
description: U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer and his staff will head to Michigan next week to meet with United Auto Workers union leaders in an effort to win labor backing for a new North American free trade deal, the union said on Friday.

title: Global shares rise on trade optimism, tame inflation
description: World equity markets rose on Friday as optimism around trade and benign U.S. inflation boosted investor sentiment, while crude oil retreated on news of weaker U.S. factory activity.

title: U.S. holds major oil and gas lease sale in sage grouse habitat
description: The U.S. government kicked off a major sale of oil and gas leases in Wyoming this week after rejecting protests over lands on offer that are considered critical areas for wildlife.

title: U.S. fines American Airlines, Delta for long tarmac delays
description: American Airlines was fined $1 million and Delta Air Lines Inc $750,000 for violating federal rules barring lengthy tarmac delays at U.S. airports, the U.S. Transportation Department said on Thursday.

title: Wells Fargo officials enter $240 million settlement over bogus accounts
description: Wells Fargo & Co executives and directors have reached a $240 million settlement with U.S. shareholders over the creation by bank employees of millions of unauthorized customer accounts.

title: Lyft's IPO filing shows surging revenue, widening losses
description: Lyft Inc inched closer to becoming the first ride-hailing company to make a stock market debut by releasing its filing for an initial public offering on Friday, revealing to the public a detailed look at its financial performance.

title: Wall Street rises as trade optimism counters weak data
description: The S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average snapped a three-day run of losses on Friday as optimism about the prospects for a U.S.-China trade agreement countered downbeat U.S. and China manufacturing data.

title: Amazon plans new grocery-store business: WSJ
description: Amazon.com Inc plans to open dozens of grocery stores across the United States as it looks to expand in the food business, the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.

title: PG&E delayed key power line safety overhaul, filings show; shares slip
description: Shares of PG&E Corp fell 3 percent on Wednesday after federal filings showed that the power utility had delayed a safety overhaul of a high-voltage transmission line, a prime suspect behind the deadliest wildfire in California history.

title: Future Retail secures deal to open 7-Eleven stores in India
description: U.S.-based 7-Eleven Inc expects to open its first branded store in India this year, after reaching a deal with Future Retail Ltd to run the chain in the Asian nation.

title: Air Canada raises long-term profit margin goals
description: Air Canada increased its long-term targets for profit margins and free cash flow on Thursday, as the country's largest airline benefits from cost-cutting efforts and an expansion into new destinations.

title: BMW, Daimler pool resources on automated driving technology
description: Daimler and BMW deepened their alliance on Thursday to share spiraling development costs for highly automated driving technologies, even as each carmaker pursues separate efforts to develop fully self-driving cars.

title: First Facebook investigation to be completed by summer: regulator
description: Facebook's lead regulator in the European Union expects to conclude the first of seven investigations into the company's use of personal data this summer and the remainder by the end of the year, Ireland's Data Protection Commissioner said on Thursday.

title: SAP says CEO McDermott bags 9.8 million euros in 2018
description: SAP Chief Executive Bill McDermott received total benefits of 9.8 million euros ($11.2 million) in 2018, according to the software maker's compensation report released on Thursday.

title: Sunrise investor Freenet to skip rights issue to fund Liberty Global deal
description: Sunrise Communication's quarter-owner Freenet said on Thursday it will not take part in a $4.1 billion rights issue to fund the Swiss telecommunications group's takeover of Liberty Global's UPC Switzerland business.

title: U.S. jobless claims rise; continuing claims at 10-month high
description: The number of Americans filing applications for jobless benefits increased more than expected last week and the number of people on unemployment rolls increased to a 10-month high, suggesting some slowing in the labor market.

title: China February factory activity shrinks to three-year low, export orders worst in a decade
description: Factory activity in China contracted to a three-year low in February as export orders fell at the fastest pace since the global financial crisis, highlighting deepening cracks in an economy facing weak demand at home and abroad.

title: JD.com shares jump on upbeat sales performance
description: JD.com Inc, China's second largest e-commerce firm, reported a 22.4 percent jump in quarterly sales on Thursday, beating estimates on the back of robust retail sales and sending its U.S.-listed shares up 13.8 percent in pre-market trade.

title: PG&E says equipment probably caused deadly Camp Fire
description: PG&E Corp, which filed for bankruptcy last month because of potential liabilities from wildfires in California, said it is probable that its equipment will be determined to be an "ignition point" of the 2018 Camp Fire.

title: Starboard to vote against Bristol-Myers-Celgene $74 billion deal
description: Activist investor Starboard Value LP will vote against Bristol-Myers Squibb Co's $74 billion acquisition of Celgene Corp, the hedge fund said on Thursday, adding to the number of shareholders declaring against the deal.

title: Sunrise hits snag after announcing $6.3 billion deal for Liberty Global's Swiss assets
description: Sunrise Communications' $6.3 billion deal to buy U.S. cable giant Liberty Global's Swiss assets, announced on Thursday, immediately hit a snag as a key shareholder said it would shun a planned rights issue to finance the acquisition.

title: Novartis faces shareholder criticism over drug prices at AGM
description: Novartis's shift into high-tech drugs won praise for providing patients with new options but criticism over prices that may run into the millions of dollars at the Swiss drugmaker's annual general meeting on Thursday.

title: Exclusive: Meeting Maduro - Inside a U.S. businessman's oil deal with Venezuela
description: In November 2017, Harry Sargeant III, a wealthy American businessman, flew to Venezuela to see about buying some oil.

title: Hyundai Motor CEO says China capacity cuts being considered: sources
description: Hyundai Motor Co, which is reeling from tumbling sales in China, is considering cutting capacity at its factories in its biggest market, Chief Executive Lee Won-hee said, according to two people with direct knowledge of the matter.

title: Darkening economic outlook threatens to cap oil price in 2019: Reuters poll
description: Oil analysts have grown more pessimistic over the prospects for a significant price rally this year, as booming U.S. shale output and a deteriorating global economic backdrop threaten to offset the boost from OPEC's crude supply cuts.

title: Sunrise seeks to compete on price after $6.3 billion UPC deal
description: Swiss telecoms group Sunrise wants to crank up price competitiveness following its 6.3 billion Swiss franc ($6.3 billion) takeover of Liberty Global's Swiss unit and also expects job cuts from the deal, Chief Executive Olaf Swantee told Reuters on Thursday.

title: Thyssenkrupp says breakup plans not contingent on Tata Steel deal
description: Thyssenkrupp will continue with its breakup plans even if the steel-to-submarines conglomerate fails to win regulatory approval for a separate joint venture with Tata Steel, Chief Executive Guido Kerkhoff said on Thursday.

title: Starbucks' China rival Luckin Coffee taps three banks for U.S. IPO: sources
description: Chinese startup Luckin Coffee, which has ambitions to overtake Starbucks at home this year, has tapped three banks including Credit Suisse to work on a U.S. IPO in 2019, said people with direct knowledge of the matter.

title: Deutsche Bank merger with Commerzbank doesn't make sense: advisor
description: A merger between Deutsche Bank and Commerzbank does not make economic sense at the moment, an advisor to Germany's Finance Ministry said on Thursday.

title: U.S. trade chief sees long-term China challenges, continued tariff threat
description: The United States will need to maintain the threat of tariffs on Chinese goods for years even if Washington and Beijing strike a deal to end a costly tariff war, President Donald Trump's chief trade negotiator told lawmakers on Wednesday.

title: Aston Martin boss: Brexit delay would prolong uncertainty
description: A delay to Brexit would be a "further annoyance" which would prolong uncertainty, the boss of luxury carmaker Aston Martin said after Prime Minister Theresa May promised to give lawmakers a vote on extending the date for Britain to leave the EU.

title: Exclusive: Istanbul airport consortium does not need new financing or partners - Limak
description: Istanbul's new airport does not need additional financing and Turkish Airlines will not be a partner in the airport consortium, the chairman of airport shareholder Limak Holding told Reuters.

title: Carmaker Aston Martin's adjusted pre-tax profit falls
description: Luxury British carmaker Aston Martin posted an adjusted pre-tax profit of 68 million pounds ($90 million) in 2018, a 7 percent fall on 2017 as it continues to invest in a series of new models and a second factory as part of its turnaround plan.

title: Carlos Ghosn's new legal team has applied for bail -Tokyo district court
description: Carlos Ghosn's new legal team has applied for bail for the ousted Nissan Motor Co Ltd chairman, the Tokyo District Court said on Thursday, the latest attempt after a string of requests were denied by judges citing Ghosn being a flight risk.

title: USTR to suspend China tariff hike 'until further notice'
description: The U.S. Trade Representative's office said on Wednesday it would move to formally suspend a scheduled tariff increase on Chinese goods "until further notice" following President Donald Trump's decision to delay his Friday deadline for a U.S.-China trade deal amid progress in their talks.

title: Inmarsat jumps on report EchoStar plans new approach
description: Inmarsat shares spiked on Thursday afternoon after a report by CTFN M&A news website said U.S. satellite group EchoStar was expected to renew its interest in the company "very soon", and no later than the next six months.

title: U.S. working on detailed trade pact with China: Mnuchin
description: The United States is working to hammer out a detailed trade agreement with China that will include specific structural commitments, U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin told CNBC on Thursday.

title: Global stocks fall on China weakness, tempered trade hopes
description: Global equities markets fell on Thursday as weak Chinese economic data and mixed messages on the progress of trade talks between China and the United States weighed on investor sentiment.

title: Russian court denies detained U.S. investor Calvey bail
description: A Russian court on Thursday ruled that prominent U.S. investor Michael Calvey should remain in custody pending trial, rejecting his appeal to be released on bail or moved to house arrest.

title: U.S. economic growth in 2018 misses Trump's 3 percent target
description: The U.S. economy fell short of the Trump administration's 3 percent annual growth target in 2018 despite $1.5 trillion in tax cuts and a government spending blitz, and economists say growth will only slow from here.

title: Fed's Powell: 'Muted' inflation gives room for wages to rise
description: A rise in productivity last year gives more room for wages to grow without the risk of higher inflation, Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell said on Thursday, offering another reason why the U.S. central bank can hold off on further rate increases.

title: Google workers support proposed U.S. laws to curb mandatory arbitration
description: Six Google employees on Thursday joined U.S. lawmakers to support bills that would ban mandatory arbitration in employment and consumer contracts, as the workers seek to build on recent success in getting the Alphabet Inc company to drop some arbitration provisions.

title: Kraft Heinz lawsuit targets 3G stock transfer, writedown, SEC probe
description: Kraft Heinz Co faces a new lawsuit questioning why controlling shareholder 3G Capital transferred $1.23 billion of stock six months before the processed foods company stunned investors with a huge writedown and other bad news.

title: Marriott revenue, FY forecast miss estimates on weak demand
description: Marriott International Inc on Thursday missed Wall Street estimates for quarterly revenue and forecast a lower-than-expected full-year profit, blaming weak demand in North America, its largest market.

title: HBO Chief Executive Richard Plepler to resign from company
description: HBO Chief Executive Richard Plepler will leave the premium television network owned by U.S. wireless carrier AT&T Inc after nearly 28 years at the company, Plepler said in a memo to HBO employees on Thursday.

title: Exclusive: KKR, China's Tencent eyeing bids for Universal Music - sources
description: U.S. buyout fund KKR and China's Tencent Music Entertainment Group are exploring rival bids for up to half of Vivendi's iconic Universal Music division, a deal potentially worth up to 20 billion euros ($23 billion), sources told Reuters.

title: In U.S. charm offensive, China's Huawei launches ad to combat dark image
description: Huawei Technologies ran a full page ad in major U.S. newspapers on Thursday urging readers not to believe "everything you hear," about the Chinese tech firm, as it defends itself against government accusations its equipment can be used to spy.

title: U.S. stocks edge downward as Wall Street takes a pause
description: Wall Street's main indexes fell slightly on Thursday as support from better-than-feared U.S. GDP data was countered by concerns about earnings and U.S.-China trade relations.

title: Trump warns he could abandon China trade deal as advisers tout progress
description: U.S. President Donald Trump on Thursday warned he could walk away from a trade deal with China if it were not good enough, even as his economic advisers touted "fantastic" progress toward an agreement to end a dispute with the Asian country.

title: Starboard joins opposition to Bristol-Myers' $74 billion Celgene deal
description: Activist hedge fund Starboard Value LP followed Bristol-Myers Squibb Co's second-largest investor, Wellington Management, in opposing the drugmaker's $74 billion purchase of biotech Celgene Corp on Thursday, sowing further doubt on what would be the largest pharmaceutical takeover ever.

title: Huawei units plead not guilty to U.S. trade secret theft
description: Huawei Device Co Ltd and Huawei Device USA Inc pleaded not guilty to U.S. fraud, trade secrets conspiracy and other charges, and a trial date was set for March 2020, the Justice Department said on Thursday.

title: China P2P lender Dianrong closing 60 stores, laying off 2,000 employees: source

title: Rolls-Royce quits race to power Boeing's planned mid-market plane

title: Allergan shareholder Chevedden backs Appaloosa's proposal to split CEO-chairman role
description: Appaloosa LP said on Thursday investor John Chevedden was backing the hedge fund's proposal to split the roles of chairman and chief executive officer at Botox-maker Allergan Plc.

description: J. C. Penney Co Inc on Thursday reported quarterly results that topped estimates as the struggling retailer sold more jewelry and women's, men's and children's apparel during the key holiday shopping season.

description: The U.S. embassy in Sweden has asked the country's financial watchdog FI for a meeting to discuss allegations about Swedbank's involvement in a Baltic money-laundering scandal.

description: Kia Motors Corp and affiliate Hyundai Motor Co said on Thursday they are recalling around 534,000 additional U.S. vehicles at risk of engine fires.

description: U.S. companies installed more robots last year than ever before, as cheaper and more flexible machines put them within reach of businesses of all sizes and in more corners of the economy beyond their traditional foothold in car plants.

title: Venezuela's oil exports drop 40 percent after U.S. sanctions: data

title: TJX holiday quarter same-stores sales beat estimates
description: Off-price apparel retailer TJX Cos Inc reported better-than-expected quarterly same-store sales on Wednesday, as steep discounts drove more shoppers to its T.J. Maxx and Marshalls stores during the holiday season.

title: Saudi Aramco adds Goldman Sachs as bookrunner for planned bond: sources
description: Saudi Aramco has added Goldman Sachs as a bookrunner for a planned bond which will help finance its purchase of a stake in Saudi Arabian Basic Industries Corp (SABIC), two sources familiar with the matter told Reuters.

title: Volvo's Polestar joins electric car race with rival to Tesla 3
description: Volvo Cars' luxury performance brand Polestar unveiled its first fully electric sedan on Wednesday, opening up online pre-orders for the five-seater fastback at a price and with a driving range to rival Tesla's mass market Model 3.

title: You don't need a PhD anymore to read Fed's statements
description: The Fed's policy statements grew so complicated after the recession that standard gauges of readability suggested people needed four years of university or more to understand them.

title: Volkswagen deepens cloud computing partnership with Microsoft
description: Volkswagen said on Wednesday it had struck a deal with Microsoft to cooperate on cloud computing in China and the United States, as part of its drive to offer connected vehicle services across the globe.

title: Campbell Soup beats earnings estimates, shares rise
description: Campbell Soup Co  on Wednesday reported better-than-expected adjusted earnings, helped by its acquisitions of Snyder's-Lance and Pacific Foods.

title: EU needs financial police, money-laundering watchdog: lawmakers
description: The European Union should set up a police force to investigate tax evasion and financial crime and create a watchdog to counter money-laundering, EU lawmakers said in a report on Wednesday, which accuses seven member states of acting as tax havens.

title: VW praises Ford's autonomous tech as partnership talks continue
description: Volkswagen on Wednesday praised its cooperation with Ford and took pains to highlight its rival's autonomous vehicles technology, as both carmakers explore deepening their partnership to include self-driving cars.

title: Ford's China JV ends some contracts with job agencies as sales fall
description: Ford Motor Co's joint venture with China Changan Automobile Group has decided not to renew its contract with some agencies supplying it with workers, as carmakers struggle to cope with slumping sales in China.

title: Credit reporting agencies face pressure from skeptical U.S. Congress
description: (This Feb. 26 story corrects the name of Equifax in paragraph 2)

description: The U.S. goods trade deficit widened sharply in December as slowing global demand and a strong dollar weighed on exports, another sign that economic growth slowed in the fourth quarter.

description: U.S. investor Cerberus, a major shareholder in both Deutsche Bank and Commerzbank, is open to a merger between Germany's two biggest lenders, a person familiar with the matter said on Wednesday, raising the chances of a tie-up.

title: Huawei, Samsung agree to settle patent dispute in U.S. court
description: China's Huawei Technologies and South Korea's Samsung Electronics have agreed to settle a two-year old patent dispute in the United States, court documents show.

title: China's CDH targets raising $1 billion in venture capital arm: sources
description: China's CDH Investments is aiming to raise nearly $1 billion in dollar and yuan funds through its venture and growth capital arm to invest in sectors including healthcare and logistics, said people with direct knowledge of the matter.

description: Standard Chartered is targeting more trade-focused business from Chinese companies by hiring around 15 bankers worldwide, a source familiar with the plans told Reuters.

title: Bayer reaps profit lift from Monsanto seeds, consumer health
description: Bayer's $63 billion purchase of U.S. seeds maker Monsanto made its mark on the German company's fourth quarter earnings on Wednesday, lifting profit and boding well for the peak season of its enlarged agriculture business.

title: Tesla's Musk must address SEC contempt bid as he calls agency 'broken'
description: A federal judge on Tuesday ordered Tesla Inc Chief Executive Elon Musk to explain by March 11 why he should not be held in contempt for violating his fraud settlement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

title: Ahold says on course to meet U.S. online sales growth targets
description: Ahold Delhaize, which operates supermarkets in Europe and the United States, is on track to meet a 20 percent U.S. online sales growth target this year as it opens automated grocery distribution points along the East Coast, its chief executive said on Wednesday.

title: Elliott pushes for Hyundai shareholder support after dividend proposals rejected
description: Elliott Management Corp on Wednesday urged shareholders of a Hyundai Motor Group firm to vote for its proposal for higher dividends and new board members, a day after the South Korean conglomerate rejected demands by the U.S. activist investor.

description: Harry Potter and Star Wars building sets helped Lego return to growth in 2018, along with strong sales in China, where the privately-owned Danish toymaker plans to open new stores.

description: Vietnamese carriers VietJet and Bamboo Airways formally announced on Wednesday deals with Boeing Co to buy 110 planes worth more than $15 billion as the fast-growing companies look to expand their operations in Asia and beyond.

description: Hyundai Motor Co said on Wednesday it plans to boost the core automotive businesses’ operating profit margin to 7 percent by 2022, compared with 2.1 percent in 2018, as part of its mid- to long-term plan.

title: Hot-rolled mess: China's steelmakers hit the skids as car sales slow
description: China's steel mills may have taken a wrong turn by adding millions of tonnes of new high-end capacity just as the country's car sector, a key steel consumer, undergoes its first contraction in decades, cutting metal demand.

description: Sunrise Communications has entered "advanced discussions" to buy Liberty Global's Swiss business in a deal which values the internet and digital television provider at 6.3 billion Swiss francs ($6.30 billion).

description: U.S. President Donald Trump said this week he may soon sign a deal with Chinese President Xi Jinping to end a trade war blamed for slowing global economic growth and disrupting markets.

title: Rattled by Vale disaster, mining CEOs move to change industry
description: After last month's deadly tailings dam disaster at a Vale SA facility in Brazil, Freeport-McMoRan Inc Chief Executive Richard Adkerson sent a memo to his 29,000 employees telling them to immediately report any safety concerns about the scores of dams his company operates.

title: Air France KLM: will look to ensure new Dutch stake does not impact company
description: Air France KLM's board will try and ensure that the stake in the airline taken by the Dutch government will not have a negative impact on the company, the airline said.

description: The Dutch government's decision to increase its stake in Air France KLM was both "incomprehensible" and unexpected, said French Finance Minister Bruno Le Maire on Wednesday.

title: Mylan shares sink as bleak profit outlook sparks growth concerns
description: Mylan NV shares slid 10 percent on Wednesday after the generic drug maker predicted poor 2019 earnings that led some Wall Street analysts to wonder if its finances would worsen further.

title: Lowe's predicts more home renovations this year after strong profit
description: U.S. home improvement chain Lowe's beat Wall Street earnings forecasts on Wednesday, and predicted that more Americans would renovate their houses this year rather than buy a home in a market where prices are rising.

title: WeWork aims for the middle with expanded 'HQ' service
description: WeWork is expanding an effort to retain mid-sized businesses which had been leaving the shared office space manager after they grew past the small-company phase, and to catch up with rivals already catering to these clients.

title: U.S. aims to combat Chinese currency manipulation in trade deal: Lighthizer
description: The United States is seeking to prevent China from competitively devaluing its currency as part of ongoing trade talks between the countries, following past manipulations of the yuan, U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer said on Wednesday.

title: Apple self-driving car layoffs give hints to division's direction
description: Apple Inc said on Wednesday it planned to lay off 190 employees in its self-driving car program, Project Titan, changes that provide a rare window into the automotive technologies the company has been pursuing.

title: Disney agrees to sell Fox Sports in Brazil to win antitrust nod
description: Walt Disney Co accepted a demand by Brazil's antitrust regulator CADE that it sell local rights for the Fox Sports channel to win approval of its takeover of Twenty-First Century Fox Inc, the regulator said on Wednesday.

title: Wells Fargo starts settlement talks with Justice Dept, SEC
description: Wells Fargo & Co said on Wednesday that it entered preliminary settlement discussions with the U.S. Department of Justice and the Securities and Exchange Commission over previously disclosed probes into its sales practices.

title: Southwest Airlines wins U.S. approval for Hawaii service
description: Southwest Airlines Co said on Wednesday it won approval from the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration to begin flying to Hawaii from California, clearing the way for the low-cost carrier to move forward with a key part of its 2019 growth plan.

title: Wall Street steadies after Lighthizer, Powell, Cohen testimonies
description: The S&P 500 closed down slightly on Wednesday but well above its session low after testimonies to U.S. Congress from trade and central bank officials as well as President Donald Trump's former lawyer brought few major surprises.

title: Disney in talks with AT&T to buy WarnerMedia's Hulu stake: Variety
description: Walt Disney Co is actively pursuing the purchase of WarnerMedia's nearly 10 percent stake in Hulu, entertainment business news portal Variety reported on Wednesday, citing sources.

title: Germany's Merck makes $5.9 billion counterbid for Versum
description: German drugs and lab supplies maker Merck KGaA offered $5.9 billion, including debt, for Versum Materials, in a cash deal that tops an offer from U.S. rival Entegris, as both seek to boost their electrochemicals operations.

title: FedEx partners with Walmart, Pizza Hut to test last-mile delivery robot
description: FedEx Corp this summer plans to begin testing a robot to handle home deliveries for partners ranging from Walmart Inc to Pizza Hut.

title: U.S. wants regular meetings to ensure trade deal enforcement: Lighthizer
description: The United States wants meetings as regularly as once a month to ensure enforcement of any potential trade pact with China, U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer said on Wednesday.

title: Boeing seeks UK decision on Wedgetail jet buy this year: executive
description: Boeing hopes Britain will decide this year on plans to buy E-7 Wedgetail early warning jets, an executive said, after talks last year sparked a row over competition in arms procurement.

title: JPMorgan hires commercial bankers, leaders across Europe, Asia
description: JPMorgan Chase & Co on Wednesday named half a dozen people to a commercial banking team in Europe and new international and Asia-Pacific regional leaders, as the U.S. bank closes in on business clients it hopes to poach from rivals abroad.

title: Oil rises 2 percent as U.S. crude stocks plunge, OPEC brushes off Trump
description: Oil futures gained about 2 percent on Wednesday after U.S. crude inventories unexpectedly plummeted and as Saudi Arabia brushed aside comments from U.S. President Donald Trump seeking to keep oil prices from climbing.

title: Global stocks slip after U.S. trade official's comments but energy up
description: Global stock indexes ended with mostly slight losses on Wednesday after U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer said it was too early to predict an outcome in U.S.-China trade talks, although a jump in oil prices lifted shares of energy companies.

title: Amazon, Comcast, Electronic Arts submit bids for Nexon holding firm-Maeil report
description: Amazon.com Inc, Comcast Corp and Electronic Arts Inc submitted initial bids for the holding firm of South Korea's biggest gaming firm Nexon, Maeil Business Newspaper said on Wednesday, citing investment banking sources.

title: J.C. Penney pulls plug on clothing subscription service
description: J.C. Penney Co Inc on Friday will end a clothing subscription service venture, the retailer said this week, a move toward sharpening its focus on more-profitable apparel sales and exiting lines like major appliances.

title: Exclusive: Exxon adds veteran traders to bulk up oil trading - sources
description: Exxon Mobil Corp has hired veteran crude traders Mitch Rubinstein and Michael Paradise in Houston, to further boost its trading capabilities, sources familiar with the matter told Reuters on Wednesday.

title: Qatar Airways suspended some destinations planned for Africa after Gulf boycott
description: Qatar Airways said on Wednesday that it had decided not to go ahead with routes to some planned destinations following a Gulf boycott, particularly in West and Central Africa, the company said in a Twitter post.

description: Qatari, Chinese and Japanese investors all sought "extras" from Barclays as the British bank raised billions of pounds at the height of the credit crisis in 2008, a landmark London criminal trial heard on Wednesday.

description: Airbus has decided to redesign the C295 military transport aircraft it builds in Spain to remove German components following Germany's freeze on arms exports to Saudi Arabia, company sources told Reuters.

description: When Air France's new Canadian chief executive met Dutch politicians in The Hague on Feb. 15, he unknowingly set in motion a new chapter in European aviation nationalism.

description: The Dutch government in recent days has stealthily built up a 14 percent stake in Air France KLM, which it said was needed to protect Dutch interests from growing French dominance in the airline group.

description: Shares in Air France-KLM fell sharply as the Dutch government amassed a 14 percent stake in the airline to counter French influence, in a surprise move highlighting tensions over the company's strategic direction.
