description: South Korea’s LG Electronics unveiled a 5G smartphone on Sunday with a dual screen, the latest handset maker to pitch a new design feature in an effort to revive flagging sales.

title: China, U.S. make 'substantial progress' in trade talks: Xinhua
description: The United States and China have made "substantial progress" on specific issues in the latest round of trade talks, China's official Xinhua news agency reported on Monday, citing the Chinese delegation to the discussions in Washington.

title: Two bodies recovered after Amazon cargo plane crashes into Texas bay
description: Two bodies have been recovered from the wreckage of an Amazon Prime Air cargo plane that nosedived into a bay outside Houston on Saturday, and a search was ongoing for a third victim, authorities said.

title: Trump sees 'very big news' in China trade talks in next week or two
description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Sunday that he wants to make a trade deal with Beijing that will be great for both the United States and China and that there could be "very big news over the next week or two" if all goes well in negotiations.

title: Caesars in talks with Icahn about new CEO as part of settlement: sources
description: U.S. casino operator Caesars Entertainment Corp is in talks to offer Carl Icahn a role in selecting its new CEO as part of an agreement that would also give the billionaire investor board seats, people familiar with the matter said on Sunday.

title: U.S., Chinese negotiators discuss enforcement in Sunday trade talks: source
description: U.S. and Chinese negotiators on Sunday are discussing tariffs and an enforcement mechanism for a potential trade deal after making good progress on structural issues during talks on Saturday, a source familiar with the situation told Reuters.

title: Microsoft workers demand it drop $480 million U.S. Army contract
description: Some Microsoft Corp employees on Friday demanded that the company cancel a $480 million hardware contract to supply  the U.S. Army, with 94 workers signing a petition calling on the company to stop developing "any and all weapons technologies."

title: Egypt's top administrative court lifts ban on Uber, Careem services
description: Egypt's top administrative court on Saturday lifted a ban on operations by ride-hailing companies Uber and Careem, which have faced fierce opposition from traditional taxi drivers, a judicial source and lawyer said.

title: NY governor orders probe into Facebook access to data from other apps
description: New York Governor Andrew Cuomo on Friday ordered two state agencies to investigate a media report that Facebook Inc may be accessing far more personal information than previously known from smartphone users, including health and other sensitive data.

title: Wall St. Week Ahead: May be time for growth to run out of gas
description: A return to fashion of growth stocks in 2019 helped lead the overall market out of a year-end shakeout, but another multi-year run of growth performing better than value may not be in the cards.

title: Trump says he's inclined to extend China trade deadline and meet Xi soon
description: President Donald Trump said on Friday there was "a very good chance" the United States would strike a deal with China to end their trade war and that he was inclined to extend his March 1 tariff deadline and meet soon with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

title: Southwest CEO says mechanics deserve new contract, but company wants 'flexibility'
description: Southwest Airlines Co's mechanics, who have been in labor contract talks for more than six years, deserve a new deal that makes them among the best paid in the airline industry, but the low-cost U.S. carrier needs "more supplier flexibility" in return, the company's chief executive said.

title: Roche nearing $5 billion deal to acquire Spark Therapeutics: WSJ
description: Swiss drugmaker Roche Holding AG is nearing a deal to acquire U.S. biotechnology company Spark Therapeutics Inc, the Wall Street Journal reported on Saturday, citing people familiar with the matter.

title: U.S., China sprint to seal deal ahead of Trump's deadline
description: U.S. and Chinese negotiators met for over seven hours on Saturday to resolve their trade dispute and avoid an escalation of the tit-for-tat tariffs that have already disrupted global commerce, slowed the world economy and roiled financial markets.

title: Cryptocurrency companies use 'backdoor' listings to ease into mainstream
description: Several cryptocurrency exchanges have moved closer to mainstream markets by buying listed companies, looking to raise funds and present themselves as embedded in the traditional financial services world they once spurned.

title: British fraud office abandons Rolls-Royce, GSK investigations
description: The UK's Serious Fraud Office (SFO) has abandoned two of its largest and longest investigations, into alleged bribery at aero engine maker Rolls-Royce and drugs maker GlaxoSmithKline, in a move described by one lawyer as "extraordinary".

title: U.S. farmers receive $7.7 billion in trade aid to date: USDA
description: U.S. Department of Agriculture has paid out $7.7 billion so far to farmers, William Northey, Undersecretary for Farm Production and Conservation, said on Friday, in aid designed to offset the negative impact of tariff imposition.

title: Exxon, Microsoft strike cloud computing agreement for U.S. shale
description: Exxon Mobil Corp and Microsoft Corp have agreed to use cloud technology in the U.S. oil producer's shale operations, they said on Friday, helping to boost profitability in the nation's largest shale field.

title: Madoff customer payout tops $12 billion
description: The court-appointed trustee liquidating Bernard Madoff's firm said he began distributing $464 million to the imprisoned swindler's former customers on Friday, boosting their recovery to roughly $12.2 billion.

title: France wants agriculture kept out of a EU-U.S. trade deal: Elysee
description: France opposes including agricultural products in any trade deal between the United States and the European Union, a source at French President Emmanuel Macron's office said on Friday.

title: EU drafting retaliatory tariff list hitting Caterpillar, Xerox, Samsonite: Bloomberg
description: The European Union has drafted a list of retaliatory tariffs  that would target Caterpillar Inc, Xerox Corp and Samsonite International if U.S. President Donald Trump imposes duties on European cars, Bloomberg News reported on Friday, citing an unnamed senior EU official.

title: France holds out over start of EU trade talks with Trump
description: France expressed reservations on Friday about proposed trade negotiations with the United States, diplomats said, while other EU countries supported talks with Washington that could ward off punitive U.S. tariffs on European cars.

title: Kraft Heinz discloses SEC probe, $15 billion write-down; shares dive 20 percent
description: Shares of Kraft Heinz Co slumped 20 percent late on Thursday after the food company posted a quarterly loss, disclosed an SEC investigation and wrote down the value of its iconic Kraft and Oscar Mayer brands as it highlighted the tough environment for the packaged food industry.

title: U.S., China haggle over toughest issues in trade war talks
description: Top U.S. and Chinese trade negotiators haggled on Thursday over the details of a set of agreements aimed at ending their trade war, just one week before a Washington-imposed deadline for a deal expires and triggers higher U.S. tariffs.

title: No clarity yet from Beijing on intellectual property: USDA trade official
description: Chinese trade negotiators have yet to provide clarity on how Beijing will address Washington's demands for more protection of American intellectual property, a key issue in negotiations to end a trade dispute between the two countries, a U.S. Department of Agriculture official said on Friday.

title: Goldman Sachs backs U.S. construction finance tech startup Rabbet
description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc has backed Rabbet, a U.S. startup that develops software to help make construction finance more efficient, the companies said on Wednesday.

title: Euro zone core inflation edges higher in Jan
description: Euro zone headline consumer inflation slowed slightly in January because of a sharp deceleration of energy price growth, but core inflation watched closely by the European Central Bank in policy decisions edged slightly higher, data showed on Friday.

title: AT&T pulls ads from YouTube over videos exploiting children
description: AT&T Inc pulled all its advertising from Alphabet Inc's YouTube for the second time in two years after a magazine reported the platform displayed ads next to videos that showed the exploitation of children.

title: EU trade chief sees EU decision soon to start U.S. trade talks
description: European Trade Commissioner Cecilia Malmstrom said on Friday she expected European Union governments to decide soon to start trade negotiations with the United States.

title: Ford probing possible problems with fuel economy, emissions tests
description: Ford Motor Co said on Thursday it has hired outside experts to investigate its vehicle fuel economy and testing procedures after employees raised concerns, and did not know whether it would have to correct data provided to regulators or consumers.

title: JPMorgan trades banker offices for shared desks
description: NEW YORK - JPMorgan Chase & Co is tearing down walls and moving its San Francisco investment bankers onto "hot desks," a space-saving layout that has long been a fixture at tech companies, while redesigning offices in Dallas and other cities.

title: FATF says EU dirty money list risks undermining its work
description: A European Union blacklist of nations it considers as anti-money laundering and terrorism-financing threats risks undermining the work of the Financial Action Task Force, the body's head said on Friday.

title: Tesla rolls out Model 3 in China ahead of schedule in sales push
description: Tesla Inc has started delivering Model 3 cars in China slightly ahead of schedule, as it looks to revive its sales that have been hit hard by Sino-U.S. trade tensions.

title: Apple teams with Ant Financial, banks for interest-free iPhone financing in China
description: Apple Inc has teamed up with Chinese payments giant Ant Financial Services Group and several local banks to offer interest-free financing, its first such move in the country as it looks to boost waning smartphone sales.

title: Societe General plans to cut thousands of jobs at investment bank: Bloomberg
description: French bank Societe General SA is planning to cut thousands of jobs at its global banking and investor solutions unit, as it looks to offset cost pressure from regulation,  Bloomberg reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.

title: Italian ruling-party lawmakers push for Huawei ban: paper
description: A group of lawmakers from Italy's ruling coalition is pushing the government to ban China's Huawei Technologies Co Ltd from supplying equipment for the country's rollout of 5G mobile communications, Il Messaggero newspaper said on Friday.

title: Puma goes up-market to join forces with Porsche Design
description: (This February 21 story refiles to give full name of Porsche Design in headline.)

title: Alibaba CEO rules out layoffs this year
description: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd expects to avoid layoffs this year despite China's economic slowdown, CEO Daniel Zhang said on Friday.

title: U.S. judge will not block Amazon-Berkshire-JPMorgan health venture's new hire
description: A federal judge on Friday declined to block a UnitedHealth Group Inc unit's former executive from working at a new healthcare venture launched by Amazon.com Inc, Berkshire Hathaway Inc and JPMorgan Chase & Co.

title: Fed to keep open mind in review of strategy, tools, Clarida says
description: The Federal Reserve will keep an open mind as it begins a broad review this year of its monetary policy framework that could result in changes to how it goes about ensuring that prices remain stable and employment plentiful, Fed vice chair Richard Clarida said on Friday.

title: VietJet to sign major Boeing deal during Trump-Kim summit: sources
description: Fast-growing Vietnamese budget airline VietJet Aviation JSC is expected to sign a major jet deal with Boeing Co on the sidelines of next week's Trump-Kim summit, according to sources familiar with the matter.

title: UBS ignored whistleblower warnings in French tax case: judgment
description: UBS was warned numerous times over a period of at least six years that its French private bank risked breaking local tax laws, according to the written judgment in a case where the Swiss bank faces a 4.5 billion euro ($5.10 billion) penalty.

title: Newmont says aware of Barrick's buyout talk but will not comment
description: Newmont Mining Corp said on Friday it was aware that Canadian rival Barrick Gold Corp said it had studied an unsolicited buyout proposal for the company, a deal that would, if consummated, bring together two of the world's leading gold producers.

title: Trump says could include Huawei and ZTE in trade deal
description: U.S. President Donald trump said on Friday he may or may not include Chinese telecommunications companies Huawei Technologies and ZTE Corp in the trade deal being negotiated between the United States and China.

title: Kraft Heinz shares fall 28 percent after writedown, dividend cut
description: Kraft Heinz Co shares fell to a record low on Friday a day after the food company disclosed a $15 billion write-down on its marquee brands, raising concern that years of rigorous cost cutting have eroded the value of its Kraft cheeses and Oscar Mayer deli meats.

title: Brazil judge suspends Embraer-Boeing tie-up negotiations: court document
description: A Brazilian judge on Friday suspended negotiations for the tie-up of Brazilian aircraft maker Embraer SA and Boeing Co, according to a court document.

title: No more MOUs! USTR Lighthizer tweaks trade terminology after dispute with Trump
description: In trade talks between the United States and China, Memorandums of Understanding - the building blocks of what would be a historic deal - are officially out.

title: Fed's policy pause sets stage for broad overhaul
description: When Federal Reserve policymakers last month put a three-year rate-hike campaign on hold and backed ending a yearlong push to shrink their $4 trillion balance sheet, they cited increased risks to U.S. economic growth and the need for more time to sort through the data.

title: Flattening U.S. yield curve in late 2018 'flashing red' on economy: Fed's Williams
description: A flattening U.S. yield curve in December, which was close to being inverted, was "flashing red" about a deceleration in U.S. economic growth heading into 2019, despite some solid data at the time, New York Federal Reserve President John Williams said on Friday.

title: FCA sets $14 million annual target compensation for CEO Manley: filing
description: Fiat Chrysler Automobiles NV (FCA) has set an annual compensation target for Chief Executive Officer Mike Manley consisting of pay, cash and equity bonuses of $14 million, the automaker said in a regulatory filing on Friday.

title: S&P 500 posts highest close since November 8 on trade optimism
description: The S&P 500 posted its highest closing level since Nov. 8 on Friday as investors clung to signs of progress in the ongoing trade talks between the United States and China.

title: Trump's economy 'a little under' 3 percent growth goal: Fed
description: The Trump administration will fall "a little under" its target of 3 percent annual growth of gross domestic product for 2018, the Federal Reserve said Friday in a report that offers an economic scorecard of sorts for the first full year of President Donald Trump's term.

title: Canada's Barrick considers buyout of rival Newmont Mining
description: Canada's Barrick Gold Corp said on Friday it considered making an all-stock bid for U.S. rival Newmont Mining Corp, a deal that would create a monolith in the global gold sector and likely push smaller peers to start buying each other.

title: Twitter co-founder Evan Williams steps down from board
description: Twitter Inc said on Friday one of its co-founders, Evan Williams, will be stepping down as a member of its board at the end of the month.

title: U.S.-China trade hopes lift stocks; oil hits three-month high
description: Stocks rose in major markets across the world on Friday on bets of progress in trade talks between China and the United States, while crude futures hit their highest level in more than three months supported by ongoing supply cuts.

title: UBS sticks to dividend, capital return plans after French verdict
description: UBS plans to stick to its proposed dividend for 2018, CEO Sergio Ermotti said on Friday, two days after the Swiss bank was hit with a 4.5 billion euro ($5.1 billion) penalty in a French tax ruling that the bank has appealed.

title: Oil hits 2019 highs on U.S.-China trade hopes, but U.S. output weighs
description: Oil prices touched their highest since mid-November on Friday and posted weekly gains for the second week in a row, boosted by hopes that U.S.-China trade talks would soon produce a deal, although new record U.S. oil supply limited gains.

title: Volkswagen warns of challenges, to redouble efforts to meet targets
description: Volkswagen warned on Friday of a tough year ahead as its preliminary annual results were weighed down by currency effects and supply bottlenecks caused by new emissions testing rules.

title: Intel says its 5G modem chips will not appear in phones until 2020
description: Intel Corp executives said on Friday its 5G modem chips will not appear in mobile phones until 2020, raising the possibility its biggest customer, Apple Inc, will be more than a year behind rivals in delivering a device that uses the faster networks.

title: Daimler, BMW to invest 1 billion euros in venture to rival Uber
description: German carmakers Daimler and BMW unveiled a joint ride-hailing, parking and electric car charging business on Friday to compete with mobility services provided by Uber and other tech firms.

title: GM extends production at Detroit factory until early 2020
description: General Motors Co said on Friday it had extended the production at its Detroit Hamtramck plant until January 2020, against an earlier plan to discontinue production in June this year.

title: AutoNation names new CEO as slowing auto sales hit results
description: AutoNation Inc said on Friday it has chosen insurance and financial services executive Carl Liebert to succeed longtime Chief Executive Officer Mike Jackson and lead the largest U.S. auto dealership chain at a challenging time, when the domestic vehicle market has been slowing.

title: Equifax says U.S. regulators seek damages related to 2017 breach
description: Credit reporting company Equifax Inc said it was informed by several U.S. regulators that they intend to seek damages from the company related to the cybersecurity breach of 2017 that exposed personal information of nearly 145 million people.

title: China has agreed to buy up to $1.2 trillion in U.S. goods: CNBC
description: China has agreed to buy up to $1.2 trillion in goods from the United States as part of the current negotiations to end the trade war between the countries, CNBC reported on Friday, citing sources familiar with the situation.

title: Kraft Heinz' problems shine light on controversial budget tool
description: Mounting troubles at Kraft Heinz, revealed late on Thursday with a triple-punch of bad news, call into question its reliance on cost-cutting as a way to generate profit growth.

title: Wild cats, boas are obstacles in Mexican president's refinery race
description: Mexican President Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador's race to build an oil refinery in record time on land that was until recently alive with mangrove, wild cats and boa constrictors, has run into trouble, complicating his effort to revive ailing state-oil company Pemex.

title: Trump says he expects to meet China's Xi soon on trade
description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Friday that if he sees progress being made in trade talks with China, he may be inclined to extend negotiations beyond a March 1 deadline, and suggested it was likely the globe's two largest economies would be able to make a deal.

title: A Fed pivot, born of volatility, missteps, and new economic reality
description: The Federal Reserve's promise in January to be "patient" about further interest rate hikes, putting a three-year-old process of policy tightening on hold, calmed markets after weeks of turmoil that wiped out trillions of dollars of household wealth.

title: Huawei to open first flagship store outside China in Vienna
description: Huawei is to open a smartphone flagship store in Vienna, its first such outlet outside China, as part of a charm offensive in Europe where its future hangs in the balance.

title: Danske bolsters board as U.S. expands money laundering investigation
description: The money laundering scandal at Danske Bank deepened on Thursday when the Danish lender said it had received an inquiry from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

title: EU governments endorse copyright reform - statement
description: Representatives of European Union governments endorsed on Wednesday a deal reached with the EU Parliament on the overhaul of the bloc's copyright rules, the Romanian presidency of the EU said in a statement on Twitter.

title: EU countries back copyright reforms aimed at Google, Facebook
description: European Union countries on Wednesday endorsed an overhaul of the bloc's copyright rules which would force Google and Facebook Inc to pay publishers for news snippets and filter out copyright-protected content on YouTube or Instagram.

title: Brazil's Vale to pay $3,200 to residents to compensate for dam burst that killed 300
description: Miner Vale SA said on Thursday it would pay adult residents in the Brazilian town of Brumadinho a total of 12,000 reais ($3,227.02) as compensation for the damage from a dam that collapsed and killed over 300 people in January.

title: U.S. won't partner with countries that use Huawei systems: Pompeo
description: U.S. Secretary of State Mike Pompeo on Thursday warned that the United States would not be able to partner with or share information with countries that adopt Huawei Technologies Co Ltd systems, citing security concerns.

title: Swedish watchdog calls Swedbank money laundering report 'very serious'
description: Sweden's financial watchdog said allegations in a media report linking Swedbank to a Baltic money laundering scandal, involving Danske Bank were "very serious" as shares in the Swedish bank tumbled on Thursday.

title: Apple, Goldman Sachs to jointly launch credit card paired with iPhone: WSJ
description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc has teamed up with Apple Inc to issue credit cards that will be paired with iPhones and will help users manage their money, the Wall Street Journal reported https://www.wsj.com/articles/apple-goldman-sachs-team-up-on-credit-card-paired-with-iphone-11550750400 on Wednesday, citing people familiar with the matter.

title: U.S. weekly jobless claims fall, but trend weakening
description: The number of Americans filing applications for unemployment benefits fell last week, but the four-week moving average rose to a more than one-year high, suggesting the labor market was slowing down.

title: Credit Suisse loses bid to dismiss lawsuit in U.S. over writedowns
description: A U.S. judge has rejected Credit Suisse Group AG's bid to dismiss a lawsuit accusing the Swiss bank of defrauding shareholders about its risk appetite and risk management before taking $1 billion of writedowns on souring debt.

title: Sweden, Estonia to jointly probe Swedbank over alleged money laundering
description: Swedish and Estonian finance watchdogs have opened a joint investigation into allegations that Swedbank played a role in the Baltic money laundering involving Danske Bank, the two supervisory bodies said on Thursday.

title: China's central bank to keep yuan stable, maintain prudent monetary policy
description: China's central bank said on Thursday that it will keep its yuan currency stable and maintain its prudent monetary policy to ensure financial stability in the world's second-largest economy.

title: Trump urges U.S. telecommunications companies to step up 5G systems
description: U.S. President Donald Trump on Thursday called on U.S. telecommunications companies to boost their work to build faster 5G wireless communications networks, saying they were lagging and at risk of being left behind other countries' efforts.

title: Exclusive: China central bank sees benchmark rate cut as last resort, may use other tools - sources
description: China's central bank is not yet ready to cut benchmark interest rates to spur the slowing economy, despite cooling inflation and a stronger yuan, which have fanned market expectations of such a move, policy sources told Reuters.

title: Google fails to disclose microphone in Nest Secure
description: Alphabet Inc's Google said on Wednesday it had made an "error" in not disclosing that its Nest Secure home security system had a built-in microphone in its devices.

title: Canadian auto union faces Catch-22 in General Motors fight
description: Jerry Dias, the leader of Canada's auto union, is unsparing in his rhetorical attacks on General Motors Co's decision to close its Oshawa, Ontario, assembly plant and lay off thousands of union workers by year-end.

title: PG&E extends deadline for board nominations
description: PG&E Corp, which filed for bankruptcy last month in the wake of potential liabilities from California's catastrophic wildfires, on Thursday extended the deadline by which investors must file paperwork if they want to install their directors on the board.

title: Investor Browder to file criminal complaint against Swedbank
description: Bill Browder, founder and CEO of investment fund Hermitage Capital Management, intends to file a criminal complaint against Swedbank with Swedish authorities over its involvement in alleged Baltic money laundering transactions, he said on Thursday.

title: Exclusive: RWE to win EU okay to buy E.ON, Innogy renewables businesses
description: German utility RWE will win unconditional EU antitrust approval to buy the renewables businesses of E.ON and Innogy in a deal that will reshape the German energy market, people familiar with the matter said on Thursday.

title: Exclusive: Nigeria hits oil majors with billions in back taxes
description: Nigeria has ordered foreign oil and gas companies to pay nearly $20 billion in taxes it says are owed to local states, industry and government sources said, in a move that could deter investment in Africa's largest economy.

title: Factbox: U.S., China drafting memorandums for possible trade deal
description: Top U.S. and Chinese trade officials are working this week to hash out language on six broad agreements that aim to resolve the most contentious issues in their seven-month trade war.

title: Standard Chartered sets aside $900 million to cover U.S., British fines
description: Standard Chartered PLC (StanChart) has set aside $900 million to cover fines resulting from regulatory investigations in the United States and Britain, potentially drawing a line under probes which have dogged the bank for years.

title: Banning Huawei from 5G would cause difficulties: T-Mobile Polska CEO
description: If Poland excludes Chinese tech giant Huawei from 5G development it would cause difficulties and possibly delay the network rollout, the chief executive of the Polish unit of T-Mobile said on Thursday.

title: Samsung announces folding phone with 5G at nearly $2,000
description: Samsung Electronics Co Ltd on Wednesday unveiled a nearly $2,000 folding smartphone in a bid to top the technology of Apple Inc and Chinese rivals and reignite consumer interest amid slumping sales.

title: Blown away by innovation or price? Samsung's foldable phone opens new frontier
description: Samsung Electronics Co Ltd has wowed the smartphone industry with the first foldable screen, burnishing its innovation credentials, banishing "fast follower" criticism and, at nearly $2,000, setting a new standard in premium pricing.

title: Google's new cloud boss has big task to catch rivals, Reuters data show
description: Google has a new cloud computing boss and big ambitions to someday produce more revenue from that business than from advertising.

title: Volkswagen boss says U.S. tariffs could cost up to 2.5 billion euros: Financial Times
description: The biggest threat to Volkswagen's 2019 profit is potential tariffs from the United States, Chief Executive Herbert Diess told the Financial Times.

title: U.S. Agriculture Secretary says hopes U.S. will ratify new North American trade deal by summer
description: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Sonny Perdue said on Thursday that he hopes the United States will ratify the U.S.-Mexico-Canada trade deal known as USMCA by summer, after Congress has a chance to understand the accord's provisions.

title: SK Hynix plans to spend $107 billion building four memory chip plants
description: South Korea's SK Hynix Inc on Thursday said it would spend $107 billion building four factories, as the memory chip maker seeks to maintain its competitiveness in the face of Chinese efforts to become a leading chipmaking nation.

title: Sony to beef up chip business with new engineers
description: Sony Corp said on Thursday it will assign 40 percent of its new engineer hires in Japan over the next two years to the chip business which includes imaging sensors, as it looks for growth from new applications in everything from cars to phones.

title: Apple car may be an electric van: Manager Magazin
description: A long-speculated vehicle to be developed by Apple may turn out to be an electric van rather than a car, a German magazine reported on Thursday.

title: Swedbank initiates external review of money laundering report
description: Swedish bank Swedbank said on Thursday it was appointing audit firm EY to carry out an external investigation after a media report linked the bank to a Baltic money laundering scandal involving Danske Bank.

title: U.S. banks record $59.1 billion in profits in fourth-quarter of 2018
description: The U.S. banking sector recorded $59.1 billion in profits in the fourth quarter of 2018, down slightly from the third quarter's record level but still up significantly from the prior year, according to data from the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation.

title: Consumer Reports yanks recommendation for Tesla's Model 3, citing reliability
description: Consumer Reports on Thursday pulled a recommendation for Tesla Inc's Model 3, citing reliability problems, and the influential U.S. magazine turned up the pressure on other automakers to include crash-avoiding automatic braking as standard equipment.

title: Nike stumbles into social media storm after basketball star's shoe splits
description: A Nike Inc sneaker worn by a college basketball superstar split in half less than a minute into a highly anticipated game between Duke University and North Carolina, prompting an outcry on social media as the company sought to figure out what caused the problem.

title: Huawei plan to fix British security fears due in H1 this year: executive
description: Huawei will present a plan to address British security concerns about its equipment by the end of the first half of this year, a senior company executive said on Thursday, following criticism the Chinese firm has not moved fast enough to fix the issues.

title: U.S. carriers compete for new slots at Tokyo's Haneda airport
description: The top three U.S. carriers announced bids for new slots at Tokyo's Haneda International Airport on Thursday as part of a push to increase daily nonstop flights to the Japanese capital ahead of the 2020 Olympic Games and beyond.

title: Exclusive: SpaceX, Boeing design risks threaten new delays for U.S. space program
description: NASA has warned SpaceX and Boeing Co of design and safety concerns for their competing astronaut launch systems, according to industry sources and a new government report, threatening the U.S. bid to revive its human spaceflight program later this year.

title: GM CEO will not appear before Canada legislators on plant closure
description: General Motors Co Chief Executive Mary Barra will not come before Canadian legislators to answer questions about the automaker's future in the country, but lower-ranking executives will appear, a lawmaker said on Thursday.

title: Former Enron CEO Jeffrey Skilling released from federal custody
description: Jeffrey Skilling, the onetime chief of Enron Corp who was sentenced to 24 years in prison for his conviction on charges stemming from the company’s spectacular collapse, has been released from federal custody, the Houston Chronicle reported on Thursday.

title: Johnson & Johnson receives federal subpoenas related to baby powder litigation
description: Johnson & Johnson said Wednesday it has received subpoenas from the U.S. Justice Department and the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) related to litigation involving alleged asbestos contamination in its signature Baby Powder product line.

title: Wall St. breaks run of gains as economic data disappoints
description: Weak economic reports pressured U.S. stocks on Thursday after the market's recent run of gains, and a drop in healthcare shares added to the bearish momentum.

title: Pinterest confidentially files for IPO: WSJ
description: Online image search site Pinterest Inc has confidentially filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission for an initial public offering, the Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.

title: U.S. stocks sag on poor economic outlook; oil, gold slip
description: Wall Street stocks fell on Thursday due to a deteriorating economic outlook that was only partially offset by signs of trade progress between China and the United States, while gold and oil prices retreated from their recent peaks.

title: Ford's Brazil shutdown highlights automakers' woes with excess capacity
description: Ford Motor Co's oldest factory in Brazil, slated for closure later this year, was a giant among auto plants, occupying a sprawling 12 million square feet (111.5 hectares), bigger than many of the automaker's U.S. facilities.

title: Philadelphia sues seven big banks, alleges municipal bond collusion
description: The city of Philadelphia has filed an antitrust lawsuit accusing seven major banks of conspiring to inflate interest rates for a type of bond used by cities, towns and other public entities, costing them potentially billions of dollars.

title: Trump to meet Chinese Vice Premier Liu He on Friday: White House
description: U.S. President Donald Trump will meet with Chinese Vice Premier Liu He, who is leading trade talks with U.S. officials in Washington, at the White House on Friday, the White House said on Thursday.

title: Airbus pencils in orders for new A321XLR jet: sources
description: Airbus has begun lining up tentative orders for a longer-range version of its A321 jetliner, seeking to exploit signs of hesitation at arch-rival Boeing over whether to develop a new model in a hotly contested niche of the airplane market.

title: Swedish and Estonian watchdogs open joint Swedbank probe
description: Sweden's and Estonia's financial watchdogs have opened a joint investigation following a media report linking Swedbank to a Baltic money laundering scandal involving Danske Bank, they said on Thursday.

title: Exclusive: U.S., China sketch outlines of deal to end trade war - sources
description: The United States and China have started to outline commitments in principle on the stickiest issues in their trade dispute, marking the most significant progress yet toward ending a seven-month trade war, according to sources familiar with the negotiations.

title: U..S can quickly recover lost farm trade to China once deal clinched: Ag Secy
description: The United States will be able to quickly recover lost markets for U.S. farm products to China once Washington and Beijing clinch a trade deal, U.S. Agriculture Secretary Sonny Perdue said on Thursday.

title: De Beers says lab-grown diamond wholesale prices fall by up to 60 percent
description: Wholesale prices for lab-grown diamonds have fallen by up to 60 percent since De Beers began selling synthetic stones for jewelry in September, CEO Bruce Cleaver said on Thursday, adding margins for the sector would continue to fall.

title: Remain or leave? Carmakers confront hard Brexit choices
description: In three cavernous former Royal Air Force hangars at an old airbase in Wales, luxury carmaker Aston Martin is forging ahead with construction of a new vehicle assembly plant.

title: Mexico president says no more Pemex oil joint ventures for now
description: President Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador said on Thursday Mexico will not offer more oil joint ventures between private companies and state energy company Pemex indefinitely, raising doubts about auctions set for October.

title: U.S. leading economic indicators fall in January, some components estimated
description: The index of U.S. leading economic indicators declined 0.1 percent in January, the Conference Board said on Thursday, but it advised that some of the components of the index were estimated due to the government shutdown.

title: Exclusive: Lyft plans to launch its IPO roadshow week of March 18 - sources
description: Lyft Inc plans to launch the roadshow for its initial public offering during the week of March 18, making it the first U.S. ride-hailing company to debut in the stock market, people familiar with the matter said on Wednesday.

title: Weak U.S. data underscore growing headwinds to economy
description: New orders for key U.S.-made capital goods unexpectedly fell in December amid declining demand for machinery and primary metals, pointing to a sustained slowdown in business spending on equipment that could further crimp economic growth.

title: Ariane 6 rocket sees first commercial deals in race with SpaceX
description: Ariane 6, Europe's next-generation space rocket, is expected to win its first two commercial launch orders in coming weeks, company officials said, a key milestone as the European launcher vies for orders against Elon Musk's U.S. competitor SpaceX.

title: For Sainsbury and Asda, watchdog's analysis leaves merger in serious doubt
description: Sainsbury's planned 7.3 billion pound ($9.5 billion) takeover of Walmart's Asda can only be salvaged if Britain's competition regulator fundamentally changes its analysis of Britain's grocery market, experts said on Thursday.

title: Oil off 2019 highs as U.S. crude stocks build, output hits record
description: Oil prices fell below 2019 highs on Thursday after U.S. government data showed a fifth weekly build in crude inventories and record production, while concerns about slowing global economic growth weighed.

title: Nestle investing $115 million to expand Purina factory in U.S.
description: Nestle is investing $115 million to expand its Purina factory in Bloomfield, in the U.S. state of Missouri, the Swiss foodmaker said on Thursday, as it seeks to increase production of cat litter.

title: Saudi Aramco to decide in first half on financing SABIC buy: CEO
description: Saudi Aramco said on Wednesday it expects to decide by mid-2019 how to finance the acquisition of Saudi Arabian Basic Industries Corp (SABIC).

title: UBS ordered by court to pay French state 800 million euros in damages
description: A French court on Wednesday ordered UBS to pay the French state 800 million euros ($907 million) in damages, after finding UBS guilty of laundering the proceeds of tax fraud.

title: UBS to appeal against French court ruling
description: Swiss bank UBS will appeal against a French court's ruling that found it guilty of laundering the proceeds of tax evasion, said UBS' general counsel.

title: UBS slams French verdict in tax evasion trial
description: UBS slammed a French court verdict on Wednesday ordering the Swiss bank to pay 4.5 billion euros ($5.10 billion) after finding it guilty of aiding tax evasion.

title: Factbox: Tesla executive departures since 2016
description: Tesla Inc on Wednesday announced the departure of its general counsel Dane Butswinkas, just two months into the job, the latest in a string of senior level exits from the electric carmaker.

title: Britain managing Huawei risks, has no evidence of spying: official
description: Britain is able to manage the security risks of using Huawei equipment in national telecoms networks and has not seen any evidence of malicious activity by the company, the head of Britain's National Cyber Security Centre said on Wednesday.

title: Steve Cohen's venture firm invests in U.S. cybersecurity company
description: Billionaire investor Steve Cohen's Point72 Ventures has invested in a U.S. cybersecurity firm that will provide a way to detect, alert, and protect against data- and identity-related attacks, according to one of the venture capital company's top officials.

title: Norwegian Air aims to fly stranded plane out of Iran in next few days
description: Budget carrier Norwegian Air expects to fly a plane out of Iran in the next few days after it made an emergency landing there in December and became stranded, partly due to U.S. sanctions on Tehran.

title: U.S. trade representative to testify on China next week
description: U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer will testify next week at a U.S. House of Representatives hearing on U.S.-China trade issues, a spokesman for the House Ways and Means Committee said on Wednesday.

title: Amid trade talks, China urges U.S. to respect its right to develop, prosper
description: The United States should respect China's right to develop and become prosperous, the Chinese government's top diplomat told a visiting U.S. delegation, reiterating that the country's doors to the outside world would open wider.

title: Qualcomm urges U.S. regulators to reverse course and ban some iPhones
description: Qualcomm Inc is urging U.S. trade regulators to reverse a judge's ruling and ban the import of some Apple Inc iPhones in a long-running patent fight between the two companies.

title: Former Barclays chairman 'not aware' of Qatar fee document, court told
description: Barclays' former chairman, giving evidence in a landmark London fraud trial, said he first saw a document detailing agreed fees for Qatari investors in the British bank four years after the payment was agreed.

title: U.S. ambassador to Italy visits Telecom Italia headquarters
description: The U.S. ambassador to Italy, Lewis Eisenberg, visited the  Rome headquarters of Italian phone group Telecom Italia on Wednesday, a Reuters witness said.

title: Airbus says A320neo India deliveries back on track
description: European aircraft maker Airbus deliveries of its A320neo aircraft are back on track in India with fewer problems being seen with the narrowbody jet's Pratt & Whitney engines, a senior company executive said on Wednesday.

title: British PM May says Honda plant closure can't be blamed on Brexit
description: British Prime Minister Theresa May said Honda's announcement that it would close its factory in England in 2021 was deeply disappointing, but could not be blamed on the country's upcoming departure from the European Union.

title: VW South Africa targets record production in 2019: official
description: German carmaker Volkswagen's South African unit expects to produce a record number of vehicles this year despite a sluggish domestic economy, power outages and looming talks with union members, its managing director said.

title: Caesars says continues to look at options after Icahn urges sale of company
description: Caesars Entertainment Corp said on Wednesday it will continue to look at options for the company, a day after activist investor Carl Icahn urged the U.S. casino operator to consider selling itself.

title: EU medicines agency loses bid to end London lease over Brexit
description: The European Medicines Agency (EMA) has lost its bid to cancel  a lease on its office in London's Canary Wharf financial district due to Brexit, in a landmark ruling that lawyers said could stave off similar such claims by other tenants.

title: Lockheed unveils new F-21 fighter jet configured for India
description: Lockheed Martin offered India on Wednesday a new combat jet to be made locally, the F-21, in an attempt to win a large military order worth more than $15 billion.

title: Ghosn's new lawyer, 'the Razor', takes aim at Nissan and prosecutors
description: Carlos Ghosn's new lawyer took aim at Nissan, prosecutors and courts on Wednesday, dismissing the charges against the ousted chairman as an internal company matter and saying Japan was out of step with international norms by keeping his client in jail.

title: FMC expects NxStage deal to close in next couple of days
description: Germany's Fresenius Medical Care (FMC) said on Wednesday it has won the green light from U.S. regulators to acquire U.S. home dialysis equipment maker NxStage and expects the deal to close in the next few days.

title: Governance panel opposed to Renault chairman being named Nissan head: sources
description: An external committee tasked by Nissan Motor Co to help improve corporate governance at the Japanese firm is opposed to the idea of Renault's chairman being appointed to lead Nissan's board, two people familiar with the matter said.

title: India's top court finds Anil Ambani guilty of contempt in RCom-Ericsson case
description: India's Supreme Court on Wednesday found Anil Ambani, chairman of debt-laden Reliance Communications (RCom), guilty of contempt of court for wilfully failing to pay 5.5 billion rupees ($77.29 million) to telecom equipment maker Ericsson.

title: Saudi Aramco in talks on further Indian investments
description: Saudi Aramco, the world's top oil exporter, is in talks on  possible investments in Indian projects involving companies including Reliance Industries, operator of the world's biggest refining complex, its chief executive said on Wednesday.

title: Revenue at Nutella maker Ferrero reaches $12 billion after Nestle acquisition
description: Revenue at Ferrero reached $12 billion in the fiscal year ended in August, as the group included sales of products like Butterfinger and BabyRuth chocolate bars bought from Nestle at the end of March.

title: Alitalia will not be nationalized, needs market solution: economy minister
description: Italian Economy Minister Giovanni Tria said on Wednesday that Alitalia, which is under special administration, will not be nationalized, adding that the government wants a market solution to keep the airline operating.

title: Tesla's top lawyer leaves two months into the job
description: Tesla Inc said on Wednesday its general counsel Dane Butswinkas is leaving the electric carmaker just two months into the job, the latest in a string of top-level departures at the company.

title: UBS CEO says French appeals process to take 'several years'
description: UBS Group expects its appeal of a French court verdict ordering the Swiss bank to pay 4.5 billion euros ($5.10 billion) for aiding tax evasion to last years, Chief Executive Sergio Ermotti told staff in a memo.

title: Daimler risks fine as German prosecutors launch new probe
description: German prosecutors have launched a probe into Daimler for allegedly failing to prevent diesel emissions cheating, possibly resulting in a fine for the carmaker, as its legal woes mount up over the affair.

title: Wall Street ends up slightly as Fed minutes support cautious stance
description: U.S. stocks ended higher on Wednesday after minutes from the Federal Reserve's last meeting reaffirmed for investors that the U.S. central bank would be "patient" with respect to further interest rate hikes.

title: Fed flags end to balance sheet runoff, patience on rates
description: The Federal Reserve on Wednesday signaled they will soon lay out a plan to stop letting go of $4 trillion in bonds and other assets, but policymakers are still debating how long their newly adopted "patient" stance on U.S. rates policy will last.

title: Global stocks rise on U.S.-China trade hopes; oil up again
description: An index of stocks across the globe hit a more than four-month high on Wednesday on hopes for progress in trade talks between the United States and China, and a supportive backdrop from major central banks also helped push risk assets higher.

title: Exclusive: Brazil's Odebrecht to propose bondholder losses of over 70 percent - sources
description: Brazilian conglomerate Odebrecht SA next week will ask its  bondholders to accept losses of more than 70 percent from their bonds' face value as part of a restructuring, two sources with knowledge of the matter said on Wednesday.

title: Microsoft says discovers hacking targeting democratic institutions in Europe
description: Microsoft Corp on Wednesday said it had discovered cyber attacks directed at democratic institutions, think tanks and non-profit organizations in Europe and would offer a cyber security service to several countries to close security gaps.

title: Canada to release federal budget on March 19: finance minister
description: The Canadian government will unveil its budget for the 2019/20 fiscal year on March 19, Finance Minister Bill Morneau said on Wednesday.

title: January FOMC minutes: Little risk in pause
description: Federal Reserve policymakers thought pausing on U.S. interest rate hikes last month posed little risk and plenty of benefit, minutes from their Jan. 29-30 meeting showed, giving them time to assess the effects of a global slowdown and the Fed's rate hikes to date on U.S. economic momentum.

title: Oil settles 1 percent higher on hopes of market rebalance, trade deal
description: Crude prices rose more than 1 percent on Wednesday to their highest level this year on hopes that oil markets will balance later this year, helped by output cuts from top producers as well as U.S. sanctions on OPEC members Iran and Venezuela.

title: Business jet deliveries rise 3.8 percent in 2018: industry group
description: Business jet deliveries worldwide rose 3.8 percent on an annual basis to 703 planes in 2018, lifted by demand from North America and the introduction of new models, the General Aviation Manufacturers Association (GAMA) said on Wednesday.

title: UBS to appeal after fined 4.5 billion euros in French tax fraud case
description: A French court found Swiss bank UBS AG guilty of illegally soliciting clients and laundering the proceeds of tax evasion, ordering it to pay 4.5 billion euros ($5.1 billion) in penalties.

title: CVS profit miss, rebate questions send shares tumbling 8 percent
description: CVS Health Corp  on Wednesday forecast 2019 profit well below Wall Street estimates due to weakness in its pharmacy business that serves long-term care facilities and slower than anticipated growth in drug prices, sending shares down 8 percent.

title: Volkswagen's Audi to cut 10 percent of management positions: CEO in Handelsblatt
description: Volkswagen's premium auto brand Audi plans to eliminate one layer of management or about 10 percent of the division's executive positions in a cost cutting drive, the unit's chief executive told daily Handelsblatt.

title: Southwest shares drop as mechanics dispute escalates
description: Southwest Airlines Co's shares fell more than 5 percent on Wednesday after the low-cost U.S. carrier said it was investigating whether a conflict with its mechanics union was leading to a spike in flight cancellations.

title: Buffett's Suncor bet to revive investor interest in Canadian energy
description: Berkshire Hathaway Inc's re-investment in Suncor Energy Inc highlights the benefits of being an integrated oil company and could revive investor interest in the languishing Canadian energy sector, fund managers said.

title: Bristol-Myers says Starboard nominated five directors, bought shares
description: Bristol-Myers Squibb Co said on Wednesday that activist hedge fund Starboard Value LP intends to nominate five directors to the U.S. drugmaker's board, one month after it announced a $74 billion deal to acquire peer Celgene Corp.

title: Sainsbury's-Asda deal in jeopardy as UK regulator condemns plan
description: Britain's competition regulator has dealt a potentially fatal blow to Sainsbury's planned $9.5 billion takeover of Walmart's Asda, saying the supermarket groups are unlikely to be able to address its "extensive" concerns about the deal.

title: Bombardier to deliver handful of Global 7500 jets in first half 2019
description: Bombardier Inc, the Canadian train and plane maker, will deliver a handful of its new flagship Global 7500 business jets to customers in the first half of 2019, with the remaining 10-15 deliveries expected in the second half, its chief financial officer said on Wednesday.

title: Danske Bank pulls out of Russia, Baltics after money-laundering backlash
description: Danske Bank will pull out of Russia and the neighboring Baltic states, the Danish lender said after Estonia ordered it to close the branch at the center of one of the largest-ever money laundering scandals.

title: Exclusive: Kinder Morgan to expand Chicago ethanol hub to calm glut concerns - sources
description: Kinder Morgan Inc will expand barge-loading capacity at its ethanol terminal in Chicago to help relieve a supply glut there that is driving down global prices for the biofuel, three people briefed on the company's plans told Reuters.

title: Estonia investigates alleged Swedbank link to money laundering scandal
description: Estonia is investigating allegations linking Swedbank to suspicious transactions in the country involving Danske Bank, Estonia's state prosecutor said on Wednesday.

title: Volvo Cars raises $215 million in bond issue months after failed IPO
description: Sweden's Volvo Cars has raised some 2 billion Swedish crowns ($215 million) in a bond issue just five months after the Chinese-owned carmaker terminated plans for a stock market flotation, blaming trade tensions and a downturn in the sector.

title: Renault's outlook cut to 'negative' by rating agency Standard & Poor's
description: Credit rating agency Standard & Poor's cut its outlook on carmaker Renault to "negative" from "stable", citing broader challenges within the automotive sector that could hit its profits.

title: Activist Bramson's unlikely Barclays board seat bid sharpens scrutiny of bank
description: Activist investor Edward Bramson's bid to join the Barclays board is destined to fail, shareholders told Reuters, though he has sharpened scrutiny of its investment banking strategy that Bramson argues has depressed profitability.

title: UK business secretary skips conference to update lawmakers on Honda
description: British business secretary Greg Clark will not speak at Tuesday's EEF manufacturing conference as billed and his deputy Richard Harrington will appear instead, the Department for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy said.

title: Nestle says it is now well positioned in confectionery
description: Nestle's success with its KitKat brand means its does not need to add new businesses after selling its candy unit to Italy's Ferrero last year, the Swiss food group's global head of confectionery said.

title: Alibaba boosts stake in investment bank CICC for $231 million
description: China's e-commerce giant Alibaba Group Holding Ltd has raised its stake in top domestic investment bank China International Capital Corp's Hong Kong-listed shares to nearly 12 percent, an exchange disclosure showed on Monday.

title: VW's Audi mulls cutting night shifts at Ingolstadt plant: Handelsblatt
description: Volkswagen's Audi is considering cutting night shifts at its Ingolstadt plant, Handelsblatt reported on Tuesday, citing the head of the luxury carmaker's works council.

title: Saab proposes to make 96 Gripen jets in India to win Air Force deal
description: Swedish defense firm Saab AB, which is seeking to sell its Gripen fighter jets to the Indian Air Force, said on Tuesday it could offer to make most of them in a production facility likely to be set up in one of the southern cities.

title: BHP CEO staying around to deal with tailings and transformation
description: The chief executive of mining group BHP has no plans to quit and will focus on the "nuclear level of safety" needed to avoid any repeat of the Vale dam collapse in Brazil, as well as on transforming his own company.

title: Get Brexit sorted out, UK business minister says after Honda plant decision
description: The United Kingdom must urgently end the uncertainty over its exit from the European Union so that businesses can have clarity about the future, business minister Greg Clark said just hours after Honda said it would close its car plant in Britain.

title: Huawei founder says will not share data with China: CBS News
description: Huawei Technologies Co Ltd's founder and chief executive pledged not to share any customer information with the Chinese government and said the company had never done so, in an interview with CBS News that aired on Tuesday.

title: UK PM May told Honda president she was disappointed by plant closure: spokesman
description: British Prime Minister Theresa May spoke to the president of Honda to express her disappointment after the car manufacturer's decision to shut a plant in England, May's spokesman said on Tuesday.

title: Glencore to cut output, jobs at copper, cobalt mine in Congo: WSJ
description: Glencore Plc is planning to cut production at one of its largest copper and cobalt mining operations in the Democratic Republic of Congo, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing sources on Tuesday.

title: HSBC warns on China, UK slowdowns as 2018 profit disappoints
description: HSBC warned it may have to delay some investments this year as Europe's biggest bank missed 2018 profit forecasts due to slowing growth in its two home markets of China and Britain.

title: British supermarkets battle to secure stocks as chaotic Brexit looms
description: Britons could face shortages of fresh food, price rises and less variety if the country leaves the European Union next month without agreeing on trade terms, food industry officials say.

title: Volkswagen customer plans to take diesel case to Germany's highest court
description: A German court on Tuesday ruled in favor of Volkswagen in a case brought by a customer seeking compensation for having bought a diesel car affected by emissions cheating, but the plaintiff's lawyer plans to appeal.

title: Elliott takes 6.1 percent stake in Dutch Intertrust
description: Paul Elliott Singer, the hedge fund manager behind activist investor Elliott, has taken a 6.1 percent stake in Dutch trust and business administration company Intertrust, according to a filing published by the Dutch Authority for Financial Markets (AFM).

title: Payless ShoeSource seeks bankruptcy protection again
description: U.S. discount retailer Payless ShoeSource Inc on Monday filed for voluntary Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection for the second time, along with its North American subsidiaries, and said it would wind down all North American stores by the end of May.

title: China's JD.com to lay off 10 percent of senior executives this year: report
description: JD.com Inc, one of China's largest e-commerce sites, will lay off 10 percent of its senior executives this year, Chinese online media outlet Sina Tech reported on Tuesday, citing unnamed sources.

title: China's Fosun makes bid for German fashion chain Tom Tailor
description: Chinese conglomerate Fosun International announced a takeover bid for troubled German clothing retailer Tom Tailor on Tuesday, further expanding its reach into Europe's fashion sector.

title: Germany sees 'most difficult part' in EU-U.S. trade talks ahead
description: The most difficult part in trade negotiations between Europe and the United States is starting now and talks should focus on reducing tariffs on industrial goods to increase the chances of a deal, German Economy Minister Peter Altmaier said on Tuesday.

title: Chinese government doesn't get involved in Huawei's business: German boss
description: The head of China's Huawei Technologies in Germany told a German newspaper that the Chinese government does not get involved in the company's business, adding the firm would work on being open and transparent in the debate about security of mobile networks.

title: Mongolia to suspend KFC outlets for inquiry after food poisoning reports
description: A Mongolian regulator said it will suspend operations at KFC restaurants temporarily to conduct inquiries, as 42 people were hospitalized and hundreds showed food poisoning symptoms after eating at one of the outlets of the fast-food chain.

title: Honda to shut UK car plant in 2022 with the loss of 3,500 jobs
description: Japanese car maker Honda is set to announce it's closing its only British car plant in 2022 with the loss of 3,500 jobs, a lawmaker told Reuters, in the latest blow to the UK car industry as Brexit approaches.

title: UK deeply disappointed by Honda's decision to close plant
description: Britain said on Tuesday it was deeply disappointed by Honda's decision to close its only British car plant.

title: Honda UK plant closure not related to Brexit: Europe boss
description: Honda's decision to close its only British car plant is not related to Brexit and is a product of global changes in the industry, the firm's Europe's boss said on Tuesday.

title: Honda CEO says decision to end production in UK not Brexit related
description: Honda Motor Co's decision to end production in Britain was not related to Brexit, its chief executive said on Tuesday, after announcing the closure of its only British car plant.

title: Britain's Cobham takes $206 million charge to settle Boeing dispute
description: British engineer Cobham will take an additional exceptional charge of 160 million pounds ($206 million) to settle a dispute with Boeing over its delayed KC-46 aerial refuelling programme, it said on Tuesday.

title: U.S. consumers forecast more spending than a year ago: NY Fed
description: U.S. consumers expect to spend more money in 2019 than they did a year ago, data from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York showed on Tuesday.

title: Goldman Sachs Asia Pacific CEO to retire: Bloomberg
description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc's Chairman and Chief Executive for the Asia-Pacific region excluding Japan, Ken Hitchner, is retiring from the company, Bloomberg reported on Tuesday, citing people with knowledge of the matter.

title: Mexico pushes mobile payments to help unbanked consumers ditch cash
description: Mexico's new leftist government is betting on financial technology to help lift people out of poverty.

title: Aviva, NatWest to join 'Brexodus' of business to EU
description: England's High Court on Tuesday gave Aviva, Britain’s second largest insurer, approval to transfer around 9 billion pounds ($11.69 billion) in assets to a new Irish company just before the starting gun is fired on Brexit.

title: Germany still in talks on Huawei 5G network role, minister says
description: Germany's government is still in talks on whether China's Huawei will be allowed to participate in building the country's high-speed internet infrastructure, German Economy Minister Peter Altmaier said on Tuesday.

title: Gold hits 10-month peak on growth worries; dollar dips
description: Gold prices rose to a 10-month high on Tuesday as concerns over a global economic slowdown spurred a safe-haven bid and were also supported by a weaker U.S. dollar, which fell on optimism for a breakthrough in U.S.-China trade talks.

title: Nissan to oppose having same chair as Renault: FT
description: Nissan Motor Co Ltd's independent committee on governance is expected to recommend against the company having the same chairman as Renault SA, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday, citing people with knowledge of the discussions.

title: Tokyo's drive to expel zombie stocks hits small caps
description: The Tokyo Stock Exchange's push to weed out small and weak firms from its main board could take years, but some fund managers are already ditching small-caps for fear they could be excluded from benchmarks.

title: Southwest vows investigation into grounded planes amid talks with mechanics
description: A top Southwest Airlines Co executive said the low-cost carrier would investigate why the number of aircraft unable to fly due to mechanical issues had doubled in recent days, causing flight delays and cancellations.

title: South Korean prosecutors raid Hyundai's office in recall probe: Chosun Biz
description: South Korean prosecutors on Wednesday raided the office of Hyundai Motor Co's quality division in southern Seoul as part of a probe into how the automaker and affiliate Kia Motors Corp handled vehicle recalls over engine defects, online media Chosun Biz reported.

title: Tesla prepares to offer Model 3 leasing to boost demand: Electrek
description: Elon Musk's Tesla Inc is preparing to launch its leasing products for Model 3 to boost demand, news website Electrek said on Tuesday, citing an email sent to employees.

title: German government unlikely to make quick decision on Huawei: source
description: The German government will probably not take a quick decision on whether to allow China's Huawei to build Germany's 5G network, a government source said on Tuesday.

title: Ford to close oldest Brazil plant, exit South America truck biz
description: Ford Motor Co said on Tuesday it will close its oldest factory in Brazil and exit its heavy commercial truck business in South America, a move that could cost more than 2,700 jobs as part of a restructuring meant to end losses around the world.

title: U.S. settles with Teva over keeping generic drugs off market
description: The U.S. government has reached a settlement with Teva Pharmaceuticals Industries Ltd over charges that its agreements with rivals impeded consumer access to lower-priced generic drugs.

title: Exclusive: Fed's Williams says new economic outlook necessary for rate hikes
description: New York Fed President John Williams on Tuesday said he was comfortable with the level U.S. interest rates are at now and that he sees no need to raise them again unless economic growth or inflation shifts to an unexpectedly higher gear.

title: Walmart holiday-quarter sales jump, says consumers still spending
description: Walmart Inc posted its strongest holiday quarter in at least a decade on Tuesday, boosted by higher grocery and e-commerce sales, and said it saw no signs of weakness in U.S. consumer spending despite recent signs of a slowdown.

title: Kellogg, Mondelez stock up on Pringles, Milka for fear of Brexit
description: As Brexit looms, Kellogg Co and Mondelez International Inc are taking measures to protect Britons from a potential shortage of Pringles chips, BelVita biscuits and Milka chocolate.

title: Wall Street rises modestly on Walmart bump
description: U.S. stocks gained ground on Tuesday as upbeat results from Walmart boosted investor sentiment and high-level U.S.-China trade talks resumed in Washington.

title: U.S. watchdog proposes 'testing waters' before public offerings
description: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) proposed on Tuesday to expand a rule that allows companies to sound prospective investors out privately before going public.

title: U.S. approves Fresenius purchase of NxStage
description: The U.S. Federal Trade Commission has given Germany's Fresenius Medical Care AG and U.S. home dialysis equipment maker NxStage Medical Inc antitrust approval for their merger, the agency said on Tuesday.

title: Allergan should explore selling itself: Appaloosa's Tepper
description: Billionaire hedge fund manager David Tepper stepped up pressure on Allergan Plc, saying on Tuesday the drugmaker should consider selling itself if management is unable to turn around recent lagging performance.

title: Google to buy data migration company Alooma in cloud push
description: Alphabet Inc's Google said on Tuesday it will buy data migration company Alooma, as part of efforts to catch up with bigger cloud service rivals Amazon.com Inc and Microsoft Corp.

title: Trump says March 1 deadline for China trade talks not 'magical' date
description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that trade talks with China were going well and suggested he was open to pushing off the deadline to complete negotiations, saying March 1 was not a "magical" date.

title: BAE Systems wins funding from U.S. Army to start production of new armored vehicles
description: Britain's defense company BAE Systems on Tuesday said it had won additional funding up to $575 million from the U.S. Army to begin production of its new armored vehicles that would replace the Vietnam War-era M113 fleet of personnel carriers.

title: Medtronic quarterly profit beats on strength in surgical products
description: Medtronic Plc beat analysts' estimates for quarterly profit on Tuesday, boosted by sales of its surgical products, and the largest U.S. standalone medical device maker raised the upper end of its full-year earnings forecast.

title: JD Sports raises its stake in Footasylum to more than 18 percent
description: Footasylum Plc said on Tuesday its larger rival JD Sports Fashion Plc has increased its stake in the company to more than 18 percent.

title: Netflix Toronto production hub to create 1,850 jobs annually
description: Netflix Inc said on Tuesday it is creating a production hub with two studios in Toronto that is expected to create 1,850 jobs per year.

title: Honda to close British car plant as Brexit looms
description: Honda will close its only British car plant in 2021 with the loss of up to 3,500 jobs, a major departure of Japanese investment announced just over a month before the United Kingdom is due to leave the European Union.

title: Barclays hoped 2008 cash call would drive international growth, court told
description: Barclays believed deals with strategic investors during the 2008 financial crisis would help to provide a springboard for its international ambitions, the bank's former chairman told a London criminal trial on Tuesday.

title: U.S. seeking stable yuan pledge in China trade deal: Bloomberg TV
description: The United States is seeking to secure a pledge from China it will not devalue its yuan as part of an agreement intended to end the countries' trade war, Bloomberg TV reported on Monday.

title: U.S., McKinsey & Co reach $15 million settlement over bankruptcy case disclosures
description: The United States and McKinsey & Company have reached a $15 million settlement over allegations that the global consulting company did not make proper disclosures in bankruptcy cases, the U.S. Department of Justice said in a statement on Tuesday.

title: Honeywell-Pratt venture protests GE's Army helicopter contract
description: A joint venture of Honeywell International Inc and Pratt & Whitney on Tuesday protested the U.S. Army's decision to award General Electric Co a $517 million contract for new Black Hawk and Apache helicopter engines.

title: Brent dips as demand worries weigh, U.S. oil prices hit 2019 high
description: Oil prices were mixed on Tuesday as concerns about global crude oil demand and uncertainty over the latest round of U.S.-China trade talks countered investor optimism around tightening supplies.

title: Honda plan to close UK plant is not due to Brexit:  lawmaker
description: Japan's Honda plans to shut its British car plant in Swindon by 2022 with the loss of 3,500 jobs but the decision is not related to Brexit, a local lawmaker told Reuters on Monday.

title: New Zealand will conduct own assessment of Huawei equipment risk: PM
description: New Zealand will independently assess the risk of using China's Huawei Technologies in 5G networks, Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern said on Monday after a report suggested that British precautions could be used by other nations.

title: SoftBank invests in Mubadala's new $400 million European tech fund: source
description: Japan's SoftBank Group has provided nearly half of the cash for Abu Dhabi's state investor Mubadala Investment Co's new $400 million fund investing in European start-ups, a source familiar with the matter said.

title: Citi in talks to buy Canary Wharf office building: source
description: Citigroup is in talks to buy the tower housing its European headquarters in London's Canary Wharf district, which is on the market with a price tag of around 1.2 billion pounds ($1.55 billion), a source familiar with the matter said.

title: Britain's FT says allegations over Wirecard reporting are false
description: Britain's Financial Times rejected as "baseless and false" any allegations accusing the newspaper or its reporters of market manipulation or unethical reporting in relation to German payments company Wirecard.

title: World stocks lifted to 2 1/2-month highs by trade optimism
description: Hopes for progress in Sino-U.S. trade talks and expectations of policy stimulus from central banks lifted world stocks to 2 1/2- month highs on Monday, though European gains were held back by concern over the outlook for auto makers.

title: Russia's Rusal is in talks to resume reinsurance with Western companies
description: Russia's Rusal, the world's second-largest aluminum producer, is in talks to resume reinsuring its risks with Western companies after Washington lifted sanctions on it, officials with Russian National Reinsurance Co (RNRC) said.

title: Citi expects privatization to bolster revenue in Brazil
description: Citigroup Inc expects to boost annual revenue in Brazil over the next years by advising potential public asset sales and through a revival in capital markets, its chief executive officer in Brazil told journalists on Monday.

title: Auto industry lines up against possible U.S. tariffs
