description: The European Commission said on Tuesday it had fined Mastercard  570.6 million euros ($648.3 million) for limiting the possibility for merchants to benefit from better conditions offered by banks  elsewhere in the European Union.

title: In Versailles, Macron vows to reform to avoid king's fate
description: President Emmanuel Macron told dozens of the world's most powerful executives on Monday that he would not follow the path of guillotined French royals and would continue to reform the French economy despite a sometimes violent popular revolt.

title: Electric guitar maker Fender launches U.S.-made acoustic guitar
description: When Bob Dylan skipped his acoustic guitar and "went electric" on stage in 1965, it was with a Stratocaster model from Fender Musical Instruments Corp [FNDR.UL], considered by many the quintessential rock 'n' roll electric instrument.

title: Brazil investor group to file lawsuit against Boeing-Embraer deal
description: Brazilian investors’ association Abradin said it would file a lawsuit claiming a proposed tie-up between U.S. planemaker Boeing Co  and Embraer SA  should come with a public tender offer, escalating its fight against the proposed deal.

title: UBS sets gloomy tone for Europe's banks
description: UBS  warned of a tough start to 2019, after reporting an outflow of funds from its flagship wealth management business at the end of last year, sending a shiver through the European banking sector.

title: Taco Bell's first Thailand outlet to serve spicy fare and local beer
description: U.S. fast food giant Taco Bell is opening its first outlet in Thailand, continuing the Yum! Brands  chain's Asia expansion, offering adapted menu items and local beer.

title: Preferred bidders for Elior's Areas arm to be chosen by March: sources
description: Preferred bidders for the Areas business of French company Elior  are expected to be chosen by the start of March, a source close to the matter told Reuters.

title: Saudi Aramco talking to credit rating agencies before bond deal: Bloomberg
description: Saudi Aramco is talking to credit rating agencies ahead of its landmark bond deal, the chief executive of Saudi Arabia's state-owned oil company told Bloomberg television.

title: Swiss Railways will not take new Bombardier trains until earlier problems fixed
description: Swiss Federal Railways said it would not take new trains from Bombardier  until the Canadian company fixes the ones already in service, raising questions over the timing of future deliveries for the 1.9 billion Swiss franc ($1.9 billion) contract.

title: P&O to change flag of UK ships to Cyprus ahead of Brexit
description: British ferry and shipping freight operator P&O will shift the registration of its UK vessels to Cyprus ahead of Britain's departure from the European Union, in part to keep its tax arrangements in the bloc, the company said on Tuesday.

title: Exclusive: Autogrill submitted a bid for Elior's Areas business - source
description: Italy's Autogrill  has submitted a bid for the railways, motorway and airport catering business of France's Elior , a source told Reuters on Tuesday.

title: Exclusive: Tesla holds battery supply talks with China's Lishen
description: U.S. electric vehicle (EV) maker Tesla Inc  has held talks with China's Tianjin Lishen to supply batteries for its new Shanghai factory, and two people with direct knowledge of the matter said the pair signed a preliminary agreement.

title: 'Fill or kill': the three weeks that saved Sears
description: The future of Sears Holdings Corp  and tens of thousands of its employees across the United States hung in the balance in the freezing pre dawn hours last Wednesday, as Wall Street lawyers and bankers sparred over the fate of the beleaguered retailer in a 50-story Manhattan office tower.

title: UBS won't take lead in consolidating European bank sector: Weber
description: Switzerland's UBS Group  will not take the lead in consolidating a fragmented European bank sector, Chairman Axel Weber said on Tuesday.

title: Japan firms have no plans to strengthen governance after Ghosn arrest: Reuters poll
description: Three-quarters of Japanese companies have no plan to create committees overseeing compensation or executive nomination, a Reuters poll found, reflecting indifference to boosting governance after the arrest of former Nissan boss Carlos Ghosn.

title: China's growth slowed by service, farm sectors, despite construction rebound
description: Weakness in the service and farm sectors slowed China's economic growth in the fourth quarter, despite a strong pickup in construction activity, official data showed on Tuesday.

title: Danske faces new investor lawsuit threat
description: Litigation funder IMF Bentham  has teamed up with legal experts Quinn Emanuel and Njord Law Firm and plans to file a shareholder lawsuit against Danske Bank  by July over a 200 billion euro ($230 billion) money laundering scandal.

title: Tokyo court denies latest bail request of Nissan's Ghosn
description: Carlos Ghosn's latest request for bail was rejected by a Tokyo court on Tuesday, despite the ousted Nissan chairman offering to wear an electronic ankle tag in an unusual bid to win release after two months of detention for alleged financial crimes.

title: Credit Suisse CEO sees conditions improving after tough fourth quarter
description: Credit Suisse  is seeing market conditions improve after a tough fourth quarter, Chief Executive Tidjane Thiam said on Tuesday as rival UBS  reported disappointing fourth-quarter results.

title: Foxconn says trying to hire 50,000 people in first quarter after job cut reports
description: Taiwan's Foxconn , assembler of Apple Inc's  iPhones, on Tuesday said it was trying to recruit for more than 50,000 positions across its China campuses for the January-March quarter, amid reports of mass lay-offs.

title: 'A List' climate change firms outperform on stock market - survey
description: Apple , L'Oreal  and Mitsubishi Electric  are among more than 120 global firms which scored top marks in a ranking of corporate efforts to slow climate change.

title: Saudi Aramco eyes multi-billion-dollar U.S. gas acquisitions: CEO
description: Saudi Aramco, the world's top oil producer, is looking to acquire natural gas assets in the United States and is willing to spend "billions of dollars" there as it aims to become a global gas player, the company's CEO said on Tuesday.

title: KPMG subject of second UK investigation over Carillion audit
description: Britain's Financial Reporting Council (FRC) has opened a second investigation into how accounting firm KPMG audited the books of collapsed UK construction company Carillion, the watchdog said on Tuesday.

title: China's Lishen says has not signed agreement with Tesla on supplying batteries
description: China's Tianjin Lishen said on Tuesday it has not signed any agreement with Tesla Inc  on supplying batteries to the U.S. electric vehicle maker's Shanghai factory.

title: Canada should ban Huawei from 5G networks, says former spy chief
description: Canada should ban China's Huawei Technologies Co Ltd from supplying equipment to Canadian 5G networks because the security risk is too great, a former spy chief said in an article published on Monday.

title: Tesla says it has no agreement with Chinese battery maker Lishen
description: Tesla Inc  denied on Tuesday that it had signed a preliminary agreement with Tianjin Lishen to supply batteries for its new Shanghai car factory, saying it had received quotes from the Chinese battery maker but did not proceed further.

title: As China's economy falters, some fund managers look to bonds
description: Despite mounting signs of a Chinese economic slowdown, 2019 is off to a good start for fund manager Du Zhenye.

title: Toyota, Panasonic announce battery venture to expand EV push
description: Toyota Motor Corp and Panasonic Corp are launching a joint venture next year to make electric vehicle (EV) batteries, leveraging the heft of one of the world's largest automakers and battery makers to expand their EV push.

title: Exclusive: Colfax picks Goldman to sell Howden business - sources
description: Colfax Corp  is pressing ahead with plans to sell its air and gas handling unit Howden as part of a shift to focus on the medical devices industry and has hired Goldman Sachs to handle the process, four sources close to the matter told Reuters.

title: Halliburton shares fall as North America lags
description: Shares of oilfield firm Halliburton Co  fell sharply on Tuesday after the company forecast lower revenues in key business areas in the first quarter, overshadowing a quarterly profit beat and a pledge to reduce 2019 spending.

title: Wall Street drops as economic outlook, corporate forecasts sour
description: U.S. stocks ended lower on Tuesday, snapping a four-session rally, as a gloomy global economic growth outlook, trade concerns and disappointing company forecasts dampened sentiment.

title: U.S. will seek extradition of Huawei CFO from Canada
description: The U.S. Justice Department said on Tuesday it will pursue the extradition of the chief financial officer of China's Huawei Technologies Co Ltd's, arrested in Canada in December.

title: Google, Facebook spend big on U.S. lobbying amid policy battles
description: Alphabet Inc's Google disclosed in a quarterly filing on Tuesday that it spent a company-record $21.2 million on lobbying the U.S. government in 2018, topping its previous high of $18.22 million in 2012, as the search engine operator fights wide-ranging scrutiny into its practices.

title: Cloud, services fuel IBM's profit beat, robust outlook; shares jump
description: IBM Corp  beat Wall Street quarterly earnings estimates and also forecast 2019 profit above expectations on Tuesday, in the latest indication that Chief Executive Officer Ginni Rometty's efforts to turn around the technology services company were gaining traction.

title: Trump won't soften hardline on China to make trade deal: advisers
description: As much as U.S. President Donald Trump wants to boost markets through a trade pact with China, he will not soften his position that Beijing must make real structural reforms, including how it handles intellectual property, to reach a deal, advisers say.

title: Bayer asks California judge to limit evidence in another Roundup cancer trial
description: Bayer AG unit Monsanto has asked a California judge in the litigation over its glyphosate-based weed killer Roundup allegedly causing cancer to limit evidence by splitting an upcoming trial into two phases, a request previously successful with another judge.

title: Explainer: The shareholder puzzle facing airlines after Brexit
description: Airlines that will no longer be majority owned by EU nationals once Britain leaves the European Union face the threat of losing their right to fly within the bloc after Brexit due to share ownership rules.

title: Explainer: What happens next in Huawei CFO Meng's case?
description: The U.S. Justice Department said on Tuesday it will pursue the extradition of Huawei Technologies Co Ltd's [HWT.UL] Chief Financial Officer Meng Wanzhou, arrested in Canada in December on allegations she participated in a conspiracy to defraud banks.

title: Equities slump on growth, trade worries
description: A gauge of world stock markets fell on Tuesday as concerns over global growth and trade gave investors incentive to look toward safe-haven assets such as the Japanese yen and government bonds.

title: J&J forecasts disappointing 2019 sales, defends talc safety
description: Johnson & Johnson on Tuesday forecast 2019 sales that fell short of analysts' estimates and said it expected further pressure on U.S. prescription drug prices, weighing on the broader pharmaceutical sector.

title: J&J, U.S. states settle hip implant claims for $120 million
description: Johnson & Johnson and its DePuy Orthopaedics unit have agreed to pay $120 million to resolve deceptive marketing claims by several U.S. states over the company's metal-on-metal hip implants.

title: Viacom will buy Pluto TV streaming service for $340 million
description: Viacom Inc  said on Tuesday it will buy Pluto TV, a free video streaming TV service, for $340 million in cash to expand its advanced advertising business.

title: Lockheed Martin wins $542 million U.S. defense contract: Pentagon
description: Lockheed Martin Corp  has been awarded a $542 million contract for equipment and spares for F-35 aircraft, the Pentagon said in a statement on Tuesday.

title: BAE Systems wins $474 million U.S. defense contract: Pentagon
description: BAE Systems PLC  has been awarded a $474 million U.S. defense contract for technical and maintenance support for the M109 family of vehicles, the Pentagon said on Tuesday.

title: BlackRock plans environmentally conscious money market fund
description: BlackRock Inc is planning a new fund for investors looking to park their cash safely while helping the environment, expanding options for "socially responsible" investments, a filing with U.S. market regulators showed on Tuesday.

title: Brazil's Bolsonaro uses Davos speech to appeal to big business
description: Brazil's new right-wing President Jair Bolsonaro threw out the welcome mat for big business and foreign investors on Tuesday, telling a summit of CEOs in Davos that his government would make the country one of the top 50 in which to do business.

title: U.S. home sales hit three-year low, prices rise slowly
description: U.S. home sales tumbled to their lowest level in three years in December and house price increases slowed sharply, suggesting a further loss of momentum in the housing market.

title: Huawei calls for swift end to case of executive arrested in Canada
description: China's Huawei Technologies wants a quick resolution of the case of its former finance chief Meng Wanzhou, who is accused of violating U.S. sanctions on Iran and has been detained in Canada, its chairman said on Tuesday.

title: Renault convenes board to turn page on Ghosn era
description: Renault  has called a board meeting to replace Chairman and Chief Executive Carlos Ghosn, in a move that may begin to ease tensions with alliance partner Nissan  in the wake of Ghosn's arrest in Japan for alleged financial misconduct.

title: Exclusive: No-deal Brexit puts Bentley's return to profit at risk
description: Loss-making carmaker Bentley is on track to be profitable this year but a no-deal Brexit puts that at "fundamental risk", its boss told Reuters, adding that the chance of Britain leaving the EU on March 29 with a deal now seemed "fairly low."

title: Pompeo voices optimism for good outcome on U.S.-China trade
description: U.S. Secretary of State Mike Pompeo voiced optimism on Tuesday for a good outcome in upcoming trade talks with China and said a superpower conflict between the two nations could be avoided.

title: Canada has not asked U.S. to drop case of Huawei's Meng: Freeland
description: Canada has not asked the United States to abandon its bid to have Huawei executive Meng Wanzhou extradited, Canada's Foreign Minister Chrystia Freeland said on Tuesday in an interview with Bloomberg TV.

title: U.S. to pursue extradition of Huawei CFO from Canada
description: The U.S. Justice Department said on Tuesday that it will pursue the extradition of Huawei Technologies Co Ltd's [HWT.UL] chief financial officer, arrested in Canada in December on allegations that she participated in a conspiracy to defraud banks.

title: BMW and Daimler to name ride-hailing venture 'Jurbey': source
description: German companies BMW and Daimler will name their combined ride-hailing and car-sharing firm "Jurbey", a source familiar with the matter said on Tuesday.

title: Oil drops nearly 3 percent on rising supplies, China slowdown
description: Oil prices fell 3 percent on Tuesday over concerns the world's stumbling economy could pinch fuel demand as U.S. crude output climbs to new heights and cuts by Saudi Arabia and its allies are smaller than advertised.

title: Brexit backer Dyson moves vacuum giant's HQ to Singapore
description: James Dyson, the billionaire Brexit supporter who revolutionized vacuum cleaners with his bagless technology, is moving his head  office to Singapore from Britain to be closer to his company's fastest-growing markets.

title: Carrefour confident over overhaul despite fourth-quarter 'yellow vests' hit
description: Carrefour  said on Tuesday it was confident its  overhaul plan was on track, although sales growth slowed slightly in the fourth quarter as 10 weeks of anti-government protests hit hypermarket sales in its core French market.

title: Hedge funds push for overhaul at eBay
description: Hedge funds Elliott Management and Starboard Value have taken stakes in eBay Inc  and are pushing for changes including the sale of some of the e-commerce company's businesses.

title: GM, facing losses in Brazil, seeks tax breaks in Sao Paulo state
description: General Motors Co's  Brazil unit is in advanced talks with Sao Paulo state to receive tax incentives, the company told public officials and union representatives at a meeting on Tuesday, a few days after telling workers in a memo that it was losing money in the country.

title: PG&E shares surge as company secures $5.5 billion in bankruptcy financing
description: U.S. power producer PG&E Corp's shares surged as much as 16 percent on Tuesday after it said it had secured $5.5 billion in debtor-in-possession (DIP) financing from four banks as it prepares to file for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection.

title: Nissan's Ghosn offers to wear electronic ankle tag for bail
description: Ousted Nissan Motor Co Chairman Carlos Ghosn has offered to wear an electronic ankle tag and hire guards to monitor him in an unusual bid to secure his release on bail after two months of detention in Japan for alleged financial crimes.

title: Sparkling Australian wine exports lose their fizz as Chinese economy slows
description: Australian wine shipments to China grew at their slowest pace in four years in 2018, industry data showed on Tuesday, in another indication that Sino-U.S. trade tensions were dragging on consumer spending in the world's second-largest economy.

title: China's Huawei in unprecedented media blitz as it battles heightened scrutiny
description: China's Huawei has launched an unprecedented public relations blitz, thrusting its low-key founder in front of international media as the telecoms firm seeks to ease concern among Western nations bent on shutting it out of their markets.

title: Global FDI skids 19 percent on Trump tax reform, may rebound in 2019 - U.N.
description: Global foreign direct investment (FDI) fell 19 percent last year to an estimated $1.2 trillion, largely caused by U.S. President Donald Trump's tax reforms, the United Nations trade and development agency UNCTAD said on Monday.

title: Xi keeps China on high alert for 'black swan' events: Xinhua
description: China must be on guard against "black swan" risks while fending off "gray rhino" events, President Xi Jinping said on Monday, adding that the economy faces deep and complicated changes, state news agency Xinhua reported.

title: German economy minister: Must do everything to support Siemens, Alstom train merger
description: Germany's Economy Minister Peter Altmaier said on Monday that he was in favor of a planned train merger between Siemens  and Alstom  and would do its utmost to support it.

title: Take Five: World markets themes for the week ahead
description: Following are five big themes likely to dominate the thinking of investors and traders in the coming week and the Reuters stories related to them.

title: European power firms aim to harness electric car batteries
description: Ever wanted to run your electric car for free? If you're open to a bit of give and take, then stay plugged in and your wishes might come true. At least that's what some European power companies and Japanese carmakers believe.

title: Detained ex-Nissan chairman Ghosn offers stock, passports for bail
description: Ousted Nissan Motor Co  chairman Carlos Ghosn has offered to post stock he owns in the automaker as collateral, surrender his passports and submit to electronic tracking as part of a renewed effort to persuade a Tokyo court to grant him bail while he awaits trial on charges of financial misconduct, a spokeswoman for the car executive said.

title: Nippon Life president says actively exploring M&A in U.S.
description: Nippon Life Insurance Co is actively seeking mergers and acquisitions overseas, with a focus on the United States and Asia's emerging economies, the president of Japan's largest life insurer said on Monday.

title: France's Casino sells stores to Fortress, hits asset sales target
description: Casino  has agreed to sell 26 stores worth 501 million euros ($567 million) to Fortress Investment Group, the French supermarket retailer said on Monday, fulfilling an assets sale target set out last year as part of plans to reduce its debt.

title: Eve-of-Davos survey shows people place trust in companies over governments
description: People around the world place much more trust in their companies than their political leaders, according to a major survey that suggests a mood of uncertainty and pessimism on the eve of the World Economic Forum in Davos.

title: Nissan, Renault not ready to discuss new capital ties: Saikawa
description: Nissan CEO Hirota Saikawa said on Monday that he had not heard directly about a reported French proposal to integrate the Japanese carmaker's management with Renault, adding that it was not the time to discuss revising the partners' capital ties.

title: GSK Chairman Hampton to step down ahead of split
description: GlaxoSmithKline Plc  Chairman Philip Hampton will step down after more than three and a half years in the role, as Britain's biggest drugmaker prepares to split its business into two.

title: Sainsbury's-Asda tie-up not a done deal yet, experts warn
description: Shortly after last year's announcement of a $9.4 billion deal to combine the Sainsbury's  supermarket group that he runs with rival Asda, boss Mike Coupe was caught on camera singing "We're in the money".

title: Data dependent? Five questions for the ECB
description: The European Central Bank holds its first meeting of the year on Thursday as concern grows about weak economic growth at home and risks abroad from global trade tensions and Brexit.

title: Western Australia claims BHP owes up to $215 million in underpaid iron ore royalties
description: The state of Western Australia said on Monday an audit had found global miner BHP Group underpaid royalties on iron ore shipments sold via its Singapore marketing hub stretching back over more than a decade.

title: Germany: Siemens/Alstom deal could increase competitiveness
description: German Economy Minister Peter Altmaier said on Monday that the aim of a planned merger of Alstom  and Siemens'  rail businesses was to increase competitiveness, adding that this goal was achievable.

title: Lockheed sees potential exports of 200 F-16 jets from proposed Indian plant
description: Lockheed Martin  sees a potential export market of more than $20 billion for its F-16 fighter aircraft from an assembly line in India it has offered to set up in order to win a large Indian military order, a top executive said.

title: Siemens: Key to have dialogue based on trust with EU about Alstom deal
description: Siemens  Chief Executive Joe Kaeser said on Monday it was important to have a dialogue based on trust with European Competition Commissioner Margrethe Vestager about a planned merger of Siemens' and Alstom's  rail businesses.

title: Oil edges up as investors latch on to OPEC cuts, supply outlook
description: Oil prices edged up on Monday, reversing earlier losses, as investors shrugged off data that confirmed China's economic growth is cooling and instead latched on to positive supply-side drivers for the market.

title: Trade worries sour CEOs' mood as leaders converge on Davos
description: Chief executives across the world have grown a lot more pessimistic about the global economic outlook due to trade disputes and tense relations between major powers, a survey showed on the eve of the World Economic Forum in Davos.

title: France, Germany step up pressure over Alstom-Siemens deal
description: France and Germany raised pressure on the European Union's competition chief to approve the merger of Alstom and Siemens' rail businesses, warning that thwarting the proposed European champion would be a strategic error.

title: SMBC urges jetmakers to erase production snags before raising output
description: The head of one of the world's largest aircraft leasing companies has told leading planemakers to "get their house in order" and wipe out manufacturing delays before pushing already record production rates to even higher levels.

title: Canadian railways ration space as commodity congestion problems worsen
description: Canada's two major railways are rationing space on trains traveling to the country's biggest port and recently prioritized some commodities over others to deal with congestion, the latest indication of their struggle to meet demand from new trade deals.

title: Japan firms wary of boosting investment amid intensifying trade war:  Reuters poll
description: Over a third of Japanese firms aim to raise capital expenditure in the fiscal year starting April, with many others worried about the impact on spending plans of a trade war between major markets China and the United States, a Reuters survey showed.

title: China's 2018 growth slows to 28-year low, more stimulus seen
description: China's economy cooled in the fourth quarter under pressure from faltering domestic demand and bruising U.S. tariffs, dragging  2018 growth to the lowest level in nearly three decades and pressuring Beijing to roll out more stimulus to avert a sharper slowdown.

title: France considers bill amendment to target Huawei: Les Echos
description: France is considering introducing a bill amendment to empower its security and defence watchdogs to make retroactive checks to telecoms operators' equipment once installed, targeting China's Huawei, Les Echos newspaper reported on Monday without citing sources.

title: IMF, CEOs sound warnings as leaders gather in Davos
description: The International Monetary Fund trimmed its global growth forecasts on Monday and a survey showed increasing pessimism among business chiefs as trade tensions and uncertainty loomed over the world's biggest annual gathering of the rich and powerful.

title: Apollo nears $3.8 billion-plus deal for packaging group RPC: WSJ
description: Private equity company Apollo Global Management  is in advanced talks to buy Europe's biggest plastics packaging maker RPC Group  for more than $3.8 billion, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday.

title: France fines Google $57 million for European privacy rule breach
description: France's data protection watchdog fined Alphabet's Google 50 million euros ($57 million) on Monday for breaching European Union online privacy rules, the biggest such penalty levied against a U.S. tech giant.

title: Global stock markets falter after China data confirms economic slowdown
description: European shares fell on Monday from six-week highs as a slowdown in China's economy stalled a global equity rally, but sterling rallied to the day's highs after Prime Minister Theresa May promised to be more "flexible" with lawmakers over Brexit.

title: Ex-Swiss banker convicted for selling secret tax data to Germany
description: A former UBS  banker accused of selling information about wealthy German tax evaders to German authorities was convicted of economic espionage by a Swiss court on Monday.

title: IMF fears trade war and weak Europe could trigger sharp global slowdown
description: The International Monetary Fund on Monday cut its world economic growth forecasts for 2019 and 2020 due to weakness in Europe and some emerging markets, and said failure to resolve trade tensions could further destabilize a slowing global economy.

title: Nissan's Ghosn offers to wear electronic ankle tag to get bail
description: Ousted Nissan Chairman Carlos Ghosn has offered to wear an electronic ankle tag and hire guards to monitor him in an unusual bid to secure his release on bail after two months of detention in Japan for alleged financial crimes.

title: Exclusive: Private equity firms circling Nestle's skin health business - sources
description: Private equity firms Cinven and Advent have teamed up to bid in an auction that could value Nestle's  skin health business at about 7 billion Swiss francs ($7 billion), three sources familiar with the matter said.

title: As outlook darkens, central banks think hard about their language
description: As central banks stock up on policy ammunition in the face of a worsening global economic outlook, they are having to reassess one of their most delicate weapons - the 'forward guidance' they use to flag their intentions to the markets.

title: Asset managers brace for more job cuts amid market turbulence
description: Turmoil on financial markets is expected to deepen layoffs and accelerate acquisitions in the fund management industry.

title: Tesla's Model 3 gets green light in Europe
description: Tesla's Model 3 has been given the green light to hit the road in Europe, clearing the final hurdle for the European introduction of the battery-powered sedan expected next month.

title: Sorrell's S4 Capital seeks more deals in digital-only drive
description: Martin Sorrell is on the lookout for acquisitions to expand his new advertising venture S4 Capital, aiming to capitalize on the disruption sweeping the industry by pursuing a pure-play digital strategy.

title: Small electric cars may be unaffordable for some: VW chairman to newspaper
description: The move to electric vehicles will make cars significantly more expensive, meaning they may become unaffordable for people on low incomes in the future, the chairman of Volkswagen  said in an interview published on Sunday.

title: Ghosn may have had questionable ethics, co-chair of external Nissan probe says
description: The co-chair of a committee set up by Japanese automaker Nissan Motor Co  to examine the root cause of alleged financial misconduct by ousted chairman Carlos Ghosn said he believed Ghosn may have had questionable ethical standards.

title: Italy regulator gives TIM's network separation plan thumbs down
description: Telecom Italia (TIM)  has suffered a setback in its plan to assuage pressures for a separation of its prized network assets by placing them into a wholly owned subsidiary, as the industry regulator said it was opposed to the proposal.

title: ProSieben sees pressure easing as Netflix raises prices
description: ProSiebenSat.1 Media believes that price increases by U.S. streaming giant Netflix could ease competitive pressures on the German group's core TV business and is bullish on growth at its e-commerce arm, CEO Max Conze said.

title: India's SBI says lenders awaiting SEBI decision on Etihad offer for Jet Airways: paper
description: The State Bank of India  (SBI)-led consortium of lenders is waiting for India’s capital markets regulator to decide on a bailout offer by Etihad Airways for the financially stressed Jet Airways , SBI Chairman Rajnish Kumar said, the Business Standard reported on Saturday.

title: China set to post slowest growth in 28 years in 2018, more stimulus seen
description: China is expected to report on Monday that economic growth cooled to its slowest in 28 years in 2018 amid weakening domestic demand and bruising U.S. tariffs, adding pressure on Beijing to roll out more support measures to avert a sharper slowdown.

title: Eurotunnel boss says a second referendum would still back Brexit
description: Britons would back Brexit again if asked to vote in a second referendum, the head of Eurotunnel said on Sunday.

title: Australian economy to be slowed, not sunk, by headwinds: Reuters poll
description: Analysts have trimmed forecasts for Australian economic growth following some disappointing numbers last year, but still tip solid outcomes ahead even in the face of falling house prices and a slowdown in China.

title: U.S. chipmakers may give clues on China hazard
description: Intel Corp  operates mostly outside the Apple-sphere, and that is exactly why whatever it says next week about business in its vital Chinese market matters so much for investors.

title: Exclusive: U.S. demands regular review of China trade reform
description: (This Jan 18 story was refiled to delete extraneous wording in paragraph 15)

title: Berkshire denies media report on accord to extract lithium
description: A unit of Berkshire Hathaway Inc denied a report on Sunday that it reached an agreement to allow extraction of lithium from its geothermal wells in California, a project that could offer U.S. carmakers and battery producers a secure supply of the metal.

title: China's survey-based jobless rate up to 4.9 percent in December
description: China's survey-based jobless rate was 4.9 percent at the end of December, the statistics bureau said on Monday, slightly up from 4.8 percent in November.

title: China December daily crude steel output at lowest since March
description: China's average daily steel output in December hit its lowest level since March, according to Reuters calculations based on official data, as producers cut output amid shrinking profit-margins.

title: Toyota, Panasonic setting up EV battery JV amid rising China competition: source
description: Toyota Motor Corp  and Panasonic Corp  are set to launch a joint venture next year to produce batteries for electric vehicles (EV) in an effort to compete with Chinese rivals, a source familiar with the matter said.

title: China's 2018 oil refinery output, December gas production hit records
description: Chinese oil refiners raised their output to a record in 2018, led by state-run oil majors which maximized operations on firm profit-margins and private refiners which increased processing after being granted higher crude import quotas.

title: China's December property investment slows in sign of fatigue for key GDP driver
description: Growth in property investment in China cooled to the second slowest pace in 2018 in December, adding to signs of a further slackening in the real estate market in a blow to a key driver economic growth.

title: China December coal output rises about 2 percent to highest in over three years
description: China's December coal output climbed 2.1 percent from the year before, government data showed, hitting the highest level in at least three years as major producers ramped up production amid robust winter demand and after the country started up new mines.

title: China's economy cools in fourth quarter, 2018 growth at 28-year low
description: China's economic growth cooled slightly in the fourth quarter from a year earlier as expected, weighed down by weak investment and faltering consumer confidence as Washington piled on trade pressure, leaving 2018 growth the weakest in 28 years.

title: China has ample room for macro policy support - statistics bureau chief
description: China has ample room for macro policy support, Ning Jizhe, head of the National Bureau of Statistics said on Monday, after the world's second-largest economy grew at the slowest pace since the global financial crisis in the fourth quarter of 2018.

title: China should boost banks' active support for economy: central bank official
description: Encouraging China's banks to actively increase support for the real economy, rather than relying on authorities' orders to boost lending, is the key to improving the supply of credit in the economy, a central bank official said on Monday.

title: China December aluminum production surges to record monthly high
description: China's primary aluminum output defied low prices to rise for a second straight month to a record high in December as falling alumina costs boosted margins, while 2018 annual output was also a record, official data showed on Monday.

title: Trump says deal 'could very well happen' with China
description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Saturday there has been progress toward a trade deal with China, but denied that he was considering lifting tariffs on Chinese imports.

title: Malaysia court rules in favor of Wynn Macau in $4.2 million case: lawyer
description: A Malaysian judge on Friday ruled in favor of Wynn Macau  in a case against a fund manager who owed the casino millions of dollars, the company's lawyer said, the first time a casino has been allowed to recover dues in the country.

title: Supermarket retailer Casino to sell six stores to rival Leclerc

description: Europe's top court opened the way to a $2 billion damages claim by U.S. delivery company UPS  on Wednesday by annulling a 2013 decision to stop it buying Dutch firm TNT Express.

title: Ford and IBM among quartet in Congo cobalt blockchain project
description: Carmaker Ford , technology giant IBM , South Korean cathode maker LG Chem  and China's Huayou Cobalt  have joined forces in the first blockchain project to monitor cobalt supplies from Democratic Republic of Congo.

title: Businesses cry out for Brexit clarity, warn of no-deal chaos
description: Business leaders in Britain and beyond warned on Wednesday of catastrophic job losses and chaos at ports if the country does not agree a European Union withdrawal, turning up the heat on politicians to deliver clarity.

title: Boeing-Lockheed's Vulcan rocket design 'nearly fully mature'
description: A joint venture between Boeing Co  and Lockheed Martin Corp  will conduct the final design review for its new flagship Vulcan rocket within months, it said on Wednesday, as the aerospace company heads for a showdown with Elon Musk's SpaceX and others in the launch services market.

title: In Papua New Guinea, Exxon's giant LNG project fuels frustration
description: From her red-roofed home near Papua New Guinea's capital of Port Moresby, Isabelle Dikana Iveiri overlooks a giant plant used by Exxon Mobil Corp to liquefy billions of dollars' worth of natural gas before it is shipped to Asian buyers.

title: Sears chairman prevails in bankruptcy auction for retailer with $5.2 billion bid: sources
description: Sears Holdings Corp Chairman Eddie Lampert prevailed in a bankruptcy auction for the U.S. department store chain with an improved takeover bid of roughly $5.2 billion, allowing the 126-year-old retailer to keep its doors open, people familiar with the matter said Wednesday.

title: Trump 'inclined' to impose new U.S. auto tariffs: senator
description: U.S. President Donald Trump is likely to move ahead with tariffs on imported vehicles, a move that could prompt the European Union to agree a new trade deal, said Senate Finance Committee Chairman Charles Grassley on Wednesday.

title: Hyundai, Kia issue new U.S. recall of 168,000 vehicles for fire risks
description: Hyundai Motor Co  and affiliate Kia Motors Corp  said on Wednesday they will recall about 168,000 U.S. vehicles at risk of fuel leaks, after recalling them in 2017 for engine fire risks, and will offer software upgrades for 3.7 million vehicles.

title: Upbeat bank earnings send Wall Street to one-month highs
description: Wall Street's major indexes hit one-month highs on Wednesday as strong earnings from Bank of America Corp  and Goldman Sachs Group Inc  boosted investor sentiment.

title: Global auto leaders urge Trump administration to end trade turmoil
description: Auto executives gathered in Detroit on Monday called on the Trump administration and Congress to resolve trade disputes, and end the government shutdown, saying political uncertainty is costing the industry.

title: Apple plans some hiring reductions after selling fewer iPhones: Bloomberg
description: Apple Inc will cut back on hiring for some divisions after lower-than-expected iPhone sales and missing its revenue forecast for the holiday quarter, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday, citing sources familiar with the matter.

title: Airbus spends $300 million on new Alabama plant for A220 jet
description: Airbus SE expanded its industrial presence in the United States on Wednesday, starting construction on a new assembly plant for the Canadian developed A220 jetliner, 18 months after agreeing to buy the plane in the midst of a U.S.-Ottawa trade dispute.

title: Sterling up after May wins confidence vote; stocks climb
description: Major world stock indexes rose on Wednesday, with the S&P 500 supported by sharply higher U.S. bank shares after strong earnings, while the pound was up after British Prime Minister Theresa May's government won a confidence vote in parliament.

title: S&P cuts rating on PG&E unit in third such cut this month
description: S&P cut its rating on PG&E Corp's  Pacific Gas & Electric Co unit on Wednesday, making it the third such cut this month, after the unit missed interest payments on its 2040 senior notes.

title: Embraer warns of little or no profit in next two years
description: Brazilian planemaker Embraer SA  said on Wednesday it expects to keep $1 billion in cash after paying off all of its debt once a proposed $4.2 billion deal with Boeing Co  closes, although it warned of little or no profit in the next two years.

title: Airbus says ministers signal optimism Britain will avoid 'no-deal Brexit'
description: The chief executive of European planemaker Airbus said on Wednesday British ministers had expressed a "certain degree of optimism" that Britain would not leave the European Union without a transition deal.

title: Bombardier CEO sees decision on loss-making CRJ jet this year
description: Bombardier Inc  aims to make a decision this year on the future of its CRJ regional jet as it "aggressively" pursues new orders to secure its industrial future, the Canadian planemaker's chief executive said on Wednesday.

title: French government calls for Renault board meeting to replace Ghosn
description: French Finance Minister Bruno Le Maire said on Wednesday the government had requested a Renault  board meeting in coming days to replace the company's scandal-hit Chairman and Chief Executive Carlos Ghosn.

title: Oil gains with Wall Street, but rising U.S. fuel stocks weigh
description: Oil prices edged higher on Wednesday, buoyed by a U.S. equity market rally and a supply cut agreement by OPEC+, but gains were limited by data showing growing U.S. refined product inventories and record crude production.

title: Snap shares hit by second CFO exit in a year
description: Shares of Snap Inc fell 9 percent in early trading on Wednesday after Tim Stone became the second finance chief to leave the Snapchat operator in a year since a much-criticized redesign.

title: IAC sues Tinder co-founder, escalating fight over valuation
description: Online dating company Match Group Inc  and its parent company IAC/InterActiveCorp  have filed a lawsuit against Sean Rad, a co-founder of Match Group's popular dating service Tinder, of secretly copying company files and other proprietary information.

title: Yelp investor SQN says shares could surge to $55-$65
description: SQN Investors LP said on Wednesday Yelp Inc's shares could surge to between $55 and $65, up to 80 percent above its current price, if the customer review company appoints new board members and considers selling itself.

title: Goldman dealmakers shine in Solomon's maiden quarter
description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc  turned in a better-than-expected profit during David Solomon's first quarter at the helm, helped by dealmakers in the division the new chief executive once oversaw.

title: Exclusive: ADM CEO says wrong time for 'monster' acquisitions
description: U.S. grain merchant Archer Daniels Midland Co (ADM) has looked at buying rivals including Bunge Ltd. and dozens of other companies but decided the time is not right for "monster" acquisitions, the company's chief executive told Reuters.

title: U.S. automakers push for deal on fuel efficiency rules
description: Executives at the major U.S. automakers are pressing the Trump administration and California to agree on standards for fuel efficiency and carbon emissions through 2025, as risks increase that a deadline for setting national standards will pass without a deal.

title: U.S. investigating Huawei for alleged trade secret theft: WSJ
description: Federal prosecutors are investigating Huawei Technologies[HWT.UL], the world's largest telecommunications equipment maker, for allegedly stealing trade secrets from U.S. businesses and could soon issue an indictment, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday.

title: French court cancels Monsanto weedkiller permit on safety grounds
description: A French court canceled the license for one of Monsanto's glyphosate-based weedkillers on Tuesday over safety concerns, placing an immediate ban on Roundup Pro 360 in the latest legal blow to the Bayer-owned business.

title: Brighter future for sterling seen if no-deal Brexit is averted
description: Britain's plans to leave the European Union could be thrown into disarray by a vote in parliament later on Tuesday but bets are mounting that a chaotic no-deal Brexit can be avoided and that sterling will rise from here.

title: Walmart opts to leave CVS partnerships over pricing dispute
description: CVS Health Corp  said on Tuesday Walmart Inc  is leaving its network for commercial and Medicaid prescription drug plans after the two companies failed to agree on pricing.

title: Weak U.S. producer prices support tame inflation picture
description: U.S. producer prices dropped by the most in more than two years in December as the cost of energy products and trade services fell, adding to signs of tame inflation that may allow the Federal Reserve to be patient about raising interest rates this year.

title: UnitedHealth profit beats expectations, shares rise
description: UnitedHealth Group Inc , the largest U.S. health insurer, beat Wall Street estimates for fourth-quarter profit on Tuesday, driven largely by growth in its Optum services business, including its pharmacy benefits unit.

title: Ex-Barclays trio 'cheated global financial system', Euribor trial told
description: Three former Barclays  bankers cheated the global financial system to gain an unfair edge over counterparties in a five-year plot to rig Euribor interest rates, a London prosecutor alleged on Tuesday.

title: Apollo Global nears deal to buy Arconic for more than $10 billion: WSJ
description: Apollo Global Management LLC  is nearing a deal to buy U.S. aluminum products maker Arconic Inc  for more than $10 billion, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday.

title: Exclusive: Jana liquidates two hedge funds, to focus only on activism
description: Jana Partners LLC, founded by Barry Rosenstein, is shutting down two stock-picking hedge funds following losses and will focus instead on its main strategy of investing in a handful of companies and pushing management to improve their performance.

title: Airbnb says profitable for two straight years amid IPO talks
description: Home-renting company Airbnb Inc said on Tuesday it was profitable on an adjusted basis for the second year in a row,  ahead of a widely anticipated initial public offering this year.

title: Fiat Chrysler looking at options to plug hole in its truck lineup: CEO
description: Fiat Chrysler Automobiles NV  Chief Executive Mike Manley told Reuters on Tuesday he is open to partnerships to develop a new midsize pickup truck the automaker could sell in Latin America and other markets outside the United States to compete with models such as Ford Motor Co's  Thailand-built Ranger.

title: Corporate investors pile into electric vehicle startups
description: (This Jan. 11 story corrects second to last paragraph to reflect that Tencent, and not Geely, is an investor in WM Motor)

title: Facebook to invest $300 million to help local news survive
description: Facebook Inc  will invest $300 million over three years in local news globally as it faces blistering criticism over its role in the erosion of the news business worldwide.

title: PG&E restructuring highlights arcane California legal rule
description: PG&E Corp's chances of emerging from bankruptcy proceedings hinge in part on an arcane California legal rule that threatens to keep the utility owner perpetually on the hook for liabilities from catastrophic wildfires even beyond the more than $30 billion the company expects to face from recent blazes.

title: Factbox: Corporate investments in EV startups
description: Corporations across a variety of industries - auto, energy, electronics, aerospace, telecom - have invested in startup companies engaged in various aspects of automotive electrification, including batteries, charging devices and complete vehicles.

title: Petrobras board nominee fined in 2016 for insider trading: documents
description: One of three new board members nominated by Brazil's government to sit on the board of state-run oil company Petroleo Brasileiro SA  was fined in 2016 by securities regulator CVM for insider trading, according to CVM documents on the ruling seen by Reuters.

title: U.S. holiday shoppers spend record $126 billion online: Adobe
description: U.S. shoppers spent a record $126 billion on online shopping during the 2018 holiday season, taking advantage of early discounts on Amazon.com  and other websites and with more people using smartphones to place their orders, Adobe Analytics said on Tuesday.

title: UnitedHealth says performing better than first-quarter consensus estimate suggests
description: UnitedHealth Group Inc  is performing better in 2019 than suggested by the Wall Street analyst consensus for first-quarter adjusted earnings, Chief Financial Officer John Rex said on Tuesday during a conference call with investors.

title: German court throws out Qualcomm's latest patent case against Apple
description: A patent lawsuit filed by Qualcomm Inc against Apple Inc was thrown out by a German court on Tuesday, in a reversal for the U.S. chipmaker after it won a recent court ban on the sale of some iPhones in the country.

title: No clear path for California as massive PG&E utility nears bankruptcy
description: PG&E Corp's announcement that it will file for bankruptcy, citing massive potential liability from deadly wildfires, puts California politicians in quandary, whether to offer a bailout or risk allowing the state's largest private utility to fail.

title: Rothschild vice chairman resigns from PG&E board
description: Struggling California power company PG&E Corp said on Tuesday Roger Kimmel, vice chairman of investment banking firm Rothschild Inc, had resigned from company's board.

description: While growing up in Seattle, Enrique Rico's mom cleaned the posh homes of Microsoft employees. When Rico tagged along on sick days from school, he dreamed of having the life of a technology worker.

title: First U.S. crude cargoes head to China since trade breakthrough: sources
description: Three cargoes of U.S. crude are heading to China from the U.S. Gulf Coast, trade sources said on Monday, the first departures since late September and a 90-day pause in the two countries' trade war that began last month.

title: China signals more stimulus as economic slowdown deepens
description: China on Tuesday signaled more stimulus measures in the near term as a tariff war with the United States took a heavy toll on its trade sector and raised the risk of a sharper economic slowdown.

title: UK gambling stocks drop after U.S. DOJ reverses opinion on internet betting
description: Shares of British betting companies, which have been pushing into the United States market because of tighter regulations at home, fell after the U.S. Department of Justice called for wider restrictions on all gambling on the internet.

title: Drug companies greet 2019 with U.S. price hikes
description: Drugmakers kicked off 2019 with price increases in the United States on more than 250 prescription drugs, including the world's top-selling medicine, Humira, although the pace of price hikes was slower than last year.

description: U.S. authorities on Tuesday charged a suspected Ukrainian computer hacker and several traders with scheming to trade on market-moving corporate earnings news stolen from a U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission database.

description: PG&E Corp  bonds and shares plummeted after the California power company failed to make a $21.6 million interest payment due Tuesday on its 2040 senior notes, as it planned to seek Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection.

description: Corruption-ensnared Odebrecht SA [ODBES.UL] has proposed that creditors take over its sugar and ethanol unit, Atvos Agroindustrial Participacoes SA, in exchange for reducing Odebrecht's huge debt load, according to two sources with knowledge of the matter.

title: JPMorgan misses fourth-quarter profit estimates as bond trading slumps
description: JPMorgan Chase & Co  missed profit estimates for the fourth quarter as a slump in bond trading revenue overpowered strong consumer loan growth and record revenues.

title: Tokyo court denies Nissan Ghosn's latest bail request
description: The Tokyo District Court on Tuesday denied former Nissan Motor Co Ltd Chairman Carlos Ghosn's request for release on bail after his indictment last week on two new charges, making it likely the once-feted executive remains jailed for months.

title: Sears chairman's takeover proposal faces moment of truth
description: Negotiations between Sears Holdings Corp Chairman Eddie Lampert and the bankrupt U.S. department store operator approached a resolution late on Tuesday as the billionaire hedge fund manager faced the choice of improving his $5 billion offer for the company or ending his takeover plans, people familiar with the matter told Reuters.

title: Best U.S. fund managers of '18 buying healthcare, pot stocks as market wobbles
description: The top-performing U.S. growth fund managers of the last year are taking the recent slide in the U.S. stock market to add to their bets in companies they expect will continue to expand regardless of the direction of the overall economy.

title: Verizon deepens ties with Apple, offers free Apple Music to some U.S. customers
description: Verizon Communications Inc  said on Tuesday it will include free Apple Music subscriptions in some of its top-tier U.S. data plans, deepening its ties with the iPhone maker.

title: USTR promises exclusion process for higher tariffs if China talks fail
description: U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer has assured lawmakers that companies will be able to request exclusions on tariffs on $200 billion worth of goods under discussion with Beijing if talks do not yield a deal by the March 2 deadline.

title: Industry must rein in spend on electric, self-driving cars: Magna CEO
description: Global automobile and auto parts makers which want to capitalize on electric and autonomous vehicles need to cut back investments and forge more partnerships instead, the chief executive of global parts supplier Magna International said Tuesday.

title: Snap CFO Tim Stone to resign, shares drop 8 percent
description: Chief Financial Officer Tim Stone will be leaving Snap Inc  less than a year after taking the job, the company said on Tuesday, the latest in a string of executive departures from Snap over the past year.

description: Delta Air Lines Inc  and United Airlines  kicked off fourth-quarter earnings reporting for the sector on Tuesday with profits that beat Wall Street expectations, but the rippling effects of a government shutdown could take a toll on the current quarter and beyond.

title: France seeks Renault board meeting to replace Ghosn: sources
description: The French government is moving to dismiss Renault's  scandal-hit Chairman and Chief Executive Carlos Ghosn and has requested a board meeting to consider candidates to replace him, sources with knowledge of the matter told Reuters.

description: Netflix Inc  is raising monthly fees for its U.S. subscribers by between 13 percent and 18 percent, the video streaming pioneer's first price increase since 2017 as it spends heavily on original content and international expansion.

description: Wells Fargo & Co's loan book shrank and revenue fell across all its major businesses last quarter, as the fourth-largest U.S. lender continued to work through the consequences of wayward sales practices at its consumer bank.

description: A former senior managing director of a firm that advises companies on shareholder votes was convicted on Tuesday of participating in a scheme to bribe a proxy adviser's employee with sports and concert tickets to learn how its investor clients were voting.

title: Ralph Winter office to invest $300 million in Medici U.S. shared housing
description: Medici Living Group said on Tuesday the family office of German real estate investor Ralph Winter has agreed to invest $300 million over three years to develop 1,300 U.S. units of Medici's Quarters brand of shared housing for young professionals.

title: VW, Ford team up on trucks, eye deals on EVs, self-driving cars
description: Volkswagen AG  and Ford Motor Co  said on Tuesday they will join forces on commercial vans and pickups and are exploring joint development of electric and self-driving technology, actions meant to save the automakers billions of dollars.

title: Stocks rise on China hopes; sterling rebounds as Brexit vote fails
description: Major world stock markets climbed on Tuesday on hopes of more stimulus for China's economy, while sterling rebounded from the day's lows after British lawmakers defeated Prime Minister Theresa May's deal on withdrawing from the European Union.

title: Shoe retailer Payless to explore options, including sale: sources
description: U.S. discount retailer Payless ShoeSource Inc has hired an adviser to help evaluate strategic alternatives, including a sale or restructuring, less than 18 months after it emerged from bankruptcy, people familiar with the matter said on Tuesday.

title: Oil rises about 3 percent on economic stability hopes
description: Oil prices rose about 3 percent on Tuesday, along with world stock markets, supported by China's plan to introduce policies to stabilize a slowing economy, reversing the previous session's losses due to grim data in the world's second-largest economy.

title: White House considering former PepsiCo CEO, Treasury official to lead World Bank: source
description: The White House is considering former PepsiCo Inc  Chief Executive Indra Nooyi, Treasury Department official David Malpass and Overseas Private Investment Corp CEO Ray Washburne among candidates to head the World Bank, an administration official said on Tuesday.

description: Drugstore chain Walgreens Boots Alliance Inc and Microsoft Corp said on Tuesday they have entered a seven-year agreement to research and develop new methods of delivering healthcare services through digital devices.

title: Citi says chance of delay to Brexit now 'very high'
description: U.S. investment bank Citi  said on Tuesday there is now a "very high" chance that Brexit will be delayed past March 29, after lawmakers defeated Prime Minister Theresa May's Brexit divorce deal by a crushing margin.

title: United profit beats forecasts as new flights from hubs pay off
description: United Airlines on Tuesday reported a fourth-quarter profit that easily beat Wall Street forecasts, sending shares higher, as the No. 3 U.S. carrier scheduled more flights out of its hubs and won back customers after a series of public relations disasters.

description: PG&E Corp's shares and bonds fell sharply for a second day on Tuesday, as a failure to make interest payments by the California power utility added to investor nerves following the company's plans to seek Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection.

title: Netflix, China boost Wall Street as investors shrug off Brexit vote
description: U.S. stocks rose on Tuesday as technology and internet stocks gained on Netflix Inc's  plans to raise fees for U.S. subscribers and hopes of more stimulus for China's slowing economy fostered a risk-on mood among investors.

title: Brazil government nominates three new Petrobras board members amid accusations of meddling
description: Brazil's government on Monday nominated three new board members for state-owned oil company Petroleo Brasileiro SA  (Petrobras), amid accusations that new CEO Roberto Castello Branco was pushing to oust board members.

title: FedEx pays $35.4 million to end NY lawsuit over illegal cigarettes
description: FedEx Corp will pay $35.4 million to settle three lawsuits in which New York state and New York City accused the company of shipping millions of untaxed cigarettes to residents over a decade.

description: President Donald Trump on Monday predicted the United States would reach a deal with China to end a tit-for-tat trade war, saying Beijing wants to negotiate and that talks are going well.

description: China's Huawei Technologies [HWT.UL], the leading global supplier of telecoms network equipment, faces questions over its access to European markets after the arrest of a sales executive in Poland on suspicion of spying.

description: The U.S. Federal Reserve is wary of giving "fintech" firms such as OnDeck Capital Inc  or Kabbage Inc. access to the country's financial infrastructure, putting the central bank at odds with other regulators looking to bring them into the fold.

description: PG&E Corp  is in discussions with investment banks about a multibillion-dollar financing package to help navigate bankruptcy proceedings, a sign that Chapter 11 filing preparations are intensifying in the wake of potentially staggering liabilities from deadly wildfires, sources said on Sunday.

description: China's exports unexpectedly fell the most in two years in December, while imports also contracted, pointing to further weakness in the world's second-largest economy in 2019 and deteriorating global demand.

title: Former Nissan boss Ghosn suffers 'harsh' treatment in jail: wife
description: The wife of ousted Nissan Motor Co Ltd  chairman Carlos Ghosn has urged New York-based Human Rights Watch to draw attention to his "harsh treatment" during detention in a Japanese jail, a letter seen by Reuters showed on Sunday.

title: Key dates in the investigation of Nissan ex-Chairman Ghosn
description: Ousted Nissan Motor Co Ltd  Chairman Carlos Ghosn was indicted on two additional charges of financial misconduct on Friday, bringing the number of charges against him to three.

title: Saudi Arabia plans $2 billion solar and carbon black complex: official
description: Saudi Arabia plans to develop a $2 billion solar and carbon black integrated complex in partnership with China’s Longi and South Korea’s OCI, a Saudi official said.

title: Embraer says cash position from Boeing deal still to be determined
description: Brazilian planemaker Embraer said in a securities filing on Monday that its cash boost from a potential sale of 80 percent of its commercial aviation business to Boeing is still to be determined.

title: CapitaLand bets on new markets with $4.4 billion Temasek real estate deal
description: Singapore's CapitaLand  is forking out S$6 billion  ($4.4 billion) to scoop up logistics and industrial assets from state investor Temasek, in a deal the developer said would create Asia's largest real estate investment manager.

title: China says biggest trade worries this year are external uncertainty, protectionism
description: China's customs said on Monday that the biggest worry in trade this year is external uncertainty and protectionism, forecasting the country's trade growth may slow in 2019.

title: China's 2018 trade surplus with U.S. highest on record going back to 2006
description: China's trade surplus with the United States rose to $323.32 billion last year, the highest on record going back to 2006, Reuters calculations based on customs data showed on Monday.

title: China car sales hit reverse for first time since 1990s
description: Car makers in China will face more fierce competition this year, after a tough 2018 when the world's biggest auto market contracted for the first time in more than two decades, the country's top auto industry association said on Monday.

title: Japan's Okada asks Manila bourse to block listing of Universal's unit
description: Pachinko tycoon Kazuo Okada has asked the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) to block the proposed listing of Universal Entertainment Corp's  domestic unit, saying the Japanese gaming company has no authority to proceed with the plan.

title: HSBC settles forex deals worth $250 billion on blockchain in last year

title: Wells Fargo settles SEC lawsuit over Curt Schilling's 38 Studios
description: Wells Fargo & Co  agreed to settle a U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission fraud lawsuit related to a $75 million bond offering for 38 Studios Inc, a now-bankrupt video game company founded by former All-Star major league baseball pitcher Curt Schilling.

title: Pernod Ricard to meet activist Elliott ahead of earnings update: sources
description: Pernod Ricard  will meet activist hedge fund Elliott this month as the family-backed spirits firm faces pressure to improve its margins, sources familiar with the situation said.

description: Newspaper chain MNG Enterprises Inc , controlled by secretive hedge fund Alden Global Capital LLC, on Monday offered to buy Gannett Co Inc  in a $1.36 billion deal to add the USA Today and scores of other newspapers to its stable of regional publications.

description: Regulators in the U.S. state of Alaska will investigate all of the oil and natural gas wells operated by BP Plc at its Prudhoe Bay oil field after the release of a small amount of crude oil and gas from a well that had earlier been shut.

description: World stock indexes fell on Monday after a surprise contraction in Chinese trade reignited fears of a sharper slowdown in global growth and caused investors to sell riskier assets.

description: U.S. stocks declined on Monday as an unexpected drop in China's exports reignited worries of a global economic slowdown and prompted caution among investors as the corporate earnings season kicked off.

description: Europe's Airbus is ratcheting up pressure on suppliers like United Technologies to cut costs for its Canadian-developed A220 jetliner as it expands factory facilities to cope with anticipated demand for the former Bombardier model.

title: Air Canada would study Airbus, Boeing for transatlantic narrowbody needs
description: Air Canada is interested in further developing the use of narrowbody aircraft to serve the transatlantic market and would look at both Airbus and Boeing models, a senior executive said.

description: Nissan  expects alliance partner Renault's  board to back its ousting of Chairman Carlos Ghosn once it sees evidence from the Japanese carmaker's investigation, Chief Executive Hiroto Saikawa said in a Monday newspaper interview.
