description: Germany's Federal Motor Transport Authority (KBA) is considering recalling more Volkswagen  cars due to its emissions, scandal, the Bild am Sonntag newspaper reported on Sunday.

title: DP World signs acquisition agreement for Chile port operator
description: Major port operator DP World  said on Sunday it had agreed to acquire a 71.3 percent stake in Chile's Puertos y Logistica (Pulogsa)  from Minera Valparaiso and other shareholders associated with the Matte Group.

title: Huawei sacks employee arrested in Poland on spying charges
description: Chinese telecommunications equipment maker Huawei  said on Saturday it had sacked an employee arrested in Poland on spying charges in a case that could intensify Western security concerns about the company.

title: Saudi energy minister says no need for extraordinary OPEC meeting before April
description: Saudi Energy Minister Khalid al-Falih said on Sunday in Abu Dhabi he saw no need for an extraordinary meeting of the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries before April.

title: Saudi energy minister says oil market on 'right track'
description: Saudi Arabia's Energy Minister Khalid al-Falih said on Sunday  the oil market is "on the right track" and will quickly return to balance, but oil producers are willing to do more if needed.

title: Bank of China to enable payment in yuan on U.S. e-commerce platforms: Xinhua
description: Bank of China's New York branch will enable Chinese firms to receive payment in yuan rather than dollars from their sales on U.S. e-commerce platforms this year, the official Xinhua news agency reported on Sunday.

title: Israel drone maker Aeronautics gets $232 million buyout offer
description: Israel's state-owned Rafael Advanced Defense Systems and businessman Avihai Stolero have offered to buy unmanned aerial vehicle maker Aeronautics  for 850 million shekels ($232 million).

title: Saudi Aramco's bond will probably be in 10 billion range: energy minister
description: Saudi Aramco will issue bonds which will probably be in the 10 billion range, Saudi Arabia's energy minister said on Sunday.

title: German antitrust body opposes Siemens-Alstom merger: report
description: Germany's antitrust authority has expressed concerns to the European Union's competition watchdog about the planned merger of the rail operations of Siemens  and France's Alstom , a newspaper reported on Sunday.

title: Chinese FDI into North America, Europe falls 73 percent in 2018: report
description: Chinese foreign direct investment into North America and Europe fell by 73 percent to a six-year low last year as the United States tightened scrutiny of deals and Chinese restrictions on outbound investment bit, law firm Baker & McKenzie said.

title: German railway to propose sale of Arriva subsidiary: source
description: German rail operator Deutsche Bahn wants to sell its Arriva international subsidiary to plug a 4 billion euro ($4.6 billion) financing gap, though Britain's looming exit from the European Union is making it hard to value the business, a source close to the plans told Reuters on Sunday.

title: Renault-Nissan's Ghosn received 7 million euros from Dutch JV: Les Echos
description: Ousted Renault-Nissan alliance chairman Carlos Ghosn was paid 7 million euros ($8 million) through a Dutch joint venture between Nissan and Mitsubishi, French financial daily Les Echos reported on its website on Sunday.

title: CEO exits as PG&E faces fire liabilities, bankruptcy preparations
description: PG&E Corp  Chief Executive Geisha Williams has stepped down, the company said on Sunday, as pressure from potentially crushing liabilities linked to catastrophic wildfires have pushed the California utility owner to the financial brink and prompted it to make bankruptcy preparations.

title: U.S. warns German companies of possible sanctions over Russian pipeline
description: The United States has warned German companies involved in the Russian-led Nord Stream 2 gas pipeline that they could face sanctions if they stick with the project.

title: Samsung to launch India-first smartphones to counter Chinese rivals
description: Samsung  plans to launch a budget smartphone series in India ahead of a global release, aiming to regain ground ceded to Chinese rivals such as Xiaomi  in the world's second-biggest mobile phone market.

title: Nissan expands Ghosn probe to more countries, executive Munoz under scrutiny: sources
description: Nissan Motor Co Ltd  has broadened its investigation into ousted chairman Carlos Ghosn to include dealings that took place in the United States, India and Latin America, three people with knowledge of the inquiry said.

title: SpaceX to lay off 10 percent of workforce
description: Elon Musk's rocket company SpaceX will reduce its workforce by about 10 percent of the company's more than 6,000 employees, it said on Friday.

title: OPEC is not the enemy of the U.S., UAE energy minister says
description: Oil producer group OPEC is not the enemy of the United States, United Arab Emirates Energy Minister Suhail al-Mazrouei said on Saturday in Abu Dhabi.

title: India's online sellers to appeal against competition commission's Flipkart ruling
description: A group representing online sellers in India will appeal against the Competition Commision of India's (CCI's) ruling in favour of Walmart-owned Flipkart, the group's lawyer Chanakya Basa said in a release on Saturday.

title: China's premier says tax cuts support employment, economic stability
description: China's plans for tax cuts targeting smaller companies will help to support employment and economic stability, and will expand the country's tax base over the long term, Premier Li Keqiang was quoted as saying on Saturday.

title: Nissan top executive Munoz resigns amid broadened Ghosn probe
description: One of Nissan Motor Co's  top executives has resigned, further rattling the Japanese automaker's management team as it broadens an investigation into ousted Chairman Carlos Ghosn's alleged financial misconduct.

title: Impact of 'Yellow Vests' protests on French and European companies
description: The "yellow vests" movement - named after the fluorescent jackets French motorists have to carry in their vehicles - started in mid-November as a protest against a fuel tax but has since grown into a broader backlash against President Emmanuel Macron's government.

title: France's 'yellow vest' protests could shake up euro zone bond markets
description: France's response to "yellow vest" protests could be a turning point for euro zone bond markets if it kicks off an era of increased public borrowing in the bloc and loads additional debt on to a market already nervous over the removal of ECB stimulus.

title: Nissan ex-chief Ghosn seeks bail after indictment on two new charges
description: Nissan ex-Chairman Carlos Ghosn has requested his release on bail after being indicted in Tokyo on Friday on two new charges, his lawyers said, as the once-feted auto executive awaits a lengthy criminal trial that could be as long as six months away.

title: China retailers slash iPhone prices after Apple sales warning
description: Several Chinese electronics retailers including Alibaba-backed Suning  and JD.com  have slashed iPhone prices this week, after Apple  recently blamed poor sales of the smartphone in the country for a rare revenue warning.

title: As world economy stumbles into 2019, eyes turn to China
description: Ten years after China helped stave off the threat of a global depression with a huge stimulus plan, investors are looking once again toward Beijing as the world economy heads for a slowdown, or worse, in 2019.

title: Timeline: Debt-laden Jet Airways' rocky ride
description: Jet Airways Ltd , India's biggest full-service carrier, has been under dark clouds for the most part of the past year, and several efforts are on to save the sinking airline.

title: Exclusive: Lessors to India's troubled Jet Airways consider taking back planes -sources
description: Crisis talks between India's cash-strapped Jet Airways Ltd  and aircraft lessors have failed to ease a row over late payments, prompting some lessors to explore taking back aircraft, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters.

title: After Monsanto patent ruling, Indian farmers hope for next-gen GM seeds
description: Monsanto's victory this week in a patent case in India regarding genetically modified (GM) cotton seeds has raised hopes among farmers that the company will now launch its next-generation seeds.

title: Volkswagen delivered 10.8 million vehicles in 2018, eyes world No.1 spot
description: Volkswagen Group's  deliveries rose 0.9 percent to a record 10.83 million last year, the German company said on Friday, putting it neck-and-neck with Renault-Nissan-Mitsubishi in the race to be the world's biggest vehicle manufacturer.

title: Geely cuts its Daimler stake by more than half: Bloomberg
description: Chinese billionaire Li Shufu's Geely Group cut its 9.7 percent stake in carmaker Daimler AG  by more than half, Bloomberg reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.

title: Exclusive: GM's Cadillac will introduce EV in fight against Tesla - sources
description: Cadillac is expected to become General Motors Co's  lead electric vehicle brand as the largest U.S. automaker gears up to introduce a new model under that luxury marquee to challenge Tesla Inc , two people briefed on the matter said Thursday.

title: BMW says group sales up 1.1 percent in 2018
description: BMW's  group sales went up 1.1 percent worldwide in 2018 to 2,490,664 vehicles, the company said on Friday, adding that it expected a slight increase this year despite challenging market conditions.

title: China's Geely says it has not sold Daimler shares, denies Bloomberg report
description: China's Geely Group [GEELY.UL] said it has not sold any shares in Daimler AG , denying a Bloomberg report that the Chinese firm had slashed its 9.7 percent stake in the German carmaker by more than half.

title: Exclusive: China to set lower GDP growth target of 6-6.5 percent in 2019 - sources
description: China plans to set a lower economic growth target of 6-6.5 percent in 2019 compared with last year's target of "around" 6.5 percent, policy sources told Reuters, as Beijing gears up to cope with higher U.S. tariffs and weakening domestic demand.

title: China banks' bad loan ratio climbs to 10-year high at end-2018
description: Chinese commercial banks' non-performing loan (NPL) ratio hit a 10-year high of 1.89 percent at the end of last year amid an economic slowdown, an official with the country's banking regulator said on Friday.

title: China's Wanda files for U.S. IPO of sports unit to raise up to $500 million: sources
description: Chinese conglomerate Dalian Wanda Group has filed confidentially for a U.S. initial public offering of its sports unit that could fetch up to $500 million, according to sources with direct knowledge of the matter.

title: Indonesia's plans to regulate ride-hailing rates threaten Grab, Go-Jek models
description: Indonesia is preparing to launch regulations fixing the rates drivers and riders for ride-hailing services such as Grab and Go-Jek receive, two government officials said this week, creating potential obstacles for the companies' expansion.

title: How Santander's Brazil unit is driving growth with car loans
description: At BM Multimarcas, a used-car dealer on the outskirts of Sao Paulo, owner Santel de Abreu Bernardo can show you jalopies that most big banks would not touch.

title: China and slow growth may keep the punchbowl brimming
description: It was meant to be the first year in nearly a decade that the world's central banks took more cash out of markets than they pumped in. Instead, China -- and slowing growth elsewhere -- may ensure yet another year of positive liquidity flows.

title: Nissan cancels lease on Ghosn's Tokyo apartment
description: Nissan Motor Co Ltd  has terminated the lease to ex-Chairman Carlos Ghosn's luxury apartment in Tokyo, Ghosn's legal team said on Friday, as the Japanese automaker cuts ties with the executive following his arrest in November.

title: Exclusive: Goldman Sachs on course to launch cash management in mid-2020
description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc  is considering paying big multinational corporations more for their deposits than other banks as it paves the way for its entry into a mundane but prized business: managing cash.

title: Autostrade executives guilty of manslaughter in 2013 motorway accident, CEO acquitted
description: Three managers at Autostrade per l'Italia, and three former managers, were found guilty of manslaughter on Friday over the deaths of 40 people in a 2013 accident on one of the company's motorways, while CEO Giovanni Castellucci was acquitted.

title: Ford plans to cut 1,150 jobs in Britain, Unite union says
description: U.S. carmaker Ford  plans to cut 1,150 jobs in Britain, the Unite union said on Friday, with nearly 1,000 job losses at its  Bridgend engine plant in Wales.

title: GE unit wins $450 million U.S. defense contract: Pentagon
description: GE Medical Systems Information Technologies Inc, a unit of General Electric Co, has been awarded a $450 million U.S. defense contract for patient monitoring systems, accessories and training, the Pentagon said on Friday.

title: Cheaper gasoline weighs on U.S. consumer prices in December
description: U.S. consumer prices fell for the first time in nine months in December amid a plunge in gasoline prices, but underlying inflation pressures remained firm as rental housing and healthcare costs rose steadily.

title: Apple considered Samsung, MediaTek to supply 5G modems for 2019 iPhones
description: Apple Inc  held talks with Samsung Electronics Co Ltd  and MediaTek Inc  along with existing vendor Intel Corp  to supply 5G modem chips for 2019 iPhones, according to an Apple executive's testimony at a trial between Qualcomm Inc  and the U.S. Federal Trade Commission on Friday.

title: Pemex's New York roadshow spooks investors, yields spike
description: Yields on the debt of Mexican state-run oil company Pemex rose sharply this week after the company failed during presentations in New York to lay out a clear plan to reduce debt and increase output, analysts said.

title: U.S. shutdown sends grain traders, farmers hunting for data
description: When the U.S. Department of Agriculture announced last week that a slew of key farm reports would not be released on Friday due to the partial government shutdown, the phones at crop forecaster Gro Intelligence blew up.

title: Apple demanded $1 billion for chance to win iPhone: Qualcomm CEO
description: Qualcomm sought to become the sole supplier of modem chips for Apple's iPhone to recoup a $1-billion "incentive payment" that Apple insisted on, not to block rivals from the market, Qualcomm's chief executive testified on Friday.

title: Slashed profit expectations may set stage for gains
description: There could well be a silver lining in all the caution around the stock market as the earnings season approaches: Shares do way better when profit expectations have fallen, and lately, they've been falling like a rock.

title: Fox says no plans to bid for sports networks Disney may sell
description: Fox Chairman Lachlan Murdoch said in November it was still an "open question" whether the company will buy back the regional sports networks it sold to Disney  in July as part of the $71 billion deal.

title: Wall Street's five-day rally flickers out as earnings near
description: Wall Street dipped slightly on Friday, breaking a five-session rally, as energy shares declined and investors looked ahead to earnings season, which kicks off next week with Citigroup, JPMorgan and other big banks.

title: Disney CEO stock award worth as much as $149.6 million in 2018
description: Walt Disney Co  Chief Executive Officer Robert Iger earned stock grants worth as much as $149.6 million in 2018, including awards related to Disney's purchase of film and television assets from Twenty-First Century Fox , according to a regulatory filing http://bit.ly/2D5dNjy on Friday.

title: Huawei Canada executive leaves post as scrutiny of company grows
description: One of Huawei Canada's top executives on Friday disclosed he was leaving his post after more than seven years with the Chinese telecommunications equipment maker, which is facing heightened scrutiny over security issues from Canada and its allies.

title: U.S. stocks pause after five-day rally; dollar rebounds
description: Wall Street ended little changed on Friday, taking a breather following a five-day winning streak, while the dollar rebounded against most currencies from earlier losses tied to expectations the U.S. central bank is in no hurry to raise interest rates.

title: Microsoft wins $1.76 billion defense contract: Pentagon
description: Microsoft Corp  has been awarded a five-year contract worth $1.76 billion for delivering enterprise services for the Defense Department, Coast Guard and intelligence services, the Pentagon said on Friday.

title: Take Five: May Day, May Day! World markets themes for the week ahead
description: Following are five big themes likely to dominate thinking of investors and traders in the coming week and the Reuters stories related to them.

title: Alphabet board sued on allegations of sexual misconduct cover-up
description: Two shareholder lawsuits filed this week accused the board of Google parent Alphabet Inc of playing a direct role in covering up sexual misconduct claims against two former executives over the last five years.

title: New Petrobras CEO pushes to oust board members: sources
description: The new chief executive of Brazil's Petroleo Brasileiro SA  is pushing for the ouster of two of the state-controlled oil company's board members, three people with knowledge of the matter said on Friday.

title: Exclusive: Trafigura refuses to hand over emails in Brazil bribery case
description: Commodities trader Trafigura [TRAFGF.UL] has refused a judge's order to hand over the email archives of two former executives in Brazil who are facing corruption charges over accusations they bribed officials at state-run oil firm Petroleo Brasileiro.

title: U.S. government shutdown may depress January job growth
description: A partial shutdown of the U.S. government could slash job growth by as much as 500,000 in January and lift the unemployment rate above 4.0 percent unless the impasse in Washington is resolved before next Friday, economists warned.

title: Battered U.S. bank stocks may get a boost this year
description: After a miserable 2018, big U.S. bank stocks could be in for a lift if upcoming earnings releases show strong fourth-quarter loan growth helps to offset weak trading revenue.

title: Citigroup allows hedge fund ValueAct more access
description: Citigroup Inc  will give ValueAct Capital more access to its books and board of directors, signaling that the bank and the activist hedge fund are deepening their relationship roughly a year after ValueAct first invested in Citi.

title: Square's payments chief joins Visa as head of seller solutions
description: Visa Inc  on Friday said https://usa.visa.com/visa-everywhere/blog.entry.html/2019/01/11/mary_kay_bowman_join-lrU0.html Mary Kay Bowman will join as head of the business that is tasked to attract more customers to use the world's largest payments network.

title: Autostrade to pay 439 million euros for Genoa bridge recostruction: sources
description: Autostrade per l'Italia (ASPI) has agreed to pay for the reconstruction of the collapsed Genoa bridge, Italy's Transport Minister Danilo Toninelli said on Twitter.

title: Ghosn's Renault lieutenant drew extra salary via holding: documents
description: One of Renault  boss Carlos Ghosn's senior executives received an additional six-figure salary unknown to the carmaker's board via the Dutch joint venture overseeing its alliance with Nissan , according to sources and documents seen by Reuters.

title: GM bucks gloomy earnings forecast trend, shares jump
description: General Motors Co  executives on Friday bucked gloomy forecasts for growth and sent the automaker's shares soaring, promising investors stronger 2019 earnings and outlining ambitious plans for its Cadillac brand to challenge Tesla Inc  in the growing electric vehicle market.

title: In Beijing talks, U.S. seeks details on Chinese goods purchases, trade promises
description: U.S. officials used three days of trade talks in Beijing to demand more details on China's pledge to make big purchases of American goods, as well as to push for ways to hold China to any commitments on changes to industrial policies.

title: Jaguar Land Rover to cut 4,500 jobs, mainly in Britain
description: Britain's biggest carmaker Jaguar Land Rover said it will cut around 4,500 jobs, mainly in its home market, as it tries to tackle a slowdown in China and a slump in demand for its diesel-powered vehicles.

title: Target posts strong holiday sales, maintains outlook
description: Target Corp  said on Thursday comparable sales grew 5.7 percent during November and December, helped by higher customer visits and strong online sales during the holiday season.

title: Nissan board reaffirms commitment to alliance with Renault and Mitsubishi
description: Nissan's board remains committed to the carmaker's alliance with Renault  and Mitsubishi Motors , it said after directors met to discuss the ongoing investigation into former chairman Carlos Ghosn and ways to bolster governance.

title: Apple cuts current-quarter production plan for new iPhones by 10 percent: Nikkei
description: Apple Inc , which slashed its quarterly sales forecast last week, has reduced planned production for its three new iPhone models by about 10 percent for the January-March quarter, the Nikkei Asian Review reported on Wednesday.

title: Exclusive: Glencore loses exclusive rights to major Libyan oil grades
description: Trading and mining giant Glencore  has lost its exclusive marketing rights for two of Libya's main crude oil export grades after holding them since late 2015, trading sources with direct knowledge said.

title: American Airlines shares fall on dour fourth quarter expectations, weigh on sector
description: American Airlines  shares fell as much as 11 percent on Thursday after the biggest U.S. carrier cut its estimate for a closely watched measure of performance, raising concerns that slowing global economic growth is hurting business travel.

title: Jaguar Land Rover to slash UK jobs after China, diesel drop
description: Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) will cut 10 percent of its workforce, mostly in its home market, as Britain's biggest carmaker faces lower Chinese demand and a slump in European diesel sales.

title: Exclusive: Modi's 'Make in India' a casualty as steel, auto firms spar over sourcing
description: India's steel ministry is putting pressure on automakers to use locally made steel by refusing to back down on tougher import rules despite warnings that the new regulations could disrupt the production of cars, government and industry sources said.

title: U.S. weekly jobless claims showcase economy's strength
description: The number of Americans filing applications for jobless benefits fell more than expected last week, pointing to sustained labor market strength that could further assuage concerns about the economy's health.

title: Airbus loses to Boeing in annual jet order race
description: Europe's Airbus lost out to Boeing in 2018, breaking a five-year winning streak against its U.S. rival for the number of jet orders, slumping to its lowest share of the $150 billion jet market in six years, data showed on Wednesday.

title: Starboard building stake in MGM Resorts: sources
description: Activist hedge fund Starboard Value LP is building a stake in MGM Resorts , two people familiar with the matter said on Thursday, as the U.S. hotel and casino operator comes under investor scrutiny over its profit targets.

title: Ford does not rule out plant closures in Europe as part of overhaul
description: Ford  cannot rule out plant closures as part of its efforts to return its European operations to profitability, Steven Armstrong, group vice president, Europe, Middle East and Africa, said on Thursday.

title: Nike's Dutch tax status investigated by EU regulators
description: The European Commission has opened an investigation into the tax treatment of Nike Inc  in the Netherlands, saying this may have given the U.S. sportswear maker an illegal advantage.

title: Sen. Sanders, Rep. Cummings introduce bill to lower U.S. drug prices
description: U.S. Senator Bernie Sanders and Representative Elijah Cummings introduced legislation on Thursday aimed at lowering the cost of prescription drugs for American consumers, critiquing President Donald Trump administration's efforts to curb medicine prices.

title: Looking past Khashoggi, investors flock to Saudi Arabia bond sale
description: Foreign investors flocked to buy Saudi Arabia's first dollar bonds since Jamal Khashoggi's death, in a clear vote of market confidence after the country's reputation was damaged over the journalist's murder.

title: M.M. Warburg sues Deutsche Bank over share trade tax
description: Hamburg-based bank M.M. Warburg & Co said on Thursday it had filed a lawsuit against Deutsche Bank  seeking 46 million euros ($53.04 million) that the bank was ordered to pay in capital gains tax.

title: U.S. buyback market support may wane in 2019
description: U.S. companies' shopping spree for their own shares helped put a floor on market declines in 2018. Don't look for the same level of support in 2019.

title: Dutch government says it will cooperate with EU probe into Nike tax status
description: The Dutch government said on Thursday it will cooperate with an investigation by the EU Commission into Nike Inc.'s  tax arrangements in the Netherlands.

title: Exclusive: Saudi private jet industry stalls after corruption crackdown
description: A crackdown on corruption in Saudi Arabia has severely dented the kingdom's private jet industry in a sign of the impact the campaign has had on private enterprise and the wealthy elite.

title: Jaguar Land Rover clear they regard UK as home: PM May's spokesman
description: Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) has made clear they regard Britain as home and are investing in the future, Prime Minister Theresa May's spokesman said on Thursday.

title: At China port, tariff drop a salve for hard-hit traders of American cars
description: In the Chinese port city of Tianjin, gray market traders of American-made cars, badly stung by a scything trade war and punitive tit-for-tat tariffs, are scrambling to take advantage of an opportunity they fear may prove only temporary.

title: AXA moves international risk to Ireland from UK ahead of Brexit
description: French insurer AXA  said it will handle its international risk and reinsurance trough an Irish unit in light of Britain's plans to leave the European Union.

title: Volkswagen sells record 6.24 million VW vehicles in 2018
description: Volkswagen  sold a record 6.24 million of its VW-branded vehicles last year despite delivery problems caused by new anti-pollution rules, but warned the company would continue to face considerable challenges in 2019.

title: U.S. oil export boom sparks a battle to build Texas ports
description: Booming U.S. oil exports have set off a scramble to build Gulf Coast ports to handle more than 3 million barrels per day in new supplies expected over the next five years.

title: Vodafone plans to cut up to 1,200 jobs from its Spanish business
description: Vodafone  plans to cut up to 1,200 jobs from its Spanish business, the company said on Thursday, though it declined to give further details ahead of talks with labor representatives expected to begin at the end of the month.

title: Stocks boosted by U.S.-China trade hope, oil prices soar
description: Stocks around the world extended recent gains and oil prices jumped on Wednesday on optimism the United States and China may be inching toward a trade deal, soothing fears of an all-out trade war and its possible impact on global growth.

title: China says trade talks with U.S. made progress on forced tech transfers, IP rights
description: China and the United States made progress during their recent trade talks over structural issues such as forced technology transfers and intellectual property rights, China's commerce ministry said on Thursday.

title: Exclusive: VW, China spearhead $300 billion global drive to electrify cars
description: Global automakers are planning a $300 billion surge in spending on electric vehicle technology over the next five to 10 years, with nearly half of the money targeted at China, accelerating the industry's transition from fossil fuels and shifting power to Asian battery and electric vehicle technology suppliers.

title: China vice president urges dialogue for stable China-U.S. ties: Xinhua
description: China's Vice President Wang Qishan urged for dialogue and consultations for healthy and stable bilateral relations between the country and the United States, China's Xinhua news agency reported on Thursday.

title: JPMorgan Chase boosting employee bonus pool 3 percent for 2018
description: JPMorgan Chase & Co  is boosting its bonus pool by 3 percent for 2018 after its investment banking division topped charts throughout the year, people familiar with the matter told Reuters on Thursday.

title: Pacific trade deal spurs Canadian farm sales to Japan as U.S. watches
description: At the Canadian embassy in Tokyo last month, beef promoters flew in a chef from Canada to cook New York strip steaks for hungry Japanese importers and restaurant suppliers.

title: Brazil approves Boeing-Embraer tie-up with new commitment to keep local jobs
description: The Brazilian government on Thursday said it would allow a proposed tie-up between planemakers Embraer SA  and Boeing Co  to go forward, capping weeks of uncertainty in which President Jair Bolsonaro expressed hesitation.

title: Trump's attorney general nominee to recuse from AT&T-Time Warner appeal
description: William Barr, nominated by President Donald Trump to become U.S. attorney general, plans to recuse himself from a major antitrust case, according to people who spoke with him on Thursday, as he navigates possible conflicts of interest presented by about $37 million in assets he amassed as a private-sector lawyer.

title: J&J raises U.S. prices on around two dozen drugs
description: Johnson & Johnson raised U.S. prices on around two dozen prescription drugs on Thursday, including the psoriasis treatment Stelara, prostate cancer drug Zytiga and blood thinner Xarelto, all among its top-selling products.

title: U.S. judge lets Buffett's Dairy Queen sue W.B. Mason over 'Blizzard'
description: A federal judge in Minnesota ruled this week that Dairy Queen, owned by Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway Inc, may pursue its lawsuit to stop W.B. Mason Co from selling "Blizzard" bottled spring water, the name it uses for a popular ice cream product.

title: Investment bank Perella Weinberg plans to name Peter Weinberg as CEO: source
description: Investment bank Perella Weinberg Partners plans to name Peter Weinberg as its chief executive officer with current CEO Robert Steel set to become the company's chairman, a person familiar with the matter told Reuters on Thursday.

title: Ford, Jaguar slash thousands of jobs across Europe
description: Ford  and Jaguar Land Rover unveiled sweeping job cuts across Europe on Thursday as carmakers struggle with a slump in demand for diesel vehicles, tougher emissions rules and a global economic slowdown led by China.

title: U.S. expects China's top trade negotiator to visit 'most likely' this month
description: U.S. officials expect China's top trade negotiator may visit Washington this month, signaling that higher-level discussions are likely to follow this week's talks with mid-level officials in Beijing as the world's two largest economies try to hammer out a deal to end a tit-for-tat tariff war.

title: Macy's cuts profit, sales forecast after weak holiday season
description: Macy's Inc  shares plunged 18 percent on Thursday after the department store operator slashed its full-year profit and sales forecast on the back of an anemic holiday season, sending a chill through the wider retail sector.

title: Trump says U.S. is having tremendous success with China on trade
description: President Donald Trump said on Thursday the United States was having tremendous success in its trade negotiations with China, a day after U.S. and Chinese officials concluded three days of talks in Beijing.

title: Chinese official 'most likely' to visit in January for trade talks: U.S. Treasury Secretary
description: U.s. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin said on Thursday that Chinese Vice Premier Liu He will "most likely" visit Washington later in January for trade talks.

title: Investors ask how the Bezos divorce will affect Amazon
description: Amazon.com Inc  shares seesawed on Thursday as investors questioned how the impending divorce of company founder Jeff Bezos would affect his control of the most valuable company on Wall Street and its ambitious expansion plans.

title: Ford's ride-share service Chariot to shut operations by March-end
description: Ford Motor Co's  ride-share service Chariot is ceasing its operations in the United States and the UK by the end of March, Chariot said in a blog post http://bit.ly/2D3DKjL on Thursday.

title: Wall Street shrugs off Macy's, rallies for fifth session
description: Wall Street extended its rally into a fifth straight day on Thursday in a session of whipsaw trading as investors responded to mixed comments by Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell, while a warning from Macy's pummeled retail stocks.

title: Moody's lowers PG&E's credit rating to junk, joins S&P
description: Moody's on Thursday joined S&P in lowering PG&E Corp's  credit rating deeper into junk territory, citing a challenging environment for the California power provider as it faces billions of dollars in liabilities related to wildfires.

title: HSBC to pay $30 million to settle bond rigging lawsuit in U.S.
description: HSBC Holdings Plc has agreed to pay $30 million to settle litigation by investors who accused 11 big banks of rigging the roughly $9 trillion government agency bond market from 2009 to 2015.

title: Stocks rise for fifth straight day as the Fed supports
description: An index of world stock markets rose on Thursday as worries over the lack of clear signs of a resolution to the U.S.-China trade spat were offset by an assurance by Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell that the U.S. central bank has the ability to be patient on monetary policy.

title: Carmaker Rolls-Royce urges UK's May to avoid a hard Brexit
description: Carmaker Rolls-Royce called on the British government to avoid a disorderly Brexit and said it was building up some stock, expanding warehouse capacity and training suppliers for customs changes in case Britain leaves the EU without a deal.

title: Fiat Chrysler agrees to $800 million U.S. diesel-emissions settlement
description: Fiat Chrysler Automobiles NV has agreed to a settlement worth about $800 million to resolve claims from the U.S. Justice Department and state of California that it used illegal software that produced false results on diesel-emissions tests, but still faces an ongoing criminal probe.

title: Factbox: High-profile corporate chieftain's divorces
description: Amazon  founder Jeff Bezos, the world's richest man, and his wife MacKenzie, who announced on Wednesday that they are divorcing, are the latest of a long line of rich and powerful couples whose marriages came to a public end, often with a hefty price tag.

title: Investor Browder asks France to investigate Danske in Magnitsky case
description: Bill Browder, founder and CEO of investment fund Hermitage Capital Management, said on Thursday he had asked French authorities to investigate Danske Bank over alleged money laundering, rather than treating it as a witness.

title: Exclusive: Brazil telecom Oi hires BofA Merrill Lynch to sell some assets: sources
description: Brazilian telecoms carrier Oi SA  has hired Bank of America Merrill Lynch to sell noncore assets such as cellphone towers and data centers, two people with knowledge of the matter said on Thursday.

title: Court says Amazon 'Dash' buttons violate German law
description: A German court ruled on Thursday that Amazon's thumb-sized ordering devices known as "Dash" buttons do not give sufficient information about the product ordered or its price, breaking consumer protection legislation.

title: VW seeks damages from ex-managers for emissions scandal: report

title: Nvidia says new self-driving platform to hit streets next year
description: Nvidia Corp on Monday announced its Drive AutoPilot platform, with artificial intelligence technologies, that can enable the next level of self-driving cars by 2020, further strengthening its position in the industry.

title: U.S., China can reach trade deal 'we can live with': U.S. Commerce secretary
description: U.S. Commerce Secretary Wilbur Ross predicted on Monday that Beijing and Washington could reach a trade deal that "we can live with" as dozens of officials from the world's two largest economies resumed talks in a bid to end their trade dispute.

title: PG&E shares and bonds plunge on bankruptcy worries
description: PG&E Corp's  shares dived more than 22 percent on Monday after sources said the California utility is exploring filing for bankruptcy protection as it fears a massive charge in the fourth quarter related to potential liabilities from wildfires.

title: Karen Peetz to retire from Wells Fargo board
description: Wells Fargo & Co  said on Monday board member Karen Peetz has decided not to stand for reelection after roughly two years on the board.

title: Stocks rise on trade talk optimism; rate outlook hits dollar
description: An index of world stocks rose on Monday, adding to Friday's strong gains, on optimism about the outcome of trade talks between Washington and Beijing.

title: Sears picks liquidator should rescue talks fall through: sources
description: A long-standing liquidator is now first in line for one of the U.S. retail sector's most daunting assignments: shutting down 126-year-old department store chain Sears Holdings Corp , people familiar with the matter said on Sunday.

title: Oil rises; lifted by OPEC cuts, steadying stock market
description: Oil prices edged higher on Monday, rebounding further from 1-1/2-year lows reached in December, on support from OPEC production cuts and steadying equities markets.

title: Canada auto union head to meet with GM on Tuesday
description: The head of Canada's auto union said on Monday he was set to meet with General Motors Co  executives in Detroit on Tuesday to discuss the automaker's Oshawa, Ontario, assembly plant, scheduled to shut down in December 2019.

title: Lilly makes $8 billion bet on drugs for rare cancers with Loxo Oncology buy
description: Eli Lilly said on Monday it will buy Loxo Oncology Inc for $8 billion, an expensive bet on a pipeline of cancer drugs that target rare genetic mutations and the biggest acquisition in the drugmaker's 143-year history.     The price represents a 68 percent premium to Loxo's Friday share price close, which some Wall Street analysts said was high for a company with only one drug on the market that it shares with a partner.

title: ICBC leads Asian jet lessor buying spree: sources
description: Asian-controlled leasing companies splashed out on passenger jets worth $25 billion at list prices to pick out bargains as planemakers Airbus  and Boeing  raced to end a relatively quiet year with fresh orders.

title: U.S. top court rejects Amgen over cholesterol medication patent fight
description: Amgen Inc on Monday lost its bid at the U.S. Supreme Court to overturn a ruling that kept the Regeneron Pharmaceuticals Inc and Sanofi SA cholesterol-lowering drug Praluent on the market, but the patent dispute among the rival drugmakers will continue in another trial.

title: Fund managers hoping for stock rally look to emerging markets
description: After emerging market stocks led global equity markets lower in a brutal 2018, some U.S.-based fund managers are betting that the asset class may have the largest rebound in the new year.

title: Mercedes aims to be among top two players to scale autonomous tech: paper
description: Mercedes-Benz's is not aiming to be the first manufacturer to develop a self-driving car but it wants to be among the first two players able to scale up the technology, Mercedes-Benz executive Christoph Schroeder told German paper Welt am Sonntag.

title: France presses Renault over executive compensation paid via Dutch holding company
description: The French government has told Renault  to provide more details on compensation paid to senior executives via a Dutch holding company jointly owned with alliance partner Nissan, Finance Minister Bruno Le Maire said on Sunday.

title: Southeast Asia wary of China's Belt and Road project, skeptical of U.S.: survey
description: Southeast Asian countries should be cautious in negotiating with China on its flagship Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) to avoid being trapped in unsustainable debt, 70 percent of respondents said in a policy survey released on Monday.

title: Samsung Electronics braces for profit drop as China slowdown chips away at demand
description: Samsung Electronics Co Ltd is set to post its first drop in quarterly operating profit in two years as slowing economic growth in China, a key market for the South Korean tech giant, erodes demand for its products.

title: Starboard buys stake in Dollar Tree, seeks sale of Family Dollar: WSJ
description: Activist investor Starboard Value LP has acquired a stake in discount store operator Dollar Tree Inc  and is asking the company to sell its Family Dollar business, the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday.

title: Apple inks deal with Samsung to distribute iTunes shows on TVs
description: Samsung Electronics Co Ltd  said Sunday that it will add an app to its smart televisions in the coming months to let owners watch content bought on Apple Inc's  iTunes service, a possible first sign Apple is looking to distribute its forthcoming television service on devices made by others.

title: South Korea's Celltrion aims to set up China JV within first half of 2019: chairman
description: South Korean drugmaker Celltrion Inc  aims to set up a joint venture in China within the first half of this year, and begin selling products in the country next year, its chairman said on Sunday.

title: Japanese prosecutors want Ghosn to sign confession, says son: paper
description: Japanese prosecutors want Carlos Ghosn, the detained auto executive who oversaw an alliance that sold 10 million vehicles a year, to confess to financial misconduct, his son told France's weekly Journal du Dimanche (JDD).

title: German state of Baden-Wuerttemberg sues VW for damages: FAZ
description: The German Federal State of Baden-Wuerttemberg is seeking damages from Volkswagen  after local authorities purchased VW diesel vehicles which now face bans in cities like Stuttgart, Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung said on Saturday.

title: Fed Chair Powell says he would not resign if Trump asked
description: Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell on Friday said he would not resign even if President Donald Trump asked him to do so, a clear assertion of the U.S. central bank's independence in the face of Trump's strident criticism of the Fed's rate hikes.

title: Brazil's Bolsonaro: worried Boeing could own all of Embraer's commercial division
description: Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro said on Friday he is concerned that a proposed sale of 80 percent of Embraer's  commercial aviation business to Boeing  could lead to the U.S. planemaker taking over all of the division.

title: Tesla to start delivering Model 3 to China buyers in March
description: Tesla Inc said on Friday it plans to start delivering Model 3 cars to customers in China in March, cementing a time frame that the U.S. electric vehicle (EV) maker's chief executive, Elon Musk, tweeted about late last year.

title: Airbus chases aircraft lessors as order race tightens
description: Airbus  has been chasing deals with leasing companies in recent weeks to try to narrow a gap in orders against rival Boeing , while industry experts took a somewhat more sanguine view on 2018 deliveries after shares took a beating.

title: Instant View: U.S. December payrolls surprise big to the upside
description: U.S. employers hired the most workers in 10 months in December while boosting wages, which could help to allay a recent upsurge in fears about the economy's health that has roiled financial markets.

title: Ex-Credit Suisse bankers arrested on U.S. charges over Mozambique loans
description: Three former Credit Suisse Group AG  bankers were arrested in London on Thursday on U.S. charges of involvement in a fraud involving $2 billion in loans to state-owned companies in Mozambique, U.S. prosecutors and British police said.

title: Celgene, Bristol-Myers set $2.2 billion termination fee for their mega deal
description: Celgene Corp  and Bristol-Myers Squibb Co  will have to pay $2.2 billion if either of the drugmakers walks away from their $74 billion merger announced on Thursday, according to a regulatory filing.

title: Chinese phone maker Huawei punishes employees for iPhone tweet blunder
description: China's Huawei Technologies [HWT.UL] has punished two employees for New Year greetings sent on the smartphone maker's official Twitter account using an iPhone, an internal memo showed.

title: Pioneering Southwest Airlines co-founder Herb Kelleher dies at 87
description: Herb Kelleher, who co-founded pioneering low-cost carrier Southwest Airlines Co and built it into an industry powerhouse stamped with his colorful, unconventional personality, died on Thursday at age 87, the U.S. carrier said.

title: China slashes banks' reserve requirements again as growth slows
description: China's central bank said on Friday it was cutting the amount of cash that banks have to hold as reserves for the fifth time in a year, freeing up $116 billion for new lending as it tries to reduce the risk of a sharp economic slowdown.

title: Audits reveal Deutsche Bank's links to tax trade scandal
description: There are "lots of indications" that some managers discussed "the reputational risks" of Deutsche Bank's involvement in a share-trading scheme that is the subject of Germany's biggest  post-war fraud investigation, according to a conclusion in one of five internal audits seen by Reuters.

title: UK consumer lending growth slows to near four-year low as Brexit approaches
description: Lending to British consumers grew at its slowest pace in nearly four years in November and the number of mortgage approvals fell, Bank of England data showed, adding to signs of a pre-Brexit slowdown in the economy.

title: German Apple reseller Gravis says still selling iPhones 7, 8
description: German Apple  retailer Gravis said it was still selling iPhone 7 and 8 models at its stores and online after Qualcomm  posted security bonds to enforce a court order that will ban sales of some Apple iPhones in Germany.

title: Yen's surge is a red flag for world markets
description: A gradual rise by the Japanese yen in recent weeks culminated in a dramatic overnight surge -- firing a warning shot for world markets and the global economy in 2019.

title: Bristol-Myers to buy Celgene for $74 billion in largest biopharma deal
description: Bristol-Myers Squibb Co  said on Thursday it would buy Celgene Corp  for about $74 billion, combining two of the world's largest cancer drug businesses in the biggest pharmaceutical deal ever.

title: Offices grow 'brains' as companies seek to attract smarter workers
description: Employees will not need a key to get into the office of the future when it opens in Berlin this year, featuring ample meeting space, plenty of copy machines always stocked with paper along with high-quality air processed to maximize worker health and minimize sick time.

title: Qualcomm kicks off crucial fight with U.S. antitrust regulator
description: The U.S. Federal Trade Commission's antitrust case accusing Qualcomm Inc  of abusing a monopoly on mobile chip technology kicked off in a California courtroom on Friday in a trial whose outcome could have a major impact on the smartphone industry.

title: Qualcomm enforces ban to halt some Apple iPhone sales in Germany
description: U.S. chipmaker Qualcomm Inc  took steps to enforce a court order banning the sale of some iPhone models in Germany following a patent dispute, a move that will likely see Apple Inc  pull those models from its German stores.

title: U.S. judge stands by ruling to limit evidence in Roundup cancer trials
description: A federal judge overseeing lawsuits alleging Bayer AG's glyphosate-based Roundup weed killer causes cancer on Friday declined to reconsider a ruling that limits evidence the plaintiffs in the litigation consider crucial to their cases.

title: China warnings signal Trump's trade war finally hitting home
description: Weak sales at Apple and Cargill, U.S. giants of technology and agriculture, may be the clearest sign yet that President Donald Trump's quest to reset world trade carries costs at home and could isolate the United States as the increasingly fragile engine for global economic growth.

title: Oil rises on China-U.S. talks, gains capped by U.S. fuel build
description: Oil rose nearly 2 percent on Friday after proposed trade talks between the United States and China eased some fears about a global economic slowdown, but gains were capped after the United States reported a sharp build in refined product inventories.

title: Take Five: Be careful out there! World markets themes for the week ahead
description: Following are five big themes likely to dominate thinking of investors and traders in the coming week and the Reuters stories related to them.

title: Nissan's executive Munoz takes leave of absence in wake of Ghosn arrest
description: A senior executive of Nissan Motor Co Ltd , Jose Munoz, has taken a leave of absence in a sudden management shake-up as the Japanese automaker deals with the aftermath of the arrest of former chairman Carlos Ghosn.

title: Wall St. rebounds on robust jobs report, dovish Powell remarks
description: Wall Street rebounded on Friday to close at its highest in two weeks after a strong jobs report and assurances from Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell that the central bank would be patient and flexible in steering the course of interest rates.

title: Trump says China woes help U.S. in trade talks, downplays Apple warning
description: President Donald Trump on Friday downplayed a revenue warning from Apple Inc that cited slowing sales in China and said China's weakening economic growth puts the United States in a strong position as negotiators from the world's two largest economies prepare for trade talks next week.

title: Tesla urges tariff exemption for Chinese-made car computer 'brain'
description: Tesla Inc has asked the Trump administration to exempt the Chinese-made car computer "brain" of its new Model 3 sedan from 25 percent tariffs imposed in August, saying they threaten the electric carmaker's bottom line.

title: Samsung, Huawei supply majority of own modem chips, Qualcomm says
description: The two largest smart phone makers in the world supply a majority of their own modem chips to help their devices connect to wireless data networks, according to evidence presented at an antitrust trial for chip supplier Qualcomm Inc .

title: Upbeat employment report underscores U.S. economic strength
description: U.S. employers hired the most workers in 10 months in December while boosting wages, pointing to sustained strength in the economy that could ease fears of a sharp slowdown in growth.

title: Nissan's Ghosn to make first public appearance in seven weeks in court on Tuesday
description: Ousted Nissan Motor Co Ltd  chairman Carlos Ghosn is set to make his first public appearance in seven weeks at a Tokyo court on Tuesday after he requested an open hearing to hear the reason for his continued detention.

title: PG&E seeks to make changes to its board
description: PG&E Corp , the electricity provider in the northern California region ravaged by a deadly wildfire, said it was searching for new directors at its holding company and its utility subsidiary Pacific Gas and Electric Co.

title: U.S. jobs data, dovish Fed comments boost equities
description: Equities around the globe rallied on Friday while bond yields rose after sharply declining earlier in the week as U.S. employment data pointed to economic strength and Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell said the U.S. central bank would be patient with monetary policy.

title: Powell tells markets Fed is flexible and aware of risks
description: Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell on Friday sought to ease market concerns that the U.S. central bank was ignoring signs of an economic slowdown, saying he was aware of the risks and would be patient and flexible in policy decisions this year.

title: Instant View: Powell pledges patience; says won't quit if Trump asks
description: Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell on Friday moved to mollify financial markets concerned about a U.S. economic slowdown, saying that while momentum is solid, the U.S. central bank will be sensitive to the downside risks the market is pricing in.

title: Supreme Court to weigh Broadcom bid to end shareholder suit
description: The U.S. Supreme Court on Friday agreed to hear an appeal filed by a subsidiary of chipmaker Broadcom Inc  seeking to put an end to a shareholder lawsuit concerning its 2015 acquisition of Emulex Corp.

title: Marriott cuts estimate on size of massive Starwood hack
description: Marriott International Inc  said on Friday that fewer than 383 million customer records were stolen in a massive cyber attack disclosed last month, down from its initial estimate that up to 500 million guests were affected.

title: Court battle, trade war and 5G spell tough 2019 for Apple in China
description: Apple Inc's chief executive Tim Cook has his work cut out in China this year: the iPhone maker faces the looming threat of a court-ordered sales ban, the uncertain outcome of trade war talks and the roll-out of a new 5G network, where it finds itself behind rivals like Huawei and Samsung.

title: UK pay gap between CEOs and staff widens -lobby group
description: The earnings of Britain's top bosses will match a typical worker's entire annual salary even faster than last year, hitting the mark by Friday lunchtime, a report by the Chartered Institute of Personnel & Development and High Pay Centre said.

title: OPEC oil output posts biggest drop since 2017 on Saudi move
description: OPEC oil supply fell in December by the largest amount in almost two years, a Reuters survey found, as top exporter Saudi Arabia made an early start to a supply-limiting accord while Iran and Libya posted involuntary declines.

title: U.S. factory activity hits two-year low, casts shadow over economy
description: U.S. manufacturing activity slowed sharply to a two-year low in December amid a plunge in new orders and hiring at factories, suggesting the economy was probably not immune to slowing growth in China and Europe.

title: Major automakers bullish on U.S. market despite rising interest rates
description: Major automakers on Thursday shrugged off declines in U.S. new vehicle sales in December and said they were bullish about 2019 even as economists warned that rising interest rates will discourage consumers from buying cars in the year ahead.

title: Apple sales should pick up when U.S.-China strike trade deal: Trump adviser
description: A sharp drop in Chinese economic growth will hit the profits of U.S. firms but sales by Apple Inc and other American companies should recover once Washington strikes a trade deal with Beijing, a senior White House adviser said on Thursday.

title: Apple's warning a bad omen for Wall Street bulls
description: Apple's  warning on Wednesday about weak iPhone demand in the holiday quarter is a gloomy omen for Wall Street bulls hoping for an early gift in 2019 following December's steep selloff.

title: Apple warning shakes European shares as tech stocks tumble
description: Apple's first sales warning in nearly 12 years sent European shares sliding on Thursday, with the tech sector particularly badly bruised as chipmakers that supply the iPhone maker fell sharply.

title: Airbus bags new orders as delivery target doubts grow
description: Airbus narrowed a sales gap against U.S. rival Boeing by finalising orders for 120 of the former Bombardier CSeries jet, but shares in Europe's top planemaker fell as doubts surfaced over a target for overall 2018 deliveries.

title: Paying the price: China shoppers, stung by slowdown, take bite out of Apple
description: Shanghai student Xu Yechuyi wanted to buy a new iPhone last year but couldn't afford one at Apple Inc's flagship store, so she opted for a used, three-year-old iPhone 6S at less than a third of the sticker price.

title: Cargill net drops 20 percent, revenues fall as trade fight bites
description: Grains trader Cargill Inc on Thursday reported a 20 percent drop in its fiscal second-quarter 2019 net earnings, as global trade tensions hit the bottom line along with challenges in the Chinese hog sector and a struggling U.S. dairy business.

title: Nordstrom heir Blake Nordstrom dies at 58
description: Nordstrom Inc  said its co-president, Blake Nordstrom, passed away early Wednesday morning at the age of 58.

title: Nestle welcomes Indian court ruling in Maggi case
description: Food group Nestle  said on Thursday a ruling by India's Supreme Court marked a partial victory in its row with the government over Maggi noodles.

title: UAW sues GM over temporary workers, escalating fight over job cuts
description: The United Auto Workers said on Thursday it was suing General Motors Co over labor contract violations stemming from its alleged use of temporary workers at an Indiana assembly plant, escalating the union's fight against GM's plans to possibly close U.S. factories.

title: Apple cuts sales forecast as China sales weaken; iPhone pricing in focus
description: Apple Inc on Wednesday took the rare step of cutting its quarterly sales forecast, with Chief Executive Tim Cook blaming slowing iPhone sales in China, whose economy has been dragged down by uncertainty around U.S.-China trade relations.

title: U.S. drugmaker J&J's India sales dip 3 percent in 2017/18: filing
description: Johnson & Johnson's  sales in India dipped 3 percent in the year to March 2018, a regulatory filing showed on Thursday, as the U.S. drugmaker grappled with the country's stringent medical device pricing policies.

title: Tesla cuts U.S. prices on all vehicles, shares drop
description: Tesla Inc  on Wednesday cut U.S. prices for all its vehicles to offset lower green tax credits, and fell short on quarterly deliveries of its mass-market Model 3 sedan, sending shares of the electric vehicle maker down nearly 7 percent on worries of future profitability.

title: Google shifted $23 billion to tax haven Bermuda in 2017: filing
description: Google moved 19.9 billion euros ($22.7 billion) through a Dutch shell company to Bermuda in 2017, as part of an arrangement that allows it to reduce its foreign tax bill, according to documents filed at the Dutch Chamber of Commerce.

title: Coffee startup Luckin plans to overtake Starbucks in China this year
description: Chinese coffee startup Luckin is aiming to open 2,500 new stores this year and overtake Starbucks Corp  as the largest coffee chain by number of outlets in the world's second-biggest economy, it said on Thursday.

title: Cost to insure Bristol-Myers debt jumps as leverage balloons
description: The cost to insure Bristol-Myers Squibb  debt hit its highest point since May 2010 on Thursday, following the announcement that the U.S. pharmaceutical company would acquire rival Celgene Corp  in a deal worth about $74 billion.

title: Delta shares fall 10 percent on lowered outlook; drags down rivals
description: Shares of Delta Air Lines Inc fell about 9 percent on Thursday, after the U.S. carrier warned fourth-quarter unit revenue would be slightly below its prior forecast due to the lower-than-expected improvement in last-minute fares booked by travelers.

title: Truckmaker Volvo to take $778 million emissions hit
description: Sweden's Volvo is setting aside 7 billion Swedish crowns ($778 million) to cover costs related to its admission in October that its truck and bus engines could be exceeding limits for nitrogen oxide emissions.

title: Apple plunge deepens Warren Buffett's book value woes
description: The plunge in Apple Inc's share price will likely cause new pain for Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway Inc, after the conglomerate suffered a big quarterly decline in its net worth that will hit its bottom line.

title: U.S. retail vacancies rise marginally in fourth quarter: Reis
description: U.S. retail vacancies inched higher in the fourth quarter, underscoring how the retail sector has withstood many store closures across the country, real estate research firm Reis Inc said in a report.

title: Detroit Three ready for 2019 rumble over lucrative pickup trucks
description: The battle for profits from sales of large pickup trucks is intensifying among the Detroit Three automakers as sales of small cars in the United States shrivel.

title: Wall Street plunges as factory data, Apple warning fuel slowdown fears
description: Wall Street plunged on Thursday after slowing U.S. factory activity on the heels of a dire revenue warning from Apple Inc  fueled fears of a global economic slowdown.

title: Instant view: Stocks slammed, Treasury yields fall, yen surges
description: U.S. stocks plunged on Thursday and 2-year U.S. Treasury yields dropped below the Federal Reserve's policy rate for the first time in more than a decade, delivering a signal the U.S. central bank could begin reversing its tightening regime before long.

title: U.S. judge limits evidence in trial over Roundup cancer claims
description: A federal judge overseeing lawsuits alleging Bayer AG's glyphosate-based weed killer causes cancer has issued a ruling that could severely restrict evidence that the plaintiffs consider crucial to their cases.

title: At Brazil's Petrobras, a 'Chicago Boy' takes the reins
description: Depending on who you ask, Roberto Castello Branco, the new chief executive of Brazil's Petroleo Brasileiro SA , will either save the indebted oil major - or strip it to the bone.

title: Apple shares dive; rare revenue warning drags global markets
description: Apple Inc shares plunged 10 percent on Thursday after the iPhone maker blamed weak China demand for a holiday-quarter revenue shortfall, with many investors worried the rare stumble was a harbinger for slowing global growth.

title: Petrobras, Brazil government expect to resolve dispute within 100 days: minister
description: Brazil's government and state-run oil firm Petroleo Brasileiro SA  expect to resolve a dispute over the oil producing zone known as the 'transfer-of-rights' area within 100 days, a minister said on Thursday.

title: Father and son advised on opposite sides of Bristol-Celgene deal
description: For most U.S. families, the holidays are all about gathering around the fireplace, overeating at festive dinners, and playing the occasional board game. But this year, a father and son were also working on the biggest pharmaceutical acquisition of all time.

title: Reuss, 35-year GM veteran, to succeed Ammann as president
description: General Motors Co  said on Thursday that Mark Reuss would succeed Dan Ammann as president, effective immediately, as part of the automaker's ongoing shift to electric and self-driving vehicles in North America and China.

title: FDIC chair says no concerns about U.S. bank health amid market turmoil
description: A top U.S. bank regulator said on Thursday she had no concerns that volatility in the equities and futures markets posed a threat to the banking system, telling Reuters the country's lenders have plenty of capital to weather further market swings.

title: Oil rises in choppy trade as OPEC supply cuts vie with demand worry
description: Oil prices rose more than 1 percent on Thursday in volatile trade, drawing support from signs that Saudi Arabia is cutting crude output but pressured by concerns that slowing global economic growth could dent demand.

title: UK minister defends giving Brexit ferry contract to company with no ships
description: Britain's transport minister has defended awarding a 14 million-pound ($18 million) contract for shipping goods after Brexit to a new ferry company that owns no ships.

title: Prosecutor drops insider trading case against former Deutsche Boerse CEO
description: The Frankfurt prosecutor's office has dropped an insider trading case against former Deutsche Boerse  Chief Executive Carsten Kengeter in exchange for payments of almost 5 million euros ($5.68 million).

title: Hyundai flags tough 2019 as U.S., China demand stays slow
description: South Korea's Hyundai Motor Group flagged another year of tepid car sales growth on the back of a slow 2018, saying trade protectionism adds uncertainty and major markets such as the United States and China remained sluggish.

title: Roku to launch subscription video channels business
description: Roku Inc  said on Wednesday it will begin offering premium video channels to customers for a subscription fee as it expands its free streaming video service.

title: U.S.-China trade war takes toll on global manufacturing
description: Factory activity weakened across much of Europe and Asia in December as the U.S.-China trade war and a slowdown in demand hit production in many economies, offering little reason for optimism as the new year begins.

title: China's Didi launches credit, crowdfunding services in diversification push
description: China's Didi Chuxing has launched a suite of financial products, including crowdfunding and lending, as it continues to diversify outside the ride-hailing business following a year of safety scandals.

title: Bill Gates' nuclear venture hits snag amid U.S. restrictions on China deals: WSJ
description: TerraPower LLC, a nuclear energy venture chaired by Microsoft Corp co-founder Bill Gates, is seeking a new partner for early-stage trials of its technology after new U.S. rules forced it to abandon an agreement with China, company officials told the Wall Street Journal.

title: Big claims strain senior living market for U.S. insurers
description: Last March, a 103-year-old resident of a Sunrise Senior Living facility in Willowbrook, Illinois, went on a field trip to the movies.  Ruth Smith, who used a walker, fell down two concrete steps in the theater and died about six weeks later. Now Smith's estate is suing Sunrise, saying that aides did not properly watch her.

title: South Koreans seek Nippon Steel asset seizure in 'forced labor' case
description: South Korean plaintiffs in a World War Two forced labor court case against Japan's Nippon Steel & Sumitomo Metal Corp have applied to seize some of Nippon Steel's Korean assets, their lawyers said on Wednesday.

title: Markets start the way they ended
description: After the worst year for world stock markets in a decade, 2019 has kicked off with the same trepidation surrounding economic slowdown, trade tension and rising interest rates that infected markets for most of the second half of last year.

title: Google wins U.S. approval for new radar-based motion sensor
description: Alphabet Inc's  Google unit won approval from U.S. regulators to deploy a radar-based motion sensing device known as Project Soli.

title: Netflix poaches Activision's Neumann for CFO role
description: Netflix Inc  said on Wednesday it had appointed media finance veteran Spencer Neumann from Activision Blizzard  as its chief financial officer.

title: Economic concerns boost bonds, yen; Wall Street recovers
description: Weak Chinese and European economic data weighed on stocks around the world and boosted safe-haven Treasuries and the Japanese yen on Wednesday, though Wall Street shares edged higher as investors took advantage of cheaper shares to ring in the new year.

title: Oil volatile, ends up 2 percent but demand concerns still weigh
description: Oil prices rose about 2 percent in choppy trading on Wednesday, supported by a slight recovery on Wall Street, even as concerns remained about weakening global economic growth which could hurt demand for oil.

title: GM sold 200,000 electric vehicles in U.S. by 2018, triggering tax-credit phaseout: source
description: General Motors Co  hit 200,000 total electric vehicles sold in the United States by the end of 2018, reaching a threshold that triggers a phase-out of a $7,500 federal tax credit over the next 15 months, a person briefed on the matter said Wednesday.

title: Global growth worries, higher oil flatten yield curve
description: Yields on long-dated U.S. Treasury securities fell to their lowest in nearly a year on Wednesday on concerns about the health of the global economy, a worry exacerbated late in the day when Apple Inc  cut its sales outlook and sent U.S. equity index futures tumbling.

title: U.S. fund investors yank most cash from stocks since February: ICI
description: U.S. fund investors anguished over economic growth and policies pulled the most cash from stocks in any weekly period since last February, Investment Company Institute data showed on Wednesday.

title: S&P 500 futures fall sharply after Apple cuts guidance
description: S&P 500 futures  fell 1.5 percent as trading resumed late on Wednesday after Apple  cut its forecast for the holiday quarter.

title: Latin America stockpicker at BlackRock is leaving company
description: A top BlackRock Inc  investor focused on Latin American stocks is leaving the company, the world's largest asset manager said on Wednesday.

title: Wall Street ekes out gain, Apple cuts revenue forecast after the bell
description: Wall Street edged higher on Wednesday after stumbling out of the starting gate on the first trading day of 2019, while fears of a global economic slowdown were exacerbated after Apple cut its holiday-quarter revenue forecast.

title: Cathay Pacific makes good on first-class ticket blunder
description: Cathay Pacific Airways said it would guarantee thousands of first and business-class flights sold at huge discounts after a ticketing error, calling the mistake a surprise special on New Years Day.

title: Teva, Amgen end dispute over generic Cinacalcet HCl tablets
description: Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd  said on Thursday it will pay an undisclosed amount to settle an ongoing dispute with Amgen Inc  over its generic Cinacalcet HCl product.

title: For Warren Buffett, sinking Apple shares a wish come true
description: Billionaire Warren Buffett has said he would love to see Apple Inc shares decline in price so he could buy more. He is getting his wish.
