description: (This december 30 story corrects name of indexes in paragraphs 4 and 22 to ICE BofAML from Bank of America/Merrill Lynch)

title: Big banks look to cut back, alter credit card rewards programs: WSJ
description: Large financial institutions including JP Morgan Chase & Co , Citigroup Inc , and American Express Co  are cutting back or altering some of the rewards plans that their credit card businesses offer borrowers, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday.

title: Exclusive: Netflix poaches CFO from Activision Blizzard - source
description: Netflix Inc is expected to announce in the next few days that it has poached media finance veteran Spencer Neumann from Activision Blizzard to be its chief financial officer, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters.

title: China December factory activity shrinks for first time in 19 months: Caixin PMI
description: China's factory activity contracted for the first time in 19 months in December as domestic and export orders continued to weaken, a private survey showed, pointing to a rocky start for the world's second-largest economy in 2019.

title: Fatalities on commercial passenger aircraft rise in 2018
description: The fatality rate on passenger jet aircraft worldwide jumped in 2018 after airlines recorded zero accident deaths on passenger jets in the prior year, according to a Dutch consulting firm and an aviation safety group.

title: Fed Chair Powell's unscripted approach sets up for rocky 2019
description: Jerome Powell had a bumpy first year as Federal Reserve chairman when it came to talking policy, by turns spooking and comforting investors even as economic data offered increasingly mixed signals and President Donald Trump stepped up his attacks on the U.S. central bank.

title: Trade wars cost U.S., China billions of dollars each in 2018
description: The U.S.-China trade war resulted in billions of dollars of losses for both sides in 2018, hitting industries including autos, technology - and above all, agriculture.

title: China factory activity shrinks for first time in over two years, 2019 looks tougher
description: China's factory activity contracted for the first time in over two years in December, highlighting the challenges facing Beijing as it seeks to end a bruising trade war with Washington and reduce the risk of a sharper economic slowdown in 2019.

title: Tokyo court says extends detention of Nissan's Ghosn until Jan 11
description: The Tokyo District Court said on Monday it has extended the detention of ousted Nissan Motor Co chairman Carlos Ghosn by 10 days until Jan. 11.

title: Canada Goose's first China store draws eager crowds despite diplomatic headwinds
description: Large crowds have been drawn to Canada Goose's new outdoor wear store in downtown Beijing, its first in mainland China, since its opening on Friday, despite sub-zero temperatures and a chill in China's relations with Canada.

title: U.S. companies repatriate over half a trillion dollars in 2018, but pace slows
description: U.S. companies have sent home over half a trillion dollars of cash they held overseas in 2018 to take advantage of tax changes, but data suggest the pace is slowing, potentially removing a key source of support for Wall Street.

title: Trump says 'big progress' on possible China trade deal
description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Twitter that he had a "long and very good call" with Chinese President Xi Jinping and that a possible trade deal between the United States and China was progressing well.

title: China's services activity picks up in December: official PMI
description: Growth in China's services industry picked up in December after a two-month slowdown, an official survey showed, offering some respite for the slowing economy though the outlook remains gloomy as domestic and external risks to growth rise.

title: Tesla has over 3,000 Model 3s left in U.S. inventory: Electrek
description: Tesla Inc had over 3,000 Model 3s left in inventory in the United States as of Sunday, automotive news website Electrek reported on Monday, citing people familiar with the matter.

title: Trade optimism lifts stocks, but 2018 ends in red
description: Equities around the world rose on Monday as possible progress in resolving the trade dispute between the United States and China engendered some investor optimism in what has been a punishing end of year for markets.

title: 'Pooey Puitton' purse said to irk Louis Vuitton, prompts lawsuit
description: A California toy company has sued Louis Vuitton to stop the French luxury goods maker from interfering with its sales of a slime-filled, poop-shaped toy purse for children, Pooey Puitton.

title: Hertz Global to pay $16 million fine to settle accounting case: SEC
description: Hertz Global Holdings has agreed to pay a $16 million fine to settle a case over accounting misstatement, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) said in an order filed on Monday.

title: Oil posts first year of losses since 2015
description: Oil prices ended with full-year losses for the first time since 2015, after a desultory fourth quarter that saw buyers flee the market over growing worries about a supply glut and mixed signals related to renewed U.S. sanctions on Iran.

title: After damaging Reuters report, J&J doubles down on talc safety message
description: Johnson & Johnson Inc's statement was unequivocal.

title: Wall Street rises, limps across the finish line of a turbulent year
description: Wall Street advanced in low-volume trading on Monday as revelers gathered to ring in 2019, marking the end of the worst year for U.S. stocks since 2008, the height of the financial crisis.

title: Deutsche Bank is strong, has no need for state aid, merger:  chairman
description: Deutsche Bank is strong and its turnaround strategy is bearing fruit, Chairman Paul Achleitner said, ruling out the need for state aid and playing down speculation that the lossmaking German bank should merge.

title: Defensive stocks top 2019 playbooks
description: Perceived safe havens like utilities and consumer staples, often an afterthought in Wall Street's cascade of year-ahead investment recommendations each December, are emerging as top picks as stocks limp into 2019.

title: China willing to work with U.S. to implement Argentina talks agreement: Foreign Ministry
description: China is willing to work with the United States to implement the consensus reached during talks between the two countries' leaders in Argentina, the Chinese foreign ministry said in a statement on Sunday.

title: Wall Street may gain Monday but unlikely to mute December losses
description: Investors could see one last boost to Wall Street stocks in the final trading session of the year on Monday, but they do not expect gains to offset losses in the worst December since the 1930s.

title: Amazon to expand Whole Foods stores: Wall Street Journal
description: Amazon.com Inc  is planning to expand its Whole Foods Market portfolio by adding more stores to put more customers within its two-hour delivery service range, the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday, citing sources.

title: Pacific trade pact takes off with tariffs cut in six nations
description: A landmark 11-country trade deal, a revamped version of the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP), came into force on Sunday with New Zealand's trade minister hailing the opportunities it presented for exporters.

title: Dell returns to market with NYSE listing
description: Dell Technologies Inc  returned to public markets on Friday, nearly six years after the company's founder and Chief Executive Officer Michael Dell took it private in what was then the biggest buyout since the financial crisis of 2008.

title: Rusal appoints independent director as new board chairman
description: Russian aluminum company Rusal said on Friday it has appointed independent non-executive director Jean-Pierre Thomas as its new chairman as part of an agreed restructuring in exchange for the lifting of U.S. sanctions.

title: Third prototype of China's C919 jet completes first test flight
description: A third prototype of China's home-built C919 narrowbody passenger jet completed its first test flight on Friday, its manufacturer said, in another step forward in the nation's push to become a global civil aerospace player.

title: Rosneft to buy at least 6 million tonnes of oil for $2 billion in 2019
description: Russia's largest oil producer Rosneft  will buy around 6 million tonnes of oil worth over $2 billion from domestic producers next year, according to an announcement on a state-owned website for purchases of companies' needs.

title: Tough to stop Nord Stream 2 now it's being built - EU's Oettinger
description: U.S. President Donald Trump's criticism of the Russian-backed Nord Stream 2 pipeline is no reason to stop the project and any attempt to do so would be difficult now that it is being built, European Commissioner Guenther Oettinger said.

title: Germany paves way for upgrading exhaust systems on older diesel cars
description: Germany on Friday cleared away legal hurdles for carmakers to upgrade exhaust emissions filtering systems on older diesel cars as a way to avoid vehicle bans, but failed to quell doubts among manufacturers and suppliers over the effectiveness of retrofits.

title: Nissan to make fewer cars in China in months ahead as demand slows: source
description: Nissan Motor Co  will produce 30,000 fewer vehicles in the coming months in China than what it had planned, a person briefed on the matter told Reuters, as global automakers grapple with falling demand in the world's biggest car market.

title: HKMA fines JPMorgan Hong Kong branch over anti-money laundering lapses
description: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) said on Friday that it had fined the Hong Kong branch of JPMorgan Chase & Co  HK$12.5 million ($1.60 million) and reprimanded it for breaching anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing rules.

title: Citi cuts Q1 iPhone production estimates on weak demand

title: Take Five: The Year of the Bear! World markets themes for the week ahead

title: Yankees in talks with Amazon, Sinclair to bid for Yes Network: WSJ
description: The New York Yankees are in talks with Amazon.com Inc and Sinclair Broadcast Group Inc about a joint bid for the team's regional sports network, Yes, the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.

title: Wells Fargo to pay $575 million in settlement with U.S. states

title: Wall Street rally pauses, but stocks mint weekly gain

title: Britain's HMV faces the music as retailer calls in administrators
description: Music retailer HMV said on Friday it was calling in the administrators, blaming a worsening market for entertainment CDs and DVDs, to become the latest victim of brutal trading conditions in Britain's retail sector.

title: Oil prices steady near year-and-a-half lows ahead of New Year
description: Oil prices steadied on Friday after a week of volatile trading ahead of the New Year holiday, supported by a rise in U.S. equity markets but pressured by worries about a global glut of crude.

title: Sears Chair Lampert makes $4.4 billion bid to keep retailer alive
description: Sears Holdings Corp Chairman Eddie Lampert submitted a $4.4 billion takeover bid for the bankrupt U.S. retailer, representing its only chance of escaping liquidation and laying off tens of thousands of workers, a spokesman for the billionaire's hedge fund said on Friday.

description: Fresh misconduct allegations brought by Tokyo prosecutors against ousted Nissan Chairman Carlos Ghosn center on the use of company funds to pay a Saudi businessman who is believed to have helped him out of financial difficulties, two company sources with knowledge of the matter said.

description: The U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Economic Analysis and Census Bureau will not publish economic data during the ongoing partial government shutdown, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday, citing an agency spokeswoman.

title: China's draft foreign investment law bans forced tech transfer, emphasizes reciprocity
description: China has proposed a ban on forced technology transfer and illegal government "interference" in foreign business operations, practices that have come under the spotlight in a trade dispute with the United States.

description: Hong Kong-based activist fund Argyle Street Management asked Japan's Toshiba Corp  on Thursday to exit more non-core businesses such as office machinery company Toshiba TEC  to bolster margins of the once-mighty conglomerate.

description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) plans to meet top-level executives of e-cigarette makers, the agency's chief said on Thursday, hinting that some companies seem to be backing away from commitments related to youth's access to e-cigarettes.

description: France's Vinci  is taking advantage of a Brexit hit to UK asset prices to buy a majority stake in Britain's second-busiest airport, London's Gatwick, for 2.9 billion pounds ($3.7 billion), the construction company said on Thursday.

description: Tesla Inc  has registered a financial leasing company in China, a local business registration filing shows, in the latest sign the U.S. electric car maker is attempting to speed up its push into China.

description: France's CGT union has called for more transparency at Renault  and its Dutch holding company and asked the French government, one of the carmaker's shareholders, to try to shed light on its workings, a CGT representative said on Thursday.

description: Lockheed Martin Corp  has been awarded a $712 million U.S. defense contract for the development of advanced hardware in support of the F-35 Lightning II aircraft, the Pentagon said on Thursday.

description: Mexico's government unveiled a plan on Thursday to step up use of the armed forces to combat fuel theft, vowing to root out corrupt officials it says are largely responsible for a problem that has cost the country billions of dollars.

description: U.S. cannabis retailer Green Growth Brands Ltd  said on Thursday it would make a hostile takeover bid for Aphria Inc  in an all-stock deal valuing the Canadian pot producer at C$2.8 billion ($2.06 billion).

description: U.S. stocks roared back to end in positive territory on Thursday following steep losses for much of the session, as equities rebounded for a second day.

title: Drop in U.S. consumer confidence stokes fears of economic slowdown
description: A measure of U.S. consumer confidence posted its sharpest decline in more than three years in December, rattling investors already nervous about the prospect that a global economic slowdown was spilling over into the United States.

description: A wild Christmas week ride in global markets continued on Thursday as stocks rallied from significant losses to post gains for the day.

title: Exclusive: Foxconn to begin assembling top-end Apple iPhones in India in 2019 - source

title: New Mexico oil producers brace for tighter regulation as output jumps
description: Crude oil output has more than doubled in New Mexico over the last four years, making it the No. 3 producer among U.S. states, but a January change in state leadership to Democratic control has industry executives fearing tougher regulations are coming.

description: Venezuela cocoa trader Freddy Galindo has battled highway robberies, kidnappings of family members and declining quality in his 19 years exporting the nation's legendary beans.

description: Chile will delay a previously announced arbitration with Albemarle Corp , the world's top lithium producer, in anticipation that the U.S.-based miner will make a new offer to bring it into compliance with a 2016 contract, a source close to the negotiations told Reuters.

description: Oil surged on Wednesday, posting its strongest daily gain in more than two years in a partial rebound from steep losses that pushed crude benchmarks to lows not seen since 2017.

description: Iran said on Wednesday private exporters have had "no problems" selling Iranian oil, and 3 million barrels of crude could be sold soon to non-government traders, state media reported, despite U.S. sanctions targeting Tehran's oil sales.

description: Russian aluminum company Rusal said on Wednesday that board chairman Matthias Warnig resigned as part of a restructuring it agreed to implement in exchange for a waiver from U.S. sanctions.

title: Brazil judge overturns injunction that blocked Embraer-Boeing deal
description: A Brazilian judge overturned on Friday a decision that put the brakes on planemaker Embraer's  proposed sale of 80 percent of its commercial aviation division to Boeing Co , as the judicial back-and-forth surrounding the deal continued.

title: Credit Suisse chairman says on track to boost equity return: media
description: Cost cuts and closing a unit where Credit Suisse  had parked underperforming assets will help boost return on tangible equity (ROTE) to at least 10 percent in 2019, Chairman Urs Rohner said in an interview published on Saturday.

title: As FAANG stocks falter, fund managers make bets on survivors
description: A bear market in the so-called FAANG stocks - Wall Street's most popular trade going into the year - is pushing fund managers into searching for the next big growth companies that can lead the overall market higher.

title: Mnuchin says Trump told him he 'never suggested firing' Fed chairman
description: U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin said on Saturday that President Donald Trump told him he had "never suggested firing" the chairman of the U.S. Federal Reserve.

title: Trump has discussed firing Fed Chairman Powell: sources
description: U.S. President Donald Trump has privately discussed the possibility of firing Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell, a move that could roil already volatile financial markets, two sources familiar with situation said on Saturday.

title: Judge accepts CVS offer on Aetna while reviewing consent decree
description: A U.S. federal judge reviewing an agreement between the government and CVS Health Corp  allowing it to buy health insurer Aetna has indicated that he will not halt most integration between the two companies.

title: Japan Inc exit from nuclear exports would leave field to Russia, China
description: The possible withdrawal of Japanese conglomerates from nuclear export projects in Britain and Turkey would leave the nuclear newbuild industry open to Russian and Chinese state-owned companies as Western private firms struggle to compete.

title: Political stumbles, savvy activists knock Canada's oil sector to its knees
description: A decade ago, Canada's oil sector was growing so fast it was predicted to become a global energy superpower, but a series of political missteps and formidable environmental activism has created a dysfunctional system requiring OPEC-style government intervention to move its oil to market.

title: Exclusive: Nigerian energy sector's crippling debts delay next power plant
description: Plans to build another privately-financed power station in Nigeria to help end decades of chronic blackouts have been delayed because of concerns about persistent shortfalls in payments for electricity across the sector.

title: Volkswagen to write off Gett investment - Spiegel
description: German carmaker Volkswagen  will write off its investment in Gett after the Israel-based ride hailing app failed to gain ground on bigger rivals Uber [UBER.UL], Lyft and Didi, weekly Der Spiegel reported on Friday.

title: Ford recalling 874,000 pickup trucks in North America for fire risks
description: Ford Motor Co  said Friday it is recalling 874,000 pickup trucks in North America with engine block heaters for fire risks.

title: Tencent shares spike as China watchdog flags video game approvals
description: Tencent Holdings Ltd's shares surged on Friday after a local regulatory official said some new video games had been cleared for sale, ending a lengthy freeze in approvals that has spooked players in the world's largest gaming market.

title: Futures extend slide on growth fears, government shutdown threat
description: S&P 500 e-minis logged their biggest losing streak in seven years on Friday, dropping about 0.6 percent on growing worries of slowing global growth and the threat of a U.S. government shutdown.

title: Foxconn to build $9 billion chip plant in China with local govt: Nikkei
description: Taiwan's Foxconn , Apple Inc's  iPhone assembler, is in the final stages of talks with the local government of the Chinese city of Zhuhai to build a chip plant there with a total investment of about $9 billion, the Nikkei business daily reported on Friday.

title: German retailer Kaufland drops Unilever products over price rises
description: The German food retailer Kaufland on Friday said that it was dropping Unilever  products from its shelves to protest against price increases.

title: Want to sue Venezuela for millions? These firms can help, for a price
description: As Venezuela collapses, one little-known U.S. investment fund is poised to win big from litigation against its socialist government: Tenor Capital Management.

title: Ghosn re-arrested on fresh allegations, likely to spend Christmas in detention
description: Japanese prosecutors arrested Nissan Motor Co Ltd's  ousted chairman Carlos Ghosn again on Friday on new allegations of making Nissan shoulder $16.6 million in personal investment losses, dashing chances he would be released on bail before Christmas.

title: Explainer: Arrested again: What are the new allegations against Nissan's Ghosn?
description: Japanese prosecutors arrested Nissan's  ousted chairman Carlos Ghosn for a third time on Friday, accusing him of aggravated breach of trust in transferring personal investment losses to the automaker.

title: SoftBank's Vision Fund nearing $1.5 billion investment in SE Asia's Grab: source
description: SoftBank Group Corp  is nearing a deal to invest $1.5 billion in Grab, three times a previously expected $500 million, as Southeast Asia's biggest ride-hailing firm looks to expand, a person with knowledge of the matter said.

title: Massages and free fish help east Europe tackle labor shortages
description: What's does a company do when it doesn't have enough workers and unemployment rates are at record lows? In eastern Europe answers includes workplace massages, free carp for Christmas and guaranteed jobs for spouses.

title: Toshiba has no immediate plans to sell memory chip stake: CEO
description: Toshiba Corp  has no immediate plans to sell its 40.2 percent stake in Toshiba Memory Corp, its chief executive told Reuters, as the world's No. 2 producer of NAND flash memory chips prepares to go public within the next three years.

title: Crude refusal: China shuns U.S. oil despite trade war truce
description: China, the world's top oil importer, is set to start 2019 buying little or no crude from the United States despite a three-month truce in a trade scrap between the two nations, with relatively high freight costs and political uncertainty choking demand.

title: China poised to buy more U.S. soybeans: sources
description: China plans to make a third round of U.S. soybean purchases within days, two sources familiar with the matter said on Thursday, after a trade war truce between Washington and Beijing this month triggered two waves of buying.

title: Exclusive: Bangladesh says to collect, test samples of Johnson & Johnson Baby Powder
description: Bangladesh will collect and test samples of Johnson & Johnson's  Baby Powder for asbestos in a couple of days, its main testing authority said on Friday, after a Reuters report last Friday that the firm knew for decades that cancer-causing asbestos could be found in the product.

title: Factbox: How man-made diamonds have grown to threaten natural gems
description: The growing acceptance of man-made diamonds by millennials has spurred De Beers to reverse its policy of shunning the sector for jewelry and to launch its own laboratory-grown diamonds through its Lightbox jewelry brand.

title: Keeping on truckin': DHL seeks to counter driver shortages
description: Faced with a chronic shortage of truck drivers, logistics firm Deutsche Post DHL Group  is trialing a new scheme to get more people behind the wheel so it can keep goods flowing across Europe, especially at peak times like Christmas.

title: Indian regulator orders J&J to stop using raw material to make Baby Powder in India
description: India's drugs regulator has ordered Johnson & Johnson  to stop manufacturing its Baby Powder using raw materials in two of its Indian factories until test results prove they are free of asbestos, a senior official said on Thursday.

title: U.S. auto sales seen falling 1 percent in Dec - J.D. Power, LMC
description: The pace of U.S. vehicle sales is set to slow for the sixth straight month in December despite aggressive discounts from manufacturers, according to industry consultants J.D. Power and LMC Automotive.

title: U.S. third-quarter economic growth revised down to 3.4 percent
description: The U.S. economy slowed in the third quarter a bit more than previously estimated, but the pace was likely strong enough to keep growth on track to hit the Trump administration's 3 percent target this year, even as momentum appears to have moderated further early in the fourth quarter.

title: Take Five: Bear-y Christmas! World markets themes for the week ahead
description: Following are five big themes likely to dominate thinking of investors and traders in the coming week and the Reuters stories related to them.

title: Exclusive: Global traders halt new Iran food deals as U.S. sanctions bite - sources
description: Cargill, Bunge and other global traders have halted food supply deals with Iran because new U.S. sanctions have paralyzed banking systems required to secure payments, industry and Iranian government sources say.

title: Citi regional executives get new responsibilities in 2019
description: Citigroup Inc  has divided up the roles of outgoing North America Chief Executive Bill Mills, according to an internal memo seen by Reuters.

title: JD.com CEO will not face assault charges in Minnesota
description: Minnesota prosecutors will not charge the billionaire chief executive officer of China's JD.com Inc, Richard Liu, after he was accused of rape by a University of Minnesota student during a recent U.S. visit, authorities said on Friday.

title: Nasdaq confirms bear market; economic worries sink Wall Street
description: Wall Street stocks fell sharply in volatile trading on Friday, with the Nasdaq confirming it is in a bear market, as concerns of slowing economic growth led investors to flee stocks in high-valuation sectors such as technology and communication services.

title: Incoming Campbell Soup CEO Clouse to be paid up to $7.4 million in 2019
description: Campbell Soup Co  said on Friday that incoming Chief Executive Mark Clouse, a food industry veteran, could be paid as much as $7.4 million in compensation for fiscal 2019.

title: Nasdaq in bear market, first of the three major U.S. indexes
description: The Nasdaq Composite Index  confirmed on Friday it is in a bear market for the first time since 2008, underscoring fears that the longest bull run in history for U.S. stocks could soon be over.

title: Factbox: Past Nasdaq bear markets lasted long and cut deep
description: On Friday, the Nasdaq Composite  closed almost 22 percent below its record high daily close on Aug. 29, signaling a nearly nine-and-a-half year bull market run for the index ended in late summer.

title: Wells Fargo moves jobs abroad after U.S. layoffs, government says
description: Wells Fargo & Co.  has been hiring overseas after pledging to eliminate thousands of jobs, according to a Department of Labor investigation.

title: Automakers boost Takata air bag recall completion rates
description: Automakers in the United States repaired more than 7.2 million defective Takata air bag inflators in 2018, as companies have ramped up efforts to track down parts in need of replacement, a report from an independent monitor released on Friday said.

title: Boeing heads for expected 2018 plane order victory over Airbus
description: Boeing Co  looked poised to beat European arch-rival Airbus for aircraft orders in 2018 by a wide margin after clinching billions of dollars in new business from Nigeria's Green Africa Airways and Saudi Arabia's flyadeal.

title: Goldman Sachs CEO to employees: our compliance is strong
description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc Chief Executive David Solomon on Friday defended the bank against criticism of its compliance and oversight related to dealings with the sovereign wealth fund 1MDB, according to a message sent to employees obtained by Reuters.

title: Dollar rallies from post-Fed losses as U.S. shutdown likely
description: The dollar gained on Friday as investors sought the currency's safety amid persistent equity market volatility and a possible U.S. government shutdown.

title: China's HNA in talks to sell Ingram Micro to Apollo Global: source
description: HNA Group Co [HNAIRC.UL] is in talks to sell Ingram Micro Inc to private equity firm Apollo Global Management Llc , a source familiar with the matter said on Friday, as the Chinese conglomerate continues to scale back operations.

title: Williams soothes markets, says Fed listening and could change policy
description: The Federal Reserve is listening to the concerns of markets and open to changing its policy views next year, one its most influential members said on Friday, even while he stood by plans for interest-rate hikes and further paring of the Fed's bond portfolio.

title: Nike shares rise as strong quarterly results allay China demand concerns
description: Nike Inc  shares rose 9 percent on Friday, after the company's solid quarterly results eased worries that escalating trade tensions between Washington and Beijing would weigh on China demand and hurt the sportswear maker's growth story.

title: Biotech swoon adds to Nasdaq's pain as bear market looms ever closer
description: As the Nasdaq Composite  continues to stumble its way toward a bear market, biotech shares are worsening the collapse of the tech-heavy index.

title: Lab-grown diamond prices slide as De Beers fights back
description: Since De Beers abandoned its decades-old policy of refusing to sell lab-grown diamonds as jewelery, the price gap between man-made stones and natural gems has widened - and the difference is set to get even bigger.

title: Zynga buys Empires & Puzzles gamemaker in largest deal to date
description: (This corrects paragraph 7 of December 20 story to say Zynga acquired a unit of Peak Games, and not the entire company. The error also appeared in an earlier version)

title: French court fines oil group Total in Iran bribery case
description: A Paris court fined French oil and gas group Total  500,000 euros ($570,000) on Friday for bribing foreign public officials in a case related to Iranian contracts in 1997.

title: EU watchdog to rule on data exchange among market regulators
description: The European Union's data watchdog will decide in coming weeks if financial regulators around the world can routinely swap information to keep markets clean without getting tangled up in the EU's new data protection regime.

title: Exclusive: Mitsui, Saudi Aramco, Russia's RDIF in talks to buy Arctic LNG 2 stakes - sources
description: Japan's Mitsui & Co Ltd , Russian sovereign wealth fund RDIF and Saudi Aramco are in talks to buy stakes in Novatek's  Arctic LNG 2 project, with the size of the investments still to be decided, sources familiar with the talks told Reuters.

title: Global stock indexes slide as U.S. government shutdown looms
description: World stock markets continued a week-long sell-off on Friday as the threat of a U.S. government shutdown and further hikes in U.S. borrowing costs compounded investor anxiety that global economic growth is slowing.

title: U.S. third-quarter growth trimmed; business spending slowing
description: The U.S. economy slowed slightly more than previously estimated in the third quarter and momentum appears to have moderated further in the fourth quarter, with new orders and shipments of manufactured capital goods falling in November.

title: U.S. weekly jobless claims rise less than expected
description: WASHINGTON (Reuters - The number of Americans filing applications for jobless benefits rose marginally from near a 49-year low last week, suggesting underlying strength in the labor market and broader economy.

title: Walgreens' cost-cut plans aim to save more than $1 billion annually
description: Walgreens Boots Alliance Inc  said on Thursday it would consolidate warehouses and shut some stores as part of a cost-cutting plan aimed at saving more than $1 billion annually.

title: Spooked global funds drive up cash and bond holdings
description: Spooked by another worldwide stocks selloff, global investors have piled up cash to a more than two-year high this month, hoovered up bonds and cut back property holdings.

title: Embraer to pay out $1.6-1.7 billion in extraordinary dividends: paper
description: Brazilian planemaker Embraer SA  is planning to distribute $1.6 billion to $1.7 billion in extraordinary dividends to shareholders, using proceeds from its recent deal with Boeing Co , the Valor Econômico newspaper reported on Thursday.

title: Tokyo court's ruling clears way for possible release of ex-Nissan boss Ghosn
description: A Tokyo court unexpectedly ruled not to extend the detention of Nissan's ex-chairman Carlos Ghosn on Thursday, meaning he may soon be released from jail where he has been since last month facing allegations of financial misconduct.

title: Bombardier delivers Global 7500 jet as corporate travel race intensifies
description: Canada's Bombardier Inc will deliver its first Global 7500 corporate jet on Thursday, premiering a full-sized bed and optional en-suite shower, in a challenge to U.S. planemaker Gulfstream at the top of the luxury jet market.

title: German court rules Apple infringed Qualcomm patent
description: A German court ruled on Thursday that iPhone maker Apple Inc  infringed a hardware patent of Qualcomm Inc  and said the U.S. company could no longer sell some iPhone models in Germany which contain a particular component.

title: Signs of trouble so far just noise to a Fed that sees growth continuing
description: Late fall brought a dust cloud of bad news for the U.S. economy, with shippers like Fedex cutting their global outlook for next year, chipmaker Micron Technology missing its revenue target as demand slides worldwide, and GM trimming 14,000 jobs as sales slow, not to mention a stock market limping into year end.

title: U.S. weekly jobless claims rise; mid-Atlantic factory activity slows
description: The number of Americans filing applications for jobless benefits rose marginally from near a 49-year low last week, suggesting underlying strength in the labor market and broader economy.

title: Airbus shares fall after report of U.S. joining corruption probe
description: Shares in Europe's Airbus  fell sharply on Thursday after Le Monde newspaper reported the United States had opened an investigation into allegations of corruption, raising the stakes of probes already under way in Britain and France.

title: Twitter Inc: Falls on short-seller Citron Research's report
description: - Shares of social media company Twitter down 11.3 percent at $29.22; set for its biggest one-day percent fall in nearly five months

title: J&J loses bid to have $4.7 billion talc verdict set aside, vows to appeal
description: Johnson & Johnson failed to persuade a Missouri trial judge to set aside a July verdict awarding a record $4.69 billion to 22 women who blamed their ovarian cancer on asbestos in the company's Baby Powder and other talc products.

title: Lockheed Martin reaches 2018 F-35 delivery target of 91 jets
description: Lockheed Martin Corp  said on Thursday it has reached its 2018 target to deliver 91 F-35 fighter jets to the United States and its allies, as the defense contractor built 38 percent more jets this year.

title: Uber resuming self-driving car testing in Pennsylvania
description: Uber Technologies Inc [UBER.UL] on Thursday is resuming limited self-driving car testing on public roads in Pittsburgh, nine months after it suspended the program following a deadly accident in Arizona.

title: Tokyo court rejects prosecutors' appeal against decision not to extend Ghosn's detention: media
description: A Tokyo court upheld a decision not to extend the detention of former Nissan Motor Chairman Carlos Ghosn and former Representative Director Greg Kelly, public broadcaster NHK said on Thursday, a move that brings them closer to a release on bail.

title: Asia's central banks have almost no reasons to hike rates in 2019
description: Weaker economic growth and tepid price pressures in Asia will leave central banks in the region with few reasons to tighten policy next year -- especially as U.S. rate hikes slow -- unless a new bout of currency weakness forces them to do so.

title: Investors association asks for tender offer in Boeing-Embraer deal
description: Brazilian investors' association Abradin has filed a motion with a São Paulo court questioning the legality of a tie-up between U.S. planemaker Boeing Co  and Embraer SA .

title: China says more trade talks with U.S. planned for January
description: China and the United States will hold more talks on trade in January, China said on Thursday, following detailed discussions about the issues to be tacked in the negotiations.

title: U.S. aims to present figures on impact of tariffs in mid-January: report
description: The U.S. Commerce Department plans to present new calculations on the impact that tariffs on foreign cars would have on the U.S. market in four weeks' time, a German magazine reported on Thursday.

title: Film studios and Sky offer to end anti-competitive movie deals
description: NBCUniversal, Sony Pictures, Warner Bros and Sky have offered to end anti-competitive movie licensing deals in a bid to stop an antitrust investigation, regulators said on Thursday, after Paramount and Disney made similar concessions.

title: Exclusive: Big Pharma returning to U.S. price hikes in January after pause
description: Novartis AG  and Bayer AG  are among nearly 30 drugmakers that have taken steps to raise the U.S. prices of their medicines in January, ending a self-declared halt to increases made by a pharma industry under pressure from the Trump administration, according to documents seen by Reuters.

title: J&J says Indian drug regulators visited facilities, took talc samples
description: Indian drug authorities visited some of Johnson & Johnson's  facilities on Wednesday and took "tests and samples" of its talcum powder, the company said in a statement.

title: Amazon error allowed Alexa user to eavesdrop on another home
description: A user of Amazon's  Alexa voice assistant in Germany got access to more than a thousand recordings from another user because of "a human error" by the company.

title: Airbus tests market for A321XLR jet launch by mid-2019: sources
description: Airbus  is talking to airlines about a longer-range version of its best-selling narrowbody jet family with a view to launching it by mid-2019 as it tries to head off a potential Boeing competitor, people familiar with the matter said.

title: Truckmaker Volvo builds safety stockpiles to prepare for no-deal Brexit
description: Sweden's AB Volvo  has triggered its hard Brexit contingency plans, with the truckmaker building "safety stock" with its British dealers and considering alternative shipping routes to minimize disruption.

title: Ten years on, Belgium drops case against Fortis ex-directors
description: Belgian prosecutors have dropped their case against former directors of Fortis, 10 years after the Belgian-Dutch bank's collapse during the global financial crisis.

title: Brazil judge again blocks Boeing-Embraer tie-up as deal nears close
description: A Brazilian judge on Thursday issued his second injunction blocking the proposed sale of 80 percent of planemaker Embraer's  commercial aviation division to Boeing Co , as attempts to stop the deal intensified while the two companies neared closing the transaction.

title: Recharge: LG and Samsung take heart as China flags more open car battery market
description: For automotive battery makers LG Chem Ltd  and Samsung SDI Co Ltd , the Chinese market has begun to offer promise after painful loss-making investments.

title: Aluminum plunges, Rusal shares soar as U.S. to lift sanctions
description: The U.S. Treasury said it will lift sanctions on the core empire of Russian businessman Oleg Deripaska, including aluminum giant Rusal and its parent En+, watering down the toughest penalties imposed since Moscow's 2014 annexation of Crimea.

title: Novartis appoints Susanne Schaffert to lead oncology business
description: Novartis  said it appointed company veteran Susanne Schaffert to lead its oncology unit from Jan. 1, replacing Liz Barrett who is stepping down to return to the United States.

title: Amazon to lower some fees for third-party sellers
description: Amazon.com Inc is going to lower some fees it charges third-party sellers on its marketplace, the company said on Thursday.

title: North America, online sales power Nike's quarterly results beat
description: Nike Inc's  quarterly results beat Wall Street estimates, boosted by strength in North America where new launches led to higher sale of more full-priced footwear and apparel online, sending its shares up 7 percent on Thursday.

title: ETFs, major supporter of U.S. stock market, stop buying the dip
description: There is no more mistletoe hanging above the markets.

title: FCC fines Swarm $900,000 for unauthorized satellite launch
description: Swarm Technologies Inc will pay a $900,000 fine for launching and operating four small experimental communications satellites that risked "satellite collisions" and threatened "critical commercial and government satellite operations," the Federal Communications Commission said on Thursday.

title: Dealmakers brace for slowdown after third-strongest M&A year
description: Dealmakers celebrating their third-strongest year on record are fretting 2019 will herald a steep drop in mergers and acquisitions worldwide, as market jitters and economic uncertainty take their toll.

title: ExxonMobil shelves Canada LNG export project
description: U.S. oil major Exxon Mobil Corp has withdrawn its WCC liquefied natural gas (LNG) export terminal in Canada from the environmental assessment process, it said on Thursday, signaling that the project has been shelved.

title: Hyundai to open car plant in Indonesia, to build EVs: minister
description: Hyundai Motor Co  plans to start producing electric vehicles (EVs) in Indonesia as part of an around $880 million auto investment in the country, the deputy minister for industry said on Thursday.

title: Exclusive: China hacked HPE, IBM and then attacked clients - sources
description: Hackers working on behalf of China's Ministry of State Security breached the networks of Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co and IBM, then used the access to hack into their clients' computers, according to five sources familiar with the attacks.

title: Nissan's Ghosn re-arrested: media
description: Japanese prosecutors have re-arrested Nissan Motor Co's  ousted chairman Carlos Ghosn for aggravated breach of trust, which means he could be detained for another 10 days, media reported on Friday.

title: Nasdaq goes bear as momentum plays run out of gas
description: Investors are finding out that it is not all puppies and unicorns when it comes to momentum plays, in a painful lesson as the Nasdaq tumbles to the edge of a bear market.

title: Apple changes how it reports U.S. national security requests
description: Apple Inc  on Thursday changed how it reports on U.S. national security requests for user data, bringing its procedures more in line with those of technology rivals such as Microsoft Corp  and Alphabet Inc's  Google.

title: Asia M&A clocks second best on record, strength to persist despite trade troubles
description: Asia Pacific M&A volumes clocked their second-highest level on record this year and dealmakers are optimistic the momentum will persist into 2019, with inbound deals into China emerging as a strong theme amid political and macroeconomic headwinds.

title: Hong Kong takes global IPO crown, looks to a quieter 2019
description: A flurry of initial public offerings (IPOs) in Hong Kong propelled the financial center to first place for IPO volumes globally, but next year is unlikely to see as many big-ticket listings.

title: Altria to buy $12.8 billion minority stake in e-cigarette company Juul
description: Marlboro cigarette maker Altria Group Inc  will buy a 35 percent stake in Juul Labs Inc for $12.8 billion, a marriage between an old-line tobacco giant and a fast-growing electronic-cigarette rival looking to make inroads among smokers.

title: Global banks chase Asia techs transaction business, as trade war rumbles
description: Global lenders including Citigroup  and HSBC  are stepping up efforts to sell day-to-day banking services to Asia's fast-growing new technology firms, amid growing competition for more traditional transaction banking.

title: Campbell Soup names industry veteran Mark Clouse as new CEO
description: Campbell Soup Co  named Mark Clouse, the former CEO of Pinnacle Foods, as its new chief executive on Thursday, a key step in the U.S. company's efforts to regain market share and boost profits.

title: Exclusive: U.S. Air Force to take delivery of Boeing tanker by year end, sources
description: The U.S. Air Force will take its first delivery this month of the long-delayed KC-46 aerial refueling tanker made by Boeing Co , people familiar with the process said.

title: Wall St. slides on Fed plans; Nasdaq flirts with bear territory
description: U.S. stocks slid on Thursday, with the Nasdaq on the cusp of confirming bear market territory, as the Federal Reserve's plan to continue its balance sheet reduction and the threat of a partial government shutdown fueled investor anxieties.

title: Mitsubishi seeks dismissal of Bombardier trade secrets case
description: A trade secrets lawsuit brought by Canada's Bombardier Inc against the aircraft unit of Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Ltd should be dismissed because the allegations are baseless and designed to "disrupt development" of a rival jet, a spokesman for the Japanese company said on Thursday.

title: Boeing, Sikorsky wins $1.1 billion U.S. defense contract: Pentagon
description: Boeing Co  and Sikorsky Aircraft, a unit of Lockheed Martin Corp , have been awarded a $1.1 billion U.S. defense contract for contractor support for MH-6, MH-47, and MH-60 aircraft, the Pentagon said on Thursday.

title: GM to respond by January 7 to Canada union efforts to save plant
description: General Motors Co will respond by Jan. 7 to a Canadian union's proposals for keeping an Ontario auto assembly plant open, the head of Canada's largest private sector union said on Thursday.

title: Lockheed Martin wins $997 million U.S. defense contract: Pentagon
description: Lockheed Martin Corp  has been awarded a $997 million U.S. defense contract for the upgrade of 84 F-16 aircraft to the V-configuration, the Pentagon said on Thursday.

title: U.S. senators write to regulators on Robinhood's botched checking plans
description: A bipartisan group of U.S. senators sent a letter to regulators on Thursday expressing concern that financial technology startup Robinhood may not be offering full transparency to its customers over the botched launch of its new cash management service.

title: Treasury chief calls market reaction to Fed 'overblown'
description: U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin said on Thursday that investors' reaction to the Federal Reserve's interest rate hikes was "completely overblown", in an unusually direct comment on financial market activity.

title: Equities slide as Fed heightens worry over growth slowdown
description: World equity markets continued a week-long slide on Thursday, one day after the U.S. Federal Reserve indicated it was set on its path to hike interest rates next year despite signs that global economic growth is stuttering.

title: Russian tycoon in GAZ sanctions talks; investors get more time
description: Oleg Deripaska's team, which secured the lifting of U.S. sanctions on the Russian tycoon's aluminum and energy businesses, is also working to get them removed from his automaker GAZ , five sources close to the talks said.

title: U.S. bank regulators sign off on 'living wills' for foreign banks
description: U.S. banking regulators announced on Thursday they had signed off on "living wills" for four foreign banks - Barclays  , Credit Suisse , Deutsche Bank  and UBS  - detailing how they could safely be dissolved in a crisis.

title: Musk, GM weigh fate of Ohio plant Trump wants saved
description: Tesla Inc  Chief Executive Elon Musk raised hopes again on Thursday that he could ride to the rescue of a threatened General Motors Co  car plant at the center of a political storm about auto jobs, and GM replied, saying the Ohio factory's fate depends on union talks next year.

title: Nasdaq drop leaves it just shy of bear market
description: The Nasdaq Composite Index , known for its high-profile technology and internet companies, closed no more than a rounding error from bear market territory on Thursday.

title: Oil prices tumble to lowest in more than a year as equities sell off
description: Oil prices fell about 5 percent on Thursday, hitting their lowest level in more than a year on worries about oversupply and the outlook for energy demand as a U.S. interest rate rise knocked stock markets.

title: Trump tariff war with China sends U.S. retailers on buying binge
description: In the nearly 40 years she has spent in trade, Amy Magnus has never seen retailers hoarding so much inventory.

title: Nissan to lay off 1,000 Mexican workers, cites market challenges
description: Japanese carmaker Nissan Motor Co Ltd  will lay off about 1,000 workers in Mexico at two factories, citing "challenging market conditions," the company said on Thursday.

title: Raytheon wins $568 million U.S. defense contract: Pentagon
description: Raytheon Co  was awarded a $568 million defense contract for modifications to a Patriot missile defense system it is building as part of a foreign military sale to Sweden, the Pentagon said on Thursday.

title: Facebook's lead EU regulator 'assessing' NYT report on data sharing
description: Facebook's  lead regulator in the European Union on Wednesday said it was assessing a report in the New York Times that the social network allowed some tech companies far greater access to data than it had disclosed.

title: Volkswagen buys Volvo's connected car unit for $122 million
description: Volkswagen (VW)  is buying a controlling stake in Volvo's  WirelessCar, a digital service developer specializing in connected driving, for 1.1 billion Swedish crowns ($122 million), the companies said on Wednesday.

title: Travel agents seek EU antitrust probe into Lufthansa pricing
description: A group whose members include Amadeus  and Expedia , stepped up their fight against German airline Lufthansa  on Wednesday, urging EU regulators to investigate booking fees it levies on travel agents.

title: Daimler told regulators about coolant-related recall: kfz-betrieb
description: Daimler  told European regulators late last month that it will have to recall 127,847 Mercedes vehicles to replace the R134a coolant, trade publication kfz-betrieb reported on Wednesday, not citing the source of its information.

title: General Mills second-quarter profit jumps on tighter costs, price hikes
description: General Mills Inc  reported a quarterly profit above Wall Street estimates on Wednesday as the maker of Cheerios cereal  raised prices and eked out higher margins from cost savings.

title: Altria nears Juul stake deal, valuing it at $38 billion: sources
description: Marlboro cigarette maker Altria Group Inc  is nearing an agreement to buy more than a third of Juul Labs Inc, valuing the e-cigarette startup at $38 billion, people familiar with the matter said on Wednesday.

title: Facebook says companies got access to data only after user permission
description: Facebook Inc  said it did not give companies access to personal data of users without their permission, after the New York Times reported on Tuesday that the social network allowed some tech giants far greater access to data than it had disclosed.

title: FedEx shares drop as economic slowdown prompts 2019 profit forecast cut
description: Shares of FedEx Corp  fell nearly 8 percent on Wednesday, after the delivery package company jolted investors with a steeper-than-expected cut in its 2019 profit forecast warning of weakening freight demand as the global economy slows.

title: SoftBank telco suffers $9 billion slump on debut after record IPO
description: SoftBank Corp  shares sank 15 percent on debut, wiping $9 billion off their value, as investors sold off the telecoms operator after its record IPO on worries about a recent service outage and its exposure to Chinese telecoms gear maker Huawei.

title: Data problems complicate U.S. regulator's watch over ratings firms
description: A decade since the global financial crisis, the U.S. securities regulator is still struggling to get a grip on the country's rating agencies because it lacks the tools and expertise needed to crunch growing reams of ratings data, people familiar with the effort say.

title: Malaysia charges another ex-Goldman Sachs banker over 1MDB
description: Malaysia on Wednesday charged a second former banker at Goldman Sachs Group Inc  in connection with a suspected money-laundering scheme at state fund 1MDB and said it had issued a summons to the bank.

title: Morgan Stanley moves to speed up collaboration with tech startups
description: Morgan Stanley is simplifying the way it acquires new technologies from small companies to speed up collaboration and address long running concerns by startups that working with big banks is slow and costly.

title: Another technical tweak as Fed wrestles to control policy rate
description: The U.S. Federal Reserve continued its quiet battle to keep a firm grip on its policy rate on Wednesday by again narrowing the gap between the effective ceiling and floor that keeps it contained.

title: Drugmaker GSK to split after striking Pfizer consumer health deal
description: GlaxoSmithKline plans to split into two businesses -- one for prescription drugs and vaccines, the other for over-the-counter products -- after forming a new joint venture with Pfizer's consumer health division.

title: Exxon Mobil opposes weakening Obama-era emissions rules: letter to EPA
description: Exxon Mobil Corp  sent a letter to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency in support of methane gas emission rules put in place under the Obama administration, according to a copy of the letter seen by Reuters.

title: MetLife settles Massachusetts case over unpaid pensions
description: MetLife Inc will pay a $1 million fine to resolve claims that it made misleading statements to investors in failing to pay pension benefits to thousands of retirees it improperly treated as "presumed dead."

title: Chip gear makers take a beating after Micron's dour forecast
description: Shares of chip gear makers fell after a tepid forecast by U.S.-based Micron Technology Inc  exacerbated fears that a two-year chip boom was fizzling due to sluggish demand from makers of smartphones, PCs and servers.

title: Huawei to spend $2 billion over five years in cybersecurity push
description: (This version of the December 18th story corrects chairman's last name to Hu in 11th, 14th and last paragraphs)

title: Thyssenkrupp to propose Merz as chairwoman as year of turmoil ends
description: Thyssenkrupp  will propose as chairwoman Martina Merz, whose background includes roles at Volvo , Bosch [ROBG.UL] and Lufthansa , the German company said, as it prepares to spin off its capital goods units.

title: German auto supplier to plead guilty, pay $35 million fine in VW emissions case
description: German auto supplier IAV Gmbh has agreed to plead guilty and pay a $35 million fine for conspiring to assist Volkswagen AG  in its effort to evade U.S. diesel emissions standards, the U.S. Justice Department said on Tuesday.

title: Renault-Nissan leaders to meet amid alliance crisis
description: The head of Nissan and acting CEO of Renault will hold talks during a two day meeting of their carmaking partnership starting on Tuesday, sources said, amid a crisis in relations sparked by the arrest of long-time alliance supremo Carlos Ghosn.

title: BP launches $3 billion sale of U.S. onshore assets to fund BHP deal: sources
description: Britain's BP has launched the sale of U.S. oil and gas onshore assets that could raise more than $3 billion to help pay for other fields in the United States it bought in October from BHP , industry and banking sources said.

title: J&J says Indian drug regulators visited facilities, company provided talc samples
description: Johnson & Johnson said on Wednesday that Indian drugs authorities visited some of its facilities and it provided them with "tests and samples" of its talcum powder.

title: Bristol-Myers gets $1.6 billion offer for French consumer health unit
description: Bristol-Myers Squibb Co  received an offer from Japanese healthcare firm Taisho Pharmaceutical Holdings Co Ltd  to buy the company's French over-the-counter drugs business UPSA for $1.6 billion, the companies said on Wednesday.

title: Boeing says Indian airfares unsustainably low; lifts country's 20-year order forecast
description: Airfares in the fast-growing Indian market are 10 to 15 percent lower than breakeven levels for airlines, a Boeing Co  executive said, as the planemaker raised its long-term jet order forecast for the nation to a record despite market challenges.

title: Asian business confidence wallows near three-year low on trade worries: Thomson Reuters/INSEAD
description: A very cautious optimism remains among Asian companies in the fourth quarter as they wait to see whether there will be any breakthrough in a trade dispute between the United States and China, a Thomson Reuters/INSEAD survey showed.

title: Italy's transport minister says he would like to revoke Autostrade concession
description: Italy's Transport Minister Danilo Toninelli said on Wednesday that he would like to revoke motorway concessions held by Autostrade per l'Italia  after the collapse of a bridge in Genoa last August.

title: Indian regulator to test samples of Johnson & Johnson baby powder: media
description: India's federal drug regulator will on Wednesday seize samples of Johnson & Johnson's  baby powder for testing, local media said, following a Reuters report that the company knew for decades that cancer-causing asbestos lurked in the product.

title: Uber loses latest UK legal bid to block worker rights for drivers
description: Uber has lost its latest court bid to stop its British drivers being classified as workers, entitling them to rights such as the minimum wage, in a decision which jeopardizes the taxi app's business model.

title: U.S. existing home sales rise, trend weak
description: U.S. home sales unexpectedly rose in November, but recorded their biggest annual decline in 7-1/2 years as the housing market remained mired in weakness amid higher mortgage rates which have made home purchases more expensive.

title: Estonia arrests ten in Danske Bank money laundering inquiry
description: Estonia has arrested 10 former employees of the local branch of Danske Bank  as part of an international investigation into alleged money laundering.

title: Shell forms joint venture to produce offshore wind energy in New Jersey
description: EDF Renewables North America said on Wednesday it had formed a joint venture with oil and gas firm Royal Dutch Shell plc's  new energies division to co-develop a lease area for offshore wind energy in New Jersey.

title: U.S. imposes fresh Russia sanctions for election meddling
description: The United States imposed fresh Russia-related sanctions on Wednesday, expanding a blacklist of individuals allegedly involved in a Kremlin-backed campaign to meddle with the 2016 U.S. presidential election, among other misdeeds.

title: Brazil court ruling casts doubt over Petrobras asset sales
description: A Brazilian Supreme Court justice on Wednesday suspended a presidential decree establishing rules for Petroleo Brasileiro SA  to sell upstream assets, casting a pall over the state-controlled oil company's ambitious divestiture program.

title: China bike-sharing firm Ofo faces 'immense' cash crunch, CEO vows to battle on
description: Chinese bike-sharing startup Ofo, backed by Alibaba Group Holding Ltd , is battling "immense" cash flow problems and disbanding the firm has been considered as an option, its chief executive said in a letter to employees.

title: In Asia, nascent men's make-up market starts drawing big brands
description: From an eye shadow that opens with the flick of a thumb, Zippo-style, to a barely-there foundation in subtle blue-gray packaging: men's make-up is getting a makeover as manufacturers bid to take it more mainstream.

title: Fed raises interest rates, signals more hikes ahead
description: After weeks of market volatility and calls by President Donald Trump for the Federal Reserve to stop raising interest rates, the U.S. central bank instead did it again, and stuck by a plan to keep withdrawing support from an economy it views as strong.

title: Noble Group completes $3.5 billion restructuring to emerge as smaller, unlisted firm
description: Noble Group , the once mighty commodity trader, on Thursday completed its drawn out $3.5 billion debt restructuring to emerge as a smaller, unlisted Asia-focused coal-trading business.

title: Nissan, Renault bosses met one-on-one in Amsterdam, Nissan says
description: Nissan Motor Co  CEO Hiroto Saikawa held a one-on-one meeting with the acting boss of automaker partner Renault  in Amsterdam this week that led to "positive" and "productive" talks, the Japanese automaker said on Thursday.

title: Exclusive: Renault, Nissan executives sought other ways to pay Ghosn - documents
description: Executives from both carmakers in the Renault-Nissan alliance looked at least twice at legal ways to pay Chairman Carlos Ghosn undisclosed income through the partners' shared finances, documents seen by Reuters show.

title: SoftBank Corp shares recover from early fall, after record IPO
description: SoftBank Corp shares fell as much as 8 percent early on Thursday before erasing the losses in volatile trading, following the telco's 15 percent tumble on debut the previous day.

title: Nissan says CEO had one-on-one meeting with Renault's acting boss
description: Nissan Motor Co  on Thursday said CEO Hiroto Saikawa had held a one-on-one meeting with the acting boss of its automaking partner Renault SA  during talks between the alliance in Amsterdam this week.

title: Oil rebounds from rout on signs of strong product demand
description: Oil prices rose on Wednesday, recovering somewhat from a sharp selloff during the previous session, after U.S. data showed strong demand for refined products.

title: China's Sinograin confirms U.S. soybean purchases
description: China's Sinograin said it had recently bought a few batches of soybeans from the United States, amid a truce in a trade war between the two nations.

title: Facebook shares drop as data privacy fallout spreads
description: Facebook Inc shares sank on Wednesday as concerns about its ability to safeguard user data sparked a government lawsuit, criticism in the U.S. Congress and a New York Times report on how it had shared data with other companies.

title: After Fed selloff, is a U.S. bear market next?
description: U.S. stocks took another body blow on Wednesday after the Federal Reserve raised interest rates again and the central bank chairman did not soften his tone about the outlook for further financial tightening to the degree investors had hoped.

title: Heard on the grapevine: How Pacific trade pact primes New Zealand wine for Japan buzz
description: From sleepy New Zealand hillsides to sleek Tokyo dining scenes, a bottle of Hawke's Bay wine shipped to Japan traces an arc that exporters like Nigel Avery see as an avenue for multi-million dollar growth built on a free trade pact.

title: A Fed tally: Nearing normal, central bank won a few, and lost as well
description: The U.S. Federal Reserve has begun signaling the end of its rate-hike cycle is not far off, winding down its sometimes Sisyphean effort to restore a semblance of normalcy to monetary policy. It has been a slow slog - the Fed has managed just nine increases in three years, and it may squeeze in just a couple more.

title: Brewer AB InBev partners with Tilray to tap cannabis drink market
description: Anheuser-Busch InBev , the world's largest brewer, and Canadian pot producer Tilray Inc  are partnering in a $100-million joint venture to research cannabis-infused non-alcoholic drinks for the Canadian market, the companies said Wednesday.

title: Wall St. tumbles as investors fret over Fed policy update
description: U.S. stocks declined sharply on Wednesday after the Federal Reserve's forecast of fewer interest-rate increases in 2019 fell short of investors' hopes of a more dovish monetary policy.

title: Payments company Square to re-apply for a bank license
description: Square Inc , the payments company led by Twitter Inc  chief executive Jack Dorsey, is refiling its application with U.S. state and federal regulators for a bank license, the company said on Wednesday.

title: Exclusive: Exxon Mobil secured U.S. hardship waiver from biofuels laws - sources
description: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency granted oil major  Exxon Mobil Corp  a financial hardship waiver this year temporarily freeing its Montana refinery from U.S. biofuel laws, three sources familiar with the matter told Reuters.

title: El Sharara oilfield to reopen, Libyan government says
description: Libya's biggest oilfield, El Sharara, will reopen, the country's    internationally recognized government said on Wednesday after   Prime Minister Fayez al-Sarraj flew there to persuade protesters to end a blockage.

title: Instant View: Stocks sink after Fed raises rates, Powell comments on balance sheet
description: U.S. stock markets tumbled on Wednesday, reversing a morning rally after the U.S. Federal Reserve delivered an expected interest rate hike but signaled its tightening cycle is nearing an end in the face of financial market volatility and slowing global growth.

title: Buffett profits as venture in Canadian mortgage business ends
description: Billionaire investor Warren Buffett is cutting ties with a  Canadian mortgage business after a nifty trade that provided the company with a potential lifeline.

title: Exclusive: Russia's Deripaska prepares to cede control of Rusal, En+ - sources
description: Russian tycoon Oleg Deripaska is preparing to cede control of Rusal  and its parent En+ , moving part of his En+ stake to a blind trust, as talks with the United States on lifting sanctions advance, three sources familiar with the talks said.

title: Global stocks sink after Fed hike, bonds rally
description: Global equity markets gave up earlier gains and continued a weeklong sell-off on Wednesday after the U.S. Federal Reserve announced a fresh interest rate hike and said "some" further rate hikes would be necessary in the year ahead.

title: LME to remove suspension on Rusal metal if sanctions lifted
description: The London Metal Exchange (LME) said on Wednesday it proposed to lift its suspension on aluminum produced by Russia's Rusal if U.S. sanctions are lifted.

title: U.S. Congress will not pass self-driving car bill in 2018: senators
description: The U.S. Congress will not vote on a bill to speed the introduction of self-driving cars before it adjourns for the year, a blow to companies like General Motors Co and Alphabet Inc's Waymo unit, key senators said on Wednesday.

title: Pier 1 CEO steps down after turnaround efforts fail
description: Home furnishing retailer Pier 1 Imports Inc  said on Wednesday its Chief Executive Officer Alasdair James has stepped down and the company is looking at various options as it struggles with falling sales.

title: Japan's Nidec to expand electric-car motor production outside China: Nikkei
description: Nidec Corp  will add locations outside China to build motors for electric vehicles as the Japanese motor maker rethinks its supply strategy, the Nikkei business daily reported on Thursday.

title: Burnout, stress lead more companies to try a four-day work week

title: IPO activity next year could dampen if markets do not rebound: report
description: The excitement of proposed initial public offerings by ride-hailing rivals Uber and Lyft next year may not be enough to encourage other firms to follow suit, as they fear that slowing global growth and rocky stock markets dragging into next year could threaten market debut valuations.

title: Treasury's Mnuchin says expects January trade talks with China: Bloomberg
description: The United States and China are planning to hold meetings in January to "document an agreement" on trade, U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin told Bloomberg in an interview on Tuesday.

title: U.S. agency to speed reviews of automaker self-driving petitions
description: The U.S. auto safety regulator said on Tuesday it is speeding up the process for reviewing whether automakers can deploy self-driving vehicles without devices such as brakes and steering wheels.

description: Elon Musk's rocket company SpaceX Corp is set to raise $500 million at a $30.5 billion valuation, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday, citing people familiar with the fundraising plan.

title: GM cutting 50 jobs at U.S. battery plant tied to Chevy Volt
description: General Motors Co  said on Tuesday it plans to cut 50 jobs at a suburban Detroit lithium-ion battery assembly plant after the largest U.S. automaker announced last month it will end production of its plug-in hybrid Chevrolet Volt in 2019.

title: Facebook's Sandberg cites need to do more after reports of Russia meddling
description: Facebook Inc's Chief Operating Officer Sheryl Sandberg said on Tuesday the company needs to step up its efforts to curb misinformation after research revealed that Russia-backed organizations targeted African-Americans, who favored Hillary Clinton, to suppress voter turnout during the 2016 election.

title: Italy's UniCredit settles dispute with Caius
description: British hedge fund Caius has made a payment to UniCredit  to settle a dispute over complex financial instruments which Italy's biggest bank counts toward its core capital, the two companies said.

title: Volkswagen may have to step up electric car plans to meet EU CO2 targets
description: Volkswagen  may have to step up its plans for mass production of electric vehicles in order to meet tougher-than-expected European targets to cut greenhouse emissions from cars, its chief executive said on Tuesday.

title: Twitter tumbles on concerns about hacking activity
description: Twitter Inc  shares fell almost 7 percent on Monday after the company said it was investigating unusual traffic that might be from state-sponsored hackers and, in what appeared to be an unrelated issue, a security firm said hackers used the platform to try to steal user data.

title: Kroger starts use of unmanned vehicles for delivery in Arizona
description: U.S. supermarket chain Kroger Co  said on Tuesday it has started using unmanned autonomous vehicles to deliver groceries Scottsdale, Arizona in partnership with Silicon Valley startup Nuro.

title: Indian regulator says Reuters report on J&J baby powder 'under consideration'
description: India's federal drug regulator said on Tuesday a Reuters report that Johnson & Johnson  knew for decades that cancer-causing asbestos lurked in its baby powder was "under consideration".

title: Malaysia says Goldman Sachs failed to disclose key facts in 1MDB bond sales
description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc  made untrue statements and omitted key facts in offering circulars for the bonds it sold for Malaysian state fund 1MDB, the Malaysian government said in criminal charges against the U.S. bank.

title: Cash-strapped South African Airways expands Emirates code sharing
description: South African Airways (SAA) said on Tuesday that it had signed a deal with Emirates [EMIRA.UL] to expand an existing codeshare agreement, in a rare bright spot for the cash-strapped airline.

title: CBS fires CEO Leslie Moonves and denies $120 million severance
description: CBS Corp said on Monday it has fired Leslie Moonves for cause and has denied a $120 million severance package as it girds for a potential legal battle with its former chief executive who has been accused of sexual harassment and assault that allegedly took place before and after he joined the company.

title: Citi reorganizes prime brokerage unit
description: Citigroup Inc  is shuffling its prime brokerage business, according to an internal memo seen by Reuters, amid reports that the unit could lose millions on a bad loan to an Asian hedge fund.

title: Uber gets approval from Pennsylvania to resume self-driving testing
description: Uber Technologies Inc received approval from Pennsylvania to resume self-driving car testing on public roads this week, state records show, nine months after it suspended the program following a deadly accident in Arizona.

title: Kinder Morgan faces proposed class action lawsuit on pipeline
description: Kinder Morgan is facing a proposed class action lawsuit, claiming that a division of the pipeline operator has emitted chemicals and toxic gas that caused damage to property and killed animals.

title: J&J moves to limit impact of Reuters report on asbestos in Baby Powder
description: Johnson & Johnson on Monday scrambled to contain fallout from a Reuters report that the healthcare conglomerate knew for decades that cancer-causing asbestos lurked in its Baby Powder, taking out full-page newspaper ads defending its product and practices, and readying its chief executive for his first television interview since investors erased tens of billions of dollars from the company’s market value.

title: Investors revolt against executive pay plans at tarnished Australian banks
description: Shareholders voted against the executive remuneration plans of two of Australia's biggest banks on Wednesday following misconduct revelations that have swept through the country's financial sector.

title: China embarks on second round of soy buying post Trump-Xi truce
description: Chinese importers returned to the U.S. soy market on Tuesday for their second round of purchases since the two countries agreed to a truce in their trade war, four traders with knowledge of the deals and the U.S. Soybean Export Council said.

description: U.S. chipmaker Micron Technology Inc  gave on Tuesday quarterly sales and profit forecasts well below Wall Street estimates, citing a market glut of memory chips as consumer and business demand for phones and computers is weakening.
