description: Bankrupt U.S. retailer Sears Holdings Corp will take a charge of about $443 million arising from store closures, a regulatory filing showed on Tuesday.

title: Oil drops over 5 percent on economic slowdown fears, supply glut
description: Oil prices tumbled more than 5 percent on Tuesday in heavy trade due to fears of oversupply and deteriorating demand, extending a selloff that has taken major crude benchmarks down more than 30 percent from an October peak.

title: High taxes could hasten bank moves from Britain after Brexit
description: Britain risks driving banks overseas if current high levels of taxation on the industry are maintained after Brexit, a bank lobby group said on Wednesday.

title: S&P flat as government shutdown threat, Fed decision loom
description: The benchmark S&P 500 stock index ended little changed in a choppy trading session on Tuesday as the possibility of a partial U.S. government shutdown raised investor jitters ahead of a highly anticipated meeting of the Federal Reserve.

title: FedEx sees global trade slowdown, says U.S. economy still 'solid'
description: FedEx Corp  on Tuesday slashed its 2019 forecast after Europe's economy weakened and the U.S. trade row exacerbated a slowdown in China, sending shares in the package delivery company tumbling more than 6 percent after the closing bell.

title: Lockheed Martin wins $585 million U.S. defense contract: Pentagon
description: Lockheed Martin Corp  has been awarded a $585 million U.S. defense contract for a Homeland Defense Radar in Hawaii, the Pentagon said on Tuesday.

title: Judge mulls using monitor to oversee CVS during court process
description: A federal judge said on Tuesday that he was considering using a court-appointed monitor to make sure CVS Health Corp refrains from fully integrating with insurer Aetna while he examines the companies' settlement with the government.

title: Yelp, Consumer Watchdog lose Google intervention bid
description: Search company Yelp and lobby group Consumer Watchdog lost their joint bid to intervene in Google's challenge of a 2.4 billion euro ($2.7 billion) EU antitrust fine after a court said they had no direct interest in the case.

title: Trump pressures Fed before meeting, warns against 'another mistake'
description: U.S. President Donald Trump on Tuesday further sought to pressure the Federal Reserve as the central bank prepared to start its two-day policy meeting, warning the Fed's board not to "make yet another mistake" ahead of an expected interest rate hike.

title: Stocks dip ahead of Fed news; oil prices drop
description: Global equity markets dipped on Tuesday as nervous investors awaited indications whether the Federal Reserve will be able to raise interest rates much further amid turbulent markets and a weakening outlook for the global economy.

title: Glencore's Katanga pays $22 million to settle Canada regulator probe
description: Glencore-controlled  Katanga Mining Ltd  said on Tuesday it agreed to pay more than $22 million to settle Canadian allegations of inadequate historical disclosures of its finances and activities in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

title: Mercedes-Benz cuts China prices after tariff on U.S.-made cars suspended
description: German luxury carmaker Mercedes-Benz on Monday said it would offer discounts on cars imported into China from the United States until March 31 after Beijing suspended additional tariffs on U.S.-made cars.

title: China, EU lambast United States for miring WTO in crisis
description: The United States came under fire from China and the European Union on Monday, accused by both major trading partners of taking protectionist measures and bringing the World Trade Organization (WTO) to its knees.

title: China says U.S. has brought back 'the ghost of unilateralism' to WTO
description: China said on Monday that the Trump administration's trade measures on items from steel to intellectual property taken under the guise national security were "bringing back to life the ghost of unilateralism".

title: Eni, Shell knew of 'sharks' in Nigeria graft case: judge
description: An Italian judge said on Monday oil majors Eni  and Royal Dutch Shell  were fully aware their 2011 purchase of a Nigerian oilfield would result in corrupt payments to Nigerian politicians and officials.

title: German union calls strike at Amazon warehouses
description: German trade union Verdi called on workers at two Amazon  logistic centers to strike on Monday, part of a long-running campaign for better pay and conditions.

title: ABB to sell Power Grids to Hitachi, revamp business structure
description: ABB  reached a deal with Japan's Hitachi  to sell its Power Grids division, with the Swiss engineering group adding it plans to return net cash proceeds of $7.6-7.8 billion from selling the 80.1 percent stake in the unit to shareholders.

title: Foxconn not in settlement talks with Qualcomm in Apple battle: attorney
description: The lead attorney for the group of Apple Inc device assemblers seeking at least $9 billion in damages from Qualcomm Inc said on Sunday the contract manufacturers are not in settlement talks with the mobile chip supplier and are "gearing up and heading toward the trial" in April.

description: Whatever the acronym, when the U.S. Federal Reserve dropped its policy rate to near zero on Dec. 16, 2008, to counter a full-scale economic crisis, it ushered in what the central bank's chairman at the time, Ben Bernanke, called "the end of the old regime."

description: (This December 15 story was refiled to correct paragraph 9 to show date Nissan fired Ghosn as chairman as Nov. 22, not Nov. 26)

description: Uber Technologies Inc welcomed on Monday the British government's response to a review into workplace rights, which looks set to preserve the business models of gig economy companies, but unions rubbished the business ministry's plans.

description: ABB  will sell a majority stake in its Power Grids division to Japan's Hitachi  and return the proceeds to shareholders, bowing to pressure from an activist investor to sell the business that makes transformers and converters.

title: Australia bank NAB's CEO to take long holiday around inquiry report release
description: National Australia Bank Ltd  said on Monday its CEO will take about two months leave around the scheduled release of a major report into the country's finance sector, prompting a rebuke from a shareholder group.

title: Taisho said to near $1.6 billion deal for Bristol-Myers's UPSA: Bloomberg
description: Japanese healthcare firm Taisho Pharmaceutical Holdings Co Ltd  is said to be close to a $1.6 billion deal for Bristol-Myers Squibb Co's  French over-the-counter drugs business UPSA, Bloomberg reported on Sunday, citing sources familiar with the matter.

title: Goldman, Morgan Stanley gain clout in Brazil as NY IPOs grow

title: Nissan CEO calls on Renault to listen to detail of Ghosn allegations
description: Nissan Motor's CEO called on directors at alliance partner Renault to heed its reasons for sacking former Chairman Carlos Ghosn over alleged financial misconduct amid tensions over how to handle the fallout from his arrest.

title: Canada gets consular access to second man detained in China
description: Canadian diplomats gained consular access on Sunday to the second of two men detained by China over the past week, Canada's foreign ministry said in a statement that gave few details, as China said it was ensuring their rights were protected.

title: Czech cyber watchdog calls Huawei, ZTE products a security threat
description: The Czech cyber watchdog warned network operators on Monday against using software or hardware made by Chinese telecom equipment suppliers Huawei and ZTE , saying they posed a security threat.

title: J&J announces $5 billion share buyback after shares extend losses
description: Johnson & Johnson said on Monday it plans to buy back up to $5 billion of its stock, after a Reuters report on Friday that the company knew for decades that its Baby Powder contained cancer-causing asbestos wiped about $40 billion from its market value.

title: BNY Mellon to pay more than $54 million for improper handling of ADRs: SEC
description: The top U.S. securities regulator on Monday said that Bank of New York Mellon  will pay more than $54 million to settle charges of improper handling of "pre-released" American Depositary Receipts, U.S. securities representing foreign shares of a foreign company.

description: T-Mobile US Inc and Sprint Corp have won backing for their $26 billion merger from two national security reviews on Monday, clearing key hurdles in their tie-up bid.

title: South Korea to provide $3 billion in financial support for troubled auto suppliers
description: South Korea unveiled a policy package to support its embattled car parts makers industry that includes providing financial support worth over 3.5 trillion won ($3.10 billion) and encouraging the use of electric cars.

description: T-Mobile US  and Sprint Corp  have received approval from the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS) for their proposed merger, the companies said on Monday.

title: Qualcomm says Apple violating Chinese court order, despite new software
description: Qualcomm Inc said it believes Apple Inc remains in violation of a Chinese court's orders to stop selling iPhones despite a software update that Apple pushed on Monday.

title: S&P 500 hits 14-month low on economic jitters ahead of Fed meeting
description: Wall Street's major indexes all slid more than 2 percent on Monday, with the benchmark S&P 500 closing at its lowest in 14 months, on concerns about slowing economic growth ahead of a highly anticipated decision from the Federal Reserve this week on the course of U.S. interest-rate hikes.

title: Oracle sees strong third quarter on cloud strength, share rise
description: Oracle Corp on Monday forecast current-quarter profit above estimates after growth in its cloud services and license support unit helped the business software maker surpass Wall Street expectations for the second quarter.

title: Embraer's net proceeds from Boeing deal the same, despite higher price
description: Brazil's Embraer SA will receive the same net proceeds from a deal to sell 80 percent of its commercial jet unit to Boeing Co, even though the U.S. aircraft maker increased the enterprise value which includes debt by 11 percent.

description: Jeffrey Gundlach, chief executive of DoubleLine Capital, on Monday said the S&P 500 stock index is headed to new lows and that U.S. equities are in a long-term bear market.

title: Google to spend $1 billion on new campus in New York
description: Alphabet Inc's  Google is investing more than $1 billion on a new campus in New York, becoming the second major technology company after Amazon to pick America's financial capital to expand and create thousands of jobs.

description: Oil prices fell more than 2 percent on Monday, with U.S. crude tumbling below $50 a barrel, on signs of oversupply in the United States and as investor concern over global economic growth and fuel demand grows.

title: J&J announces $5 billion share repurchase plan

description: Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman was sidelined during the official "family photo" of world leaders and other dignitaries at the Group of 20 summit in Buenos Aires on Friday, standing at the far edge of the group portrait and ignored.

title: U.S. Trade Representative says any U.S.-China agreement entirely up to leaders
description: There will be good discussion on "very serious issues" between U.S. President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping on Saturday but any agreement will be "entirely up to" the two leaders, U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer said on Friday.

title: Honeywell to shift global headquarters to Charlotte
description: Honeywell International Inc  said on Friday it is relocating its global corporate headquarters to Charlotte, North Carolina, which is closer to several of the U.S. industrial conglomerate's businesses in the Southeast of the United States.

title: Trump: 'something could very well come out' of trade talks with China's Xi
description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Friday "something could very well come out" of his meeting on trade with Chinese President  Xi Jinping on the sidelines of a Group of 20 summit in Buenos Aires, a Voice of America reporter said on Twitter.

title: Exclusive: Vodafone, Liberty Global deal faces full EU antitrust scrutiny - source
description: Vodafone's  $21.8 billion proposed acquisition of Liberty Global's  assets in Germany and eastern Europe is likely to face a full EU antitrust investigation, a person familiar with the matter said.

title: Losses at Einhorn's hedge fund Greenlight grow in November
description: Billionaire investor David Einhorn told investors on Friday that losses at his hedge fund Greenlight Capital grew this month, leaving the fund down nearly 28 percent for the year.

title: Microsoft's market value overtakes Apple's to close out week
description: Microsoft Corp's  stock market value closed above Apple Inc's  for the first time in eight years on Friday as the Windows maker benefited from growth in cloud computing while Apple was hit by investor concern about iPhone demand.

title: United moves deeper into Latin America with Avianca, Copa tie-up
description: United Continental Holdings Inc  on Friday said it had  finalized a three-way joint venture with carriers Avianca Holdings SA  of Colombia and Copa Airlines of Panama, giving the U.S. airline a deeper foothold in Latin America where travel demand is rising.

title: Wall Street rises on trade hopes; S&P, Nasdaq post best weeks in 7 years
description: Wall Street rose on Friday as investors hoped for progress on trade in a critical U.S.-China meeting over the weekend, and the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq posted their biggest weekly percentage gains in nearly seven years.

title: U.S. to conduct additional Keystone XL pipeline review
description: The U.S. State Department will conduct another environmental review of TransCanada Corp's long-pending Keystone XL oil pipeline, a U.S. official said on Friday, a move that could lead to additional delays of the project.

title: Macron and Abe seek to avert Renault-Nissan row
description: France and Japan's leaders met for bilateral talks to avert a diplomatic row over the Renault-Nissan-Mitsubishi alliance on Friday following the surprise arrest of its Chairman Carlos Ghosn in Japan.

title: Fed's grades slip in Wall Street's latest report card
description: Wall Street last month gave the Federal Reserve its worst grade since Jerome Powell took the helm of the U.S. central bank earlier this year, docking points for a communications misstep early in October that sent U.S. stocks tumbling.

title: U.S., Canada, Mexico sign trade deal, Trump shrugs off Congress hurdle
description: The United States, Canada and Mexico signed a North American trade pact on Friday, with President Donald Trump brushing aside concerns that he could face difficulties getting the deal through the U.S. Congress.

title: Abe tells Macron Renault-Nissan's future up to private shareholders: spokesman
description: Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe told French President Emmanuel Macron on Friday that the future of the Renault-Nissan alliance was up to private shareholders, a spokesman for the Japanese leader said.

title: Oil tumbles on supply glut; Wall Street up on G20 comments
description: Oil prices retreated on Friday amid a global glut, racking up a 20 percent drop for November, while world equity markets were mixed ahead of weekend talks between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping.

title: U.S. judge gives preliminary OK to $48 million Volkswagen investor settlement
description: A U.S. judge in California has granted preliminary approval to a $48 million settlement for investors who said Volkswagen AG  made false and misleading statements over its excess diesel emissions.

title: Oil drops; losses limited by hopes of OPEC, Russia output cut
description: Oil prices edged lower on Friday due to concerns of oversupply and a strong dollar but losses were limited by expectations that the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) and Russia would agree some form of production cut next week.

title: Buenos Aires locked down for G20 summit, protest tightly controlled
description: Thousands of demonstrators marched in Buenos Aires on Friday to protest the G20's economic policies as the world's leading industrialized nations opened their annual summit in the Argentine capital.

title: Former Autonomy boss Lynch to fight U.S. fraud charges
description: The United States has filed criminal charges against British entrepreneur Mike Lynch over the $11 billion sale of Autonomy to Hewlett-Packard seven years ago, accusing him of making false statements that inflated the value of the software group.

title: France's Macron urges Renault-Nissan stability in talks with Japan's Abe
description: French President Emmanuel Macron met Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe and stressed that the Renault-Nissan   alliance should be preserved, following Chairman Carlos Ghosn's arrest in Tokyo, an Elysee official said on Friday.

title: PVH plans fixes for Calvin Klein, sees strong start to holidays
description: PVH Corp  on Friday allayed investor concerns over its Calvin Klein business and said early holiday sales were above its expectations, sending its shares up as much as 5 percent.

title: Tesla achieves Model 3 production of 1,000 cars per day: Electrek
description: Tesla Inc met its production target of 1,000 Model 3 cars per day, automotive news website Electrek reported on Friday, citing Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk's email to employees.

title: Russian and Saudi energy ministers to meet at G20: RIA
description: Russia's energy minister Alexander Novak will meet his Saudi counterpart at the G20 summit in Argentina and discuss an oil output reduction in 2019, RIA news agency cited Novak as saying on Friday.

title: Trump says some good signs on talks with China
description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Friday there were some good signs on talks with China ahead of his meeting with Xi Jinping on Saturday.

title: SKF settles last carmaker lawsuit over ball bearings cartel
description: SKF  has reached a settlement with Daimler  over the Swedish engineering group's alleged participation in a ball bearings cartel, drawing a line under its disputes with automakers over this issue.

title: Saudi-owned TV says Trump and Saudi crown prince had friendly meeting
description: Saudi-owned Al Arabiya TV reported that U.S President Donald Trump and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman had a friendly meeting on the sidelines of the G20 summit in Buenos Aires on Friday.

title: Police search offices of Deutsche Bank board members
description: Police have searched the offices of all the members of Deutsche Bank's  board as part of an investigation into money laundering allegations linked to the Panama Papers, a source told Reuters on Friday.

title: BRICS slam protectionism as China-U.S. spat overshadows G20 talks
description: Chinese President Xi Jinping and the leaders of major developing economies condemned protectionism at a G20 summit in Argentina on Friday overshadowed by U.S. President Donald Trump's threat to escalate tariffs on China.

title: Does Google harm local search rivals? EU antitrust regulators ask
description: EU antitrust regulators have asked Google's rivals if the internet search giant unfairly demotes local search competitors, according to a questionnaire seen by Reuters, a move which could lead to a fourth case against the Alphabet  unit.

title: Factbox: Tariff wars - duties imposed by Trump and U.S. trading partners
description: U.S. President Donald Trump has rattled the world trade order by imposing unilateral tariffs to combat what he calls unfair trade practices by China, the European Union and other major trading partners of the United States.

title: Progress made on trade component of G20 statement: Argentine minister
description: Progress has been made on the issue of trade for the final communique of the G20 meeting, Argentine Foreign Minister Jorge Faurie said on Friday.

title: GM's CEO to meet U.S. lawmakers next week over job cuts
description: General Motors Co  Chief Executive Mary Barra plans to visit Capitol Hill next week to discuss its plans to halt production at five plants in North America next year and cut up to 15,000 jobs, two congressional aides said on Friday.

title: Trump studying new auto tariffs after GM restructuring
description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that new auto tariffs were "being studied now," asserting they could prevent job cuts such as the U.S. layoffs and plant closures that General Motors Co  announced this week.

title: Nissan-Renault-Mitsubishi alliance won't appoint interim chairman
description: Mitsubishi Motors'  Chief Executive Osamu Masuko said on Thursday that the company's three-way alliance with Nissan and Renault would not appoint an interim chairman and would shift instead to a system where the group would be led by the three CEOs.

title: Deutsche Bank offices raided in money laundering probe
description: Police raided six Deutsche Bank offices in and around Frankfurt on Thursday over money laundering allegations linked to the "Panama Papers", the public prosecutor's office in Germany's financial capital said.

title: Barry Callebaut, Dutch partners launch sustainable mass-market chocolate
description: Swiss chocolate maker Barry Callebaut  on Thursday signed a partnership with Dutch No.1 retailer Albert Heijn to make its private-label chocolate fully traceable from 2019, reflecting consumers' growing interest in ethical sourcing.

title: Former Nissan executive Kelly denies financial misconduct allegations: lawyer
description: Nissan Motor Co’s  former representative director Greg Kelly denies allegations of financial misconduct at the automaker, his lawyer said on Thursday.

title: Jaguar Land Rover to lay off staff temporarily at UK plant
description: Britain's biggest carmaker Jaguar Land Rover  is to reduce the workforce at its plant in Wolverhampton, central England, by about 500 in a temporary move, it said on Thursday.

title: Fiat Chrysler to spend 5 billion euros in Italy to fill plants, keep jobs
description: Fiat Chrysler plans to spend more than 5 billion euros ($5.7 billion) on new models and engines in Italy over the next three years to try to make better use of factories and boost jobs and margins.

title: Elon Musk ducks out of one Los Angeles tunnel but pursues another
description: Billionaire entrepreneur Elon Musk has scrapped plans for a high-speed passenger tunnel under the West side of Los Angeles but is moving ahead with a similar proposal across town designed to whisk baseball fans to and from Dodger Stadium.

title: France's Safran aims to topple U.S. rival as no.1 aerospace supplier
description: Safran  unveiled ambitions to become the world's leading aerospace supplier in 15 years, overtaking United Technologies , as it pledged a research and development (R&D) spending drive while increasing cash returns to shareholders.

title: Marriott to open nearly 30 business hotels in Europe in two years
description: U.S. hotel chain Marriott International Inc  said on Thursday it plans to open nearly 30 Courtyard by Marriott hotels in Europe in the next two years, as it targets newer markets including Finland and Iceland.

title: Goldman names co-chief operating officers for Asia investment banking unit, ex-Japan
description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc  has named Aaron Arth and Iain Drayton co-chief operating officers of its investment banking division in Asia Pacific, excluding Japan, according to a memo seen by Reuters.

title: Ford backs PM May's Brexit plan to avoid no-deal 'catastrophe'
description: Carmaker Ford backed Prime Minister Theresa May's Brexit deal on Thursday to avoid a no-deal "catastrophe," but said she still needed to guarantee long-term frictionless trade, which is key to the future of its plants in Britain.

title: Abercrombie & Fitch forecasts upbeat holiday quarter, shares soar
description: U.S. teen apparel retailer Abercrombie & Fitch Co  forecast same-store sales for the holiday quarter above analysts' estimates on Thursday, driven by strong sales at its Hollister and flagship stores, sending its shares soaring 24 percent in early trading.

title: Unilever CEO change not connected to HQ climbdown: chairman
description: The replacement of Unilever's CEO Paul Polman was not connected to a shareholder row earlier this year over a proposed move of the headquarters of the Anglo-Dutch consumer goods company from Britain to the Netherlands, said the group's chairman.

title: Amazon picks New York City, Washington D.C. area for new offices
description: Amazon.com Inc  picked America's financial and political capitals for massive new offices on Tuesday, branching out from its home base in Seattle with plans to create more than 25,000 jobs in both New York City and an area just outside Washington, D.C.

title: Factbox: Amazon to get billions in breaks for HQ2 development
description: (The Factbox updated on Nov. 15 corrects to fix total New York City incentive figure to $2.81 billion from $1.525 billion.)

title: BMW mulls converting hybrids to electric only mode in polluted cities
description: BMW said it can force its hybrid cars switch to an electric-only mode in heavily polluted inner-city areas, helping its vehicles compete with pure battery-driven rivals as a raft of cities seek to create emissions-free zones.

title: Factbox: Unilever names beauty unit head Alan Jope as new CEO
description: Anglo-Dutch consumer goods company Unilever  said its CEO Paul Polman was retiring and would be replaced by the head of its beauty unit Alan Jope, 54, from January 1.

title: Ad buyers skeptical as Snap looks beyond teens for growth
description: Snap Inc  has pinned its hopes on the over-35 crowd to revive user growth for its photo messaging app, a shift ad buyers said could backfire.

title: South Korea indicts group for leaking Samsung display tech to Chinese firm
description: South Korean prosecutors on Thursday said they have indicted nine people on suspicion of leaking Samsung Electronics Co Ltd flexible display technology to a Chinese company.

title: Supply chain reaction: trade war refugees race to relocate to Vietnam, Thailand
description: Fred Perrotta spent four years building a network of Chinese suppliers for his line of trendy backpacks, but as soon as the United States announced tariffs on almost half of its Chinese imports, he started looking for suppliers in other countries.

title: Tokyo prosecutors plan to seek extension of Ghosn's detention: Kyodo
description: Tokyo prosecutors plan to seek an extension of Carlos Ghosn's detention, after the ousted chairman of Nissan Motor Co  was arrested last week for alleged financial misconduct, Kyodo News reported on Thursday.

title: Indonesia's Go-Jek starts trial launch in Singapore, challenges Grab
description: Indonesian ride-hailing firm Go-Jek kicked off a trial launch in parts of Singapore on Thursday and plans to roll out an array of services through its app in early 2019, challenging dominant player Grab in the small city-state.

title: Trump administration to study tools to raise U.S. tariffs on Chinese autos
description: U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer said on Wednesday that he was examining all available tools to raise U.S. tariffs on Chinese vehicles to the 40 percent duties that China is now charging on U.S.-produced vehicles.

title: Japan central banker mum on alleged involvement in Ghosn transaction
description: A Bank of Japan board member declined on Thursday to comment on a media report that she was involved in an alleged attempt by former Nissan chairman Carlos Ghosn to shift personal investment losses to the automaker during her time at a commercial bank.

title: Huawei seeks clarification after New Zealand intelligence agency rejects 5G bid
description: Huawei Technologies Co Ltd said it was seeking clarification from New Zealand after the country's intelligence agency rejected the telecommunication industry's first request to use the Chinese firm's equipment in its planned 5G mobile network.

title: Bull run finale for global stocks not far off now: Reuters poll
description: An end to the bull run in global stocks is not far away, according to a Reuters poll which also showed a broad cut to forecasts for next year on concerns over global growth and tightening financial conditions.

title: Volvo Cars has no current plans for stockmarket listing: CEO
description: Volvo Cars, owned by China's Geely, has no current plans to go for a stockmarket listing, its chief executive said, more than two months after the Swedish carmaker postponed its flotation blaming trade tensions and an automotive stocks downturn.

title: Trump says 'long way to go' on tariffs and China
description: U.S. President Trump said on Thursday said there was "a long way to go" on tariffs with China and urged companies to build products in the United States to avoid them.

title: Renault-Nissan crisis meeting fails to name interim boss
description: Renault  and Nissan  vowed to stick by their  industrial alliance on Thursday but failed to name an interim boss to stand in for Chairman Carlos Ghosn, whose arrest has threatened the French carmaker's control of the partnership.

title: German car bosses finalizing White House meeting next week
description: Top executives from German carmakers Volkswagen , BMW  and Daimler  are finalizing plans for a White House meeting on trade policy next week, German and U.S. officials said on Thursday.

title: Nio, China rival to Tesla, says U.S. head to step down
description: The U.S. head of Nio Inc , an electric carmaker seen as one of the main Chinese rivals to Tesla Inc , will leave the company, the firm said in a filing on Friday, the first major management departure since its September IPO.

title: Mitsubishi Motors ousts Ghosn as chairman, days after Nissan firing
description: Mitsubishi Motors Corp said on Monday its board removed Carlos Ghosn from his role as chairman, following his arrest and ouster from alliance partner Nissan Motor Co last week for alleged financial misconduct.

title: Unilever CEO retires after headquarters row, replaced by insider Jope
description: Unilever's  Chief Executive Paul Polman will step down  next month after 10 years in the job, leaving insider Alan Jope to step into his shoes after the Anglo-Dutch group's failed attempt to shift its headquarters.

title: Samsung Elec says it will cancel $4.4 billion worth of shares
description: Samsung Electronics Co Ltd  said on Friday it would cancel 4.9 trillion won ($4.4 billion) worth of its shares.

title: HP Inc revenue tops estimates on personal systems business
description: HP Inc's  quarterly revenue beat analysts' estimates on Thursday, driven by growth in its personal systems business that sells notebooks and desktops and the acquisition of Samsung's printer business.

title: Dell posts revenue jump ahead of voting on VMware offer
description: Dell Technologies Inc  reported a 15 percent rise in quarterly revenue on Thursday, as businesses were forced to upgrade their systems running on older Windows technology and on strong performance by software maker VMware.

title: AT&T commits to cutting up to $20 billion in debt in 2019
description: AT&T Inc  said on Thursday it has committed to cutting its heavy debt load next year through a variety of measures, including a review of all of its non-core assets such as its stake in streaming video company Hulu for possible sale.

title: Fed minutes: Further hike 'warranted soon,' debate opened on pause
description: Almost all Federal Reserve officials at their last meeting agreed another interest rate increase was "likely to be warranted fairly soon," but also opened debate on when to pause  further hikes and how to relay those plans to the public.

title: Fed may tweak excess reserves rate again soon: minutes
description: The U.S. Federal Reserve looks set to make its second adjustment in six months to the systems it uses to control interest rates as it appears on course for yet another rate increase at its meeting next month.

title: Japan brokers readying for new client surge ahead of SoftBank's mammoth IPO
description: Japan's stockbrokers are rubbing their hands ahead of SoftBank's record-breaking $21 billion share sale, banking on the telco's brand power and unprecedented marketing campaign to boost business in a country replete with IPO-hungry investors.

title: Wall Street edges down as tech, bank stocks weigh
description: Wall Street closed slightly lower on Thursday as tech and financial shares slumped, erasing earlier gains stemming from Federal Reserve minutes showing the central bank opened the debate on when to pause further interest rate hikes.

title: Fed retunes message for 2019, opening door to 'slow down'
description: With the Federal Reserve expected next month to raise rates to what some U.S. central bankers believe is at or near a neutral level, Chairman Jerome Powell is retuning his message to signal a more cautious approach on further rate hikes next year.

title: Financial wrongdoing allegations against Carlos Ghosn
description: (This Nov. 26 story, corrects date and clarifies condition of deadline by which authorities must file charges against Ghosn or let him go, in first paragraph)

title: World shares mixed as markets consider Fed, Trump impact
description: Wall Street seesawed on Thursday, dragged down late in the day by technology and financial stocks, while the dollar and the U.S. yield curve flattened in the wake of U.S. Federal Reserve news.

title: Trump coy on China trade deal before meeting Xi
description: U.S. President Donald Trump sent mixed signals on Thursday about the prospects for a trade deal with China, saying an agreement was close but he was not sure he wanted one, just as he left for Argentina for a meeting with President Xi Jinping.

title: Oil rises as Russia indicates open to cuts with OPEC
description: Oil reversed course and rose as much as 2 percent on Thursday, after industry sources said Russia had accepted the need to cut production, together with OPEC ahead of its meeting next week.

title: GM President Ammann will take over Cruise self-driving car unit
description: General Motors Co  President Dan Ammann will take over as chief executive of the automaker's majority-owned Cruise self-driving car subsidiary, trading in the No. 2 job at one of the world's largest automakers for a front-row position in the race to render traditional cars obsolete.

title: Exclusive: Elliott steps in to boost Arconic's sale process - sources
description: Elliott Management Corp, the activist hedge fund that sits on Arconic Inc's  board, is working to address potential liabilities weighing on the sale process for the U.S. aluminum products maker, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Twitter tumbles on fear of conservative backlash
description: Shares of Twitter Inc  tumbled 6 percent on Thursday after reports that Fox News had not tweeted for three weeks sparked fears of a backlash by conservatives protesting a perceived liberal bias by the company.

title: U.S., China exploring deal to delay more tariffs, start talks: WSJ
description: The United States and China are exploring a trade deal in which Washington would suspend further tariffs through the spring of 2019 in exchange for new talks "looking at big changes in Chinese economic policy," the Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday.

title: U.S. consumer spending rises strongly, inflation moderates
description: U.S. consumer spending increased by the most in seven months in October, but underlying price pressures slowed, with an inflation measure tracked by the Federal Reserve posting its smallest annual increase since February.

title: Bayer to sell businesses, cut jobs after Monsanto deal
description: Bayer , the German drugmaker that bought U.S. seed company Monsanto, announced on Thursday the sale of a number of businesses, around 12,000 job cuts and 3.3 billion euros ($3.8 billion) in impairments.

title: Amazon's treatment of sellers comes under scrutiny in Germany
description: Germany's antitrust authority has launched an investigation into whether U.S. ecommerce giant Amazon is exploiting its market dominance in its relations with third-party retailers who use its website as a marketplace.

title: U.S. trade restrictions have hit $369 billion of Chinese exports: monitoring group
description: U.S. trade restrictions have hit a total of $369 billion of Chinese exports this year, much higher than the $278 billion of goods impacted by tariffs alone, a regular monitoring report of G20 trade restrictions said on Thursday.

title: Exclusive: Burger chain Jack in the Box explores sale - sources
description: Jack in the Box Inc , a U.S. hamburger restaurant chain with more than 2,000 restaurants, is exploring options that could include a sale of the company after divesting its Qdoba brand earlier this year, people familiar with the matter told Reuters on Thursday.

title: State-owned Israel Aerospace to partner with Boeing on potential aviation contracts
description: State-owned Israel Aerospace Industries (IAI) said on Wednesday it signed an agreement with U.S. planemaker Boeing Co  last week to cooperate on commercial and military aviation in Israel and some other markets.

title: Danske Bank charged over alleged violations of money laundering law
description: Denmark's state prosecutor has filed preliminary charges against Danske Bank  for alleged violations of the country's anti-money laundering act in relation to its Estonian branch.

title: Insurer AXA raises profit targets in wake of $15 billion XL deal
description: AXA , Europe's second-biggest insurer, expects its profitability to improve in the next two years thanks to U.S. business brought in by its new XL arm, and said it would now focus on expanding in Asia.

title: U.S. new home sales drop to more than 2-1/2-year low
description: Sales of new U.S. single-family homes tumbled to a more than 2-1/2-year low in October amid sharp declines in all four regions, further evidence that higher mortgage rates were hurting the housing market.

title: BMW chief says considering second U.S. manufacturing plant
description: BMW  is considering a second U.S. manufacturing plant that could produce engines and transmissions, Chief Executive Harald Krueger said on Tuesday, shortly after a report that U.S. President Donald Trump would impose tariffs on imported cars from next week.

title: Wall Street grows cautious but still optimistic: Reuters poll
description: Fears of a prolonged U.S.-China trade war and a potentially overzealous Federal Reserve have left Wall Street strategists less optimistic about stock market gains next year, but they still expect a decent increase, a Reuters poll found.

title: Daimler to start making electric cars in China in 2019
description: Daimler  will start building electric cars in China next year as a way to meet Beijing's stringent anti-pollution quotas for carmakers, even as demand for conventional models like the Mercedes-Benz Maybach remains strong.

title: NBA strikes betting data deals with Sportradar, Genius Sports
description: The National Basketball Association (NBA) struck its first betting data partnerships, allowing Genius Sports and Sportradar AG to distribute data to licensed sports betting operators in the United States.

title: Siemens CEO received pay rise in 2018: annual report
description: Siemens paid its chief executive Joe Kaeser a total of 7.82 million euros ($8.82 million) during its 2018 financial year, the German engineering company said in its annual report on Wednesday, up from 7.65 million euros a year earlier.

title: Bitcoin up 10 percent, on course for its biggest daily rise since April
description: Bitcoin rallied 10 percent on Wednesday to more than $4,100, putting it on course for its biggest daily rise since mid-April as it pulled itself out of a recent slump.

title: Cryptocurrencies to survive sell-off - Allianz's El-Erian
description: Cryptocurrencies are here to stay despite a prolonged slump this year, and will gain wider acceptance after the recent entry of more institutional investors in the space, Mohamed El-Erian, chief economic adviser at Allianz, said on Tuesday.

title: Seeds of Renault-Nissan crisis sown in Macron's 'raid'
description: The arrest of Renault-Nissan boss Carlos Ghosn has triggered new attempts by the Japanese carmaker to shake off the control of its French parent - adding to the problems piling up on President Emmanuel Macron's desk in the Elysee Palace.

title: Dismantling the oil industry: rough North Sea waters test new ideas
description: (This Nov. 27 story has been refiled to correct spelling of surname of Oil and Gas UK decommissioning manager.)

title: Deutsche Bank Americas head expected to leave: sources
description: Deutsche Bank's  head of the Americas, Tom Patrick, is likely to leave the bank, possibly by the end of the year, two people with knowledge of the matter said on Wednesday.

title: Bangladesh factory safety group seeks to delay closure, flags lingering risks
description: A group set up by European fashion brands to improve factory safety in Bangladesh has sought a stay on a court order that calls for its local operations to end this week, its executive director said on Wednesday.

title: Bitcoin gains 6 percent as it heads for best day since July
description: Bitcoin bounced more than 6 percent on Wednesday, climbing above $4,000 and heading for its biggest daily jump since July as it clawed back ground after recent heavy selling.

title: Exclusive: Russia plans stiffer fines for tech firms that break rules - sources
description: Russia plans to impose stiffer fines on technology firms that fail to comply with Russian laws, sources familiar with the plans said, raising the stakes in the Kremlin's fight with global tech giants such as Facebook  and Google.

title: New Zealand rejects Huawei's first 5G bid citing national security risk
description: New Zealand's intelligence agency has rejected the telecom industry's first request in the country to use 5G equipment provided by China's Huawei Technologies Co Ltd, citing concerns about national security.

title: 'Out of control': Chinese authorities slam ride-hailing giant Didi over safety
description: Chinese authorities announced a broad crackdown on China's ride-hailing industry on Wednesday, targeting market-leader Didi Chuxing with fines following the deaths of two passengers in separate incidents earlier this year.

title: Auditor had questioned Nissan on payments to Ghosn at heart of scandal: source
description: Nissan Motor Co’s  auditor had repeatedly questioned transactions at the heart of allegations of financial misconduct by former chief Carlos Ghosn but Nissan said they were proper, a person with direct knowledge of the matter said on Wednesday.

title: Exclusive: Brazil oil tanker collision reveals offshore regulatory gaps
description: Brazil has more than doubled the number of risky ship-to-ship oil transfers this year, but its monitoring of such offshore maneuvers is lax, to a point where a July 2017 collision between two tankers was not reported, according to a Reuters review of government and shipping records.

title: Fed's Powell: Financial risks 'moderate' despite vulnerabilities
description: The U.S. faces only moderate financial risks despite elevated asset prices and concern over the possible impact of rising corporate debt, U.S. Fed chairman Jerome Powell said on Wednesday as the central bank released a broad overview of the health of credit markets and the financial system.

title: Judge orders new talks in Fiat Chrysler diesel emissions case
description: A federal judge in San Francisco on Wednesday ordered the U.S. Justice Department and Fiat Chrysler Automobiles NV  to hold new talks with a court-appointed settlement master to try to settle the government's civil suit over the Italian-American automaker's diesel vehicle emissions.

title: Instant View: Fed's gradual rate hikes balance against risks - Powell
description: U.S. Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell said on Wednesday that while there was "a great deal to like" about U.S. prospects, the Fed's gradual interest-rate hikes are meant to balance risks as it tries to keep the economy on track.

title: Jewish Americans sue Airbnb over West Bank listing ban
description: A group of Jewish Americans sued Airbnb Inc on Wednesday in U.S. federal court, accusing the home rental company of religious discrimination over its decision last week to remove listings for about 200 homes in the Israeli-occupied West Bank.

title: Ford reshuffles U.S. plants to beef up SUV, truck production
description: Ford Motor Co  said on Wednesday it will reshuffle workers at several of its plants to meet rising demand for pickup trucks and large SUVs, a process that will require finding new positions for 150 workers displaced by the changes but not result in job cuts.

title: Volkswagen planning new North America factory for electric vehicles
description: Volkswagen  is deciding where to locate a new factory in North America to build electric vehicles for the U.S. market, the German automaker's new head for the Americas said on Wednesday.

title: Two U.S. pipelines rack up violations, threaten industry growth
description: Energy Transfer LP  and its Sunoco pipeline subsidiary have racked up more than 800 state and federal permit violations while racing to build two of the nation's largest natural gas pipelines, according to a Reuters analysis of government data and regulatory records.

title: Microsoft wins $479.2 million contract from U.S. Army
description: The U.S. Army said on Wednesday that it has awarded Microsoft Corp  a $479.2 million contract to supply prototypes for the Army's augmented reality systems helping soldiers in training and combat missions.

title: Altria in talks to take minority stake in Juul: sources
description: Tobacco company Altria Group Inc  is in talks to take a minority stake of 20 to 40 percent in e-cigarette maker Juul Labs Inc, people familiar with the matter said on Wednesday.

title: Tiffany sales to Chinese tourists disappoint, shares fall sharply
description: Tiffany & Co  on Wednesday reported quarterly sales that missed estimates as Chinese tourists spent less than expected at the jeweler's stores in the United States and Hong Kong, a shortfall that sent the company's shares down as much 13 percent.

title: Fed's Powell, in apparent dovish shift, says rates near neutral
description: U.S. Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell injected investors with a strong dose of optimism on Wednesday, saying that the central bank's policy rate is now "just below" estimates of a level that neither brakes nor boosts a healthy U.S. economy, comments that many investors read as signaling the Fed's three-year tightening cycle is drawing to a close.

title: Saudi Arabia inks deal for Lockheed's missile defense system
description: Saudi Arabia will buy Lockheed Martin's  $15 billion missile defense system, a U.S. Department of State spokesman said on Wednesday, after aggressive lobbying by the administration to close the deal that included a personal call between President Donald Trump and Saudi King Salman.

title: Wall Street jumps as Powell hints interest rate hikes may taper off
description: Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell boosted U.S. stock markets on Wednesday when he said the policy rate is now "just below" estimates of a level that neither brakes nor boosts a healthy economy, comments that many took as signaling the Fed's three-year tightening cycle is drawing to a close.

title: Exclusive: U.S. senators ask White House to probe ZTE work in Venezuela
description: Two U.S. senators on Wednesday asked the Trump administration to investigate whether Chinese telecommunications company ZTE Corp  violated U.S. sanctions by helping Venezuela set up a database that monitors the behavior of its citizens.

title: Wells Fargo to combine private bank with ultra-rich client business
description: Wells Fargo & Co  said on Thursday it is restructuring its wealth and investment management business to combine its two high-net worth operations, the private bank and Abbot Downing, under a new unit leader who it has not yet named.

title: Wall Street rallies on U.S. elections; tech, health stocks lead
description: (This Nov. 7 story corrects paragraph 8 to read "Brian Nick, chief investment strategist for Nuveen in New York," instead of "Nuveen Asset Management")

title: U.S. Senate hearing over Hyundai, Kia engine fires on hold
description: The U.S. Senate Commerce Committee said on Thursday that a hearing planned for Nov. 14 on reports of engine fires involving Hyundai Motor Co  and Kia Motors Corp  vehicles was on hold, but could be rescheduled for a future date.

title: Factbox: German cities ban older diesel cars
description: German cities are starting to introduce bans on older diesel vehicles that emit higher amounts of pollutants than later models after the country's highest administrative court in February confirmed such bans are permissible.

title: Toshiba sheds more assets, cuts jobs to regain investor trust
description: Toshiba Corp  announced on Thursday it is shedding assets, cutting jobs and buying back its stock starting this week, sending its shares up 13 percent, as the once-mighty Japanese conglomerate aims to regain investor confidence.

title: A changing New York neighborhood wonders how Amazon would fit
description: It was the lunch-hour rush at the Court Square Diner in New York's Long Island City on Wednesday, and co-owner Nick Kanellos pointed to the elevated subway tracks that rattle overhead as he fretted over the news that Amazon may build a major outpost in the neighborhood.

title: Apple not in settlement talks 'at any level' with Qualcomm: source
description: Apple Inc  is not in talks "at any level" to settle its wide-ranging legal dispute with mobile chip maker Qualcomm Inc , according to a source familiar with the matter.

title: U.S. agency to mandate Boeing bulletin issued after Lion Air
description: The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration said Wednesday it will require airlines to follow a safety bulletin issued by Boeing Co reminding pilots how to handle erroneous data from a key sensor in the wake of last week's Indonesian jetliner crash.

title: No blockbuster from Fox results before Disney sale
description: Twenty-First Century Fox Inc  fell short of estimates for quarterly revenue on Wednesday, hit by the absence of a major movie hit at the end of the U.S. summer as it prepares to sell the bulk of its business to Walt Disney Co .

title: Norwegian Air: all our 737 MAX 8 operate as normal after Boeing statement
description: Norwegian Air said on Wednesday all fourteen of its 737 MAX 8 Boeing planes were operating as normal after receiving a safety bulletin from the U.S. plane manufacturer.

title: Regulators warn Wells Fargo over technology oversight: WSJ
description: Wells Fargo  received a warning from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) in recent weeks related to its technology operations, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday citing people familiar with the matter.

title: Former Intel CEO Brian Krzanich to head CDK Global
description: CDK Global Inc  on Wednesday named Brian Krzanich as its new chief executive officer and president, more than four months after he resigned from the top job at Intel following a probe that found he had a consensual relationship with an employee.

title: EU's Vestager says probe into Google AdSense case nearing end
description: EU regulators are close to wrapping up their third case against Alphabet  unit Google involving its AdSense advertising service, Europe's antitrust chief said on Wednesday, suggesting the company may soon be hit with another hefty fine.

title: Michael Kors shares slide 16 percent as European stores struggle
description: Michael Kors  shares slumped 16 percent on Wednesday as the fashion group missed Wall Street estimates for quarterly revenue, hurt by lower sales at its stores in Europe, where it is struggling to create a stronger luxury identity.

title: Ryanair, CEO are sued in U.S. over stock price, labor relations
description: Ryanair Holdings Plc  and longtime Chief Executive Michael O'Leary have been sued in New York by a shareholder that said Europe's largest airline defrauded investors and inflated its share price by overstating its ability to manage labor relations and keep costs down.

title: U.S. agency probes 1.7 million GM SUVs over wiper failures
description: The U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) said on Tuesday it was investigating whether General Motors Co , should recall an additional 1.7 million sport utility vehicles due to an issue with windshield wiper failures.

title: Ahold ups stakes in U.S. grocery war with mini-'robot supermarkets'
description: Grocery group Ahold Delhaize will roll out small, automated warehouses to speed order picking and cut delivery times, Reuters has learned, as it revamps its ecommerce business in response to rising competition in a fast-growing sector.

title: GE and Rolls Royce finalists for Chinese-Russian CR929 jet engine, designer says
description: General Electric  and Rolls Royce  are the two finalists to supply engines for a new long-haul jet developed by a Russian-Chinese joint venture that aims eventually to switch to a Sino-Russian engine, a chief designer of the aircraft said.

title: How Apple is losing its grip on India
description: Software engineer Samee Alam was ready to take the big leap and buy an iPhone in this week's Diwali festival sales, but at the last minute he opted for cheaper Chinese competitor OnePlus instead.

title: BMW dented by upfront expenditure for new car launches
description: German carmaker BMW  will deepen cost cuts after higher development expenses contributed to a 27 percent drop in third-quarter operating profit, falling short of analyst expectations as currency effects also took a toll.

title: German prosecutors search BlackRock in sham trades inquiry
description: German state prosecutors confirmed they searched the Munich offices of investor BlackRock as part of a probe into an illicit tax trading scheme but exonerated the company's local chairman, who is vying to succeed Chancellor Angela Merkel.

title: U.S. companies team up with hospitals to reduce employee maternity costs
description: General Electric Co  and other large companies are trying to chip away at rising childbirth costs for U.S. employees, working directly with hospitals to reduce cesarean sections and related complications.

title: Firepower for U.S. stocks may lose spark as Democrats gain clout
description: The U.S. stock market may be facing the remainder of Donald Trump's presidential term with the prospect of less juice to supercharge it.

title: Goldman Sachs CEO: I feel horrible ex-bankers broke law in 1MDB case
description: Goldman Sachs Chief Executive David Solomon said on Wednesday he felt "horrible" that two former employees "blatantly broke the law" in their dealings with Malaysian state fund 1Malaysia Development Berhad.

title: Ahold Delhaize CEO says robots to speed up U.S. deliveries
description: Ahold Delhaize's chief executive on Wednesday confirmed the Dutch retailer will partner with start-up Takeoff to build small, automated warehouses to speed order picking and cut delivery times from its U.S. stores.

title: Telecom network maker Nokia wins $2.3 billion frame deals in China
description: Finnish mobile telecom network maker Nokia announced on Wednesday that it had signed frame deals with China Mobile, China Telecom and China Unicom worth more than 2 billion euros ($2.3 billion).

title: Indian government set to turn up heat on central bank governor: sources
description: The Indian government intends to keep pressing demands for the country's central bank to relax lending curbs and hand over surplus reserves even if it risks provoking a resignation by the bank's governor, three sources familiar with the government's thinking told Reuters.

title: EU executive conditionally approves Daimler, BMW car-sharing deal
description: The European Union's competition authority said on Wednesday it had approved the plan of German luxury carmakers Daimler  and BMW  to combine their car-sharing businesses, subject to conditions.

title: Health stocks up on U.S. vote; insurers hit records
description: Shares in drugmakers and U.S. health insurers rallied on Wednesday, after election results delivered a split Congress that is unlikely to significantly cut government healthcare programs or reduce drug prices in the world's biggest and most profitable market.

title: Adidas slips in Europe as Stan Smiths, Superstars go out of fashion
description: Adidas  cut its 2018 revenue forecast on Wednesday after third quarter sales fell in western Europe, where it was hit by changing fashions and Nike's  gains in soccer.

title: SEC fines Citibank more than $38 million for mishandling ADRs
description: Citibank  will pay more than $38 million to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for abuse in handling American Depositary Receipts (ADRS), the regulator said in a statement on Wednesday.

title: Boeing to report lower 737 deliveries amid supplier delays: executive
description: Days before the numbers are due to be announced, Boeing Co  warned that October aircraft deliveries to airlines would be lower than normal as the world's largest planemaker continues to be dogged by supplier delays on engines and other components.

title: China, Russia unveil life-size model of planned widebody jet at Zhuhai airshow
description: China and Russia on Tuesday unveiled a life-size model of a proposed wide-body long-haul jet at the opening of China's largest airshow, giving public shape to their joint efforts to break into a market dominated by Boeing  and Airbus .

title: Bombardier to sell Q400 Turboprop aircraft program to Viking Air: source
description: Bombardier Inc  is set to announce the sale of its Q400 turboprop aircraft program to Canadian aircraft manufacturer Viking Air, a person familiar with the matter said late on Wednesday.

title: UBS expects to be sued by U.S. Justice Department over crisis-era mortgage securities
description: UBS Group AG, Switzerland's largest bank, said it expects to be sued by the U.S. Department of Justice as early as Thursday on civil charges related to the sale of mortgage-backed securities in the run-up to the 2008 global financial crisis, according to a company statement.

title: Google plans to expand office space in New York City: WSJ
description: Alphabet Inc's  Google is nearing a deal to buy or lease an office building in New York City that could add space for more than 12,000 new workers, The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday, citing sources.

title: Global stocks rise after U.S. vote splits power; dollar slips
description: Most major stock markets rose on Wednesday, led by a strong rally on Wall Street, after the outcome of the U.S. midterm congressional elections drove expectations of political gridlock in Washington, boosting risk assets and weighing on the dollar.

title: Roku forecasts surprise loss for holiday quarter, shares fall
description: Roku Inc forecast a surprise holiday-quarter loss and missed third-quarter revenue estimates for its high margin video streaming platform, sending its shares down nearly 13 percent in after-market trading on Wednesday.

title: Self-driving car industry needs standards and security: executives
description: Automakers need standards for key equipment, a wide-reaching 5G broadband network and strong partnerships to make self-driving cars and electric vehicles a success, top European car industry executives said on Wednesday.

title: Comcast plans to roll out new video-streaming device: source
description: Comcast Corp  is planning to launch a product that will allow its broadband subscribers to aggregate some video streaming applications, including Netflix, Amazon Prime and YouTube, according to a source familiar with the matter.

title: Qualcomm forecast falls short as Apple sales disappear
description: Qualcomm Inc  forecast sales revenue for the holiday shopping quarter below analysts' estimates on Wednesday as it took a hit from the loss of chip sales to Apple Inc , sending its shares down 3.4 percent.

title: Garnier goes organic in L'Oreal bid to lift mass market sales
description: L'Oreal  is rolling out organic skincare treatments at its Garnier brand as it looks to lift sales in its sluggish mass market unit, tapping a growing demand for more naturally-sourced products that is upending industries from cosmetics to food.

title: China's Sinopec signs purchase agreements worth $45.6 billion at Shanghai Expo
description: China's state-owned Sinopec signed purchase agreements worth $45.6 billion on Thursday, covering supplies of crude oil, chemicals, coal and equipment.

title: Cannabis shares light up as U.S. voter support for industry grows
description: Shares of cannabis companies rose on Wednesday as results from the previous day's U.S. elections pointed to more favorable political conditions for the cannabis industry.

title: Michigan vote to legalize pot fires up investor momentum behind cannabis
description: Michigan's vote Tuesday to become the 10th U.S. state where the recreational use of cannabis is legal is adding more momentum to a trend that some investors now say is inevitable: that marijuana will become legal nationwide within the next 5 years.

title: U.S. political gridlock may create investment opportunity
description: Investors hope the split between Republicans and Democrats controlling the U.S. Congress will open up opportunities to pick new winners and losers because some government policies will be harder to predict.

title: Italy's antitrust opens probe into Ryanair's, Wizz Air's hand luggage policies
description: Italy's antitrust said on Wednesday it was opening a probe against Ryanair  and Wizz Air over their new hand luggage policies.

title: Trump would consider regulating social media but urges caution
description: U.S. President Donald Trump said he would consider working with Democrats to regulate social media companies, after he and other conservatives accused companies such as Twitter Inc, Facebook Inc and Alphabet Inc's Google of allegedly stifling right wing views.

title: Starbucks partners with UberEats in Japan
description: Starbucks Corp  said on Wednesday it was partnering with UberEats to deliver coffee and food in Tokyo starting Friday, as the world's largest coffee chain looks to boost sales in Japan, one of its major Asia-Pacific markets.

title: Dish beats profit estimates, expects more subscriber losses
description: Dish Network Corp  beat Wall Street estimates for quarterly profit on Wednesday, as the U.S. satellite TV provider benefited from lower programming costs due to a blackout of Univision channels.

title: Strong car sales lift spirits at Brazil auto show
description: Automakers in Brazil last month notched their strongest sales in nearly four years, a leading trade group said on Wednesday, adding to optimism as the auto industry kicked off the biannual Sao Paulo International Motor Show.

title: Tableau, Twilio, New Relic reports send cloud stocks skyward
description: Shares of cloud software sellers surged on Wednesday following quarterly reports and forecasts from Tableau Software, New Relic, Twilio and Rapid7 that added to Wall Street's high expectations for the fast-expanding sector.

title: SpaceX circulates price guidance on $750 million term loan
description: NEW YORK (LPC) - Elon Musk’s rocket and spacecraft company SpaceX on Wednesday circulated pricing on a proposed $750 million term loan that will put cash on the company’s balance sheet, two sources said.

title: U.S. issues directive after Boeing alerts pilots following Indonesia crash
description: The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration issued an emergency airworthiness directive on Wednesday to address how to handle erroneous data from a sensor on the new Boeing 737 MAX jet in the wake of last week's Indonesian jetliner crash.

title: Apple's Asia suppliers fall on report iPhone XR production boost canceled
description: Apple Inc's  Asian supplier and assembler stocks fell on Tuesday on a media report that the iPhone maker had told its smartphone assemblers to halt plans for additional production lines dedicated to its new iPhone XR.

title: EU digital tax plan flounders as states ready national moves
description: A European Union plan to tax big internet firms like Google and Facebook on their turnover was on the verge of collapsing on Tuesday after several EU governments rejected it and announced national initiatives instead.

title: U.S. ends safety probe into nearly 50,000 U.S. Ford police vehicles
description: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration is closing an investigation into nearly 50,000 Ford Motor Co  Explorer Police Interceptor vehicles over reports of sudden brake failures, it said on Tuesday, without seeking a recall.

title: Trulicity leads mixed third quarter for Lilly; shares sink
description: Eli Lilly and Co's  diabetes drug Trulicity helped power higher-than-expected third-quarter profit on Tuesday, while sales of some other newer treatments fell short of Wall Street estimates.

title: Bitcoin volatility sinks to lowest in nearly two years
description: Bitcoin has experienced one of its worst annual price performances of its short 10-year-old life but also appears to have become more stable in the process.

title: CVS quarterly profit beats; expects to close Aetna deal this month
description: CVS Health Corp , which expects to close its $69 billion purchase of Aetna Inc  this month, reported third-quarter profit that beat analysts' estimates on higher sales of prescription drugs.

title: Iran says it is selling the oil it needs to, despite U.S. pressure
description: Iran said on Tuesday it had so far been able to sell as much oil as it needs despite U.S. pressure, but it urged European countries opposed to U.S. sanctions to do more to shield Iran, as Russia and Turkey also voiced their objections.

title: Two years in, Trump holds stock market bragging rights
description: U.S. President Donald Trump has taken credit for the stock market's gains during his nearly two years in the White House, and those claims are reasonable given the impact of tax cuts and pro-business policies on investor sentiment.

title: Airbus stages maiden flight of upgraded A330-800
description: Airbus  staged a maiden fight of the upgraded A330-800 jetliner on Tuesday, hoping the key milestone will boost the fortunes of a variant that has failed to make headway against newer types.

title: VW brand warns 2018 operating return on sales to be at lower end of range
description: Volkswagen  on Tuesday said the operating return on sales at its core VW passenger car brand would come in at the lower end of its 4 to 5 percent target range this year.

title: Lilly to consider more acquisitions like $1.6 billion Armo buy
description: Eli Lilly and Co  will consider more acquisitions similar to its $1.6 billion purchase of cancer drug developer Armo Biosciences earlier this year, the drugmaker's chief financial officer said on Tuesday.

title: European automakers BMW, Volvo to trial new LME steel contracts
description: European automakers BMW and Volvo plan to experiment with steel contracts to be launched by the London Metal Exchange early next year, a move which could eventually change the way the industry hedges and prices contracts, industry sources said.

title: Germany says EU should revise, delay digital tax plan
description: Germany's Finance Minister Olaf Scholz said on Tuesday the European Commission should revise its plan for a EU-wide tax on large digital companies and stressed the new levy should be applied only if there is no global deal by the summer of 2020.

title: Ford goes local in India, aims for bigger slice of competitive market
description: Ford Motor Co made a profit in India for the first time in a decade in the last fiscal year, signaling that a strategy conceived two years ago by the U.S. car manufacturer for one of the world's most competitive car markets is starting to show some success.

title: Boeing optimistic about speedy resolution to U.S.-China trade dispute: exec
description: Boeing Co  is optimistic of a quick resolution to the trade dispute between the United States and China, an executive at the U.S. planemaker said on Tuesday.

title: China grants more trademark approvals for Ivanka Trump firm - including voting machines
description: China last month granted initial approval for 16 new trademarks for the fashion brand of U.S. President Donald Trump's daughter and adviser Ivanka, including voting machines, a search of official records on Tuesday showed.

title: Exclusive: Chinese upstart Luckin Coffee seeks funds to double valuation to $2 billion - sources
description: Luckin Coffee, an up-and-coming coffee chain with ambitions to challenge Starbucks Corp  in China, is targeting a valuation of $1.5 billion to $2 billion as it launches a new round of funding, people familiar with the matter told Reuters.

title: U.S. renews Iran sanctions, grants oil waivers to China, seven others
description: The United States snapped sanctions back in place on Monday to choke Iran's oil and shipping industries, while temporarily allowing top customers such as China and India to keep buying crude from the Islamic Republic.

title: China says ready for U.S. talks, sees no winners in trade war
description: China is ready to hold discussions and work with the United States to resolve trade disputes because the world's two largest economies stand to lose from confrontation, Vice President Wang Qishan said on Tuesday.

title: Iran oil exports to plummet in November, then rebound as buyers use waivers
description: Iran's oil exports have fallen sharply since U.S. President Donald Trump said at mid-year he would reimpose sanctions on Tehran, but with waivers in hand the Islamic Republic's major buyers are already planning to scale up orders again.

title: Iran predicts 'difficult days' for oil consumers worldwide: SHANA
description: Iran's oil minister said on Tuesday that U.S. sanctions on  Iranian crude exports mean difficult days for oil consumers worldwide, adding that waivers issued by Washington to eight importing countries will not satisfy market demand.

title: HSBC discloses customer accounts hacked at its U.S. bank
description: Hackers breached some HSBC  customers' accounts in the United States in October and accessed their information, the bank said in a regulatory filing on Tuesday.

title: KKR, Allianz among four contenders for Altice Europe fiber sale: sources
description: Rival consortia led by U.S. buyout fund KKR  and Germany's insurer Allianz  are among the four main contenders for a stake in the fiber network business of Dutch-based telecom company Altice , sources said.

title: Chairman of BlackRock's German arm orders investigation cooperation
description: Friedrich Merz, chairman of the German arm of BlackRock , the world's biggest fund manager, said he had ordered the fund's management board to fully investigate all incidents involving so-called cum ex transactions and cooperate with prosecutors.

title: Caution grips European stocks ahead of U.S. mid-term results
description: European shares ended a choppy session in negative territory on Tuesday as investors punished companies like Zalando that missed expectations and remained cautious while waiting for the results of U.S. mid-term elections.

title: S&P 500 futures drop as U.S. election results trickle in
description: S&P 500 e-mini futures fell 0.3 percent on Tuesday as U.S. election results began to trickle in, with Democrats picking up a House of Representatives seat in Virginia, according to  projections from media outlets and data provider DDHQ.

title: Hyundai raises Southeast Asia bet with second investment in Grab
description: Hyundai Motor Co has raised its stakes in growing Southeast Asian markets with a $250 million investment in Singapore's Grab, its second in the ride-hailing firm, as it chases rivals in the race for new-age transportation.

title: Papa John's new advertising blitz helps North America restaurant sales
description: Papa John's International Inc  on Tuesday reported a smaller-than-expected decline in quarterly comparable sales in North America, helped by new advertising and rebranding as it tries to recover from bad publicity stemming from an acrimonious split with its founder.

title: Wendy's surprise same-restaurant sales drop burn shares
description: Wendy's Co  on Tuesday reported quarterly sales at  established outlets in North America below analyst estimates and lowered its same-store sales forecast for the year, as the burger chain struggles to lure customers in a fiercely competitive U.S. fast-food industry.

title: Wells Fargo's wealth management head to retire
description: Wells Fargo & Co's  head of wealth management Jay Welker will retire at the end of March after more than two decades with the San Francisco-based bank.

description: U.S. shares rose on Tuesday while the dollar held steady as Americans went to the polls in elections that could shift the balance of power in Congress.

description: Wells Fargo & Co executives were warned that an auto insurance plan could be overcharging customers four years before the bank scrapped the program, according to a complaint released by a judge this week.

description: NEW YORK (LPC) - Elon Musk's Space Exploration Technologies Corp, known as SpaceX, is looking to line up a $750 million leveraged loan, sources said.

title: German prosecutors search BlackRock in dividend-stripping inquiry: source
description: Prosecutors searched the Munich offices of BlackRock  on Tuesday, a person with knowledge of the matter said, as part of the country's largest post-war fraud investigation.

title: Frost thaws in U.S.-China ties ahead of G20 meeting
description: The United States and China will hold a delayed top-level security dialogue on Friday, the latest sign of a thaw in  relations, as China's vice president said Beijing was willing to talk with Washington to resolve their bitter trade dispute.

title: Boeing, Airbus fret over trade war as China displays aviation ambitions
description: The world's two largest planemakers signaled on Tuesday that they were keen to see an end to a bruising trade war between Washington and Beijing, as China opened its largest airshow with a display that showcased its aviation ambitions.

title: Judges named to hear government's appeal of AT&T Time Warner deal approval
description: A panel of three federal appeals court judges named by former Presidents Ronald Reagan, Bill Clinton and Barack Obama will hear the Justice Department's appeal of a ruling allowing AT&T Inc to acquire Time Warner, court records show.

title: Thomson Reuters eyes 'substantive' purchases after Blackstone deal
description: Thomson Reuters Corp   is looking to make "substantive" acquisitions to boost its legal and tax units after selling a majority stake in its financial terminal business, Chief Executive Jim Smith said on Tuesday.

title: EU approves Disney buy from Fox if makes TV divestments
description: Walt Disney's  $71.3-billion offer to buy Twenty-First Century Fox Inc's  entertainment assets won approval from the European Commission on Tuesday, subject to Disney selling interests in factual TV channels in Europe.

title: Buy, sell or hold: Ten ways to trade the U.S. election
description: Buy the dollar but sell FAANGs, buy real estate and machinery, but sell the overall market. Or, do nothing at all.

title: Cracks emerge in global aviation finance boom
description: An unprecedented boom in the $280 billion aircraft finance industry is showing signs of faltering as rising interest rates, cut-rate competition and higher oil prices trigger a shakeout in a sector that has attracted a flood of Chinese funding.

title: Verizon to reorganize business segments

title: Goldman Sachs, mega-M&A purveyor, looks for smaller deals
description: The top echelons of Goldman Sachs Group Inc's investment bank hosted a dinner over the summer with the representatives of almost 20 private equity firms at Manhattan's Legacy Records restaurant.

title: Citigroup appoints Philip Drury head of EMEA investment banking: memo
description: Citigroup Inc  named Philip Drury to run its London-based banking, capital markets and advisory business across Europe, the Middle East and Africa, according to a memo seen by Reuters.

title: Netanyahu says Trump made courageous decision on U.S. sanctions on Iran
description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu hailed on Monday what he called U.S. President Donald Trump's courageous decision in reimposing U.S. sanctions on Iran.

description: The United States has granted exemptions to eight countries allowing them to temporarily continue buying Iranian oil, Secretary of State Mike Pompeo said on Monday, as Washington reimposed sanctions on Iran's banking, energy and shipping industries.

title: Iran tells U.N. chief: U.S. should be held accountable over sanctions

title: Takeda CEO confident of investor backing for $62 billion Shire deal
description: The boss of Japan's Takeda Pharmaceutical  said on Monday he was confident of securing investor backing for its $62 billion acquisition of London-listed Shire , despite some shareholders' fears about the resulting debt burden.

title: How Hyundai Motor, once a rising star, lost its shine

description: Italian banking shares fell on Monday, with a Goldman Sachs downgrade on Italy's top retail bank Intesa SanPaolo  outweighing its strong performance in European regulatory tests.

description: The European Union is opposed to the United States' decision to reimpose oil and financial sanctions against Iran, European Economic Affairs Commissioner Pierre Moscovici said on Monday.

description: U.S. President Donald Trump has warned that his favorite measure of success, the stock market, is imperiled if voters favor Democrats in next week's congressional elections.

title: Iran in contact with other signatories of nuclear deal as U.S. reinforces sanctions
description: Iran is in constant contact with other signatories of a 2015 nuclear deal reached between Tehran and powers as the United States reinforces lifted sanctions under the pact, Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Bahram Qasemi said on Monday.

title: Underwriter Hiscox reports higher gross written premiums

title: Take Five: World markets themes for the week ahead
description: Following are five big themes likely to dominate thinking of investors and traders in the coming week and the Reuters stories related to them.

title: Japan's Subaru recalls more cars, slashes guidance as cheating issue widens
