description: Comcast  expects to pay the banks, law firms and other advisers on its 25.9 billion pound ($34.23 billion) bid for Sky  as much as 243 million pounds if it wins the battle for the British broadcaster, the U.S. cable giant said on Friday.

title: Facebook, Twitter, Alphabet to testify at U.S. House hearing
description: The U.S. House Judiciary Committee will hold a hearing on Tuesday to take testimony from Facebook Inc, Alphabet Inc's YouTube unit and Twitter Inc on whether social media companies are filtering content for political reasons, the committee chairman said.

title: U.S. lifts ban on suppliers selling to China's ZTE
description: The U.S. Department of Commerce on Friday lifted a ban on U.S. companies selling goods to ZTE Corp, allowing China's second-largest telecommunications equipment maker to resume business.

title: AT&T CEO confident Time Warner deal on solid ground
description: The U.S. Justice Department has only a remote chance of overturning AT&T Inc's takeover of Time Warner, Chief Executive Randall Stephenson said on Friday, adding that the move could affect the bidding war for Twenty-First Century Fox Inc.

title: Exclusive: Jeff Bezos plans to charge at least $200,000 for space rides - sources
description: Jeff Bezos' rocket company plans to charge passengers about $200,000 to $300,000 for its first trips into space next year, two people familiar with its plans told Reuters.

title: Build-A-Bear CEO apologizes after 'heartbreaking' sale crowds
description: Build-A-Bear Workshop Inc's  chief executive on Friday apologized to disappointed customers and offered an extended discount, a day after its one-day pay-your-age event prompted massive crowds and shortages at some stores.

title: J&J vows to overturn $4.7 billion talc verdict but experts see hurdles
description: Johnson & Johnson has vowed to appeal a $4.7 billion verdict awarded to 22 women who claim asbestos-contaminated talc in the company's products gave them ovarian cancer by arguing the plaintiffs' science was flawed and the case should not have been heard in Missouri.

title: Trump vows 'great' trade deal with UK, abruptly changing tack on May's Brexit plan
description: President Donald Trump said on Friday the United States and Britain could secure a "great" post-Brexit trade deal, lavishing praise on Prime Minister Theresa May and contradicting his own withering assessment of her strategy publicized hours earlier.

title: 'Together Against Trump', thousands protest peacefully in London
description: Chanting "Donald Trump has got to go," tens of thousands of protesters marched through London on Friday waving banners and banging pots to demonstrate against the U.S. president on his first official visit to Britain.

title: Republican Senator Rubio slams lifting of U.S. ban on China's ZTE
description: Republican U.S. Senator Marco Rubio criticized on Friday the decision by the United States to lift a ban on suppliers selling to ZTE Corp <000063.SZ), allowing China's second-largest telecommunications equipment maker to resume business.

title: Papa John's to remove founder from promotions; Yankees cuts ties
description: Papa John's International Inc  will remove founder John Schnatter from its promotions, the pizza chain said on Friday, and baseball team New York Yankees suspended business relationships with the company.

title: S&P 500 at five-month high, but banks weigh after results
description: U.S. stocks rose slightly on Friday, putting the S&P 500 at its highest closing level in more than five months, as gains in industrials and other areas offset a drop in financials after results from three of the big banks mostly disappointed.

title: U.S. stocks rise on industrials; dollar flattens
description: The benchmark S&P 500 index hit a more than five-month high on Friday on gains in industrial stocks and energy companies, while the safe-haven U.S. dollar flattened after touching a two-week high.

title: China's trade surplus with U.S. hits record as exporters rush to beat tariffs
description: China's trade surplus with the United States swelled to a record in June as its overall exports grew at a solid pace, a result that could further inflame a bitter trade dispute with Washington.

title: Wells Fargo's loan book shrinks, profit misses estimates
description: Wells Fargo & Co  said on Friday its loan book shrank and it raked in less fee revenue than a year ago, factors that contributed to lower-than-expected quarterly profit and sent its shares lower.

title: Boeing to incur charge related to sale of production facilities
description: Boeing Co  said on Friday it would incur a charge of $124 million in the second quarter related to the sale of some production facilities to Spirit Aerosystems .

title: U.S. sanctions seen barring IT platform of insurer Lloyd's for Iran trade
description: New U.S. sanctions are likely to prevent the use of a Lloyd's of London IT platform for any Iran insurance, adding to difficulties for European insurers providing cover for the country.

title: Dollar fades from two-week high tied to trade fears
description: The dollar dipped against a basket of currencies on Friday, fading from a two-week peak which was tied to news of a record Chinese trade surplus that may fuel U.S.-China trade tensions and that briefly spurred safe-haven bids for the greenback.

title: U.S. banks gain from Washington policy changes but trade worries loom
description: Second-quarter earnings reports from three of the biggest U.S. banks on Friday showed the sector is benefiting from policy changes in Washington that have lowered their taxes, boosted interest rates and allowed them to buy back more stock.

title: China's imports to U.S. ports start peaking early amid tariff threat
description: Chinese imports to U.S. ports rose more than expected in June, suggesting that some retailers moved up orders to insulate themselves from an intensifying trade war that threatens to send up costs on a growing number of consumer products.

title: Fed emphasizes 'solid' U.S economic growth, repeats gradual approach
description: The Federal Reserve on Friday pointed to "solid" U.S. economic growth during the first half of the year in its semi-annual report to Congress, where it also reiterated that it expected to continue to raise interest rates gradually.

title: Oil rises but declines for the week as supply concerns ease
description: Oil prices rose about 1 percent on Friday as strike actions in Norway and Iraq hit supplies, but futures were set for a second straight week of decline after Libyan ports reopened and on the view that Iran might still export some crude despite U.S. sanctions.

title: Wells Fargo CFO says reputation issues a challenge for wealth unit
description: Wells Fargo & Co's  wealth and investment management unit may be having a harder time generating new business because of damage to the bank's reputation from scandals over its sales practices, Chief Financial Officer John Shrewsberry said on Friday.

title: China says industrial policies mainly serve as guidance, open to all
description: China's commerce ministry said on Thursday industrial policies including "Made in China 2025" mainly serve as guidance under market conditions and they are open to all foreign firms.

title: U.S. DoJ will not challenge Aetna-CVS deal: report
description: Shares of CVS Health Corp  and health insurer Aetna Inc  rose more than 2 percent on Thursday after CNBC reported that the U.S. Justice Department will not challenge their planned merger.

title: Microsoft debuts free tier in competitive workplace chat app market
description: Microsoft Corp on Thursday introduced a free tier of its workplace collaboration software Teams to better compete against rival Slack Technologies Inc in a market analysts view as a main battleground in the world of enterprise software.

title: Trade war may steer tax cuts' windfall to even more buybacks
description: The escalating trade war between the United States and China may prompt U.S. companies to shift money they had earmarked for capital expenditures into stock buybacks instead, pushing record levels of corporate share repurchases even higher.

title: Sky shares leap as Comcast and Fox lock horns in bid battle
description: Sky  shares leapt to an 18-year high on Thursday as investors bet a transatlantic battle for the European pay-TV group had further to run, after Comcast's $34 billion bid trumped an offer from Rupert Murdoch made just hours earlier.

title: Exclusive: Linde and Praxair to win EU antitrust nod for $83 billion deal - sources
description: Linde  and Praxair  will win approval regulatory clearance for their planned $83 billion merger after pledging to sell Praxair's assets to boost a Japanese rival in Europe, two people familiar with the matter said on Thursday.

title: U.S. inflation steadily firming; labor market strong
description: U.S. consumer prices recorded their largest increase in nearly 6-1/2 years in the year through June, while the monthly pace continued to suggest a steady buildup of inflation that could keep the Federal Reserve on a path of gradual interest rate increases.

title: Rising fares push Delta past profit estimates
description: Delta Air Lines Inc  topped estimates for quarterly profit and operating revenue Thursday as a rise in average fares trumped an almost 40 percent surge in fuel costs, pushing shares higher.

title: Tesla hits 200,000 cars, meaning lower tax credit for buyers
description: Tesla Inc has delivered 200,000 electric cars to buyers in the United States, a spokesperson said on Thursday, meaning tax credits will now begin to be lowered, while rivals such as Mercedes-Benz, BMW AG and Audi AG will bring electric models to the market with a full tax credit in place.

title: Glencore shares under cloud after U.S demands Congo documents in probe
description: A U.S. demand for documents related to Glencore's  assets in Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) as part of a corruption probe has rattled investors and is likely to weigh on the miner's performance until there is more clarity on the case.

title: Goldman Sachs, Prysmian, others lose challenge against EU cartel fine
description: Investment bank Goldman Sachs , the world's biggest cablemaker Prysmian , Nexans  and eight other cable companies on Thursday lost their challenge against a 302 million euros ($353 million) EU cartel fine.

title: Main Fiat Chrysler unions dismiss Ronaldo strike call as stunt
description: Unions representing the majority of workers at Fiat Chrysler in Italy rejected a strike called by an independent labor group in protest against the huge sums of money spent by Italy's Juventus soccer club  to sign Cristiano Ronaldo.

title: China says has not been in touch with U.S. about restarting trade talks
description: China's commerce ministry said on Thursday that China has not been in touch with the United States about restarting trade negotiations and said complaints about forced technology transfers and IP theft are unacceptable.

title: Papa John's Chairman John Schnatter resigns
description: Pizza chain Papa John's International Inc  said on Wednesday its founder and former chief executive, John Schnatter, resigned as chairman of the board.

title: China's ZTE clears hurdle to lifting U.S. ban
description: The United States said on Wednesday that it signed an agreement with ZTE Corp  that paves the way for the Chinese tech company to resume operations after a nearly three-month ban on doing business with American suppliers.

title: Britain finally clears Murdoch's Fox to bid for Sky
description: Britain finally cleared Rupert Murdoch to buy Sky  on Thursday, removing the final obstacle to a head-to-head battle between Murdoch's Twenty-First Century Fox  and U.S. rival Comcast  for the European pay-TV prize.

title: Chipmaker Broadcom inks $19 billion deal to buy software company CA
description: Broadcom Inc announced a $18.9 billion deal to buy U.S. business software company CA Inc on Wednesday, venturing far beyond its realm of semiconductors and testing investors' confidence in its Chief Executive Hock Tan's dealmaking credentials.

title: As Trump amps up trade war, China plays nice with foreign investors
description: Long accused of protectionist tactics that make it a difficult place for foreign firms to operate, China is trying to reverse that narrative amid an escalating trade war with the United States, green-lighting huge investments and portraying itself as a champion of openness.

title: China does not need U.S. soybeans for state reserves: Sinograin official
description: China, the world's top soybean buyer, can fully meet the needs of its state soybean reserves without importing from the United States, an official with the state stockpiler told state TV on Thursday.

title: China says hopes U.S. firms will lobby Washington to defend their China interests
description: China's commerce ministry said on Thursday it hopes American firms operating in China will lobby the U.S. government and defend their interests as they will be impacted by U.S. trade action.

title: Panasonic plans to halve cobalt content of car batteries in two-three years
description: Panasonic Corp  plans to halve the cobalt content of its mass-produced automotive batteries "in two to three years", an executive at the Japanese conglomerate said on Thursday, as battery makers look to reduce costs.

title: U.S. companies in China mostly oppose tariffs, survey shows
description: Most U.S. businesses operating in China oppose using tariffs as a weapon to solve their problems ranging from market access to poor protection of intellectual property rights, a survey suggested on Thursday.

title: Goodbye inverted yield curve? Fed looks for alternative signals to guide policy
description: Federal Reserve officials are scouring new niches of the financial markets to find signals accurate enough to warn the central bank when it is time to stop hiking interest rates before they risk tipping the economy into a recession.

title: BMW says developing joint venture with China's Brilliance
description: German carmaker BMW  said it was developing its joint venture with China's Brilliance  but did not confirm reports it would raise its stake in BMW Brilliance Automotive (BBA).

title: U.S. would re-open trade talks if China makes major changes: Mnuchin
description: The United States and China could reopen talks on trade but only if Beijing is willing to make significant changes, U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin said on Thursday.

title: Japan's ANA cancels more flights for engine inspection
description: Japanese airline ANA Holdings  canceled 330 domestic flights from July 23 through July 31, and warned of further cancellations in August as it continues to inspect engines built by Rolls-Royce .

title: EU unconditionally approves Ryanair purchase of LaudaMotion
description: The European Commission said on Thursday that it had approved Ryanair's  planned acquisition of LaudaMotion without conditions.

title: Intel acquires small chipmaker to bolster efforts beyond CPUs
description: Intel Corp  said on Thursday that it plans to acquire  eASIC, a small chipmaker that will help further Intel's efforts to diversify away from CPU chips.

title: Importers snap up cheap U.S. soybeans as China stops buying
description: China's retaliatory tariffs on U.S. soybeans, threatened for weeks and enacted Friday, have driven down prices and triggered a wave of bargain shopping by importers in other countries stocking up on cheap U.S. supplies, according to a Reuters analysis of government data.

title: Wall Street bounces back; technology, industrials lead
description: U.S. stocks climbed on Thursday as top technology names hit record highs and industrials rebounded from losses driven by trade worries the day before.

title: Apollo Global, CEO Leon Black sued by Caldera Holdings
description: Apollo Global Management  and its Chief Executive Leon Black are being sued by Caldera Holdings, a venture founded by Imran Siddiqui, a former managing director at the buyout firm, a court filing on Thursday showed.

title: Apple launches $300 million green energy fund in China
description: Apple Inc  will launch a $300 million clean energy fund in China, the firm said in a statement on Friday, working with its suppliers to invest in renewable energy projects that could power close to 1 million homes in the country.

title: Ryanair Irish pilot union announces two more one-day strikes
description: Ryanair's Irish pilots are planning to hold two more one-day strikes on July 20 and July 24, a spokesman for the IALPA/FORSA union told Reuters on Thursday.

title: U.S. stock futures hit five-month high
description: U.S. stock futures rose to a five-month high on Friday, extending their recent rally on expectations of solid earnings growth among U.S. firms despite threats from trade wars.

title: Walmart says no decision to sell Japan Seiyu supermarket unit
description: U.S. retailer Walmart Inc  on Thursday said it has not decided to sell its Japanese supermarket chain Seiyu and would continue to develop its business in Japan.

title: Jury orders J&J to pay $4.7 billion in Missouri asbestos cancer case
description: A Missouri jury on Thursday ordered Johnson & Johnson  to pay a record $4.69 billion to 22 women who alleged the company's talc-based products, including its baby powder, contain asbestos and caused them to develop ovarian cancer.

title: EU, Mexico, Volkswagen among those to testify at U.S. import tariff hearing
description: The European Union, Japan, Canada, Mexico, along with automotive trade groups, Volkswagen AG , and the United Auto Workers union are among those scheduled to testify at a July 19 hearing on the Trump administration's investigation into whether imported autos and parts pose a national security threat, according to a document seen Thursday by Reuters.

title: P&G says Canada denies tariff exemptions, many products hit
description: Many Procter & Gamble Co  products sold in Canada - from Febreze candles to Gillette shaving foam - will be affected by retaliatory tariffs on U.S.-made goods after Canadian authorities rejected a request for exemptions, a P&G spokesman said on Wednesday.

title: Beef, eggs, animal feed fatten Cargill's profits
description: Strong global demand for beef and animal feed fattened grain trader Cargill Inc's profits in fiscal year 2018, which were also boosted by trade tensions and South American weather woes, the company said on Thursday.

title: Brent oil rises on concerns about spare capacity
description: Brent crude strengthened late on Thursday, recouping some of its losses from the previous session, as market focus returned to concerns about spare capacity following a warning from the International Energy Agency (IEA).

title: UK nears decision to buy Boeing AWACS planes: sources
description: Britain's government is nearing a decision to buy four to six surveillance planes built by U.S. aerospace giant Boeing , sources familiar with the plans said on Thursday, a move that could stir a growing debate over UK and European defense jobs.

title: Top Twitter users lose 2 percent of followers on average as policy changes
description: A Twitter Inc  policy change on Thursday to increase the service's credibility cost its 100 most popular users about 2 percent of their followers, on average, according to social media data firm Keyhole.

title: Singapore's GIC flags lower long-term returns in tough investment climate
description: Singapore sovereign wealth fund GIC has trimmed its exposure to developed market equities such as U.S. stocks over the past year on high valuations, and cautioned it expects lower long-term returns in an uncertain investment climate.

title: Broadcom's ambitious deal history under CEO Hock Tan
description: Broadcom Ltd made an $18.9 billion bid for software firm CA Inc on Wednesday, the latest in the company's acquisition spree aimed at diversifying beyond semiconductors.

title: A decade on, pre-crisis mortgages linger for big banks, homeowners
description: A decade on big U.S. banks are still running down and selling off crisis-era mortgages, a process executives point to as weighing on loan growth.

title: Dollar gains sustained by trade war risk, rising inflation
description: The U.S. dollar held steady at a six-month high against the Japanese yen and a two-month high against the Swiss franc on Thursday, bolstered by solid inflation data and investor sentiment that the greenback stands to benefit from a trade war.

title: German state premier opposes breakup of Thyssenkrupp
description: The premier of the German state where Thyssenkrupp  is based on Thursday backed the company's chairman in opposing a breakup of the industrial conglomerate following the resignation of CEO Heinrich Hiesinger.

title: House Speaker casts doubt on Congress acting to stop trade tariffs
description: U.S. House Speaker Paul Ryan said on Thursday that while he does not support President Donald Trump's moves to impose tariffs on major U.S. trading partners' goods, he questioned the wisdom of Congress taking legislative action to stop such sanctions.

title: Fed's escape from crisis holdings could hit dead end
description: Not long ago the Federal Reserve expected to quietly shed nearly half of its $4.5-trillion portfolio by around 2022, leaving little trace of the extraordinary steps it took to face down the financial crisis. But an unexpected market kink could force the Fed to scrap the plan two or three years early and permanently leave it holding $1 trillion more than it wanted.

title: Broadcom loses $19 billion in market value after bid to buy CA
description: Chipmaker Broadcom Inc's surprise bid to buy software company CA Inc for $18.9 billion wiped off the same amount from its market value on Thursday, with investors and analysts struggling to find a clear reason for the deal.

title: France's La Poste plans to buy stake in insurer CNP Assurances: source
description: France's La Poste is planning to buy the stake in insurer CNP Assurances  held by state-owned investment fund Caisse des Depots though the details of the deal are not yet finalised, a source close to the mail company told Reuters on Thursday.

title: Tech stocks touch record highs, dollar steadies as trade fears ebb
description: U.S. stocks closed higher on Thursday as industrials rebounded and technology names soared, while commodities recovered and the dollar held steady after concerns over an escalating U.S. trade war with China took a breather.

title: China says 'bully' United States started a trade war
description: The United States has started a trade war and China will defend itself, Chinese Vice Minister of Commerce Wang Shouwen said on Thursday, urging the United States to "take the gun" of tariffs away to smooth the way for talks.

title: Beijing urges U.S. firms in China to lobby Washington over trade war
description: China on Thursday said foreign firms operating in China would suffer in a trade war, urging U.S. companies to lobby their government to protect their interests, and said no talks to end the impasse were currently under way.

title: China to its state media: keep calm, don't inflame trade row with U.S.
description: China is clearly angry about Washington's hard line on trade, but has controlled coverage of the row in its media, limiting open commentary and banning attacks on U.S. President Donald Trump, several sources with knowledge of the matter said.

title: U.S. producer inflation rises on strong services gains
description: U.S. producer prices increased more than expected in June amid gains in the cost of services and motor vehicles, leading to the biggest annual increase in 6-1/2 years.

title: U.S. House Speaker Ryan: tariffs not the way to go in China trade dispute
description: U.S. House of Representatives Speaker Paul Ryan said on Wednesday tariffs are not the right tool to use in the trade dispute with China, although Beijing engages in unfair trade practices.

title: BlackRock plans its largest ever alternative investment fundraiser
description: BlackRock Inc  is planning to raise $3.5 billion for investments in energy infrastructure in what is poised to be its largest alternative investment fund yet, an executive at the world's largest asset manager told Reuters.

title: Facebook faces small but symbolic UK fine over data protection breaches
description: Britain's information regulator slapped Facebook with a small but symbolic fine for breaches of data protection law after millions of users' data was improperly accessed by consultancy Cambridge Analytica.

title: U.S. May wholesale inventories revised higher
description: U.S. wholesale inventories were a bit higher than initially estimated in May amid strong increases in the stocks of machinery and a range of other goods.

title: Credit Suisse nears $360 million deadline in fraud suit built on a hunch
description: When the high-end property development Lake Las Vegas collapsed during the 2008 financial crisis, 31 funds that helped finance the project lost a total of $540 million. But only one of them, Dallas-based hedge fund Highland Capital Management, aggressively pursued legal action against Credit Suisse Group AG, which arranged the financing and appraisals for the project.

title: U.S. home refinancing requests drop to lowest since 2000: MBA
description: U.S. loan applications to refinance existing homes fell to their lowest in over 17-1/2 years even as most 30-year home borrowing costs fell last week, data from the Mortgage Bankers Association showed on Wednesday.

title: After Tesla deal, Shanghai to speed up cancellation of foreign ownership limits
description: Shanghai will accelerate efforts to cancel restrictions on foreign investment in the auto manufacturing sector, a government official said on Wednesday, a day after Tesla  said it would build a wholly owned auto plant in the city.

title: China's CIC sovereign fund says trade war would hurt its investments
description: The president of China's CIC sovereign wealth fund said on Wednesday that a trade war appeared unavoidable, and that the dispute would have a negative impact on CIC's investments.

title: China says it stands on the right side of history in protecting multilateralism
description: China stands on the right side of history in defending multilateralism, its foreign ministry said on Wednesday, after U.S. President Donald Trump's administration threatened 10 percent tariffs on $200 billion worth of Chinese imports.

title: Ex-Apple worker charged with stealing self-driving car trade secrets
description: U.S. authorities charged a former Apple Inc  employee with stealing trade secrets on Monday, accusing him of downloading a blueprint related to a self-driving car to a personal laptop before trying to flee the country for China, according to a criminal complaint filed in federal court.

title: India's Vistara orders Boeing, Airbus jets worth $3.1 billion in growth plan
description: Indian airline Vistara has placed firm orders for six Boeing Co  787 jets and 13 Airbus SE  A320neos valued at $3.1 billion at list prices, as it looks to add more domestic flights and launch international routes later this year.

title: Malaysia reviews monopoly risk in ride-hailing market after Grab-Uber deal
description: Malaysia is studying monopoly risk in the ride-hailing market in the country triggered by the merger of Grab and Uber, and is bringing the service under some existing regulations, the transport ministry said on Wednesday.

title: Glencore to cooperate with U.S. corruption investigation
description: Glencore Plc  said on Wednesday it would cooperate with U.S. authorities after they demanded documents about the mining firm's business in Democratic Republic of Congo, Venezuela and Nigeria as part of a corruption investigation.

title: Australia prepares to ban Huawei from 5G project over security fears
description: Australia is preparing to ban Huawei Technologies Co Ltd from supplying equipment for its planned 5G broadband network after its intelligence agencies raised concerns that Beijing could force the Chinese telco to hand over sensitive data, two sources said.

title: Japan watchdog: Apple may have breached antitrust rules with iPhone
description: Japanese regulators said on Wednesday Apple Inc  may have breached antitrust rules by forcing mobile service providers to sell its iPhones cheaply and charge higher monthly fees, denying consumers a fair choice.

title: Citi readies for Asia investment surge with new China desk as trade war intensifies
description: Citigroup Inc  will set up a China business desk in India within the year betting on a pickup in investment flows within the Asian region, its Asia-Pacific corporate banking head said, as concerns grow about the impact of a Sino-U.S. trade war.

title: China says plans by U.S. for additional tariffs completely unacceptable
description: China's commerce ministry said on Wednesday the proposed U.S. tariffs on an extra $200 billion of Chinese goods is completely unacceptable, adding that Beijing will have to respond to the latest moves by Washington.

title: Morgan Stanley manager steps down amid complaints against brokers
description: Morgan Stanley  said on Wednesday that Robert Perry, manager for the firm's Beverly Hills, California, wealth management office, has left the firm.

title: Canada's Tim Hortons to enter China as it battles slump at home
description: Fast-food company Restaurant Brands International  said on Wednesday it plans to open 1,500 outlets of its Canadian coffee-and-donut chain Tim Hortons in China over the next decade, capitalizing on a growing cafe culture in the world's second-largest economy.

title: Papa John's drops after report alleges chairman used racial slur
description: ** Shares of Papa John's International Inc  pizza chain down 3.5 pct to a more-than-two-year low on Wednesday a report that Chairman, founder and former CEO John Schnatter used a racial slur on a conference call

title: Exclusive: Airbus faces A330 delivery delays amid HNA Group woes - sources
description: Airbus faces a logjam of undelivered A330 jets worth well over $1 billion for airlines affiliated to China's debt-laden HNA Group following a stand-off over late payments, according to industry sources and a Reuters examination of parked aircraft.

title: Embraer counts on Brazil's public-sector funds to approve Boeing JV: sources
description: Planemaker Embraer SA  is counting on the votes of public-sector Brazilian shareholders to outweigh any potential investor objections to its tie-up with Boeing SA , two people with knowledge of the matter said.

title: Trump told Pfizer CEO price hikes hurt his drug plan: source
description: U.S. President Donald Trump called Pfizer Chief Executive Ian Read on Tuesday to say the company's July 1 price hikes had complicated the administration's drug pricing plans, prompting the company to defer its planned increases, according to a source familiar with the matter.

title: Comcast raises bid for Sky to $34 billion, tops Fox's offer
description: Comcast Corp  on Wednesday raised its all-cash offer for Britain's Sky  to $34 billion, topping a raised bid of $32.5 billion for the pay-TV group from Rupert Murdoch's Twenty-First Century Fox .

title: Walmart looks to exit Japan with Seiyu supermarket sale: NIkkei
description: U.S. retailer Walmart Inc  has decided to sell Japanese supermarket chain Seiyu and has already approached major retailers and private equity funds, the Nikkei business daily reported on Thursday.

title: Walmex's new e-commerce VP eyes groceries to propel online business
description: Wal Mart de Mexico's  new e-commerce head plans to play to its strengths in grocery deliveries to help the country's largest retailer stand apart from rivals, like Amazon.com Inc and his former employer MercadoLibre Inc, he said in an interview Wednesday.

title: China vows to hit back over U.S. proposal for fresh tariffs
description: China accused the United States of bullying and warned it would hit back after the Trump administration raised the stakes in their trade dispute, threatening 10 percent tariffs on $200 billion of Chinese goods in a move that rattled global markets.

title: U.S. says the 'reckoning' over China trade is too big for WTO
description: A "reckoning" over China's unfair trade policies is urgent and is too big for the World Trade Organization to handle, U.S. ambassador Dennis Shea told a WTO meeting on Wednesday.

title: ZTE shares soar after clearing last hurdle to lifting of U.S. ban
description: Hong Kong shares of ZTE Corp  surged nearly 24 percent on Thursday after China's No. 2 telecommunications equipment maker cleared the last hurdle to lifting a U.S. ban on component supplies.

title: Dollar hits six-month high against yen on strong inflation
description: The U.S. dollar strengthened against the Japanese yen on Wednesday as trade tensions mounted and after the Labor Department's expectation-beating inflation report, which increased prospects that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates another two times this year.

title: NBA's Silver sees win-win in bidding war for Fox
description: NBA Commissioner Adam Silver said he expected the league to benefit from a battle between Comcast Corp  and Walt Disney Co.  for Twenty-First Century Fox Inc , regardless of which suitor pulls ahead.

title: Glencore faces lawsuits over U.S. subpoena, stock drop
description: Glencore Plc faces at least two lawsuits by U.S. shareholders accusing the big Anglo-Swiss mining company of having made false and misleading disclosures before it received a subpoena in a corruption probe, and its stock tumbled.

title: Stocks, oil prices slide on trade war worries
description: Concerns about an escalating U.S.-China trade war made markets topsy-turvy on Wednesday, with U.S. stocks breaking a four-session winning streak and Brent crude prices seeing their biggest one-day drop in two years.

title: Twitter says removal of fake accounts does not hurt user metrics
description: Twitter Inc  said on Monday it has removed fake accounts but that does not impact its reported user metrics as was indicated in a report by The Washington Post.

title: Uber executive Hornsey resigns in email to staff following discrimination probe
description: Uber Technologies Inc's Chief People Officer Liane Hornsey resigned in an email to staff on Tuesday, following an investigation into how she handled allegations of racial discrimination at the ride-hailing firm.

title: Pfizer separates consumer health unit in business rejig
description: Pfizer Inc announced plans on Wednesday to reorganize into three units, separating its consumer healthcare business that the U.S. drugmaker has been trying to sell since last year.

title: Brazil prosecutors allege jailed GE executive helped company partake in medical cartel
description: General Electric Co's  chief executive for Latin America took part in a medical equipment price-fixing scheme while at the conglomerate, making it a member of an international health-care cartel, according to allegations in a document filed by federal prosecutors.

title: JD.com's finance affiliate raises $2 billion, more than doubles valuation
description: JD.com Inc's finance affiliate said on Thursday it has signed binding agreements with investors to raise 13 billion yuan ($1.96 billion) in fresh equity at a valuation of nearly $20 billion.

title: Wall Street snaps four-day rally; latest trade threat weighs
description: U.S. stocks fell on Wednesday, breaking a four-session streak of gains after Washington's threat to impose tariffs on an additional $200 billion worth of Chinese goods fanned trade war fears, while a sharp drop in oil prices hit energy shares.

title: Comcast makes higher offer for Sky, tops Fox bid
description: Comcast Corp  on Wednesday raised its offer for Britain's Sky  in a deal valuing the pay-TV group at $34 billion, challenging a raised bid from Twenty-First Century Fox .

title: Bike-share schemes battle for Paris turf, but it's not all free-wheeling
description: Grabbing a bicycle from a docking station and riding the streets of Paris used to be one of the city's many charms, but the once-loved Velib system has fallen into disarray and some new dockless bike-share schemes are struggling to survive.

title: Success with Snap helps venture firm Lightspeed raise $1.8 billion for new funds
description: Venture capital firm Lightspeed Venture Partners has raised $1.8 billion to invest in startups from cryptocurrency to beauty supplies, hoping to build on its streak of lucrative bets in companies such as Snap Inc , the firm's partners told Reuters.

title: U.S. job quits rate hits 17-year high; labor market tightening
description: More American workers voluntarily quit their jobs in May, government data showed on Tuesday, a sign of confidence in the labor market that economists say will soon boost wage growth.

title: Morgan Stanley's Pick promoted to head of institutional securities: memo
description: Morgan Stanley  has promoted Ted Pick to head of its trading and investment banking businesses, the most recent elevation for an executive who has overseen several key initiatives at the Wall Street bank.

title: Air France-KLM CEO hunt signals industry strategy shift under Macron
description: The hunt for a new chief executive to lead Air France-KLM, a group hobbled by union resistance to cost-cutting at its French brand, is testing President Emmanuel Macron's resolve for a lighter state touch on the economy.

title: Stability needed after CEO exit, say Thyssenkrupp workers, foundation
description: Thyssenkrupp's  workers and its leading shareholder will serve as an anchor of stability at the company following the sudden departure of Chief Executive Heinrich Hiesinger, they told a German regional newspaper.

title: PepsiCo beverage sales signal gradual recovery, shares rise
description: PepsiCo Inc's  better-than-expected quarterly results on Tuesday pointed to signs of a gradual recovery in its struggling soda business as the company doubled down on efforts to promote colas, setting shares up for their best day in seven years.

title: Airbus renames Canadian jet as A220, seen near U.S. deal
description: Airbus gave its newly acquired Canadian CSeries jet a new name and looked close to winning an inaugural order on Tuesday as it prepares to broaden its battle with Boeing for jet sales.

title: VW names Sedran as head of commercial vehicles
description: Volkswagen  has named Thomas Sedran to lead its commercial vehicles division, VW said on Tuesday, confirming media reports.

title: Tesla moves first to hike prices in China as trade war hits car makers
description: U.S. carmaker Tesla Inc has hiked prices on its Model X and S cars by about 20 percent in China, the first automaker to do so in the world's top automotive market in response to mounting trade tensions between the countries.

title: VW agrees Chinese cooperation on e-mobility, autonomous driving
description: Volkswagen  said it has agreed to cooperate with China's FAW Group  and the China Intelligent and Connected Vehicles Research Institute (ICV) on technologies including e-mobility, connectivity and autonomous driving.

title: Japan's Takeda gains U.S. approval for $62 billion Shire buy
description: Takeda Pharmaceutical Co Ltd on Tuesday said it has received U.S. approval for its $62 billion acquisition of London-listed Shire Plc, taking the Japanese firm one step closer to its goal of becoming a global top 10 drugmaker.

title: China raises tariff rates for some U.S. optical fiber products, from July 11
description: China's commerce ministry said on Tuesday it is raising "anti-dumping tariff rates" for some optical fiber products originating from the United States, effective on Wednesday, July 11.

title: Fuji Xerox chief sees no breakup of Fujifilm-Xerox JV
description: The head of Fuji Xerox Co Ltd, the joint venture between Fujifilm Holdings Corp  and Xerox Corp , on Tuesday said an escalating dispute between the partners will not lead to the venture's dissolution.

title: Former Goldman Sachs banker in 1MDB plea talks with U.S.: WSJ
description: A former Goldman Sachs Group Inc.  banker is in talks with U.S. prosecutors to potentially plead guilty to criminal charges stemming from an alleged scheme to steal billions of dollars from a Malaysian state investment fund, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

title: Old fashion: Vintage boom buoys RealReal and jolts luxury labels
description: Second-hand fashion, once confined to thrift stores, is outstripping sales growth in the primary luxury goods sector, helping market leader The RealReal expand its business and prompting international labels to look at tie-ups.

title: RSA's Martin Scicluna lined up to chair Sainsbury's: Sky News
description: Sainsbury's , the British supermarket group that is merging with rival Asda, has lined up Martin Scicluna as the successor to chairman David Tyler, Sky News reported on Tuesday.

title: SoftBank tightens grip on Yahoo Japan via $2 billion deal with Altaba
description: SoftBank Group  is increasing its stake in Yahoo Japan  through a $2 billion, three-way deal with U.S. firm Altaba  to deepen ties with the internet heavyweight ahead of an IPO of its telecoms unit.

title: SEC charges ex-Heartland Payment CEO with insider trading
description: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on Tuesday charged the former chief executive of Heartland Payment Systems Inc with insider trading for tipping his longtime romantic partner about the payment processor's $4.3 billion takeover by Global Payments Inc .

title: Offshore yuan falls more than 0.5 percent after U.S. announces new tariffs
description: The offshore yuan fell more than 0.5 percent in early trade on Wednesday after Washington announced a plan to slap tariffs on $200 billion of imports from China, escalating tensions between the world's two biggest economies.

title: Airbus wins JetBlue order for its newly rebranded A220
description: Airbus SE scored a key victory on Tuesday, with U.S. airline JetBlue  announcing it would buy 60 of its A220-300 narrowbody jets, the first major order for the planemaker's newly rebranded program as its battle with rival Boeing Co intensifies.

title: SoftBank's Son says to carry on with deals despite trade jitters
description: SoftBank Group Corp  CEO Masayoshi Son said on Tuesday he was optimistic that U.S. President Donald Trump's escalation of trade disputes and heightened scrutiny of foreign investments would not affect the Japanese firm's prolific dealmaking.

title: U.S. says to slap tariffs on extra $200 billion of Chinese imports
description: The Trump administration raised the stakes in its trade war with China on Tuesday, saying it would slap 10 percent tariffs on an extra $200 billion worth of Chinese imports.

title: China commerce ministry official says new U.S. tariff plan harms WTO system, globalization
description: China's assistant commerce minister said on Wednesday that the latest proposed tariffs from the United States harms the World Trade Organization system and hurts globalization.

title: Pfizer delays drug price hikes after talking with Trump
description: Pfizer Inc  said on Tuesday it was deferring drug price increases for no more than six months after the company's chief executive officer had an extensive conversation with U.S. President Donald Trump.

title: Criminal case sheds light on Apple self-driving car technology
description: The criminal complaint filed Monday against an ex-Apple Inc  employee for allegedly stealing self-driving car trade secrets from the Cupertino company provides a handful of new details about its work on the technology, experts said.

title: Dow Jones futures extend fall, down one percent in Asian trade
description: U.S. stock futures extended their losses on Wednesday after Washington announced a plan to slap tariffs on an extra $200 billion of imports from China, sharply escalating a trade war between the world's two biggest economies.

title: Tesla goes big in China with Shanghai plant
description: Tesla Inc  Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk on Tuesday landed a deal with Chinese authorities to build a new auto plant in Shanghai, its first factory outside the United States, that would double the size of the electric car maker's global manufacturing.

title: S&P 500 posts highest close since February; futures fall late on tariff fears
description: The S&P 500 rose on Tuesday to post its highest closing level since Feb. 1, the day before the market began a sharp extended selloff, as strong results from PepsiCo boosted optimism about the earnings season.

title: U.S. may list tariffs on $200 billion more Chinese products: official
description: U.S. President Donald Trump is likely to publish this week a list of $200 billion in additional Chinese products to be hit with tariffs, possibly as early as later on Tuesday, an administration official said.

title: Daimler, Bosch to deploy self-driving taxis in California test program
description: German automaker Daimler AG and auto supplier Bosch Corp [ROBSCJ.UL] will deploy self-driving taxis in California's Silicon Valley region next year as part of a test program of vehicles designed for city driving, the two companies said on Tuesday.

title: Boeing's first-half deliveries up seven percent, orders surge past Airbus
description: Boeing Co's  first-half aircraft deliveries rose more than 7 percent, lifted by demand for its bestselling 737 jetliners as airlines seek more fuel-efficient planes, and orders were more than double those of European rival Airbus SE .

title: Raytheon, Lockheed, Northrop Grumman win $4.1 billion U.S. defense contract
description: Raytheon Co , Lockheed Martin Corp  and Northrop Grumman Corp  are each being awarded a multiple award U.S. defense contract worth a maximum $4.1 billion for ballistic missile defense, the Pentagon said on Tuesday.

title: Oil rises on supply disruptions, large U.S. crude stock drawdown
description: Oil rose on Tuesday, supported by a larger-than expected U.S. stock draw and supply concerns in Norway and Libya, though gains were tempered by the United States' indication that it would consider requests for waivers from Iranian oil sanctions.

title: U.S. stocks rise on earnings optimism; dollar gains
description: The S&P 500 stock index closed at a more than five-month high on Tuesday, boosted by expectations for strong earnings, while the U.S. dollar rose against the safe-haven Japanese yen as waning trade war fears drove a bid for riskier assets.

title: U.S. judge allows lawsuits over Monsanto's Roundup to proceed to trial
description: Hundreds of lawsuits against Monsanto Co by cancer survivors or families of those who died can proceed to trial, a federal judge ruled on Tuesday, finding there was sufficient evidence for a jury to hear the cases that blame the company's glyphosate-containing weed-killer for the disease.

title: BOJ keeps upbeat view on regional Japan, labor shortages cloud outlook
description: The Bank of Japan maintained its upbeat economic assessment for all nine regions of the country but some areas saw companies fret about rising costs from labor shortages, a sign that a tightening job market could constrain business activity.

title: Saudi Arabian Airlines in Boeing 777X order talks: sources
description: Saudi Arabian Airlines is exploring a potential order for Boeing  777X widebody jets, according to three sources familiar with the matter.

title: Sea of red in Treasury market may signal bond boom is over
description: The 10-year U.S. Treasury note that debuted in August 2016 <9128282A7=RRPS> when the bond market was near its peak has had a rough ride, its price falling ever since and no reprieve in sight.

title: Carillion collapse exposed flaws in UK government policy: lawmakers
description: The collapse of Carillion  exposed the risks of using private companies to cut the cost of delivering public services and its failure could be repeated if the government does not learn lessons, lawmakers said on Monday.

title: Air France KLM's traffic rises, sources coy on latest name in CEO frame
description: Air France KLM , hit by strikes and without a CEO since May, reported higher traffic figures that lifted its battered shares, while sources voiced caution about the possible appointment of a top French transport executive as its new boss.

title: Chinese customs clears some U.S. goods as new tariffs take effect: sources
description: Major Chinese ports have started clearing goods from the United States on Monday, as new tariffs on U.S. imports have gone into effect, three sources told Reuters, as a trade spat between Beijing and Washington escalated into an outright war last Friday.

title: China says tariffs on U.S. goods to be used to ease impact of trade fight
description: China's commerce ministry said on Monday that it will use funds collected from tariffs charged on imports from the United States to help ease the impact of U.S. trade actions on Chinese companies and their employees.

title: Aramco more resilient to oil slump than listed rivals: accounts
description: Saudi Aramco is more resilient to oil price slumps than its biggest listed rivals, its 2016 accounts indicate, giving a rare insight into the state energy giant's finances ahead of a proposed flotation.

title: The Foxconns of fast beauty propel South Korean cosmetics' success in China
description: At a factory two hours south of Seoul, women clad in plastic caps and masks put peach-colored eye-shadow into cases, right next to a machine churning out a skin-color face powder.

title: Higher oil prices to spur Farnborough jet orders: IBA
description: Global planemakers could reap 900 orders and commitments at next week's Farnborough Airshow, down only slightly from last year's comparable event, as strong oil prices prompt airlines to add to their bulging order books, aviation consultancy IBA Group said.

title: Third of sovereign funds plan to cut equity holdings, cite trade war fear

title: Citi bolsters Paris hub ahead of Brexit
description: Citigroup  is boosting its operations in France ahead of Brexit with a series of senior appointments, according to an internal memo reviewed by Reuters on Monday.

description: Starbucks Corp's  outgoing Executive Chairman Howard Schultz said on Monday that a recent slowdown in China would be short-lived, seeking to salve investor concerns that the U.S. coffee chain is under pressure in the fast-growing market.

description: Shares in French carmaker Renault  fell on Monday, dragged down by a drop in the stock price of its partner Nissan  after the Japanese firm said it would issue an explanation about its emissions measurement processes.

title: U.S. metal tariffs could hurt output in western Japan: BOJ official
description: U.S. metal import tariffs could have a big negative impact on auto and other final goods production in the Kansai western Japan region, a senior Bank of Japan official said on Monday.

title: Xiaomi's weak debut signals trouble for upcoming Hong Kong tech listings
description: Xiaomi Corp made a weak debut in Hong Kong on Monday, with the Chinese smartphone maker's shares sliding as much as 6 percent on valuation concerns, in an ominous sign for its technology sector peers lining up listings in the city.

title: Comcast lining up buyers for Fox sports assets: sources
description: Comcast Corp  is identifying potential buyers for Twenty-First Century Fox Inc's  regional sports networks in an attempt to ease antitrust concerns about a new bid to acquire most of Fox's assets, people familiar with the matter told Reuters.

title: Norway denies holding up Tesla move to improve service
description: Norway has rejected a suggestion it is holding up Tesla's  efforts to improve service in its third-biggest market, saying the electric carmaker has not yet applied to use the mobile service vans it says it needs to solve its problems.

title: Fox preparing to top Comcast offer for Sky: FT
description: Twenty-First Century Fox Inc  is preparing a new bid for Sky Plc  that values it at about 25 billion pounds  ($33.14 billion) to top the offer it has received from Comcast Corp , the Financial Times reported on Monday.

title: Do not blame OPEC, oil producer group says of Trump criticism
description: The president of OPEC defended the oil producer group on Monday against U.S. President Donald Trump’s recent demands for higher oil output, saying OPEC does not shoulder the blame.

title: Uber, Alphabet invest in bike sharing service Lime
description: Bike sharing service Lime said on Monday it raised $335 million from a group of investors including ride-sharing firm Uber Technologies Inc and Alphabet Inc .

description: Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co  can boost manufacturing at its facility in Wisconsin if trade tensions with China escalate, Chief Executive Antonio Neri said on Monday.

description: Four senior U.S. House Republicans sent letters on Monday to the chief executives of Apple Inc  and Google parent Alphabet Inc  asking questions about location data and mobile phone privacy practices and the handling of customer data.

title: BlackRock expands in Paris with new hires ahead of Brexit, source says

description: Siemens  and Alstom  are set to face a full-scale EU antitrust investigation this week after declining to provide concessions to allay regulatory concerns about their plan to combine their rail operations, two people familiar with the matter said.

title: Twitter shares fall after report says account suspensions to cause user decline

title: Embraer shareholder files complaint against Boeing deal: paper

description: A departing senior executive at China's ZTE Corp , which is fighting a crippling U.S. supplier ban, said in a letter to staff on Friday that his departure amid a Sino-US trade war was "deeply humiliating".

title: Orange says open to French telecom tie-up talks, not an instigator
description: French telecoms firms Orange  is open to discussing potential tie-ups with other operators in its home market but is not likely to be the instigator of consolidation in the sector, financial chief Ramon Fernandez said.

description: Venezuela's domestic airline industry is struggling to maintain operations due to hyperinflation and shortages of spare parts, according to an industry association, making it increasingly hard to obtain tickets and causing chronic flight delays.

description: At an abandoned train station in Buenos Aires' working-class suburb of San Miguel, hundreds of Argentines gather with bags of clothes, rice, flour and sugar to trade.
